item.title: Scores - 2022
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Below are the scores since I started playing. Link it the date column is the scorecard, link on the course is my writeup of the round in the blog. Lots of 2 ball practice in there at the moment.

Even though some may argue to not score early on, I'm hoping to find value with this as part of the journey.

Hoping to add in a bunch more here in the near future. Northwest Executive 9, Blue Mash, Needwood proper. I'd like to get the executives at least in the high 40s before I start playing the 18 hole course.

I'm linking the scores to the Grint. I know I'm not at the point of scoring, but watching improvement over time is a high motivator to get better.

item.title: Goals
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Goals for 2026

SIM Stuff

  • SIM round below 80 on a 5000 yard+ course Par 72 course ( your getting close with the recent 82).
  • SIM Average less than 83 (you've gone from a 105 to 88, 5 strokes to go)
  • SIM handicap down below 10 (current 16.5 1/29). This is a stretch, but as much as your playing. The 83 average should be close, but you probably need a good run of 83 or lowers.
  • Lower the boost down to zero, and figure out how to get more than 200 yards off the tee consistently (new club?)
  • Increase iron consistency - your can measure this with improved stats
  • No double bogey rounds -- at least 1

Outdoor goals

  • Play 3x a month through the season --- I'd like to try to get at least a round in a week, but 3x is probably going to be about right. I am thinking of buying a push cart, and walking my rounds often this season. Combine the exercise
  • Translate within 10 strokes of your SIM average. I'm an 88 now, so I'd like to at least be a 98 on course.
  • Break 90 legitimately -- this seems legit for this year, a good day, the right course, you could do this if things translate from the SIM.

Goals for 2025

Big Theme stuff (a few changes but mostly the same as last year)

  • Stay healthy and play at least 2x month from June thru November --- didn't really happen, I recorded 7 short rounds over the summer
  • Transform your swing so your not working so hard --- Halfway there, it's been a gradual improvement in the SIM
  • Work up to playing a full 18 - I would sway your there from a health perspective, hard to say though since you didn't do this outside but once in June.
  • Get your average below 100 = NO
  • Get some more accurate distances on Irons by EOY - NO , if anything they have gotten worse
  • Track your mulligans, no cheating your putting scores. SORTA - you got better about this, but still wasn't quite there.

Scoring Goals:

  • Break 100 on a Par 72 18 Hole course with no Mulligans - NO
  • Stretch goal Break 90 on Par 72 18 Hole course with no Mulligans - NO
  • Break 46 on 9, without any mulligans at Northwest 9 - NO - best score was a 49

Distance goals

  • Every driver hit in a round goes over 200 yards - NO
  • Hit a legit 250 yard+ drive again (think your close on this) - NO , best case was River Marsh and the shot scope went belly up
  • Hit a legit 275 yard+ drive again - NO --- couldn't track

Birdie Goals -

  • Set a goal for at least 3 legit birdies this year. Once you get the first, your likely to want to play more - YES -- got one at sligo, felt good

Stat Goals

  • 2 putt or better 75%+ of holes in either 9 or 18 hole round - NO
  • Improve worst of your strokes gained stat by at least 3: Approach (current at -5.85). So move that to better than -2.86 or better. - NO

Goals for 2024

Copying some goals from before shutdown. Key right now is getting ankle healthy so you can ramp up some volume

Big Theme Stuff:

  • Stay healthy and play at least 2x month from September thru December - This worked until about October
  • Fix your slice off the tee - You've been better with the slice, but it was still a problem at times
  • Work up to playing a full 18 - You only did this once, and we're wrecked so no
  • Get your average below 100 - Not even close
  • Get some more accurate distances on Irons by EOY - Continued to be all over the place with all your clubs, swing has been in constant evolution

Scoring Goals

  • Break 100 on a Par 72 18 Hole course with no Mulligans. - Nope you had some theortical scores of under 100, but they weren't counting the mulligans, so NO
  • Stretch goal Break 90 on Par 72 18 Hole course with no Mulligans
  • Break 46 on 9, without any mulligans at Northwest 9 - C I only got all 9 holes in once, and it was a 46 (with 3 mulligans) Not a bad score, but not great either

Distance goals

  • Driver average for 9 holes or more over 200 yards (this would be a slice fix) - Driver was 211 over last 36 Driver was over 211 for last 36 shots, Miss right was 33%, which was down from 53% the prior year, so slice semi-fixed. Did you ever really get the 9 holes at the average above, probably not.
  • Hit a legit 250 yard+ drive again -C 240, not great. It was on the downhill. The way I've hit driver this year at the range, I expect to break this in 2025.

Birdie Goals No legit birdies on the score card - one fake one in needwood? did I take a mulligan or not, have to look at post

  • Par 3
  • Par 4
  • Par 5

Stat Goals

  • 2 putt or better 75%+ of holes in either 9 or 18 hole round - Looks like last time at needwood, you hit 6 out of 9 with a 2 putt or better! Also at laytonsville and poolselville you went 5 for 7. Lets track
  • Improve worst of your strokes gained stat by at least 3: Approach (current at -5.85). So move that to better than -2.86 or better. You ended with a -4.63 against 20HDCP ,

The one big goal, score under 100 by the end of 2023! You got a 99 with a few mulligans so,.

Goals for 2023

Scoring goals

  • Break 100 on a Par 72 18 Hole course - (2/11/2023) - 99 Laytonsville first time thru 18. I didn't count my mulligans though. Update 4/10 - you actually still need to get this one, that course was a Par 71! Matters less than the next (without mulligans).
  • Break 100 on a Par 72 18 Hole course with no Mulligans.
  • Break 90 on Par 72 18 Hole course with no Mulligans
  • Break 46 on 9, without any mulligans (Northwest 9), or 48 on any Par 36 9
  • Break 40 on 9, without any mulligans (Northwest 9), or 42 on any Par 36 9
  • End season consistently shooting in the low 90s.
  • Stretch goal to an 18 handicap
  • Get through 9 holes without shooting worse than double bogey on any hole
  • Get through 18 holes without shooting worse than double bogey on any hole

Now for the fun ones for 2023, the stat goals:

  • Ego/Distance goals all ON COURSE with Shot Scope
    • 250+ yard drive - 244 was last years long, so far coming up way short
    • 275+ yard drive
    • Average 225+ drive on course for 9 holes
    • Hit a non-driver\tee shot > 200 yards
    • Hit my 6 iron or hybrids > 180 yards
  • Birdie a
    • Par 3 -
    • Par 4 - Hole 13 Laytonsville 2/11/2023
    • Par 5 -
  • 2 putt or better 7 out of 9
  • 2 putt or better 14 out of 18
  • 7 FIRs streak
  • 7 GIRs streak

Virtual Goals - these are new in April 2023

  • Get consistent distances in the sim with your irons, hybrid and wood
  • Score 100 or better in a Virtual 18 hole course
  • Score 95 or better in a Virtual 18 hole course
  • Score 90 or better in a Virtual 18 hole course
  • Score 85 or better in a Virtual 18 hole course
  • Fix your bay to support all swings

General

  • Play at least 3 new courses - As of February - Blue Mash, and Hampshire Greens are new, one more to mark this done.
  • Get kids out with me more - doing good here, 2 out of 6 rounds
  • Find some playing partners my age

Goals for 2022

  • (Done July 2022) Par your first hole - Multiple Pars now
  • (Done August 16 2022) Birdie your first hole. #6 at Needwood.
  • (Done August 2022) Find a coach - Jim
  • (Done Sept 9 2022) Play one other executive course (Northwest or Sterling)
  • (Done Dec 2022 - NW 9, 49 - great putting) Executive 9 (updated 10/9) - Score better than double bogey on one the executive courses. 46 or lower on Needwood, 49 or lower on Northwest.
    • Updating this to, 2 extra shots per hole over par. This is basically shooting under 108 on a normal course. I lost a lot of momentum on this goal, but hoping I might be able to turn it around and get a lucky round in there.
  • (Partial) Play your first 18 holes real course -- been able to play Northwest front 9, 3 times now. I haven't gotten through all the holes yet, but gotten close. Might be able to put it together in 2 sessions.
    • Stretch goal Score below 126 that first time out (triple bogey golf) . I doubt I will get an 18 in before the weather turns. - On track for this, as I'm scoring around 60 on this course.
    • Update: Last week of December, and not sure if I want to mark this complete or not. I do average well below 126, but I only got through 15 holes before a backup on course. Not sure if the weather turns I'll have the patience to wait out the other golfers, so we'll see.
  • (Done Nov 2022) 2 Putt 70% or greater of your holes for 9. Last round 11/18)

Skills goal:

  • (Done - December 2022) Get your hips properly involved in your swing --- better but not there yet in August/September 2022. Really improved in October, but still not sequenced quite right. My hips are constantly sore after golfing in December, coach likes what he sees.
  • Fix your loft issue of hitting the ball too high in the air - Also getting better, but not quite there. Removing this one, as it seems to be a non-issue now that I'm swinging with my hips.
  • More lag. This is improving but not fixed yet as of August 2022. As of December, I can't consider this done. I've got a wrist thing going on and it's not really lag enough at impact.
  • (Done August 2022) Get your grip right --- you finally figured this out with the help of a good coach. Not up and down!
  • (Done - December 2022) Learn to chip properly - Almost there, really decent short game most of the time, still make some mistakes. Consider this done, even though chipping isn't great, I know the proper technique
  • Cut out the mishits to less than 15% - New goal for September. Thought I was close here, but this week (9/10) hasn't been great. Update December 2022, not a chance. More than 15% of hits are hit poorly in a round. More like 40%

Goals for 2023 (set in July 2022):

  • Score 3 over par per hole (~125) by end of June
  • Score 2.5 over par per hole (~115) by end of August
  • Score 2 over par per4 hold (~105) or below by end of September
  • Score 100 or below (~1.5 over par) by end of November 2023
  • Score 1 over par or better on one of the short 9 hole courses.

item.title: 10+ Lessons learned from a beginner golfer
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Lessons learned in my journey. Hoping that other new golfers may find my top 10 useful, and few extras at the bottom. I wrote this after I first started, but I think most of these tips still hold true today.

1) You must become a student of the swing

Nobody comes to golf with a naturally perfect golf swing. It's an abnormal movement pattern and takes time, instruction, patience, and lots of self evaluation to get better. It's individual to the persons proportions and flexibility. The goal is to make the ball move in the direction you want a distance you can accurately gauge.

A real live instructor at the range helps. However, it really comes back to you the individual to take what you learn from them, put it in to practice and keep self evaluating and improving.

In the age of YouTube golf videos, you have lots of different instructors to supplement your learning. Your not going to understand everything they are talking about at first. But as you learn mechanics of the swing and golf terms, those videos will start making sense and you will be able to apply the right fixes to your swing.

2) Improve your Putting will have the greatest effect on lowering your scores

You'll find this all over golf sites, and it seems so obvious. Work on your short game and it will pay massive dividends on your scores. If you can turn your 3 or 4 putts, into 2 or 3 putts, you start gaining a stroke per hole. You use your putter more than any other club in the golf bag, so you should give it the most attention.

In my short time playing, after my first couple of putting lessons, my game completely changed. I don't 2 putt every hole, but I have a shot at it most times, and can hit some longer putts on occasion.

3) Go out and play

The driving range and putting areas are just practice. The real joy is being out on the course and playing. Even if you're hitting a ton of balls into a pond or slicing into thick grass, you need to get out there.

Now as a beginner this can be intimidating. Start with the 9 hole shorter par 3 course designed for beginners. If you don't have that available , look for 18 hole twilight hours where they have the tees setup closer. As a beginner you should play from the closer tees, no shame in that. It helps keep pace of play and makes a hard game just a bit easier. Everyone around you will be thankful for it.

Most sites post the scorecard and the distances to the hole by tee color. Look for distances in the lower range, around 2000 yards on 9 holes is a good place to start. If you can pick times where the course will be less busy, especially in your first few rounds, do it! The shorter those courses, the more beginners you'll see out there struggling along with you.

4) Score each hole, but okay to have an incomplete card

This one might be controversial, but I strongly believe there is value in scoring each hole as a beginner. Many caveats to this advice though. First and foremost, take pace of play in to account if your slowing things down too much. If you need to pickup and move the ball on to the fairway to keep up, then mark a penalty and keep going. If your really struggling, it's okay to not complete the hole and mark an X on your scorecard. Eventually those will disappear.

Caveat 2, It's important score yourself consistently as it's the way to see progress and where you might be failing. I like to count penalties, others may not. I like to give myself a mulligan off the tee. Make your scoring consistent so your cards can show improvement or deterioration in play.

There will be holes where you duff your first shot, slice your second, drop on the fairway somewhere, hit over the green in the tall grass, miss the ball when trying to pitch it on the green, and then 5 putts to hit it in. You also may have the miraculous great shot on a par 3 and putt it in. Nothing will feel better than marking that first par and birdie on your card.

5) Learn about golf Etiquette, Rules, pace of play, and 'Ready Golf'

So many resources out there on etiquette. It's important, and you should read. A great primer from the PGA

Ready golf is a way to keep up pace. Read about it here

Pace of play is super important for everyone, especially when the course is busy. Just because your a beginner doesn't mean you can't keep up. Your biggest problem at the start may be the mishits requiring you to search for balls. Keep the searching to a minimum and keep moving. I've played with some decent golfers, and it's easy to keep pace with them even at my early stage. Just hit from the closer tees, and be ready to hit when you get to your ball.

6) Skill progression will not move in a straight line

Be prepared for lots of bad days, followed by good days. Your swing gets decent, and falls apart. Golf does this more than any other sport I've encountered.

My swing got pretty consistent, and then fell apart, and now is working back to consistency. Same thing with my chipping. Lots of lots reps doing things the right way is required to gain consistency.

7) It's not your equipment, it's you

Great golfers can play with crap equipment and do really well. I watched my pro easily hit my 7 iron 160-170 yards. Those clubs aren't fitted for him. I'm about 7 inches taller and 10 years younger than he is. Yet he chokes down and hits with my stock clubs a long ways. Same thing with putting and chipping.

All that technology that is out there could probably help, but get the basics down and then you might think about new clubs. This post suggests around a 15 handicap. I might go a little earlier, but double bogey golf seems about right over a few rounds.

https://thegolfingpros.com/confused-about-when-to-upgrade-from-beginner-clubs-my-story/

Along those lines, I believe that you don't need to be fitted when starting. This is especially true for beginners, who have nowhere near a consistent swing. I do suggest if your not of normal height you might go half to full inch up or down in length. You also want to purchase clubs that are going to be extra forgiving at the start. When your consistently hitting your clubs where you want them to go you can opt for a fitting, but I'm of the opinion that if you know your sizes you'll probably be better off.

Caveat to this after playing a few months. It seems like 6 months of playing consistently seems to be a good spot for the first fitting. When the swing starts to get consistent, you have a good bang for your buck in upgrading from a boxed set.

8) You have to learn all the different shots, it's not just a swing

When you are starting out you think, I just need to get the ball moving forward with one consistent swing. I wish it were that easy, but every shot is different.

Your hybrids hit different than the irons. Your short irons hit different some from your long. The Woods/Drivers are even more different. The swing mechanics are similar, but the setup and swing are different on each.

You need to learn to pitch and chip. You need to learn to pitch out of a sand bunker, which is very different than pitching from other areas. You need to hit irons from different lies.

And like I said before, you'll hit more shots with the putter than anything. You'll have both long and short putts on greens with different speeds, elevations and conditions. Get good with your putter and start learning to read greens.

9) Keep a positive mindset

Golf is a mind game. You are going to hit bad shots. Watch pros, they hit bad shots. Watch guys that have been playing 20-30 years, they will hit plenty of bad shots.

There is fun in managing those bad shots. Keep it positive. It's okay to be a little angry at yourself but throw it away and get positive for the next shot. Use all those mistakes as learning opportunities, not only looking at why you missed, but challenging yourself to get out of whatever poor situation you got yourself in. This is part of the fun!!!

10) The finer points of setup, ball position, grip, posture, aim, back swing plane, shaft lean, finish, etc. are all important

It's so hard when you're starting when getting input on your grip, ball position and aim. All contribute to hitting good shots. Build that stance from the grip, to every other part. I still struggle with distance from the ball both vertically and horizontally when setting up. It's tough but makes a ton of difference.

My bonus tips, that fell out of the top 10:

11) Driving range balls and declines vary. Don't let that mess you up

This one messed me up. Each driving range seems to have a different profile on balls and decline/incline. Don't try to match your distances if you are visiting multiple but focus on aim and swing mechanics more. Your distances will be different when you're out on the course. Ball

12) The golf swing is driven from the hips, not the arms

So my biggest issue with my swing when I started. It's about the hips, not the arms!

Well, now that I turned to more a stack and tilt swing , the hips are important, but so are the shoulders... it's all important. So strike through 10/2024.

13) After putting, inside about 60-70 yards is the 2nd most important part of scoring better. Then it's your driving, the approach. You need it all but need to adjust

14) Learning to aim is harder than it sounds, it's all about the setup.

item.title: Planning the course
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
It all really depends on how your hitting. That first hole has typically sailed straight over. No teeing up this time unless you get a wild hair and decide to hit driver.

I'd say the goal for the short round is keep the kids happy, try to get under 50 and not lose any balls! Keep the swings consistent and don't try to over do it.

  1. First hole has been trouble for me. I've over hit the 8 or 9 iron a few times at 135, which is always shock. Setting up at 170 should be a 6 iron, and land short for a chip. I've lost at least 3 or 4 balls in the tall grass behind this hole.
  2. 9 Iron or pitching wedge. 2nd easiest hole on the course, whatever you hit prior guides this shot.
  3. Tricky, because you've lost quite a few in the water here. 6 iron for 150 to 180 with some roll. Another 100 with the 9, but depends on where you land, often need 2 shots to get close to the tree with a direct line to the hole.
  4. 8 Iron hit right should get you over the water in a good safe position.
  5. PW or 9, it's super short. Hitting the 9 over isn't terrible here. Easiest hole on the course
  6. 9 Iron from 94, 6 or 7 from 140. Likelihood of birdie again here is very low
  7. 6 Iron (Cause your hybrid and woods stink). You've got stuck in the trees a couple times here, and had some luck getting out.
  8. 6 Iron, 6 Iron, gets you to hopefully 50 yards away. You could try the driver and see if you can get 200+, but probably not worth it. Pitching wedge to the green, putt.
  9. 7 Iron, don't screw up your putts.

item.title: About
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Hi, I'm Jack. About time I updated this. I started playing golf later in life at the age 45. My goal was to score under 100 before I turned 47. I hit that goal (although pretty rough with a couple 99s on Par 71 courses). I then proceeded to get injured and take over a year off from golfing (about 15 months), and then sparingly for the next couple years. I am 4 years in to my golf experience, and I've recommitted myself here in 2025 through playing sim golf in the hopes that I can improve to mid 80s handicap or lower.

How it started

In a bid to get my son exposure to different sports, and some bonding time we took a trip to Top Golf for a lesson. We both actually hit the ball and watched it fly. We were both hooked with the euphoric feeling of hitting a golf ball when you make solid contact.

At this point though, my goals weren't much at all. Learn to hit the ball, and see where it goes. Fast forward a month, school's out and I sign my eldest up for golf camp. My younger one decides he wants to go too. 2nd day back the kids come in to my office and say, "you must take us to play on a golf course! "Dad, it's amazing, you have to take us.... today". That was after they had played for 4 or 5 hours.

We didn't go that day, but a few days later I took them to the Par 3, Needwood Executive 9. I think we only got through 5 or 6 holes, but now I am officially hooked. I am obsessed beyond belief, and watch YouTube videos all day on swings. I repeatedly hit the driving range , and play a few more times at the executive 9. I somehow manage to par and birdie a hole. I still don't really know what I'm doing

HIRE A COACH - CHANGE THE SWING

So the original coach at top golf got me making solid contact, but I was doing lots of things wrong with the swing. I realized I got decent distance, because of my strong upper body, but I knew my mechanics were all wrong.

So I go to a legit PGA professional, a guy who played on the tour who didn't sugar coat anything. That first lessons was the realization that my swing was entirely upper body and no lower body. Lots of work to do, so many things wrong.

Since then the experience has been really up and down. I've put in the practice time, but the swing is still evolving (even as I update this in early 2026, my swing is evolving again) . It's been good weeks and bad weeks. I've had moments where I hit the ball so damn consistently at the range, followed by a week where I top or hit fat every ball.

I've gotten really good at putting, and have some semblance of a short game close to the greens (September 2022)

WHERE I AM HEADED

I am a highly goal oriented person. It's served me well in other areas of life. Set a goal and doggedly work towards it. I am working with a coach, and plan to keep at this till I make that progress I want:

  • A consistent proper swing with my irons and driver
  • A decent short game with the wedges and putters.

If you look through my blog posts that are areas of success and frustration. The goal is to stay positive, do the work, and figure out this game so you reach an enjoyable place.

Where I am January 2nd 2026.

So most of the above was written 3 years or more years ago. Today is 1/2/2026. As I mentioned earlier, I built a sim late last year, and have been playing on it for a little over 2 months now. I currently have a sim handicap in the high teens with a pretty awful indoor swing. I'm playing adequately with bad swing mechanics at the moment, and probably a high to mid 90s real course player right now. I know where my faults are generally and understand the game much better from swing, to what it takes to score.

Right now I'm just looking at grinding in the SIM through mid-March and the weather starts warming. I have found some ugly swing mechanics that I want to correct, and just continue to improve the game. I just have so much fun playing for someone who isn't really good at things.

My medium term goals is start scoring where I am scoring now on the SIM --- mid 80s --- on real courses this coming years. That means my SIM score probably needs to drop to the low 80s, to high 70s, but that feels very doable at the moment.

item.title: Sick of writing, want to play
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So all I can do at this point is write. Ankle is getting better slowly, morning are pretty good. I'm planning at the very least a range session late this week or weekend.

I really liked my last post, and feel like I am good space to start working on my swing again. I have a plan to follow and know what to do, just need to get healthy.

I'm super excited, because I think I can get some lower 90s scores by the end of the year. Not because I've fixed something yet, but I know how what it will take to fix it and execute it. I kind of got there before when I was learning, and now it's just another step forward from 2 steps back.

item.title: Need new wedges?
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I'm already over my misery of yesterday and ready to get back out there. Realizing I need to address my wedges before I play again.

  • Currently playing with old SW - need to get a tag on it at least. This is the most lofted club, and actually played fine, I could supplement, but probably should lineup the larger
  • Broken PW - it's 42 degrees, and having trouble finding something close to that config that doesn't break the bank.
  • 8i, 9i current gapping is right. PW to 9i wasn't quite as good, but it did tend to play about 100 yards which is right
  • PW, GW were 99 to 85 yards... this is probably right too. Playing a Gap this size though

I am in a weird spot. I don't love my irons, but I did like 9-SW and now missing two of those. I am considering graphite, and getting a new iron set... yea, I know, just to mess you up some. I do love my two hybrids and how they feel in the swing.

item.title: I've gone down a dark hole... of iron research
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So to recap, I'm down two clubs. PW broke (42), and SW lost(54). I've got a temp solution for the SW, and I'm considering just repairing the PW

I've been browsing Maltby's site, and I kind like what I've been seeing. I've been considering trying a PW from them, and filling things out with a SW.

Pros on this

  • I can try a new iron. It may be more 'playable'. If you look at it using the MPF (Maltby Playability Factor) my Irons are rated 564. That falls in Game Improvement territory. The other clubs I'm looking in the Super to Ultra game improvement area. The only area that really deviates is the MOI is higher on the PXG then most of the Maltby I'm looking at, so it's hard to say. There's a lot to digest here
  • I get to pick my grips, and I love the GolfPride MCC grips on my hybrid
  • If I like it, it's only a few hundred more to fill out the bag with same config.
  • I get to pick my shaft but, ...

Cons

  • I get to pick my shaft, but I don't know that I love my shafts. I sometimes really love the shafts on the hybrids which are graphite. I could go with the same steel shafts I have, and at least if you could delay any decision for some time.
  • It's not fitted, no lie adjustment. Fine if you end up liking it and not needing the lie adjustment anymore. You may not, now that your doing a better job of coming from the inside
  • There is a ton of research to do on this, and your running an experiment to get it right.
  • You still don't know about your wedges.

item.title: My clubs shipped -- so hopefully next week? Courses played
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So hallelujah... took almost 30 days but my clubs are in a box waiting to be picked up. I expect to receive on Sunday! Gives me a week to make a decision on the clubs.

I wanted to see what courses I was playing the most, so had copilot do up the list. To my surprise, I've played only 19 unique 18 hole courses. At first I liked to replay the same courses, but now variety helps keep things new. It's nice to replay to see improvement, but the fun level of an unexpected new course is better.

The not so surprising -- Wynn 5 times. It has been a fun under 5000 course. I haven't played it this month, as I've outgrown the course a bit and enjoying playing new courses. Arizona National is probably the least memorable despite the 4 times played. . There is one long hole there that sticks, but that's about it. River Creek I've played a bunch, because it plays so true to the course and is a bit fun --- however I got bored with it. Wolf Creek has been fun, but gotten 'stuck' in a bunch of dessert traps which makes the course a bit annoying. The novelty of having played in WGT has worn off some... but I will come back to it.

The local courses Falls in particular, is pretty boring from the last play through. It's the closest 18 hole course I could actually play, so I imagine I will play it in the near future. Woodmont I remember being a mix of fun and boring... There are 2 18 hole courses here, will have to try the other sometime. It's close, but I'll likely never get an opportunity to play it.

I struggled on Whiskey Creek which is the next closest likely to play course. That was back in November so probably deserves a replay. I really loved Rocky Gap the first time, but the 2nd time I struggled.

Recently, I had first shots at Torrey and Pebble. Scored okay on both, and probably deserves a revisit. Valhalla came up twice ... fun name, course has some really challenging areas. Pinehurst I didn't like

There seems to be a correlation between how well I scored, and how much I liked the course.

item.title: I laid an egg
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I played the front 9 like I've been playing lately. 41. A 51 on the back killed me, and I ended up with a 92.

What went wrong --- I couldn't hit fairways. Driver all over the place. I was really punished on these shots, I'm not sure if it's a course designed decision, or something else, but I had shots that carried 190, that only traveled 110 in game. I also hit trees twice, and lost 2 strokes with that. One drop. Just playing out of lots of bad places.

Last time I played this course (Cypress), I scored 10 better. April 1st. Granted, it had the 3% boost, but I hit 43% of fairways, and it also looked like I putted better. Exact same front 9 score 41. Back 9, matched it with 41, so 10 strokes better on the back 9.

The 10 stroke swing move the handicap in the game up a stroke to 14.1 from it's low. The rolling SAS didn't reasonably change, maybe .3 strokes higher. The average on the normalized boosted, also only went up by .3. 85 is your current boosted normalized score over the last 10.

I think what this tell us. I should be scoring in the upper 80s on most courses is where I'm trending. GPT says the gravity is 87-8, celining at 79 on a good day, and floor of today of 92. A little better than the 14.1 handicap.

item.title: Year to Year Progress
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Generated from gpt 5.4. Pretty good synopsis, e

I started golf in 2022 and, despite a long layoff, have logged about two and a half years of real playing time while chasing the same goal from day one: turning a late start into consistent scores in the 80s and 90s.

2022
This was the start of everything. You picked up golf later in life, got hooked almost immediately, and set the early goal of becoming a legitimate golfer who could regularly break 100. Most of the year was about surviving beginner golf: lots of penalties, inconsistency, trouble with driver and chipping, but also real excitement from early pars, your first birdie, and visible improvement. You took multiple lessons, built swing thoughts around grip, hips, wrist hinge, delofting, and compression, and started learning how much short game and course management mattered. By the end of the year, you had played more real golf, tracked your first 120 holes, started using stats tools like Shot Scope, bought and tested clubs, and reset your goals for 2023 around breaking 100, then 90, and becoming more consistent.

2023
This year reads like the first real push from “beginner” to “golfer.” You upgraded a lot of equipment, worked through driver numbers, wedges, hybrids, irons, and putters, and kept refining your swing through both coaching and self-analysis. A big milestone was your first full 18-hole round, where you posted a 99 with some caveats, but it still showed the ceiling was getting closer. The year mixes optimism and frustration: good shots kept proving the potential was there, but inconsistency, putting, and recurring swing issues still held scores back. As the year went on, the focus broadened from swing mechanics to score tracking, on-course decision-making, hip pain, and eventually simulator planning with Garmin R10. By late 2023, golf was no longer just range work and rounds, it had become a more data-driven project.

2024
This was largely a comeback-and-setback year. Early on, you were still trying to restart progress, test your swing, and get back into real scoring shape, but hip and ankle problems kept disrupting momentum. A lot of the middle of the year has the feel of someone stuck outside the game: monthly check-ins about not being able to play, rehab, trying to hit balls again, and missing golf badly. When you did get back out, the posts show rust immediately: slices returning, inconsistent striking, stamina issues, and the struggle of regaining timing after time away. At the same time, the blog shows a more experienced golfer’s perspective than in 2022. You were no longer just asking “how do I hit this?” but “what actually matters for scoring, gapping, consistency, and long-term improvement?” Late in the year, gear questions came back too, especially around wedges and irons.

2025
This looks like one of the biggest transition years in the file. You were back to playing, tracking scores seriously, and trying to move from low-100s golf toward the low 90s. Garmin replaced Shot Scope, and the blog became more analytical again, with score tracking, course reviews, consistency analysis, and a lot of thought around how to turn flashes of good golf into repeatable scoring. You also went deep into building a garage simulator, which became a major part of the year. The sim posts show a shift from simply playing golf to engineering a practice environment: launch monitor questions, netting, screen builds, calibration problems, GSPro setup, and figuring out whether simulator numbers matched real-world distances. By the end of 2025, your goals had sharpened into consistency targets, especially using sim golf to bring 9-hole scores down and build a repeatable practice system.

2026
So far, 2026 reads like a golfer who has advanced a long way from the 2022 beginner version of himself, but is still fighting inconsistency. You’re analyzing rounds in terms of trends, handicap, gravity score, fairways hit, and what separates an upper-80s day from a low-90s blow-up. The posts suggest your scoring has risen to a point where a 92 feels disappointing rather than miraculous, which is a major shift from the original goal. There’s also more reflection on where you play, which courses you like, and how your broader golf life now includes simulator golf, course variety, and strategy rather than just lessons and survival. Even the rough rounds sound like the thoughts of someone who expects better golf and knows roughly what is missing.

item.title: Starting Golf - Damn this is hard
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So this blog is all about my quest to becoming a semi-competent golfer. My goal is regularly score under 100 after starting the game later in life. A 28 handicap on a typical course. Today is August 3, 2022, and I will set this goal a little off for September 2024. A 28 handicap seems achievable with the work put in.

So the background. I came to golf a little later in life at 45. In my quest to find sports for my son, he and I took a golf lesson at Top Golf and had a blast. That turned in to more lessons for us, and then camp for both my sons. After the second day of camp, both kids came to me with the biggest smiles on there face and said 'you need to take us out on the course, it is the most amazing thing in the world.'

I was hitting the ball decently well at the range at this point, so I took them to an executive nine, and I was totally hooked. This was June 27, 2022. I've done this course 3 more times since. Twice with the kids and once on my own. Typical beginner golf. A lot of really bad shots, and a few lucky ones. I don't have the score from the first outing, but I have my cards from all 3 since and put in the Grint web site so that I can track my progress.

My scores in order were 60, 52, 60. I count all the penalties best I can. I want my scores to be legitimate, and so hit the ball in the water, then you take a 2 shot penalty and either drop in front of the hazards, or shoot from prior location. Lots of golf balls have been lost!

So the good first. The first 60 actually went pretty well, as I saw gradual improvement as I moved through the course. I scored a 5 (double boogie) on hole 5, and then scored a 4 for my first ever single boogie. Felt awesome with that little win. I played with a couple that were also beginners and took all the pressure off. They were super nice and fun to play with.

The next time around I did much better. Surprising since I was with the kids, and I had to do a bit of emotional management with them. I parred two holes! Granted they were short, but I felt pretty good about this. I parred hole number 2 and hole number 5! I felt on top of the world, and thought I might actually be able to get the hang of this.

Now the bad. All of the problems. If I were to list them it would go on forever. I'll rank the top ones though:

  1. Keeping the ball in play. Too many balls went into the penalty areas (water or tall grass). Cut those out and you have a chance. Slices, mishits, topping the ball... I do it all still. No consistency
  2. I have no idea how to chip. The first time out I chipped over and under the green plenty. This has gotten better each time out, but I need to dedicate practice time to this part
  3. I can't hit the driver, fairway wood or hybrid well at all. There are a couple of par 4s on the course that call for a driver off the tee. I have no consistency there. I have a bit of consistency with the irons when I'm hitting well, but it's a coin flip when I pull the driver whether I can keep it in play or not.
  4. Putting. Probably the strongest part of my game so far. I've hit some nice 8 footish putts, but the problem lies when I miss too far and then get in that rut of going up and down the green trying to get it in the hole.

So I'm a beginner, and I give myself a lot of slack, as this is to be expected. I'll dedicate my second post to some simple goals to get me to where I would like to be.

item.title: The short and long term goals
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I am very goal oriented, and have always been great at setting near, intermediate, and long term goals. So here goes the goals to set me up for that eventual under 100.

Short term goals for the rest of this golf season (through sometime November)

  • On the executive 9 close to home
    • Score 40 or below. With a best of 52, this seems hard, but I think a bit more work and practice I will get there. I'd like to see a week of playing every evening. These holes are short enough that one over on each seems in the realm of possibility.
    • Birdie at least one hole
  • Play at least one other executive 9 or 18 course (Northwest or Sterling)
  • Play your first real 18 holes - thinking late October, early November.
  • Swing & Skill Goals
    • Get more consistent and clean with the irons
    • Find a coach to work with
    • Cleanup the arm bend , casting, general ugliness of my swing
    • Learn to really hit the driver and fairway woods consistently enough so you could use them. This will likely extend in to the heated driving range in the winter.
    • Learn to chip properly
    • Get better at putting

So that set of goals should get me through the rest of this season. I really like the idea of on a non-busy week instead of my usual workouts, just golf 6 or 7 days in a row. Would like to have my swing pretty consistent before doing that.

So moving in to intermediate goals for the following year (starting in March)

  • Play 18 holes around twice a month, weather and time permitting
  • Keep playing the executive 9 to hone skills
  • Score 125 or below on 18 holes by June next year
  • Score 115 or below by end of November next year
  • More coaching

Trying to leave myself plenty of room here. Lots of things could get in the way of this new hobby. Hopefully the kids find as much joy in it as I do and we can spend some quality time playing together.

Now for the following year, time to dig in and move that score that is likely in the 110s down below 100. Too hard to put in specific goals at this point. I will need to find the problems, address those and move forward.

I've contacted a Pro for some more group lessons. My hope is to start Saturday and go from there.

item.title: More lessons start Saturday
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Knocked off goal number 1! I have found a coach and scheduled time!

So after a hiatus from lessons, and seeing my swing deteriorate some, I'm getting back at it with someone who has an eye for this. I found a guy that has good reviews everywhere and generally very well liked. I am going to give it a go with group lessons for a month to keep the skills moving forward. I like this idea, and his sales pitch is pretty good.

The instructor has a great pitch about getting guys from 120 down to 80 in a matter of months. That's not me either athletically or time wise. Going from playing executive courses terribly to something that looks respectable on a normal 6700 yard 18 is the goal. I am happy to do this for 3 months and see how far I get!

I like the idea of the lessons being on the longer side (90 minutes), including both long and short game.

I am super competitive, but don't want to put the pressure on myself to say you should score under 100 in 3 months. The little voice in the back of my head says it's possible with work.

item.title: Golf Lesson #1
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
It's like I'm starting over. My swing and grip were so messed up , and my address isn't great either. I wish I had started with the new coach much earlier. So lets go through some problems in order of how I will address them this week

This is just with swing:

  1. My hips don't move at all in my swing. I entirely use my upper body power (which is pretty powerful), to move the ball. I lack internal rotation in the hips which probably limits the amount of power I can produce there, but I do have some mobility and so I should be able to do better. The coach gave me some hip drills and stretches to get my hips moving better in the swing. I think I get away with a lot because of my fairly powerful shoulders. I can hit the ball 'far enough' by just using my shoulders. It does explain why guys half my size hit the ball twice as far.
  2. My grip stinks. Whatever I was taught just wasn't right. I need to watch a lot of videos on grips this week and practice that.
  3. My address should be a bit different, more upright. Will likely have to wait till next week to fix some of this.
  4. My elbow bends. Probably not as big as problem as I thought, but still the coach immediately pointed it out. S
  5. I'm not hinging my wrists at the top properly. Sequencing is all off, and I over swing it.

With chipping, I learned something new. Cock the wrist and hold it through the swing

Putting was okay. A couple of small things and I need to figure out the right amount of force, but I'm not really giving myself much here as it's the first time with the coach on putting.

item.title: Two views of the swing
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I've been using this golf fix app for a bit, and it does a decent job in looking at my swing and giving me pointers. As I learn a bit more, I can analyze my swing a bit better. So taking a look at two captures of my swing in the back yard (no ball)

Analyzing my own swing here, by frame (Right to Left 1st row then second). This one scored a 9.3, which is on the high end

  1. Shoulders are not square at address
  2. I'm okay here, but my hips haven't started moving yet, and not sure if they should
  3. Glad to see my arm straight, and a little bit of hip movement.
  4. My arm is straighter than usual, but probably a bit higher than I need. I am glad to see my wrist cocked here. Pushing out here to cock the wrist is a new sensation
  5. My hips are back square. The app always views me as 'casting', which has something to do with my wrists releasing/unhinging too early in the swing.
  6. Like tat my head is down, feel like my hips should be more like 7 at this point
  7. I guess this is okay
  8. I always feel like I am down here, and need to get up.

Now lets look from the back. This was an 6.0 Again not horrible, but looks like a of hip movement is obvious

You can see the line on my short should be move higher and back. It does a little by frame 4, and turns a tiny bit at impact on frame 6. I've got all sorts of issues with the golf plane. The app says I lift my upper body at address. Not sure what that means.

I like frame 4, as my arm looks fairly straight again. I'm going to take a few more shots this afternoon and see if we can improve.

item.title: Grips & Hips
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
This weeks focus is on the grip and hips.

Grip, I'm still unsure what is right. I find most the videos hard to follow on grip. Lots of variation. I did like this video, and I'm going with that until I get more time with the coach

With the hips,, besides what the coach had me working on mobility and some exercises, I found this video with a 'step back' , and a 'step up' . Lots of videos on hips, but suprisingy variation of content out there. Hard to know what will work for me or not.

So a couple captures today. Some good things happening. Still figuring out the wrist hinge thing, but like my hips moving at least in one plane.

item.title: Lesson #2
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
There was nothing to save from my old swing. I have started over. That stiff, non-body movement is on it's way out. The consequence is now that I am hitting the ball more correctly, it doesn't go as far, and I mishit more often. I am now doing something that is more of a half swing but really working on the wrist hinge portion of my swing, the arcing and body rotation of the swing , and trying to be in proper position when striking the ball.

I think I got the grip right yesterday. Lot of straight up and down and now rotating it. That's going to take some work to get use to. The have the 'V' crease pointing back the to the right shoulder is correct. On the right hand as well.

Frustrated that I was practicing wrong for weeks, and now just really undoing that stuff. Not much carry over at all from my old practice to new. Turn this around to correct is all I can do, and I am positive about that.

I would say the biggest change is actually getting my weight over the leg as I downswing. Not hinging the wrist. Doing the first thing helps the 2nd thing. It's overall just a very big swing change. I anticipate that my goal should just be to get this right before October (I think it will take that long to dial in).

The AI app has been all about telling me I am casting. I knew it was there and had no idea how to fix it. Now I have a clue how to fix it. The first big fix is to use the body correctly , and the wrist action becomes a little

Let me talk through a few key pointers for me:

  • Keep you head and body down as you rotate back
  • Grip needs to be stronger ... more 'over'
  • Wrist position at the back of your swing should be different (not exactly sure how to describe this one, but seems to help create more of an arcing motion)
  • Shift weight to left leg.
  • Don't break the wrist as you come through.

Some captures that highlight this all

Instructor right at impact

item.title: Wrist hinge
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I'm really getting focused on my wrist hinging now. I think I've got the grip better squared away, and doing better on the shifting weight. The coach and AI app are both pointing out wrist hinge being wrong. I have a problem in the follow through that isn't right yet. Trying to become a student of the swing and understand this. It's coming together in my head now.

A few problems as I see it now. I've got the latest swing vs older swing.

On the backswing.

Frame 2, is about right. Looking at earlier swings, I actually have a bit more hinge at this point than before. The club is straight out rather bent down towards the ground at about 15 degrees down in older swings. Looking at the pro example from the app, positioning is similar. On the latest swing. Keep in mind, I'm making an effort here to hinge.

Frame 3 is better here. In older swings the club was way outside, pointing about 45 degrees up, this is just over 90. The wrist is hinged, but I'm not entirely sure it's correct. It looks pretty good compared to the model, but I also think that I should have more weight on the left leg at this point.

Frame 4 is not good. The top, the arm is bent. I should probably not even be doing this at this point, and stick with the shorter swing as instructed.

Frame 5 things get worse. Probably need more weight shift to the right at this point, and my lag is not there. It's better, but not there. I should be at maybe a 30 degree angle pointed up, instead of what I think is a 20 degree down.

Frame 6. Not awful, looks like the model pretty good. I'm not square over the ball like before in the older swing sequence. This is a huge difference, but the question here 'is the club square'.

Frame 7 & 8. Not messing around much with here. The one thing I've seen is pushing the body more towards the target in the follow through. That's too much to remember.

Looking at this from the down the line will probably introduce a whole new set of issues. Will work on that once I can get through this. The instructor showed me how to get things in more an arc, but it hasn't gotten built in to my body motion yet.

Everything still feels forced and less flowy at the moment. Need to work on swinging and not just trying to kill the ball.

item.title: Lesson 3 - Putting, chipping, swing
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Putting and chipping are harder then they appear. I need to spend a lot more time practicing chipping and putting. At this point, I have a MUCH better idea on how to do these things, but they require reps and feel to get it right.

  1. Putting 71-75 bpm forward and back always. Longer the distance, further the backswing and consequently faster the club moves
  2. Chipping ... keep the wrist hinged through the movement , don't follow through as much and keep your shoulders level.
  3. Try to bounce on the green in front of you and get it to roll.

Again, the biggest spot of work is my swing. It's a rework. I'm back to where I am hitting about 20-30% playable balls. I need to get this back to 80-90% again, but hopefully with more distance and accuracy and well... a proper swing and not what I was doing before.

Big things are on sequence ...

  1. Back swing get in position with wrist hinge. Don't go too far, and ELIMINATE MY SWAY
  2. Start the movement by shifting everything to your left hip. I need to get my left hip more forward... see the gap in the image.
  3. Turn the wrist over (Turn the face of the club more towards the ground https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Mx6P2_NudGw around 4 -5 minutes ) ... not sure I'm saying this right, and don't unhinge. Turning the wrist over to square the club face
  4. When you get to impact and follow through, straighten up your left knee (this why everything bends down)

Swinging with the hips is key, not swaying in the back swing. I need to keep on that.

There is so much going on here, and I feel like it's just a start. Once I get the motion right, then I just need to repeat a few 1000 times.

item.title: Good range and putting session
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I went to the range with the kids yesterday. Took about 20 balls, but I started hitting pretty okay. Got a bit more distance, and I think that is due to the hips finally moving. I should have taken notes on distance. On good shots the irons were going in the 90-140 range. If I look at this chart, I would say I'm hitting between the short and mid-length amateurs at this point. I'd say a good shot with the 7 iron was about 130 yards.

I'm questioning now whether my wrist hinging was anywhere near correct, as I started to try to create space to get rid of that arm bend. The 'create space' cue in my head seemed to help with striking. 90% sure I am still casting pretty terribly at the moment. Watched a lot of videos today and now

Anyhow, it kind of came together and hit a drive around 200 yards or so. That hasn't happened in weeks. Granted that one case, and the others sliced away. I do think if I can stop breaking my wrists/casting so early, I can easily add another 20-30 yards to this and start getting closer to the 150+ with the 7 iron.

I'd say about 40-50% were going where I liked. I was able to work that number up to 80-90% before so hopefully I can do that again with a better swing. Until I throw something new at the swing and it drops again.

The putting went well too. More for my son than me though. 12 year old hit 2 putts that were about 25-30 feet. We were doing the game of , get a two putt and you get a point, and I had to amend it to, get a 1 putt and you get 2 points. He crushed it with those 2 putts from 25 feet.

Priorities this week...

  1. Fix the hip sway and get more forward on the left
  2. Fix the casting,
  3. Keep the hip rotation working.
  4. Keep working on the wrists.

Adding in a shot from my backyard practice. My face on shots are scoring pretty well now, but my down the lines are not.

The good on this one: Hips rotate and push. There is lag. Arm is straighter than usual. The bad. Could use more shoulder turn still. The hips might have shifted too much, and too early to the left.

item.title: My first Birdie!
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Hole #6 Needwood Executive, Par 3 140 yards. I had over shot this hole a couple of times before. I actually was not hitting the ball well at all. I had stopped teeing the ball with the irons, as I had been awful with that thus far. I believe I hit a 7 iron, and knocked it straight. Think it traveled 115, and then got a nice role to about 4 feet of the pin. I made sure to lineup my putt, and knocked it in with ease! Birdie! THIS IS WHAT WILL KEEP ME COMING BACK.

The first few holes were meh. A 6, a 5, on Par 3s. Terrible tee shots, no control. The 275 yard par 4 turned in a 7 with some luck. Kept the ball in play and played it safe.

I had a disaster on hole 4, I hit my first shot in to the water, took my second shot and hit it out of bounds. That's 4 strokes right there without advancing the ball.

The only other highlight, was the 359 yard par 4. I tried my driver with my first shot, hit my 7 iron a couple more times and got lucky enough to get the ball on the green in 4 and 2 putted it. A 6 on a par 4 is a win. The last hole was another save of a bad first shot.

The chipping and putting were pretty solid. Not a ton of misses. Get it close , tap it in. A few 3 putts, but lots of 2 putts. Total score 52 on a par 29, but some good take aways. Take out the one disastrous hole and you get a best around 46-47.

So a few take aways. My biggest problem is swinging consistently at this point. Not terribly surprising. Swing consistently on this course I should be on the green on all Par 3s, and be able to par or bogey those holes. I need a lot of range time ahead of the next outing to get my new swing back to consistency.

Putting is better, less mistakes. Chipping needs work in different dimensions. I often get the ball near the green but sometimes I'm 30-40 yards and have trouble playing that. I had a nice layup on to the green , but that was mostly luck. A few chips were a bit too much, but I think I'll get that in time.

The longer holes aren't near as bad, but can only imagine if I can could consistently hit driver and 250 yards, I might be on the green in 2 instead of 4 or 5.

item.title: Swing evolution
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So a few practice swings today. This is evolving to hopefully something much better. The AI tells me a few things bad, here is the analysis and my commentary:

  1. Lack of Shoulder Turn - I don't turn enough. I think it's partially mobility , and partially just not moving correctly at the top. More time just practicing that top position before hitting might help.
  2. Hip Slide at impact -I am less concerned about this. I am bumping my hips out really early to get my hips involved, although I'm seeing more turn after impact in these shots. I'm sure the coach will get in on me on this.
  3. Loss of Spine Angle at Top - Keep yourself steady from address to backswing. I come up each time. Although I just watched the video, and said I was only a 2% change.

So a bit of good and okay from my own analysis

  1. Hips are improving, there is movement, but might not be sequenced right. My hips probably move too far right early, but at least they are moving!
  2. I have some lag in these shots, not as much as the model, but there is lag.
  3. Arm is less bent here (but I didn't turn as much)

So onward until I get this right.

item.title: Vacation week & lesson 4
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
On vacation this week and not a whole lot of opportunities to practice. The driving range here is quite a distance, so haven't made it up there yet. I had a lesson on Saturday before we left and made some progress. Chipping is getting better, putting is improving. The swing is coming around, but still needs work. I think it's about to come together, but we'll see.

So during the lesson there was a lot to work on. I sometimes go hip silent and don't get things forward. The image above is an exception. When I think about making space in the backswing, apparently I swing much faster. This is good.

Contact has been a problem (again). This happened before when I was learning, but I think once I get this new swing down, that will come back and hopefully can find some consistency.

What I don't like in the above image is my left knee bend. That knee needs to be straight as I get to frames 6,7,8. More open towards the target here as well.

I still come over the top some. Lag and casting are issues. I'm not sure either will be fixed quickly.

I'm hoping to get a lot of range time when I get back, and lots of course time. I'd like to really put in some time over the next month to see if I can get this swing and game to a decent point. I'm hoping I can play a lot of holes over the next month. Instead of every 2 weeks, more like 1-2 times a week get the 9 holes in. Combine that with a range session and hopefully I can see some improvement.

item.title: What to work on
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Unfortunately not much a chance to practice golf, so instead I've been thinking and obsessing over my game until I can get back to the range. Practice at home although useful, leaves a lot to be desired. Video of swings, using the practice clubs and the putting mat all help, but are not enough.

I am trying to prioritize what to work on. Common sense would say work on putting the most (it's the most used club), however right now my putting seems to be way more consistent than my long game. I still suck at putting, but at least I can eventually get the ball in the hole.

#1 - Hitting fairways with irons. I'm not even worried about the driver yet. I started swinging better last week, and feel like I'm a step away from getting back to consistency again. If I can hit fairways with the irons and move the ball the right direction I may have a prayer.

#2 - Consistency with clubs and learning my distances. The more I play the more I realize how important it is to estimate distance, and know what clubs can get me in range. This is especially true on the executive as most of the holes are short. Hitting a full pitching wedge , vs a 6 iron. Once I get consistent, hopefully can start getting a measure.

#3 - Chipping. It seems less important, but the coach has me working on it. Most has been short chips, but I think I need to learn a bit more about the 20-30 yard from the green shots. The chipping of course needs to improve as well.

#4 - Putting. Once on the green , two putting. I get the practice with the coach every week, but should do this each time I go to the range. It's less fun.

#5 -Woods, Hybrids, and Drivers At some point I will need to hit the driver to get some distance off the tee to the hole. At some point I'll want to hit a wood if I'm on the fairway and I'm 200 yards to the hole. The way I look at it now though is , if I can get 140 to 150 consistent with a 6 iron and hit a fairway then I'm pretty good from the closer tees. For example, say a 350 yd par 4, two iron shots gets me within 50 yards hopefully, a chip and two to three putt for bogey to double. The driver and woods we can save for next year unless I have a breakthrough.

item.title: 2 rounds, still trending down.
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I think the floor has lowered. I played 2 rounds, scored two 84s. These felt like floors more than ceilings. Both were longer, 5900+ and 5872 on a Par 3. Given the extra yardage, these rounds felt like what they should have been. The new problem is confirmed, you just need a bit more distance to move up tees now, but even when it's long, you can still score, it's just tougher.

First round whiskey creek. Tough thin here were the greens, and a slower start driving again. I basically played bogey golf for most of it, but played the Par 3s and Par 5s a bit better and averaged just a bit over par.

On Wynn the next course, some fatigue was building . I didn't play as well, but what stood out, was greens 11.1%, vs a 58.3% FIR. I couldn't hit a green, and it was a lot of distance issues on 5872. I did putt well this time around, and actually had a couple of makes, which kept the score in check.

Whiskey creek I've played 3 times, each with successively further tees, and dropping boosts. First time was junior 4336 with a 116% boost. I scored a 104. SEcond was back in February, I played Red and scored a 91 with 104% boost (5200 yards) , and today a White, with full realism 5952, a 84. That's a pretty amazing improvement!

Wynn, I've played a lot more, one of the most played. I've stuck with yellow, the last 2 times, however when I removed the boost I scored a 90. Before that at 103%, I scored an 84, and 116% another 84 (and easy pins and keep in mind this was a shorter course at 4800 yards). Best was an 80 with the 116% boost, back in december, which was my low score back then (again 4800 yards). This would be a 'best', if you take into account 'non-boosted' and over 1000 yards longer version. Not as much fun at that distance, but that is because I lack distance.

I will go through an do a swing breakdown. Nothing is working on keeping from OTT, except for holding my back at target longer. And by longer I mean like through the swing, which is no good. I tried some drills to start, but I dont' think that made it much better

item.title: Step backwards
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I really thought i had some fixes coming, but the latest cues aren't working (yet) , and I'm a bit frustrated with my over the top , and lack of distance swings.

The course i played today was one where I thought mid to high 80s, scored a 92. I was lucky to score that well, actually made a few decent putts.

in general though nothing was working. My shots were mostly over the top. I was starting to get a more I to out profile but took two steps back this weekend. My driver stunk. I was lucky to get it 170 yards, and that was long for thr day on carry. Lots of shots blocked left. Occasional slices. The rest of the woods were similiar... shorter than they should and over thr top mostly. Occasional lucky flight paths

irons , usuall struggles. Not all bad, but struggled with distance for the most part. Wedges, same deal a mix of few good and bad shots. Putter despite having some makes was not great with a few 3 putts.

I am distraught as I thought the changes I was making were starting to smooth out and take shape. A couple mitigating factors (less warmup, and playing with kids) . But even after they were done back at the range I couldn't keep the path moving outside for the life of me. I think fixing that is still number 1, and I am failing terribly.

I almost just want to take a multi week break and get some lessons with

item.title: So another bad score, but improvement
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
The path is starting to move, and my speed is starting to stabalize on the long clubs again. I was really happy with how I hit Driver and 3W, and the hybrids today. Felt like my distance was back.

I was till OTT, but not as much, and even had some I-O. While I was playing just focusing on the practice swing coming out to right field seemed to help . Surprisingly, my club was actually squaring some. It wasn't great, but I was hitting some good shots. Average distance on the driver was 195 with some shots down hill 240 yards.

I'll grab a couple examples

  • 120.8 ball speed, 206 carry, 242 total, Aoa 1.1 down Path 1.2 I-O, spin only 2850.
  • 121.6 ball speed, 206 carry, 237 total, 3.0 O-I, 3708 sping .2 D Aoa,

And the 3W - not bad

  • 119 ball speed, 182 carry, 203 total, 6.9 O-I, 4.9 D AoA
  • 121 ball speed, 184.6 carry, 197 total, 7.7 O-, AoA 5.5 D

Interesting on those... both shots were less than a yard offline . Angle attack was probably too far down, and spin was highest on those shots. Also interesting from this is that the LLM thinks my delivery on the W3 is actually fine. It produces a good shot. Very interesting, and I could go down a rabbit hole on equipment on this. The delivery right now is achieving carry/distance that is good.

The LLM says it's the same swing, just expressed differently.... I'm not sure I entirely buy this argument, but it makes a pretty good argument. It's one sequence, with different setups.

Anyhow, I feel better about speed, I think I am actually hitting the ball slightly further again and freerer. It's not an easy swing, but it travels, and right now I am preferring that. PRactice slow to fast should hopefully start to move the swing to something easier again

item.title: SIM practice, and sort of play
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I played a round today. It was a practice round, too many mulligans to count, because I was working on some things. I decided to focus less on the club path and more on my tempo and feels while doing this today... and it I think it kind of worked out.

MY score was an 81 (but really that was more like a 95 with the number of mulligans I took, had I played them).

So lets talk driver first... I was all over the place as expected, BUT there were some moments of really good. I was able to smack the ball pretty good. While surprinsingly I had no carry distance over 200, I was regularly getting readings of carry over over 200 from the monitor. I had a cluster of drivers 209, 177, 224,208, 174, 189. A 196 average in the SIM isn't terrible. While I had some earlier shorter balls that brought down the overall average

I did get the ball speed up to 129 a couple times, which is on the faster end for me... more on this later... it really was about tempo. Then the woods... had some shots 18 range with 175 carry ... 120+ ball speed

The i7 with a 4 shot sample sizse went way left, but averaged 131. That is pretty good, with a long of 140

I hit an i8 119 , which I think led to my loan birdie.

I feel like the break, and the weight lifting work led to a bit of an easier swing and distance. It wasn't great, but was okay. Hard to tell in the sweltering heat and humidity of the garage, but these numbers felt faster

My i8 warmup was a steady injcrease in speed and distance, getting the ball speed up to aroudn 95
