item.title: Driving range - Too much loft
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So the good first --- I had a very good range session. I'd say I was hitting 70-80% playable shots. I paid a lot of attention to distance today, and came to a huge realization. I'll get to that in the bad, but overall very pleased. Much more awareness around what's happening and why. With 70-80% of the balls going in 'playable' areas, this is good to, means I can actually play.

I kept loosening my grip a little bit, which seems to loosen the body some. The coil on the back swing is pretty good usually.

Lets take a look at some distances:

I really think I should be a long hitter. I am fit mid-40s male with lots of length and strength (but not so much flexibility). I should be able to hit my 6 iron 160, or further. I should be driving 250. Will get there if I can fix the current issue which leads us to the bad.

I have too much loft when I hit the clubs. It goes pretty far, but damn if there were wind I'd be screwed. My 9 Iron was hitting about 10 yards in front of the 100 yard marker, but damn was that thing hanging in the air for a LONG time. My guess is it's going 20 yards too high in the air, instead of further down the fairway.

So with this realization YouTube to the rescue. Video below was the first one I watched.

So he goes through several problems. Not in any particular order, the ones I think could be an issue.

  1. Chicken wings - need to loosen up the arms, and take them out of equation. This might be better than I think, as I don't see it in recent videos, but those are mostly without at a ball. I've done it in the past to make solid impact compressing some when impacting with the arms. Need more videos at the range. The fix.. point lead elbow down or point trail wrist down
  2. Too much weight on the back foot at impact. I need to figure out if I am doing a reverse pivot. Think I may still not be moving enough weight forward. This is likely playing a role, but not sure if it's the primary cause of the loft.
  3. Face open at address. Do I have the club correctly aligned, or am I too open in my setup. An alignment stick will help, and the next video.

Of course with every video, there is another set of videos that tell a different story. This one below I think fits me even more, especially since this is what the instructor has been trying to get me to do. "Get the club excessively pointed towards the ground", at the midpoint.

And another one. This one resonates because my shoulders do point up now that I'm trying to keep my body more upright as I come through.

Other problems, also in no particular order

  1. Lag - I'm thinking of buying a lag shot or gforce. The marketing is so good. I know my wrists break early, but fear of using these tools will mess me up more than they help.
  2. Posture- working on it, but need to consciously do it on EVERY swing.
  3. Driver/Woods/Hybrids. This is atrocious. I hit each of those the same distance as the 6 iron. Again, I don't care about this right now, but it doesn't stop me from trying. Perhaps the

No work on putting or chipping today.

Planning on hitting the range every day this week to see if I can really make some improvement. I'd like to do a round towards the end of the week!

item.title: 2 Days in a row at the range
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Day number 2, and I went to a different driving range. This one has lots of flags, but no yardage markers (they took them down). I likely won't go back there in the near term as I need some marker to know how far I'm hitting it, even it's rough.

So again, good clean hits with too much loft. Trying to 'deloft' the ball with the turn down mid swing. I did this a bunch of times, but it mostly ended with me slamming the club in to the mat and the ball hooking left. However on occasion subsequent hits would do well and be a little delofted.

I would try to hit my 'normal' which is high, and then try something else. The one thing that seemed to have the most effect was in the setup getting the club a little more closed at address. Leaves me with less to think about during the swing. Hit some nice shots. A little less consistent than yesterday, but mostly because I was working on a couple things.

Liked this video as well and discussion on delofting. The swing plane discussion was interesting. Balancing out with lagging the wrist break. So many things to take in to account.

One more thing to try at the range next time. Take a look at below video, around 3:30 and his drill

item.title: Deloft and Compress Today!
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I found this great video yesterday. It's long, but the first part covers a delofting drill. Forward shaft lean and compress the balls to get the feel. I will try this today. 'Sensation of the heavy hit'.

He also talks about turning the hands down to hit the draw around the 5:00 minute mark. Exaggerate it. This is all working around the same principals Jim has been teaching.

The other thing to work on here is my hips. A constant source of problems for me. The below explanation here with some more focus on the lower body. Really good job of explaining where the impact position is, and how the hips and spine relate to this.

I've got an impact bag that should help drive this home. Shaft lean at impact.

The weather has been nice here, hopefully will try to get a 9 hole round in tomorrow.

item.title: A little success in delofting
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
It worked! I'm not fully there, but I definitely made some progress in delofting my irons today and hitting a bit longer. I'd say 5-10 yards longer, with a bit less loft. I'll describe what has worked and what hasn't so far for me.

  1. The drill where you put your feet together at an angle behind the ball (see previous post), helped get a bit of feel. Moving my feet from the start position to a middle position was very hard, so I skipped back to a normal stance. Lo and behold , the ball didn't fly as high after doing this, but I also did step 2...
  2. Working on impact position, where your hips are forward the club has a lean to it. This seemed to have the most effect. In the practice swing before hitting the ball, I make sure to focus on the wrist position at impact and where I would like to be. Am I finally getting it.
  3. Turning the club face down as you swing through is still leading to me pounding the mat, and I'm not having as much success with that. However... successive hits after doing this, seem to be better. Exaggerate and then back to normal.
  4. I'm still manipulating my club face at address to a bit more closed, and this seems to help.

Other things that went well today:

  1. Think swing not hit.
  2. Think coil and swing around. That coil feeling is starting to sink in. Wonder how bad my arm is bending though. Hard to get a good shot from the front at the driving range.

I just figured out how to video out of the app. Here is a decent example, but holy crap do these look I'm swinging way too fast. And my posture sucks.

Now lets look at some photos more of the bad:

So I keep working on this, but need to figure out how to get through my swing a little better. I know what to work on at the range. Posture, address, coil, start with hips, move through

I did a little putting and chipping practice. They aerated the putting area, and holy wow was it fast.

I really am feeling enthusiastic, and if the weather is good tomorrow might take some time off to do the northwest 9 by myself. I'm hitting 6 irons 150, so playing from the red seems reasonable

1/3/9 all in the 285-300 range. Two good shots to the green possible, one good, one bad, we'll see. I can do the range prior and hopefully dial it in.

item.title: It all came together today
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
After a whole week of working, I started to get better distance with less loft today. I was hitting a lot of 6 and 7 irons, and getting some good distance for me, in that 160 yd+ range.

When hitting the 6 iron I was getting carry close to the 160 marker on many hits, sometimes even a little past. It's hard to tell, but it felt damn good. Still had some high shots, but felt like I was compressing it, and my shots looked more like the pros then what I had been doing. Even the bad hits were going 100 yards. I knew almost every time where the ball would be going right after I hit it too. Still 30% or so bad hits. Those were usually caused by trying to fix something.

The key was to relax the hands and the body, and just don't try to do too much. The setup for me is pretty key. I've come to doing a half rehersal, where I make sure I know where the wrists should be at impact while moving the hips. Sometimes I would throw a lot of weight behind it, and other times I would relax, and it would go just as far. Giving me lots of confidence. Lots of straight shots. A fair share of pulls and pushes, but lots of playable shots when I relax. Even the hybrid 5 did well today, and a few wood shots off the matt had decent distance.

I really thought about playing the 9, but after a jumbo bucket and some putts I didn't have it in me. I think with what I was doing, I could keep the ball in play. I think it will be key to warmup at the range with just easy hitting when playing, not trying to put distance on the balls.

I've got my lesson tomorrow, and have this awful feeling this will all fall apart working off the grass instead of the matt. I'm hopefully though this is the breakthrough I was waiting for. This felt so good!

item.title: Lesson 5 - Bunkers, chipping and pitching
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Seems as though I need to take some notes on certain things. First off, I still have a lot of trouble with pitching. Here are my notes, on what to do for these type shots

  • Feet pretty close together 
  • Let the club fall
  • Keep shaft lean the SAME throughout the chip
  • Think trajectory and swing path - club comes up then down, trajectory
  • Sternum just a little in front of the ball at setup
  • You can choke down for a bit more control
  • Aim ahead to a spot, and roll 

Some notes on pitching (and from the sand):

  • Dig in the sand
  • You need to hit the ball pretty hard out of the bunker
  • SQUAT DOWN
  • Weight on heels

And for both, weight towards the target not sure if this is at the start, or a shift, but can't hang out with the weight in the back ... a golf killer

The putting improved again. I feel like I should try a mallet putter at this point, but I've had luck with the current crap putter I'm using. I did a 2 putt challenge, same hole, 3 shots , 6 feet further back each time. Get it close, then tap it in.

So as far as swing, pretty proud moment as the hips were forward in the box. I should have a video of this a little later. The balls were flying a little shorter, but were going right at the flag. Took some adjustment time to go from hitting off the mat to the grass. 7 Iron was 130 yards, not many over 140.

Sometimes I'm pretty dumb with instructions, but lining up a club in front to aim at the target really helped me, so I was hitting the right direction.

item.title: When to get new clubs?
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I found this story had the best advice on new clubs. A few key points

  • It's the golfer, not the clubs. Very evident by how far my instructor hits my clubs.
  • New tech is pretty good in the last 5-10 years, if your coming from older clubs
  • Typical ordering of replacement: Putter, Driver, Woods/Hybrids, Wedges, Irons. Argument for this is pretty sound.
  • Upgrade once your swing gets consistent - around 15.

I think the last statement could be interpreted in a few ways. I am hoping that once I work up to hitting to the green consistent, then it might be time.

I am debating on a putter upgrade. I'm starting to get decent with my blade putter, and may stick with that style. I need the pro or a fitter to weigh in.

The driver is somewhere down the road, when I learn to hit that driver a bit better. I think my irons could last quite awhile for me. I did watch a video of a guy much better than me who pointed out that he was hitting much shorter with my clubs.

If I had to do it over again, I think I would have spent a bit more money and upgraded to the Stix sets. They get great reviews. It's hard to say though, I do know iron's are pretty forgiving, and maybe the Stix are less so.

item.title: Screen caps from lessons
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Left arm is still bent (more on this later). I need to move my right knee more to the left. I'm getting the hips more involved, but it's way more pronounced on the practice swings than the actual swings. This is still way better than a month ago. The hips move first. The ball is really moving too.

There is very little lag on this shot. I'm getting the lag shot next week in hopes of getting the tempo a little better and develop a bit more compression with the lag. We shall see if the marketing hype lives up.

I'm still really annoyed with the back swing bent arm. Even when I think I'm not doing it, I'm doing it. I am also annoyed that it bends on the follow through. Chicken wing at the top, and in the follow through. Ugh. Going to work on that this week.

Its hard to make changes when your hitting it pretty good, because each successive change messes things up somewhere else. Golf doesn't work like ' make a change and the ball flies better'. It's more like make a change, and take 100 balls to figure out the change, and then maybe 3 days later you start hitting the ball better, but you messed something else up in the process.

So top issues:

  • Arm bent in backswing
  • Move right knee towards the left
  • Come through the swing without chicken-wings
  • Lag

Biggest corrected issues:

  • Start the downswing with the hips

item.title: F"ing range balls
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So feeling pretty stupid today. Went to the range, ball was flying very short again. I'm thinking, what the hell is going on, my swing feels really good. I keep swiping at it thinking I must be doing something different. I keep working different things to try to get the same distance I was getting before.

It then occurs to me, maybe these balls are way different. So I've been going to 4 different ranges lately. Northwest, Needwood, Blue Mash, and Olney Golf Park. Northwest flies really far. I mean regular 150+ on my 6 iron. Blue Mash is decent, but off the grass I mishit a lot. Needwood has a warning about hitting over the fence. The ball doesn't fly very far there, and assumed the balls are the lower flight ones. The Olney Golf Park (which is an awesome facility), balls are either really old, or also the kind that don't go as far.

They took the signs down with the distances, but I remember fairly well from prior visits... flag in the middle is around 130-140 yards depending on where you hit from.

So anyhow, feel stupid that I was trying to get more distance, when more distance wasn't really a thing. Just working on hitting the different targets should be the goal.

I will likely head to Northwest more in the future, or maybe even Blue Mash. Better balls, at Northwest, better practice facility at Blue Mash (free putting and chipping areas), and can work off the grass. Needwood is the closest, but it's facility is lacking. Could do Olney in a pinch when you want to work on targets.

What would be much better would be just to try to do 9 in the evening and play multiple balls if you can. Ie, try to do 2 or 3 balls. With 2 balls you should hit anywhere between 35-60 strokes per pall. 3 balls is like a big bucket. Better exercise too if you walk, but always the danger that you have to play with a stranger. I think I could do 2 balls at Needwood in about an hour on a good day.

item.title: 2 steps back 1 step forward
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Last week was great, a huge amount of progress. Yesterday and today's range session paint a different story. No consistency in the number of playable balls. Maybe I'm being a little hard on myself, but too many topped, fat, sliced, pushed.

Hell, I even sent an 8 iron shot over so high on a pull it went over the driving range net.

At the start of my session, I got in to a groove fairly quickly, but then things went off the rails and had trouble finding my way back. I felt like my balls were traveling well with 9-7 irons for a bit. 9 going past the 100 marker, 8 at the start was hitting in the 130-140 range, and then some 7 shots were hitting about 5 yards from the 150 marker. Lots of straight shots, with a mix of playable misses.

The less I think and try to change, the better I do... but can't improve that way.

The biggest issue seems to be hitting the ball fat. Could be a weight turn issue, got to watch lots of videos again.

item.title: Play 9- maybe 18 :)
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I'm going to play 9 holes at Northwest today! I found a good block at 130 to give this a try. I may take the kids later if they want to go to Needwood for some practice which would make a short 18!

I'm a bit nervous, as I'm not hitting the ball as well this week as last. But then again, by day 3 things came together for me last week. I'm going leave in about 20 minutes and get a little practice time at the range.

So Northwest. Plan to do the Red tees. Red is: 2312, White is 2637, and Blue is 2774. Hopefully nobody around, and I can play 2 ball.

Going through the holes, the under 300s I equate to the 3rd hole at Needwood. For the 300+ I equate to something a bit longer to hole 8 at Needwood.

So the holes for Red:

  • 285 (4) - Shorter 4, should be 2 shots to the green with good irons
  • 376 (4) - Longer 4, should be 3 shots to the green with good irons
  • 285 (4) -Shorter 4, should be 2 shots to the green with good irons
  • 295 (4) - Shorter 4, should be 2 shots to the green with good irons
  • 85 (3) - Almost too short from the red for a 9 iron, may have to try the wedge
  • 372 (5) - Longer 4, should be 3 shots to the green with good irons
  • 180 (4) - 6 Iron and some role to the hole might get you there, probably best birdie Opp of the day
  • 145 (3) - A good 7 or 8 iron (depending on how your hitting), should get you in range
  • 289 (4) -Shorter 4, should be 2 shots to the green with good irons

Goal would be to avg +2 each hole. I see no water hazards from the flyover, except for maybe a creek. Just need to keep it in bounds. With any luck I can do this alone and play slow. Lots of 2 putts, and some chip opportunities.

Par is 34. Anything 52 in and under would be a amazing.

item.title: Lost scorecard and a club. Great short game, no other game
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I fulfilled one of my goals to play a different 9 at Northwest! It wasn't a good 9, but whatever.

The highlights were, I lost my scorecard .. .doh! I one putted the 9th. Did some great pitching, chipping and putting for the most part. Very solid on the greens, lots of 2 putts, a few disappointing 3 putts, but I'm mostly 2 putting.

I'm going to try to capture what I think I did while it's still pretty fresh

  • 285 (4) - 8-
  • 376 (4) - 7
  • 285 (4) - 5 or 6. Great pitch on to the green and great putt
  • 295 (4) - 5 or 6. Was actually a pretty good hole, but think I missed a short putt
  • 85 (3) - 5 with a penalty... not horrible as I lost the first ball.
  • 372 (5) - 10 - turned in to bloody mess
  • 180 (4) - 6 , not bad
  • 145 (3) - 5 (3 if you don't count my mulligan, 2nd best hole of the day)
  • 289 (4) -8 - shotting across the fairway, put may a nice chip and single putt to finish.

So I'll put this in, and hope my scorecard shows up. I'll err on the side of higher here, but unfortunately won't count the putts. 61 on Par 34. 27+. 9 strokes off my goal, but a pretty terrible day striking the ball. This would be roughly a 126. This should be easy to improve from the next time out.

I hit some really shot shots when I wasn't messing up. The guys I played with noticed me coming up on my left, and leaning back. All that work, and still messed it up on the course. Fix that, and you actually can play a decent game.

item.title: Shake it off
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Yesterdays performance was a tough one. My play with the irons was terrible. After some good range time last week, I didn't perform where I thought I could What is the right mindset here.

  • Shake off the bad day - you didn't perform the way you wanted to, and had a frustrating time making good contact. When you did though, you did hit some really goods shots (see next bullet point)
  • Take the good
    • You pared the 8th, and had a great shot at birdie if you ignore your mulligan (you scored the mulligan as you should though for a double bogey 5).
    • Didn't lose a lot of balls
    • Short game was relatively good, especially inside about 75-100 yards.
    • More 2 putts than 3 putts.
    • You hit a great pitch shot after taking a penalty on 3 to get it up on the green from right in front of the creek. On 4 you did really well getting on the green, however you missed your putts.
    • You made an amazing putt on 9 after not getting enough energy from the rough
    • People can be great. The guys I played with had some great advice that was awesome to learn from.
    • It's okay as a beginner to play from the red tees.
    • You actually played well getting out of trouble a few times. You got out of a bunker on 2
  • Learn from the bad
    • Consistency in your clubs needs to be found. With my adequate short game, you are getting close if you can just get a decent enough consistency with your swing. You can play the long holes once this is found. If I could just hit the 6 iron consistently I'd be better than double bogey golf.
    • Slow things down and hit 3/4 shots when things aren't doing what you want.
    • Stop hitting consecutive bad shots at the range --- slow it down, this will transfer over to the course.
    • Get more weight on your front (left) foot through the swing. Your biggest problem is still with the weight shift.
    • Aim is super important, on the 8th hole I had one of the players yell to me to aim right. Thank freaking god, got me within 10 feet of the hole and a birdie opportunity.

So lets talk about how to gain consistency. I've had moments on the range where I can hit within a good circle range of the target. 100-110 yarders with the 9, 150-160 with the 6. Next step is to make that habit. Don't fuck around with shooting bad shot after bad shot. Get it right, keep it right. Hit a bad shot, take a break, analyze what you did wrong, take some practice swings and get back at it.

I feel like at this point learning to drive the ball with consistency would be good. For Needwood you barely need the driver (2 holes), however yesterdays course would have been 6 out of 9 holes called for a first shot driver.

Stay positive, you will get there. I am tenacious and goal oriented, I will figure it out.

item.title: Another lesson and more frustration
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I'll start with the good.

  • I 2 putt more than I 3 putt now
  • I still struggle with chipping form, but it's improving

The bad

  • I really struggled with the new shorter shot from the fairway. I'm decent on the course with trying to control a full swing, but he was teaching me something new and it totally threw me off.
  • My swing issues were still there yesterday. Lots of fats and thins, and a few nice ones. I hit it right and it goes
  • My sequencing is all off -
    • I fire my shoulders and hips at the same time. Jim wants me to fire my hips before I get to the top of my swing to exaggerate it.
    • The hip movement is still not right. My hips slide, but don't turn. I think Jim was just trying to get me to move them some before, and now that I can feel it, get the turn involved. The wrong movement leaves me left leg kind of bent at impact where it should be straight, and the hips turned... more work on this.

I am so damn determined to get this swing right. I feel like once I do I can start getting consistent on the course and watch the scores drop. I plan to take another week of hitting the driving range a lot. Lots of video analysis this week. Hopefully the lag shot will come this week, and it can provide some assistance on feeling some of these things.

Considering a golf net, since my striking and swing are just so bad right now. More reps on video in the back yard might help

item.title: The Problems Move
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
One of the typical frustrations of golf, is just when you think you have something down, something else goes wrong.

So I thought I had my swing moving in the right direction by seeing better consistency and distance. Then the last week happened and things started getting worse, and by Friday and Saturday my swing was a wreck.

What have I been doing differently.

  • Less practice videoing in the backyard.
  • A change in hip turn movement.
  • Trying to fix thin and fat shots.
  • Thinking too much when you over the ball, and changing your setup
  • Not getting enough weight on the front foot (again)... falling back on old habits

So, the goal is to do this right. I actually got to a point where if I kept my swing the same I could hit the ball decently off the matts. I am still losing distance, and possibly consistency, but not initiating the movement with my lower body. Lower body first should lead to more lag, more power, more distance. If you are able to get to that stage, then you can go beyond what you've been able to do. I can imagine, when hitting the ball right ever club would travel 20-30 yards further.

I think it's a matter of fixing the error, getting the feel, and then not thinking about it when over the ball. Make it automatic.

I am considering changing my practice sessions over to the grass for the most part this week. I struggle on the grass more so than the matts, and I believe the various aches I have came from overdoing the matts. It's a longer drive to blue mash, but maybe I can get the kids into it as well. They have the best practice area in the area.

item.title: Breaking down the swing - Resources
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Loved this breakdown of the swing with lots of focus on weight shift and organizing the swing with emphasis on using the lower body feel.

"That leads, this follows"

More on compression

item.title: Another range session mixed bag
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I hit my new favorite range again yesterday, Northwest. Many observations

  • I hit too many irons too quickly, and then at the end the swing fell apart a bit.
  • In the middle I was hitting a 7 iron with a good strike over the 150 yard flag
  • A lot of my backswings felt shorter than normal, but the ball went plenty far.
  • Lots of inconsistency again. I kept playing a game in my head, no moving on to the next club until you hit 5 in a row playable. That game didn't last long as I couldn't seem to get more than 3 in a row.
  • My driver (woods, and hybrids) absolutely stink. Need to learn to at least get comfortable with the driver of the tee again. It's probably as important as your irons at this point. You could play driver + irons + wedges + putter (and ignore the 3 wood/hybrid).
  • Hip movement is getting better. Worked on more turn vs slide in the front hip. Think relax arms, start hips.
  • Lots of fat and thin shots. The fat shots lose about half their distance, the thin shots go all over the place. There is still a timing, tempo, striking thing going on.
  • Not sure what I'm doing with the wrists , and could use a few videos on this. Especially true in the follow through
  • Wish I had spent some time putting/chipping, but was in a hurry.
  • The more I think , the worse I seem to hit it. I need to keep it to one cue per swing. Sometimes that cue is 'move hips first', sometimes it's 'push wrist on backswing', or 'use coil'. When I get more than one of those in a swing I usually fail pretty bad. Better to practice a few different things then step up to the ball.
  • Thinking relax the swing helps to an extent. Funny that the more tired I got, the more I started muscling it with the upper body.
  • You should be taking more videos to validate you swing

What to do next. Hoping to get another session today. Need to rewatch videos prior again. Good exercises in there, and just need to take your time with them. Hoping to get to the grass driving range more often now. So what to remember next time

  • Swing not hit
  • Relax, don't kill it ,
  • Relax arms, start hip
  • Initiate with the hips - try hips early, hips at top of backswing, etc.
  • Take videos to validate
  • Use wrists to maintain straight arm in backswing

item.dc:creator: jacksod

So I've got covid, so no golf practice. I liked what was happening before this forced break happened though.

My swing was feeling really natural, but who knows since there was no ball involved. I'm very eager to get back out there, but it's going to have to wait till Saturday likely.

item.title: Bought a new putter! Sigma Ping 2 Anser
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I had some 'Dick's points' that were about to expire, so I pulled the trigger and bought a new putter! Couldn't be happier with my Sigma Ping 2 Anser Putter, except they failed to include the putter adjustment tool. So far on the my practice putting area downstairs the feel is amazing.

I had gone up to Dicks a few weeks ago, and tried a whole host of putters. I originally decided on the Tommy Armour No. 2 wide. It was a golf spy best, and felt pretty good first time I was up there. All of the putters were pretty roughed up at the store, and I had some uncertainty so I decided to wait a few days and go back.

It went on sale down to 120, and I went back up, and didn't like it as much the 2nd time. So I went through all the putters on the rack. I tried pricey and cheap. I ended up not liking the heaver mallet putters. To me, they tended to have no feel, and I had actually developed quite a good feel with my stock Wlson putter that came with my new set.

My favorite face of all the putters was a ping sigma 2 fetch. I didn't particularly like the design. I tried a ping sigma putter, and that was my favorite feel of them all. So I took a bit of a risk without trying first, and decided to put those two things together and order the club as I couldn't find it local.

I liked that this putter was labeled 'slight arc', which I think matches up well with my stroke. I like that it has 'some MOI' for forgiveness. I'm sure it's not quite as much some of the larger mallet putters, but so far I can tell compared to my previous putter. The price was right (under 200 dollars). Anser style putters are the top ones played by the pros. I liked the feel and feedback I was getting from my current putter, so felt good about sticking with a blade putter. I really liked that I could adjust the putter height as well (although I don't have the tool yet).

I have to admit, I was giddy when I hit it on my perfect put putting mat. It was just such a perfect mix of feedback and soft feel. Will make putting a lot more enjoyable. Now I just need to figure out how to get the ball on the green.

item.title: Looking at too many things
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I have been swinging a ton in the backyard the last few days at I recover. Itching to get another group lesson.

Good.

  • Hips are moving a little better. You need to spend time going 'hips first' arms follow in your warmup.

Okay

  • Arm bend is better but not great. Wrist pushing out cue helps.
  • I need to jam my foot in the ground so that the left knee is not bent as I come through.
  • Lag is doing better if you start correctly. The lag shot actually helps.
  • Hip slide and turn aren't sequenced great. Maybe over doing the hip slide, and not enough hip turn.

Bad

  • Shoulder turn. Your using your wrist and hands instead of your body to get more backswing speed. Rotating your body more feels weird. My muscles start to get a bit bunched up.
  • Overswing
  • Takeaway path
  • Follow through is terrible
  • Still tendency to go over the top when your backswing is not right.

Practice routine

Without the ball:

  • Find the right backswing spot and camp out there (fix overswing, lack of shoulder turn, bent arms and swing path).
  • Hip slide/turn after you camped out with arms following without actually consciously moving it (helps lag, and hips)
  • After a few of those, think coil back then hips. (puts it together)
  • After a few of those, focus on jamming the left foot in to the ground coming through (fix bent knee at impact)
  • Practice a few more lag shots, by doing the set, keep release.
  • Practice post the follow through and reverse it back to impact

With the ball with the new focus on getting the driver right.

  • Same as above 1-3, keeping it 3/4 to half swing with a 7 iron. Focus is on letting the hips do the work
  • Then 4 and 5 with the balls - 5-10 shots
  • Switch Lag Shot/7 Iron shots 5 then 5
  • Keep working the irons mixing them up
  • Switch to Driver, and hit at least 40-50.

item.title: Liked this video on lag
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Lag exercise

I like how he reversed the concept a bit. Get the club face closing, so that you have a reason to lag. It's something Jim has been trying with me with not enough success. Because I don't lag, it was sending the ball left. The exercise seems really good. Need to give this a try today.

item.title: Back at it
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I made it to the range yesterday. I had a pretty inconsistent hitting day, but I did get to work on some things. I went through my plan for the most part. I played around a bit with trying to close the face as I come through. Various results, but I do have more of sense of where the clubface is.

The lag shot was actually pretty decent, and I did a few exercises from the videos and was feeling lag after I initially got use to the club. Was actually hitting the ball pretty far and high with it. It had some carry over back to the 7 iron. The hips were moving well yesterday, but they feel really tight today. I felt like I was more turning then bumping. If I could just do them at the same time. My two big cues are 'swing back coil', 'start hips'. Occasionally I'll add in 'lag your wrists', or 'swing through it', 'close your club face'. It's when I get too many of these things go wrong.

I spent some frustrating time with the driver. Still having a ton of issues with it. The irons are inconsistent, but the driver is REALLY inconsistent. I don't think I had a good hit the entire time I was there. I had the driver 'on' for brief second where I was hitting over 200 yds at northwest, but I lost it and still haven't found my way back. I took a look at some videos last night, and thinking I need to hit up in to it on the tee more, unlike the irons where I hit down on. I also think I need to start with more weight on my left foot.

Have a lesson today, hopefully will get some good practice with my putter, and chipping. Hoping that the swing comes together a bit more today and tomorrow as I get back at it.

item.title: Group Lesson
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I hit some good balls, but also plenty of bad like usual. The putting was decent, and started off the competition with some 2 putts. Feeling good about that. The chipping went okay, still working on how hard to swing on those, but it's coming along.

The coach was pleased with the hip movement of my swing. Keep doing it. Wants to shallow out the swing plane, but we are getting there. I notice my posture could be better too. It also seems like I could get a bit more hip turn before impact.

item.title: Continue rebuild of swing
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Another group lesson today.

Highlights . I chipped one in the hole, that was a first. Made some other improvements on my chipping/bump and run. Remember to keep the ball either centered or a little back. No wrists, use your shoulders. Keep your shaft leaned. Less 'strong' a grip and more centered.

On the putting's... more 2 putts than 3 putts from a distance.

On the swing a few things. Number one, I needed to fix grip a little. It's decent but need the hands a little more overlapped. On the back swing working on getting my elbows a little closer together. Still getting that shoulder position right, I run in to my muscles a bit in the backswing which gets things gummed up.

The big topic, is things are still out of sequence. Jim wants me doing a bit more bump and turn before I even reach the top to start. This leads to me getting the lag. This is hard one to get right, but when I do it right, things tend to go well. It needs to be the same each time. I rehearse right, but then over the ball I mess it up. Need to figure this one out. It's really exaggerating the hips while still feeling like your back swinging for me. I think I was getting too far left and not enough turn, and need to find a happy medium. Shots to come. Hopefully can practice a ton this week, and really hone in on the swing. I keep thinking I'm close to developing a bit of consistent swing. Once that happens....

item.title: Frustrating range session
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Went to the range and thought I would see some improvement. Been practicing my swing mechanics with the hips first, but everything was just off yesterday. Frustrating when the ball doesn't go where I think it should and your very inconsistent.

Really trying to initiate the swing from the bottom, but that is leading to more mishits at the moment. Maybe it's just reps, maybe it's something else. This frustrating golf journey continues.

item.title: Some indoor drills for body movement
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded: Love this... I can do this every day/night to ingrain that body motion.

item.title: Still pretty bad
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
A 55 at Needwood Executive today. Lots of mishits... lots of either too short or too long with the irons. 55, but probably not the most legit 55, as I may have mis-calced a couple penalties, and allowed myself a mulligan on hole 1.

So lets see from my memory.

Hole #1, hit a line drive with an 8 iron then chipped long on the green.

Hole #2, took the 9 iron and hit a beautiful shot over the hole in to the bunker long.

Hole #3, went off the rails. Hit good distance on my drive, but lost the ball and took a penalty, then dropped the ball, hit a wedge (?) over the pond in to the rough, another penalty, and then 3 putted out.

Hole #4, trying to remember, but think I hit a 7 iron, and went over the green on a perfectly hit shot. Straight over the pin.

Hole #5, 9 iron shanked it , terrible putting.

Hole #6, I think I went 7 iron and hit right in to the front bunker.

Hole #7, this has always been my nemesis. Went 6 Iron and mishit, then wedged it up. Took a bunch of putts as the hole placement was particularly tough.

Hole #8, Drive was playable, but then I penaltied the next shot in the rough... argh. Can't even recall what happened after that, but a 7 was lucky here.

Hole #9, First shot was a 6 or 7 iron, and I mishit over to the red tees. Then I wedged it on again, but 3 had a really long 3 putt.

Score again was shaky here...Really just trying to have some fun with my son, and take all the pressure off him. He did really great hitting the ball straight, but struggled a ton with putting. If you didn't count his putting, you'd say he did awesome from the kids tees.

I'll post and link the score. Hopefully between now and the next lesson in 2 weeks I can get a ton of practice time in.

item.title: Will it ever just click?
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I was pretty frustrated after yesterday's 55 on the Needwood 9. Fun, but frustrating. Left me wondering if there will there ever be a time where things just click?

I felt like right before I got Covid I went to the range and I could actually aim at a target and get a playable ball between 100-160 yards. It was very consistent. I thought I had captured lightning in a bottle. Even my drive was rolling over 200 pretty straight. That week, I had gone to the range just about every day. I probably had a little bit of a false sense since I now know the range is downhill and I was getting a bit more carry because of it.

The following week everything fell apart when I played, and then I had Covid, and took another few steps back. On the course I had shifted back to keeping my weight on my back leg. I feel like I've corrected that now, but way more inconsistent.

2 weeks ago, after going out the first time with my new putter, I felt like my putting was really coming together, then yesterday's wet course happened and I couldn't hit anything, had something like a 5 putt yesterday after getting to the green in 2 .

Some internet searches suggest that there are times when things click for a golfer, but you only get to ride it for so long.

For me right now, it's standing over the ball and not getting all the swing thoughts in my head. I want to go back to not thinking, but I'm not there yet. Starting at my late age, and making the mistakes I did, means I've ingrained a bunch of crap that I still have to undo. If I don't think, I'll still swing with my shoulders way more than my hips (I could write a ton on this, as now I just think my shoulders and arms engage too early even though I initiate with the hips. My arms are strong, and end up catching the hips).

item.title: Another range session
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I'm rushing. I'm rushing these range sessions and focusing on too many things. It takes me through a giant set of balls before my swing comes together. I try too many things once I get something right. I do so many things wrong.

I spend most of my time switching between 2 flags and clubs for 5-10 swings. Was hitting the irons really long on the downhill yesterday. I was hitting the 7 iron just in the 150-160 on clean strikes. 6 Iron I hit past the 160-170 range a few times. 8 Iron had some really long shots too, creeping in to that 150 range. No consistency again till the end when the irons finally started separating a bit.

Too many mishits... I'd say the fat shots usually go straight and short. If you take those out since they are somewhat playable usually, you probabbly get 2/3 playable shots. The driver was okay yesterday, but not great. More mishits than playable. Either really high, or really low. Although I turned it around after a good shot and saw the ball mark right in the center. Driver is still too dangerous for me to play, as a 6 iron is a bit more consistent and typically only 20 yards shorter on a perfect shot (maybe I need a driving iron)

New goal. Play 9 holes and keep it in play, only allow you to go out of the fairway 2x out of 9 holes.

item.title: More range time
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I need to video every range session. I took a look at my videos, some good and bad from down the line. I'm reviewing one swing right now and actually thought I was coming way too far over the top, but now looking at it, it doesn't look as bad. Still more inside outside. See screen shot below, and I think I should be a little more shallow, but it's not as terrible as I thought on initial watch.

A ton of inconsistency yesterday... and a bit of fatigue. I need to get back on my regular cardio workouts for one. I also did this after a medium intensity lift session.

Good ball flight you can see on video below. The less I think about the swing, the better I tend to do. I played around a lot with different swing thoughts, but 1-2, coil, hips seems to be the winner. I still feel like everything moves too quick in my swing. I think jims lesson of getting the club a bit less upright is a good cue, and I think I need to be pulling more with the shoulders back (You can hear all the swing thoughts in my head when I over think things).

I am able to manipulate the club face consciously now, but that usually leads to over corrections. I think a good lesson to learn as I get a little better. I use the lag shot on some shots, and it usually goes right, cueing me to close the face a bit more on the next shot. It's easier to create lag with that club, so you get to correcting, but it doesn't translate as well back to my regular clubs. I understand why having a whippier club can generate more speed for some.

Hoping to get in a 9 today.

item.title: Bogey-Bogey-Par
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Played 7 with the little one today. He was having an off day, and I had a disastrous first 3 holes, then was turning things around. TERRIBLE off the tee with the irons. Here's what I remember

  1. Couldn't hit a putt... Line drive off the tee, then chipped over, then too many putts. Greens were fast
  2. Last time it was bunker, this time short with a wedge. Another terrible line drive with an iron off a tee
  3. Disaster from the tee again , hit one in the woods. Then hit a decent shot short of the green, and lost the damn ball after hunting around the grass for 5 minutes. Dropped and hit an awesome 2nd shot with a 6 iron, that got in range. Then chipped over (again), and at least 3 putted... is that really 8?
  4. Last time I flew over the water, this time I sliced it luckily away from the water and landed off the green. Chipped on, and got a 2 putt.
  5. Don't remember where I hit it, but chipped on and 2 putted again.
  6. My par hole. Setup at 160 yards. Mishit shot one, but luckily it landed at the next tees. Then I hit a clean 7 iron (no tee... theme here) to about 15-20 feet from the hole. I hit best putt of the day from 15-20 for par. Saved the day
  7. Hit more junk from the tee, another push or slice right. Then I hit a crap wedge, and then some more nasty putting

The kid was tired, so we quit there. I put in the score of double par for the next 2 , which is generous considering how I played.

Only penalties came on 3 though this time, despite hitting the ball terrible from the tee. I supposed that helped, along with a decent short game. Chipping still tough, but getting better. So many different shots there. Putting is still my strongest part of the game.

item.title: I can do this
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
It clicked a little today. This is somewhat deceptive, since I played 2 balls, and your seeing the better score on holes 4-9.

So let me give a range instead. Par was 34, best I scored a 53, 19 over. At worst I scored a 59. I should probably record both. If you do both like that though, it's not that bad a 112 over 18 holes. Par, par on 4/5 is the highlight.

Here is what I remember.

  1. Not much a recollection here, but felt like I was chopping at the ball and moving too quick out of excitement. I scored an 8 here. Could have done a lot better had I slowed down. Terrible chipping
  2. Things started to get good. Hit a drive that really flew and landed on the fairway. THIS WAS THE FIRST TIME I'VE EVER HIT A DRIVER FAIRWAY. My 2nd shot was a 6 iron, and it went left. Third shot was a miss hit, 4th went over the green, once I finally got on I hit a great putt for a 6. This was a fail from the mishit.
  3. Hit another great drive (I think, or was it 6 iron). In the fairway again, then went in the water with an 8 or 9 iron for penalty. Got the ball up and over the green, and once I was on, I two putted.
  4. This is where I started playing 2 balls. I'll cover what I remember of my better balls. I took a drive and a 6 iron. The drive hit the fairway, the 6 iron went a little right. From the driver I hit a great shot over the creek, and just off the green. I chipped on the green cleanly and hit a nice 8 foot putt. Par!
  5. Hit a 9 iron, hit it as a line drive on to green. Hit a decent 2 putts for Par! The other ball was off the green, but still managed a bogey.
  6. Long hole, and a big disaster. Toughest one on the course. I hit a great drive, and actually a decent shot over the creek. Then things went sideways and I was hacking a the ball, and missed some putts. Terrible chpping here, 8.
  7. Better hole. A bogey. I hit a Canadian goose on the way in. Decent drive (I know shocking) again! Then I hit a chip in to the bird, and but missed a putt I should have had on the green to go bogey.
  8. Another disaster... It was getting dark, Hit 6 iron but went right. Chipped over, and a mess of putting on a par 3. 6.
  9. Last hole. Nice drive, nice approach... chipping on was a problem again, and putting should have been better. It was basically dark at this point, and amazing that I found my balls

The good. Putting is still strong for the most part. Some good work there. Driving was amazing this time out. It went just a little further and stayed in play. Iron play was inconsistent, I missed some, hit some. My swing was feeling very on point, and my ball striking pretty good when I didn't over think it.

My biggest problem was the wedges. Just off the green I kept having issue. 50 yards in is a problem. Getting a little more consistent there, could have easily taken 4-5 strokes off today. The plain mistakes whether they are wedges, drives, irons. Most of the mishits today came from irons that didn't go anywhere, or were line drives.

I had so much fun playing by myself. I had a guy in front of me moving kind of slow, which lead to me playing 2 balls so I wasn't pestering him. Great idea once I got into it.

I hadn't planned on playing, but after hitting at the range and driving the ball really straight I was feeling so good. I had figured out something with the irons, and really a feeling in the backswing of brining my shoulder up to my chin as cue. I think the little bit of extra shoulder turn I was getting was giving me a little bit of extra distance.

So many take aways from this session, I learned a ton about my game. I'm not afraid of the driver anymore, and I do hit it longer than any other club. It's around 190 yards carry now on well hit shots. My putting is really good compared to my other skills. I don't try to kill it every time, and that helps. Not having to manage the kids, or play with other people helps takes the pressure off.

I need to work on my short (not putting) game. I need to figure out those in between distances. The approach shots with a wood or hybrid are not a thing for me. I always go, driver then iron. Sometimes this left me a bit short. I need to work on slowing down (granted the sun was going down).

This was a rambling post, but I am so excited about my golf yesterday. You wouldn't think shooting just over double bogey would be so fun. It was a step in the right direction though.

item.title: Lesson - new wedge drill for me
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I had trouble 'finding my swing' when I got out on the range yesterday for the lesson. Took quite a few balls. Instructor happened to see a few of my really good swings, and was kind of shocked... good thing he missed many of the bad.

A few problems. Wrist hinge on the back swing set and hold. I wasn't hinging the wrist back enough. Still not compressing the iron enough, and I'm chicken-winging through. So Jim got me working with my PW. It's more of a 3/4 swing, swing back hinge , and think 'hold hinge' on the way through. This is still pretty tough for me, but I kind of get it. I think if I can combine that with really turning my body during the swing and I'm putting together even more good distance!

I spent some time yesterday working on the feel on the bump and runs. Here are my cues

  • Grip - more up and down and not strong
  • Shaft lean
  • Choke down
  • Use the weight of the club

I cut down the number of times I would hit it wrong and roll across the green. Still a problem , just need to go slow. Mostly I was coming up pretty short, but I can live with that better as long as I'm getting to the green.

Tomorow is Friday, I have another lesson Saturday. Hoping to get in some time tomorrow at the range, and do the same 'late 9', rinse and repeat on Sunday if I can get the kids to come with either. Also tomorrow, considering dropping by a PGX store and trying their clearance drivers. My driver is really good right now, 180-200yds straight. If I could get that up in the 200-220s by just changing drivers, I would do it. Worth 120 bucks to me on an equipment change. Same thing on woods.

Funny how things have switched. Before I was killing my irons, and now they are just super inconsistent again, and the driver is the most consistent club in the bag with the putter.... I love it all though...

item.title: Lesson - Short game only
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
THIS POST INCLUDES A TON OF TIPS TO BE REREAD BEFORE PRACTICE OR A ROUND.

I had a practice session, that turned in to a private lesson. All short game. Lots of Jim correction on the chipping, really working on 30 yards in in from the green. Some key take aways

  • Setup with ball in the middle of your stance, you tend to be too far back, so bias the other way,
  • Shift your weight to the left now so your in front of the ball
  • Shaft lean to hip bone
  • Grip... adjust club open left hand, then grip with right, then left.
  • Aim with your feet a little left of the hole. Your aim perception sucks
  • You don't need much, as you move up in clubs (ie, from PW to 8). Your backswing becomes smaller. Lots of feel here still figuring out.
  • Use the club weight coming down and brush the ground
  • DONT MOVE YOUR HEAD BACK AND FORWARD- this disrupts the weight shift! Deadly
  • HOLD THE SHAFT LEAN THROUGH , stop chicken-winging!

Re-read this every time before you play.

Out of the sand

  • Squat down, and hit hard
  • 2 inch in front of the ball in the sand, to get it up. You want the sand to fly
  • Dig in by shifting your fit back and forth
  • Don't make all the mistakes you make everywhere else!

Putting

  • Make sure your not leaning the head up or down... This was a mistake I didn't even realize I was doing.

item.title: Another 2 ball round - from the whites this time
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I had nobody in front or behind me. I played from the whites. After hitting straight drives 220 yards repeatedly at the range, I had to get out there. Then I had trouble through the first 5 holes with the driver, and lost a ton of balls with it. Chipping was decent though, putting struggled, and iron play had too many bad shots. The scores are a bit inflated (again). 51 at best, 57+ at worst. I didn't penalty ever ball from the tee, and there was another one I didn't take somewhere in there.

Here is the writeup as I remember (time to maybe get a watch and track this better).

  1. Both drives went left. Too hurried on the first as usual. A couple 2 putts for a 6 and 7
  2. Both 6s, but not counting the ball I sent off in to the tall grass (or the one that went way left). 3 putts were the problem on this hole, 3 to the green, and then a mess on putting. I also attempted hitting the 5 hybrid, and it was so lousy it stayed in the bag the rest of the round.
  3. I think I decided to go 7 iron on this, because I was concerned driver would end up in the creek. Worked out well, with one shot fairway, and the other just off the cart path. I pitched one back on, and then both balls went over (although I thought I lost one, as I missed where it went, and then lucky find). Putting here was good according to the card, but I don't recall what happened. My putting was very up and down this round.
  4. Went driver (took a penalty on 2nd driver shot , couldn't find in grass so took a +2). If you don't count the penalty, I would have hit 5 on this one, as I hit some good shots. Both balls ended as 7s though, triple boogie with 2 putt. This hole was better than the scorecard says. Good practice again.
  5. Finally a hole I can par, but I did not. Hit 9 irons, one hit the green , but then 3 putted, the other I had to pitch on and then pitch again, but then 2 putted. A 4 and 5 (but maybe 5 and 5) . Pretty sure one was a 4. Harder to track when you do 2 balls.
  6. Hardest hole. Hit one good driver, and one okay one (one fairway). Was very happy with this start. 2nd shot to get over the creek was lucky, got a bounce over the creek, but couldn't find the ball (need to figure this out in the future). The other one I hit an iron over on to the fairway. A chip miss, then some decent chipping, and some lackluster putting led to 7/8.
  7. Best hole of the day despite the crap scores. Hit 2 drivers about 200 yards, right in the middle of the fairway. This was blind to the fairway, and a it was a little bit of a draw. They were right next to each other. LOVE THAT CONSISTENTCY. From there I got lucky with a iron line drive shot to the fringe. Another that lofted in to the sand trap. Should have been better from here, but ended with 6/7.
  8. Starting to get dark. Because it was practice I went driver , and then decided that was a bad idea. 6 iron, both went right. Chip, messy pitching and putting, 4 and 5. I should have done better here.
  9. Decent hole here... 310 yards. Hit my driver easily 200 twice! Somehow in the darkness I only found 1 ball in the fairway. This frustrated me, as the other ball felt so damn good. So I played a second just off the fairway for practice. Next shots were good, just off the green. Pitching and chipping were decent, 5 & 6. The 5 here was a very solid hole for me. 2 shots to basically the green, a decent short chip and putt.

Great practice. I love my lessons, but I learn so much just doing this myself. Apply the lesson from the week and just have fun. Hopefully will move lessons to the mornings going forward and pray to get kids out there.

I imagine if I had done Reds again, I might have gotten under 50. Really though, it's only holes 1 & 7 where the difference is big. Fun, fun, fun. 2 Balls is great practice. I need to do this 3 or 4 more times and I think the scores will really drop. Practice/Play/Practice/Play... November is the month and I think it can happen. I did well today with double bogey golf. Cut out a few mistakes and actually par some holes and you are there. I will only mark that is a goal if you actually do it legit without the penalties, and legit tracking on 2 balls (ie, you get the score either on your first or 2nd ball).

I am so damn f*ing obsessed.

item.title: Obsessed and the week ahead
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
The more I play, the more I want to play.

I feel like I've gotten over a hump, and ready to take it to the next level. I can get a few parts of the game working together in concert I could hit my goals.

So this week, I'd like to do another practice. Time permitting another 9 holes with the practice, but this is a tough one. I need to really keep working on the short game. Surprising from yesterday how good I was with a more normal wedge shot and feeling it, vs technique just off the fringe shorter. I hit a few nice wedges right in the middle of the green. This was good... Still struggle after the lesson with any type of consistency, but hopefully that comes in time.

There are still a few of the PXG drivers left, and may drop in tomorrow for an upgrade. Depends on the timing, and not making it a priority. I am getting distance with my driver now, and probably shouldn't screw with it. Getting a little control now to. The two drives on 7 yesterday that landed in the fairway were golden. A few of the others were good to.

Possible to play 9 after the meet tomorrow, or Thursday or Friday.

item.title: More range time - distances
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Lack of consistency at the range today. Hurried again.

I think I am squarely in the 'long hitter' distance on my irons now. It has to be hit right though, and that is 1 out of every 3 or 4 shots. On average I'm probably worse than a short hitter because I have so many poor shots, but when I hit it straight and correct I hit pretty long. I'm pretty sure Ion the 6 iron I got over 160 a few times.

I hit the 5 hybrid, and 5 wood again today. MUCH better, but still pretty inconsistent. The driver is still slightly more consistent for me. I think when I really bomb it I get about 230 yards, but most of the time, I'm just short of 200.

I stopped focusing on my hips, and probably need to again. For all I know, the last 2 weeks could be back to swinging with my arms again. I noticed my hips tend to be turned towards target in the follow through, but I probably need to revisit.

The good thing about swinging on the course is I tend to slow it down a little and not try to hit as far. It would do me good to do this on the range as well.

I am seeing lots more slices and hooks. I was really spraying the ball around today.

item.title: Rushing and making mistakes
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So today I decided to run down to Northwest again and do 9 holes. If I normalize scores it ends up being 115-131. Sunday prior was 106-118. In both cases I did not count my errant tee shots. I played from the whites again, and probably should have played forward again.

I rushed things and didn't have the best outing. Two balls again, here is the rundown:

  1. Tee shots were okay, had some trouble around the green, but had a good putt to save one of my balls. The other was a 3 putt.
  2. Best hole of the day IMO. Two good tee shots on the fairway. I got good distance with my 5 hybrid but the ball went right of the hole. The other shot was dead center with the 5 or 6 iron, then I mishit on one, while I hit a great chip with the other. I 2 putted one of the balls, and 3 the other. A bogey on a 385 yd hole is great for me.
  3. Disaster strikes, and I think I've had some relative luck on this hole in the past. I got lucky that I found both my drives, one on fairway, the other just off. I hit a 6 iron over the creek with one shot, and was psyched, because even though I didn't end up on the green, I was in the bunker and close. The other ball mishit, and then went up the hill. Then chipping and putting nightmare with both balls. I messed up coming out of the sand, and ended up over the green... on both balls. When I finally got on, it was 3 ugly putts.
  4. Always a fun hole. I hit 2 decent drives... one on the fairway, the other on the right rough. I hit both shots over the creek. Both a little short. Chipped on and 1 putted for bogey. The other ball I 2 putted for double. This was a good hole (pattern, good - bad - good )
  5. A short par3, and I messed up both of my tee shots with the iron. My irons just seemed a mess today. I think my swing got worse again. The hole placement was tough today, but I did decent with 2 putts, although it took some extra shots to get on the green. 5/6.
  6. One good drive, one so-so to the left. Both playable. Then I messed up the 2nd shot on the closer ball, and took a penalty for myself. The other shot went straight in to the trees! I was blocked a full swing by the tree branches handing down. So I was forced to play it all weird. Then chipping was pretty bad when I got close. No feel and too hard.
  7. It's getting dark... I took a mulligan on a couple driver shots. Then I hit a couple decent ones. 2nd shots weren't terrible, 3rd shots were a mess. Putting was terrible on one ball, the other not as bad for a 7.
  8. It's really dark. 175 from the whites. So I try the 5 hybrid off a short tee. The driver feels too long. The 5 hybrid didn't work. So I lost a ball or 2, and then went to an iron. It wasn't much better. Quickly working the ball in , one of the balls miraculously ended with a 5, and the other a 6.
  9. DARK. Hit two drivers, but couldn't find them... they felt straight :)

I felt rushed today with sun going down. Made more mistakes than Sunday. Perhaps having the lesson before made things click more on Sunday. The driving continues to improve. Irons were trash, and felt like my swing was a total wreck!

I need to work on my irons again. The longer I practice before a round, the better I seem to swing. A small bucket was not enough to dial in my swing. This will likely get better over time, but it takes me a long time to get that swing feeling good.

item.title: Latest lesson, and a break
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I have had a few days break from the golfing. Haven't hit a ball since Saturday morning and skipped the Sunday night golf in great disappointment.

The Saturday morning lesson was good. Chipping continues to improve, but I still have trouble keeping everything in my head to adjust the shot setup. Weaken grip, body weight forward, etc. etc. Too many mistakes here. Need to practice this like I practice my swing.

My swing corrections this week were around my wrist again. I'm not flat enough at the top, and appear to be cupping. May be leading to a bit over the top. It's not terrible over the top, but it's probably one source of my inconsistency. That could be a bit of hips, and the backswing. So I will work on that, along with half shots with the irons keeping my trail elbow tucked through the swing and not chicken winging. Hoping to get the practice session in this afternoon!

Aiming is always a problem as well. Long and short. Get your feet set right, and the aim will be more correct.

Hoping for practice session today, and playing Northwest or 9 on another course on Thursday or Friday.

item.title: Played a real course (sorta)
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I played 8 holes on Northwest today. When I got to the clubhouse he said I could take either. The inside 9 looked more busy, so off I went.

Here is the rundown (harder to remember this time as it was a first and quick)

  1. Drive - Right of fairway, 6 Iron - left of fairway. Eventually found my way to the green, chipping and putting were way off (need to warm these up in the future). I 3 putted this hole. Also had to get out of sand trap. 412 yard hole, might have been my longest, but then there were 2 more that exceed that this round
  2. Vague memory of hitting my first drive lost, and second was again fairway right. 3 Putt on this one too, the approach was back and forth and moving across the fairway instead of in the fairway
  3. This is respectable, however I didn't count my first ball that I shanked off. Hit a good putt here.
  4. This was kind of a fun hole, and think I should have done better. Hit almost on the fairway, and then over again, but got close to the green in 3. Then screwed up a chip over, but got the 2nd one in play and a 2 putt.
  5. Longest, and best hole of the day. I don't exactly recall, but I know I went across the fairway several times, but mostly got it close to the green, and hit a good putt.
  6. I barely recall this hole. Again, didn't count one of my duffs, but then hit a decent 6 iron off tee, and then I think I pitched on. 2 solid putts.
  7. I actually played 2 balls on this, and scored a 6 on both! 336 yard. Good drive, one in the fairway, another in the rough. The rough approach shot actually landed well, while the fairway one was off target. Eventually got it around to the green, and hit a couple good chips on. One of them I single putted for the 6, the other was a 2 putt for 6. So 4 and 5 on to the green for these, which wasn't bad.
  8. t's getting dark. I hit drive again right of fairway! Good enough distance. I then hit a couple of decent irons to get to the green and 2 putt. I missed a pitch somewhere here, but a 6 is a damn good score for me on a 336 hold.
  9. Group in front of me was moving like molasses. I teed off and hit what I though the best drive of the day. Uphill... but alas, it was too dark and the ball did not appear (despite being sure I hit fairway!) I dropped a colored ball and then thought I hit green . Was about to finish while I was walking up towards the path, found my red ball right by it, so quickly chipped and messed with some putting. Didn't count this hole, as it was just a bunch of messiness.

Takeaways. You need to practice chip and putt more. One day a week isn't cutting it. Irons were better today, but aim and misses are still problems. The driver was mostly miss right. Correct his. Distance is tricky.

item.title: Lesson and rest
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Chipping improves... just not consistent. Same thing with putting. The thing remember with chipping is HOLD THE WRIST ANGLE!

Irons were really nice today. Jim got me using the alignment rod to keep from coming over the top, and go back further in my swing. All the sudden without any effort the ball was flying. I felt like I was so fatigued across my body that I was letting the club do the work. It was going what I would say normal distances straight with little effort to swing. Tempo was so much better. Not as long as when I'm really getting distance, but considering the effort this seems the better direction to go. One little change and things get better.

My driving was way off today. And yesterday. Things were going left at the range today, yesterday it was mostly right. I'll find it. I am pretty sure I'm going to get a driver upgrade here pretty soon. Wedges on the list as well. The only clubs I like are my putter and irons. I wish I had a 5 iron too assuming it would go a little longer than the 6 without much difficulty. The fairway woods I seem to have trouble with as well.

Hard to make the time to practice, but I need time on my own at the putting and chipping area, and time at the range of course.

I am very sore from the round and workout a couple days ago, and then yesterdays practice. I'm definitely not recovered, but also really looking forward to playing my next 9. Thinking I might be able to convince the kids to do one of these late rounds with me, either tonight or tomorrow.

item.title: My first 120 Holes - 4 months of playing
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So since July 11th I've played 121 holes. Scoring average sits at the same, 121! Not great, but little wins here and there.
The good:

  • Hitting lots of 2 putts. Not enough in a round, but typically you are > 50% 2 Putts or less.
  • Learning to hit the driver. It doesn't work every day but when it bring a ton of fun to the game. Good days your topping what seems like a bit over 200.
  • Occasionally hitting a great chip shot. Can remember in the last 9 holes, hitting one that landed 4 feet from the hole. Need to keep getting better there.
  • When the irons are working they go really straight and you can do really well.
  • Shot your best equivalent at a 106 10/23. Everything was on, and you were having fun. Cooler weather usually do better.
  • Hit your first birdie way back in August. What an awesome feeling
  • You almost don't think about using your lower body to swing anymore, it just happens.

Some of the bad:

  • Lots of penalties, and errant shots. Lack of consistency throughout the game
  • You have one part of the game going well, and others fall apart
  • Haven't been able to par a hole in the last few weeks. Not much improvement in scoring overall during that period. A nice downtrend then a tick up with some poor rounds. Not that big a deal though
  • Your swing and ball striking is still inconsistent
  • Bunkers are your enemy again.
  • You lose a ton of balls! Sometimes it's because of daylight, other times it's just crap slices and hooks.
  • You miss the fairway a ton, and end up going back and forth from the rough.
  • You can't hit your fairway wood or hybrid consistently at all!

Goals for the next 120 holes (which might not happen till next year):

  • Get that scoring average down. I'm targeting to get in the 100-110 from the red or white tees.
  • No more than 1 terrible chip shot per 9 holes (ie, chip and then have to chip again)
  • Keep improving the driver straightness, distance and consistency
  • Feel more comfortable playing with strangers
  • Learn the rules a little better.

item.title: Played a few more holes with the kids
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I'm not going to mark this one in the history , but I played with the kids today. First time using a cart. We had a blast, even though we had some rain. Got through 8 holes.

Here's what I remember...

  1. Perfect drive. Hit an iron just off the green. Hit an amazing high pitch shot, and was 5 feet from the hole. Missed the par putt, and then missed the next putt, and ended up with a 6. Should have been a 4.
  2. Sliced two drives (this is starting to turn in to a problem). When I did drive right, it wasn't great. Can't remember if I hit the hybrid or iron, but I crossed the fairway and then took me 4 to get on, but putted a little better.
  3. It's pouring rain. Terrible drive in the trees. Pitched back on. I then hit an iron too long (can't remember if it was a 7 or 8), and actually ended up in the next tee box. Pitched over. I think I ended up with another 6 or 7 here
  4. Hit a great drive just a little left of the fairway, but it was lost in the leaves. Very disappointed. This threw me off, and then I dropped the ball and hit over the creek, and pitch and hit. I screwed up some putting here
  5. Another crap iron shot off the tee. Maybe I should go back to hitting them off the deck.
  6. Another couple sliced drives. Dropped and hit the ball over in the trees, and then played it out. I stopped scoring here, as I accidently chipped in the bunker, and then couldn't get out.
  7. Amazingly drove it left this time (a little pulled), and ended up with a playable shot. I hit an iron over the green, and another lost ball. Inconsistent distance was a problem today. Putting was terrible on this hole as well
  8. I pulled a terrible shot with the 5 hybrid off the tee that hooked, but landed decent enough. Chipping was a mess here, and

That was it. That first hole I looked like a pro, and then it went down hill. It was fun though with the kids. I wasn't taking it too seriously, and viewing it more as practice today. Not bad for 45 bucks.

Here are your problems again

  • Driver slice (right) -- too many lost balls.
  • No consistency with the chipping
  • Aim is off
  • Irons can be unpredicatable on distances. When you hit it right it goes too far, but dangerous when you hit it wrong.

item.title: Over the top
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Where my hands are at. The box is where I want to be on the back swing. bit lower, and a bit behind. This is leading me to come over the top.

Hoping that my over the top is causing the driver issue as well. Just a little bit from yesterday, and I think I'm starting to get the right thoughts.

item.title: Sick... no golf this week - more over the top analysis
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I got sick with some upper respiratory thing this week. Very busy at work, so no practice. I got a little bit of practice on Sunday after the lesson taking the kids out, but not as much as I'd like.

I did spend time working at home with that swing weight thing, and really liked how things were feeling. Paying attention to more back than up in the backswing. I do believe my over the top (especially on driver) is leading to the slices. How to drive this swing change to permanent is going to be a little tricky.

Also found with the short swing trainer a really good hips first feel. With the weight, it's so much easier to feel the hips moving first and arms follow. A good practice routine to me now on the swing at home is :

  1. Takeaway to the top feeling the right lat tighten up and the left deltoid almost in my mouth
  2. Hold it, and then think rotate hips. My hips almost always bump now, so thinking rotate first seems to get both going at the same time. Let the arms just follow.

Will see what this looks like when I'm actually over a golf ball tomorrow.

item.title: A lesson on chipping and putting on fire. Late 7 holes pretty bad
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Start out with my lessons this morning. I ended up private with the rest of the group being no shows. What a lesson it was. My short game went miles today. I hit 6 our 7 two putts from various distances, was able to chip and putt successfully 3 times in a row (chip to one putt).

Got some work on the fairway in that 30-50 yard range. Came a long way with that. My swing was pretty bad, but it improved by the time I left. It wasn't quite as smooth as I thought it would be but then who knows.

I took my youngest and ended up playing 7 holes on the northwest course front 9 again. I really though I would have a great time with the short game, but it was big mess:

  1. Short drive, rough. 5 Hybrid, short, 6 iron, short. Chip over green, chip on to green too long, 3 putt. 8 or 9. Awful start and moving too fast.
  2. I'm slicing drives again. I hit two balls in the trees, next shot was recovery, and eventually found the green for a better 2 putt.
  3. Par 3, hit the 6 iron, just short of green, pitched over long which led to 3 putt. 5
  4. 9. Not even sure what happened here...
  5. Par 5, and a good hole again, but got a bit lucky. Drive sliced again, but was playable. Took 3 more shots to the green with the irons. I believe I hit either a good pitch or 9 iron, and then hit a 10 putt for par. A par on a par 5 is a first
  6. Another 5 on a Par 3. Missed left this time, but had good distance with the iron off the tee. Bad pitch shot (again), and I'm 3 putting when I didn't put enough on my first putt.
  7. Last hole played and a 7. More pitching and putting woes here. After all the great early play in the short game I fell apart. Oh well.

Despite the somewhat poor short play, I think it wasn't all bad. I lost a few drives to slices (and didn't count all the penalties). I would like to get rid of this, or at least reduce to 1 or 2 per nine holes. How about at least hit the fairway 50% of the time.

Irons were not long, and several mishits. Not all terrible, but definitely not on. I need another week of good range time.

item.title: Things to work on this week
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Busy week at work ahead, but Thursday-> Sunday should hopefully be able to get some reps in. Here's what you need to work on:

  1. Full swings with the clubs
    • #1, Coach Jim says need to maintain wrist angles/triangle through the swing like I did on the chip and pitch shots which greatly improved.
    • #2 Coach Jim continue to workout on the setup and getting the hands a bit lower, but behind. This will help with the inside/outside thing.
    • #3 Lots of balls. The more I hit, the straighter and better the aim gets.
    • #4 Work on the driver slice. It went from great club to crap club over about 2 weeks. Range time...
    • #5 Irons, hybrids and woods aim and distance.
      • The more I hit the better I get at all of these.
      • Finding the right distance on these is getting more and more important
  2. Lock in the short game.
    • Pitch - learning to modulate the distance with different clubs and backswings
    • Chip - hang on the goodness you found yesterday (see image below of shots in the circle. 4 balls, 2 gimmes, and 2 makeable putts.
    • Putt, work on the lag and distance. Remember these things
      • Steps x3 = Feet
      • Divide by 2 to get inches on your backswing to target
      • Correct distance some by slope - uphill downhill
      • Correct line by slope halfway 1 degree - 1 finger, 2 degree 2 fingers, etc...
