  3. Stretch and Lift and Exercise - your getting too stiff from the golf in certain areas.

So the goal this week will be to get the work done so I can practice Wed/Thursday, and play 9-18 on Friday mid-day. Lesson Saturday and then maybe 9 on Sunday. Lots of golf in the cold. Despite some crap scores, I feel like I am close to the next breakthrough with all the pieces coming together for 9 holes.

item.title: Going to buy a watch - Shot Scope vs Garmin
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Like always, I over research before making a purchase. Rather than upgrading a club, I want to start tracking and getting stats on how far I hit the ball with my current clubs. Lets see what I'm really doing.

I narrowed down to a couple options Shot Scope v3 GPS, and Garmin Fenix 6. The pricing right now, $159, and $329.

I know, and love Garmin for the running and workouts. I know they do GPS well. I've watched the videos on using the Garmin golf app while using on the app. Looks pretty good, but I didn't like the amount of scrolling and info that you needed to put in on each hole. I did like the auto shot detection, but also that looked like something that could mess up with practice shots.

So I got to the shot scope trough some very good targeted advertising. I thought I might want to the belt buckle one, but it almost seemed easier to just get the watch. I looked at some videos of the UI, and looks like it provides info that could really help. It comes with tags, so you tap the tag, and then you hit the club. Post edit after the round. Seems like an awesome deal for 159, so I'm going to go ahead and do it!

It's not going to do a ton in round, besides tell you distance to front/middle/back. But that's all I really care to know. I'd like to really just see where most of my mistakes are coming from, how bad is my dispersion, and how inconsistent are my distances.

item.title: Northwest - 57, playing in the cold
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I played a full 9 holes today (got out earlier than usual). The good news... the cold did not bug me. The bad news, I made a lot of mistakes. This is a pretty legit 57, couple times I dropped 2 balls, and played that, but mostly just from the tee.

  1. I hit 3 drives, and turns out the first was the most playable ball. I ended up playing 2 balls here, and both ended with a 7. 2 Putt.
  2. Again, hit a couple drives, and just ended up playing 1 ball since I had a guy coming up behind me. Got to the green in 3. If I could do this each time, I'd be golden. I even used the 5 hybrid here. I ended up 3 putting here though, trouble gauging speed on the green. 6.
  3. Really great drive, and then I got lucky and bounced a 9 iron over the creek. Hit up over the green with the pitching wedge, then pitching wedge, back over the green, then pitching wedge one more time with a 1 putt. Another 6. IF I could just get all 6s.
  4. Disaster. I decided to let the guy behind me play through. He was in a cart and moving a bit faster than I was. I ended up hitting a couple long drives in to the trees. Then I shanked it, and followed that up by hitting in to the creek. So now 3 strokes becomes 5, and I hit another shot but end up going right over just behind the bunker. Chip shot goes in the bunker, and then two to get out. I lost count, but at least I putted well .. This may have been a 9 or 10, but I gave myself an 8.
  5. I par'ed a hole. Good approach, just off green. 2nd chip shot rolled within about 6-7 feet of the cup, and then I putted in for par.
  6. Nemesis hole. This hole to me is harder than any of the ones I've played on the main course. So my drive sliced, not terribly, but bad enough that I ended up in the trees. I decide to punch out, but miss the fairway a little short, but at least I'm open. Then I slice it again with one of my irons. Then I'm just off the cart path, and hit over with my pitch shot. 5 shots to just off the green now, I pitch 6, and then 2 putt for my snowman!
  7. Crap drive, but it somehow hit the fairway. 5 hybrid again, but didn't get the distance I wanted. Then a bad iron shot. I'm on the green in 5 this time, and 2 putt it. Putting was good. 7.
  8. Good drive with the 5 hybrid off the tee. Chip went too far, and then too far again. This was par'able, but screwed up the chip by over hitting it. No feel! A long putt went too far, setting up a 3 putt, for a 5.
  9. A good crisp long drive gave me hope. I hit the fairway, 130 yards out from the hole, and then more disasters with irons and chips. 2 putt. \

So overall, some good. At least I pared the easy hole. A few of the double boogies were really good. A few good chip shots.

Driver was better today. Irons were inconsistent, and so was chipping. Lost fewer balls then I typically do. My range session was really good, but left too much of it on the range. I was deadly on the range, hitting really consistent with my 7 iron, same spot over and over again. I think had I played shorter tees, my score drops 52-53.

What will it take to get this under 50. I've got to single boogie 3 holes, and double the rest. I need to cut out the mistakes. Bunkers are terrible for me, as I'm really having trouble getting out as of late (I didn't count my miss of the ball in the bunker). Mishits, every other hole are problematic. Sliced drives are problems, but not as bad.

It just feels so damn close, but so far away. Wish I could play every day.

item.title: Last lesson - golf today?
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
My last lesson was great. Entirely short game. Chip, Putt, Pitch. Jim gave the group a great practice routine. 2 balls from the edge to chip and putt in. 2 balls from the middle of the green (long putts). 2 Balls from the fairway, to pitch and putt in. 6 balls total, 12 is par. Goal is to get under 16.

I failed my first and second rounds with scores in the 20s. 3rd time was a charm, I holed my first chip, and chip and 2 putt the second = 4. Then 2 3 putts, so now your at 10.

Over to the fairway, one short, one long. The short one wasn't terrible, down in 3. The long one, I hit a great shot, and great putt to get down in 2 for a 15. If I did that every time out that's 2.5 per hole, and 22.5 per 9 holes.

Lets see I can average 3 on to the green, that's a 27 +22, and would get you to your score sub 100 score over 18 (two 49s). It never works like that though. I probably average closer to 4 shots to the green on par 4s, and 2 shots for par 3s. What does this tell us though... equal time on long game and short game. Both are coming along at the same pace, so I hope that I see a drop off here soon.

I'm really hoping to get out on the course for a bit today. I got my shot scope watch, and itching to give it a try. The weather is in the mid to high 50s, so all good here. Low wind, and sunny. So the course may be extra busy unless you play late.

One way or another I will try to get a few holes in. Golfing afternoon yea!!!

item.title: Shot Scope - first 8 with the V3 watch
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I got my shot scope in, and was able to play my first few holes with it today. Overall initial impressions are very happy with the purchase. Price point

I'll go through my pros/cons after this first partial round.

Pros:

  • Total unobtrusive. This is what I bought it for, as I didn't want to think too much about what I was doing when I was doing it. The only thing you need to do is get the end near the watch (sometimes it picked it up without me remembering to get it nearby). Was easy to just play, and not think too much about it and get yardages. This helped, while not feeling like it was in the way.
  • Editing in the web site is awesome. I'll go through this some in the cons, but it was easy to make the corrections. I made one mistake when I started, but after that I got the hang of the editing very quickly. Highly intuitive interface, and don't mind doing this at all.
  • The web site stats are fantastic! This is what I was looking for. Already worth the sale price tag for this.
  • The pin collect feature works well when you use it correctly! It's a one button thing when you are over the tee.

Cons:

  • First time out I had a shot miss on the first 5 holes, but the last 3 it got all strokes. The misses below would have been nice to have gotten right, but I can live with it. The corrections are easy enough, and I tend to remember how a hole played out.
    • 1 . Start driver location was way right. Think the GPS was going a little haywire at the start, and likely my fault for not trying to get a lock earlier.
    • 2. 2nd shot missed, so it looked like I drove it 300 yards. Really wish I had gotten this one. Easy correction
    • 3, missed one shot where I landed in the sand bunker. Was basically a mishit, but I went back in and counted in.
    • 4, 2nd shot missed again, so it looked like another 300 yard drive. Easily corrected
    • 5, registered a weird starting location. Easily corrected
  • The pin collect came up several times while I was chipping. Confusing, but didn't seem to effect tracking
  • Still should keep score on a scorecard in case you forget something.
  • Yardages got weird during the round a couple times, good thing I'm not really good enough for it to make a difference. It was not at times it would have mattered.

So overall first impressions are that I am quite pleased. IT's easy without having to remember too much. I would have like to have all hits registered, but I think over time it will get better. I think perhaps if your hanging around a spot and it picks up a club, then maybe it knows your likely hitting.

The stats are going to be awesome, and I should really be able to inform what to work on.

item.title: 48 Over 8 Holes Northwest Inside
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So played decently today. If you take out the two 'blow up' holes, and the drives that went out of bounds that I didn't play, it was pretty good.

Really helped to have the shot scope along for the ride on this one. So here goes the review. Image below is the pitching disaster on 8

  1. I hit two driver shots. I found the one I should have lost, and missed the other one. I thought I wasn't going to play this hole correctly so I just dropped and continued. I flushed the first drive, but it did not reveal itself. My approach with the 7i left me just right of the green. 117 yards. I pitched over, and then pitched on. The second pitch was really good, and was able to 2 putt. Could have saved a stroke here on a better putt.
    • Improve on longer pitch (-1), and putting within 6 ft (-1)
  2. Hit a roughly 200 yard drive. Left me roughly 160 or so yards out. So I went 5 hybrid, but came up a little fat and short and right. Pitching wedge again OVER. Decent pitch and 2 putt on a tough green
    • Improve on longer pitch (-1)
  3. Driver again, and found fairway. This was one of only 2 legit drives that got recorded 173 yards. Second shot was a line drive 7 iron that went left, and landed just in front of the bunker. I then attempted to hit it over the bunker with the SW, and ended up in it. I actually hit a great shot out, and landed 4 ft of the hole, but missed a makeable putt
    • Missed pitch (-1), and missed 4 ft in putt (-1)
  4. Driver again, sliced a couple off, and then hit one around 190 yards. Left me about 110 from the hole, so I went 8 iron and missed the green left. Good chip and 2 put for boogie.
    • 90-120 yard shot on the green (-1)
  5. 9 iron off tee, but came up a little shorter than I would have liked. 60 ft to the hole. Long putt was good within 7 feet, and
    • 90-120 yard shot on to the green (-1) , putting within 8 ft (-1)
  6. A semi-disaster. I mishit the driver, but it fairway so I played it , despite it only going 133 yards. Hybrid mishit, 23 yards, Hybrid slice right to trees, 100 yards. 8i lucky to the fairway 96 yards.
    • Pitch wedge over the hole (again). Pitch on to green, and 3 putt. Score: 9, disaster!!
  7. 166 yard drive ... felt longer. 7i, 111 yards, but missed right. Pitch wedge, to actually hitting the green and a 2 putt
    • Irons 90-120 yard out to green (-1)
  8. Semi disaster #2. Hybrid off the tee. Fortunate that I got 138 yards out of it, as it went line drive instead of lofted. I was hitting that 160+ at the range before. Here was the nastiness. Pitch #1, mishit right. Pitch #2, too hard over the green and a bad bounce off, pitch #, Too hard again!! Pitch number #4 finally your on, 2 putt, score 7!
    • Pitch madness (-3)

So takeaway holes 6 and 8 and you are looking damn good. 3 double boogies, 3 boogies. Play that and your under 100 in no time! Lets analyze the issues though

  1. Pitch too hard too far, 1,2,6 and 8. Total improvement if you cut this out -5!
  2. Pitch miss on 3. -1
  3. Putting within 8 ft. -4
  4. Irons 90-120 yards better approach accuracy -3
  5. Mishits -2

So clearly, the intermediate longer pitches are a problem. 6 Strokes saved by figuring this out. When your just off the green your doing much better, less mistakes, but throw me 10-20 yards from the green and I start messing up.

Long putts were really good, short putts were fine, but medium putts were terrible. I feel like within 8 feet, I should be making half my putts. Maybe cutting 4 strokes there is a lot, because putting isn't terrible, but I think on a good day.

Iron accuracy. I am often coming up left or right on my iron shots instead of on the green. Not like 5 yards off, but more like 10-20. It's lack of straightness.

What's going okay... fairways with the driver when not slicing. I can live with not counting these Lag putting.

So an opportunity to improve by as much as 15 strokes. That would put me at 33 for a par 30. That's wishful thinking, but getting halfway there is doable. 7 strokes and your 10 over for 8. Less than +2 a hole.

item.title: Stats - Strokes Gained and Distances
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I love stats. After my in depth analysis yesterday, I came up with ranked in order of Pitching, approach accuracy, and putting.

So turns out, this came through in the shot scope app. This is strokes gained compared to a 20 HCP. That's where my goal is at right now.

So the short game is where I need the most work as I analyzed. Cut that in half and your down 5. Approach accuracy was surprising ranked above putting. I need to work on my irons. I also think this might be by the hybrid, and a couple of poor shots with it.

Lets talk distance now. These were 20-30 yards shorter than my range session. I can say I had quite a few line drive iron shots. They actually played pretty well, but still lost distance there.

I'll talk 9 thru 7 Iron first. Good to see slight gaps. 9 iron was a one shot sample size though, and off the tee. 7 iron was traveling about 140 on the range, 8 iron a little bit shorter. Both were going straight. Now granted, I only got 3 shots of each, so the sample size is probably too small, but I tend to think each of these clubs should have, and could have been 10 yards longer. I tried to stay in my game and just hit the balls cleanly, so I know I lost some range there.

For the driver, the ones I registered were 166, and 172. I'd say I'm probably a little bit more like 180 calm on the course. The 203 long one, was an estimate. A good drive for me with my current driver is probably 220, and average should probably be about 190, trying to keep in play and stay calm.

The hybrid average is thrown down by the 20 yard mis-hit. The performance average... I was hitting it at least 150+ on the range. Perhaps it's the mats

Last is the putting stats. I need to make sure next time out to do a good pin collect over the hole, but these stats feel pretty right

Within 3 feet you didn't screw up this time, and hooray for that. 3-6 feet I would love to see around 80 %, and anywhere between 6-12 feet, I'd like to see a make in there somewhere.

item.title: A new course - shot scope broke mid-round
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I'm loving these twilight rounds. Today I did Laytonville for the first time, front 9 from the whites.

It was great, except I am super disappointed as I was trying to collect more data with the shot scope and it failed. I got through 2 holes, and then it stopped registering the clubs. Bah... Oh well, it was a decent round, with some really good and some really ugly.

  1. 3 terrible shots that somehow made it to the green for what should have been a 2 putt, that turned it to a 4 putt. Driver ended up way short 126 yards. Then 70 yards out of the rough with a 7 iron, and a decent pitching wedge full shot that went 73 (went about 20 yards further than I wanted) onto the middle of the green. Then, 20 ft putt that went way past the hole, and then back up again for 24 ft, then missed a 3 footer, and hit the 2 footer. 7
  2. Another crap drive, slice. 115 yards. Then the hybrid over hit, 148 yards to the left of green. 44 yard shot with the PW to 2ft of the hole, and 1 putt in! Par, 4!
  3. I'm not going to count the hybrid tee shot I didn't play. The drive that I did play I ended up line driving right of the hole. I hit another great pitch, a little longer putt this time, put another 1 putt! Par, 3.
  4. Long hole, 412 yards from the whites, all up hill. Drive was crap right again. I hit a massive 5 hybrid , that I lost +1 penalty, then I think 9 iron (miss), and 9 iron clean, with a two putt. 7 on a par 5, with the penalty stroke
  5. Perfect 9 iron, think I was about 12 feet from the hole. I could have birdied , should have parred, but ended up boogie with a bad 3 putt. Last 3 putt of the day though.
  6. Another long one, 444 yards. Drive was decent, but sliced right again. I then hit too far left with the hybrid, then iron, and pitch, and pitch for a two putt. Crap, I said 6, and pretty sure this was a 7! Correcting...
  7. Another penalty for a lost ball. Can't even remember if it was the drive or the second shot that I lost, but +1. Then I ended up in the bunker. Short game was on point though, out of the bunker and 2 putt. 7.
  8. Drive, slice right. Theme here. Good recovery, bad pitch. Then another bad pitch. Then another decent pitch. 2 Putt, your at 7.
  9. Drive, slice right. Again. Okay recovery, then crap pitch, a mishit in there somewhere, then a decent shot to get on the green, 2 putt again. 7.

Overall, pretty happy with 53, or a par 36. That's a 106 score, and right where I'd like to be. This didn't count some of the drives that I sent off , so you probably are looking at a real score in the 110s. The short game was on point, and you don't mess up the 4 putt and 3 putt, and your putting would have been out of this world.

Pitching was better, but a mixed bag. The sand bunker shot was great, and couple others were decent. More good than bad, but some of that was luck.

Driver was ugly today. Very slicey. Some decent distance a few times, but overall tended to be short of where it should be. More lost balls from the tee box than anything.

Irons again were inconsistent. Was hitting the 7 iron 150 at the range, and on the course 30 yards shorter. It's so funny how I catch the feel and then lose it quickly. A few good shots though, damn I wished the shot scope had recorded. Would like to see what I'm doing when I hit cleanly.

I think the watch would have painted a picture today of poor driving, and great short game. Fairways were not hit well.

item.title: Two balls at Northwest
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Okay, this time I tracked it as orange ball vs white ball. I scored a 56 and 51. If I take the best ball out of each, it's a 48, which would be a new record. However, the worst ball would be 59. So some good and bad.

Here goes my synopsis

  1. One drive fairway, one left. 6s for both with 2 putts. Was still adjusting to the greens, no green warmup.
  2. Again, one fairway, and one rough. The fairway played into the rough from what I recall, and the rough played into the fairway. The better driven ball had an over the green shot, but the other one came back nice, and hit a 2 putt. A 5 on one of these is good
  3. One drive in another out again . Took the second one, and pitched it back to the fairway, and was able to hit a good iron shot that come me just off green. The other one ended up in the bunker. I don't remmber which was which, but one was a boggie, and the other was a double. Putting was good.
  4. First disaster. Two fairway misses... one left, one right. The left miss had to be pitched back on to fairway. The right miss had to be pitched back on the fairway... left miss I had to move a little because it was too close to the cart path, but I hit that one square. It played well, but ended up in the bunker. The other one I felt like I was hacking at, but ended up okay too. One ended up in the bunker, the other was big mess. I had an 8 on one ball, and 6 on the other. Not a good hole.
  5. I missed the green on both balls. 2nd ball I over hit on the 2nd shot. Putting was decent again-- 2 putts, for a 5 and 4 on the par 3.
  6. Hard hole. Two terrible drives, one ended up on the other tee box, the other ended up left hooked to the rough. I ended up penalty on 3rd shots for both ... in the creek. Then got over on to the green. This is by far the hardest hole I've played period. This one kills me every time. A 7 and 8, with the penalty
  7. The only noteable thing about this hole was that I hit the wrong fairway (again). I then finally hit a great 3 wood, which is a weakness. It felt like enough distance to get to the green, but it smacked in to a tree, and came crashing down.
  8. Crap off the tee, no greens with the hybrid. 2 5s... one was a 3 putt, the other a 2.
  9. Finally a par. I hit a couple in the fairway. 2nd shot went right in to the rough , the other rolled right on the edge of the green as I recall, and then I 2 putted. The other took a couple of bad pitches to get in , and 3 putted.

So not a terrible outing. I find my back starts hurting, and I run out of energy. Perhaps I need to take a cart sometimes.

Where are the holes in my game. Consistency through all clubs, driver to approach. Short game mistakes (but not so bad). Putting still decently strong. A little more distance off the tee would be nice, in all situations.

item.title: Last lesson, back aches, new clubs
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So the last lesson we did some speed training. It was actually a bit of a workout. My fitness isn't what it was 6 months ago when I was running more often. Spent the 2nd half of the lessons trying to use a hybrid to work our way on to the green from 50 yards by putting it to the green. Had a lot of trouble with this.

I find my back is really aching after 9 holes. I am highly considering getting a push cart to see if that helps things. A better warmup should be in order.

I have my new shot scope on the way. After going back and forth with support they agreed it was a problem. I loved it when it worked, hopefully the next unit will be more durable. They replaced for free.

I ordered a chipper club. 50 bucks, thought it was worth a try. Using it for those shots like in the lessons where your in a medium range. I think I might be less likely to screw up, so I'll give it a try.

I am highly considering purchasing a driver now. PXG offers this 50 dollar full bag fitting thing. My thinking is that spending some time working from driver down to irons to see if distance and consistency gains can be made. It's cheaper than a lesson.

The problem is , even though my swing is getting better, it's still not quite consistent enough. I am still working on shallowing a bit more to avoid that over the top nonsense.

The driver will be great one day, and then terrible the next. Prior to the last round, I was hitting at the range anywhere between 180 and 240. Yes 240... granted it was coming down an incline some. On the course it was a different story, I was hitting things more like 150-175. I'd love to get all the clubs up a bit. Driver in the 230-250 range on the course, and everything else appropriately gapped. 180-230 with woods and hybrids, and irons and wedges from 90-180. Can 'real' non-beginner clubs get me there. I think it's possible. It might be wishful thinking to see that driver go up much, but I think possible.

I'd be pretty happy just to stop slicing and get consistent with distance, but yea, a bit of ego would like to see me hit something a bit longer for my size. When the ball travels close to 200 it feels pretty awesome... can only imagine what hitting a 250 drive might feel like. So yea... I'm chasing distance a bit.

item.title: Northwest, 49!
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Super happy with today's performance. Took the cart with my son, and had a good outing. Hit the ball reasonably well. Great putting at times, with a few big missed opportunities, so it evened out. Short game was good, but not the best it's been. Fairly even. Oh, and the shot scope worked so got some distances.

Driving wasn't terrible, but wasn't a strong point either today. My 5 hybrid was on point though and really played well today. Averaged over 150, which is good for on course conditions for me (although I can hit a 7 iron 160, it doesn't happen on the course).

A big takeaway today, don't warmup too much. If you do, keep it to 20-30 shots tops. Running through that jumbo bucket and playing f*es you up.

Okay the overview, and will try to do some captures in here

  • Drive came up short, 138 yards. Was just fairway right. Then 122 yard with the hybrid, pitch, and an awesome lag putt from the fringe. 2 Foot tap in for bogey. Wish every hole would go that well.
  • Drive a little better, but missed fairway right again 189.2 yards (downhill). A decent hybrid shot to the middle of the green. I pitched over (I do this alot), and then 3 putted in, but really more of a two putt, as the first one came off the fringe.
  • Terrible drive, popped it up and only went 92 yards. I then played the hybrid, and knew it was a stupid shot, ended in the water, take a penalty and drop. Pitch 65 yards a little too far left up the hill, 3 putt starting from 84 feet. A 7 with the penalty. Driving the fairway on this hole is key.
  • A terrible drive that was saved. 117 yards, again popped it up high but landed in the fairway playable. Then 151 yards with the hybrid over the water on to the fairway . Looks like a par opportunity, but I pitch too far on the 3rd shot, goes about 60 yards, and then pitched on, and then holed a good 15-20 ft putt. It says 2 on shot scope, so I guess I didn't hit it correctly.
  • 9 iron slices 127 yards... when I do want distance I get distance!!! Pitch over, then great bump and run to get within 5 feet of the hole for a bogey.
  • My nemesis, but played well today. I hit a fantastic drive, 191 yards (downhill again)! Middle of the fairway, right in front of the creek. Then the hybrid from 180 yards out, seems like I might have something good. I hit a tree, and it drops at 82 yards, still 100 yards out. And now I need to come up on to the green. I choose my 8 iron, and in retrospect this was a mistake, I was exactly 100 yards from the middle of the green. I hit the 8 iron what I'm supposed to hit it and it flies over the hole (great line),. but ends up dropping in some brush for another penalty. A decent pitch a 2 putt.
  • Hole number 7, and the best hole of the day! 172 yard drive that sliced, but stayed in well enough to be just right of the fairway. 7 iron from 145 out, I didn't want to overshoot again (I've done that a few times on this hole). 7 iron stays a little further right than I wanted, and ends up hitting a tree and dropping down at 102 yards. Hit the best wedge shot of the day... a 50 yard leaving me 18 feet from the hole. I sink the 18 footer!!! Second big putt of the day, and a PAR!
  • This is where you almost cut 2 more strokes off your score. A terrible sliced hybrid off the tee went 130 yards. Pitch was decent though and got on the green 30 feet from the pin. I putted, and hit the pin and bounced out!!! I then took 2 more putts to get it in, from 4 and 2.
  • Was almost a disaster. 163 yard drive (Slice again). I hit a great hybrid, 131 yards, despite knocking a tree again. Then a 45 yard pitch over, and a 3 putt from the fringe.

A 49. I don't count my slices off the tee with the driver yet. Those just demoralize me. Take those out, and this is your best score yet. 1.5 over per hole.

I only played 6 clubs today, and some funny analysis:

Only 3 regular iron shots through 9 holes! So those numbers are meaningless. The hybrid on the other hand I hit a bunch and averaged at 142 which is decent all things considered.

The pitching wedge numbers are odd, since some of those were some really short shots. It was so so.

I look at the driver today. 5 missed right, 2 missed left. Not great. No fairways. Looking over stats... from 75% the previous round to 0%

Approach is pretty ugly too. 64% short, 18% long, 18% green.

Short game, a few misses here in the 50 yards ranges. Putting today was really good, with a shot made at 24-30 foot range! 3 to 6 feet seems to be a problem again. Only 33% made, but 100% within 3 feet.

The shot scope in 2 rounds sums it up pretty well, you lose strokes in all facets except from off the tee.

item.title: A new driver!!! A fitting and a great on course lesson
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I went for my first fitting. Decided the PXG deals seemed so good I needed a visit. I knew I was going to order one of the drivers when I walked in, and was already biased towards the 0311 as it had adjustable weights. I figured for 100 bucks more I get something that might last me several seasons.

I started with my 7 iron warming up, and then started hitting their 7 iron. The quality feel between my Wilson boxed set and the PXG was night and day. I would describe it as solid and balanced. Just felt quality.

I hit a driver close to 250 with the PXG. Compared with the Wilson that was short of 200 had me sold. Where things got interesting was the fitter kept switching from regular to stiff shafts. My top swing speeds were in the higher 90s, but average was below 90. The stiff ended up feeling better and had tighter dispersion. I didn't end up in the 'most stiff', but the least stiff from the stiff category. I felt like I had a better sense of where the club was.

I learned a ton about where the club face is at impact and how it effects the shot. To make a long story short... 0311 9 degree (adjustable to 10.5) with a Mitsubishi Tensi raw 65 stiff.... whatever that means.

I got fit for irons and hybrids as well. Stiff shafts again. I like the weight, helps me feel. I will likely order in 10 days as I can use with my company benefit.

Separate subject matter. I had another lesson Friday after missing a week. Nobody shows up when it's cold, so I get an hour and a half with a pro. It's pretty damn awesome and I learn a ton each time. This time we went on the course, and I'm starting to get a better concept of aim. My driving was awesome, and my par 3s were decent. Putting was out of this world. My lag putting is on point. MY chipping game needs a ton of work. It's that feel within about 60 yards that struggles.

So I played 5 or 6 holes at Blue Mash. It was like a 5 or 6 (saved by an awesome putt), on the first hole. I played 2 par 3s for 4s, I think a 5 and 7 on the other par 4s. I am creating opportunities. The iron play was atrocious, and Jim thinks it's my wrists at impact causing my inconsistency. Another lesson today, and hopefully we figure that out... just in time to get new clubs and screw everything up again. I love this game!

item.title: One thing gets good, another goes bad.. a few club updates
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Had another lesson. One thing improves, and then another starts messing up. Had another lesson yesterday. My long game was okay yesterday. My short game was crap, especially my normally awesome putting. Patience on putts within the scoring range is a problem (8 ft in). Spend more time on that and making sure you score I think will take a few strokes off. Playing at speed is an issue when you start duffing shots.

I do find, I can make adjustments while playing now. It helps when your coach is there, and yells at you 'stay down' , and then you come up and screw up on an iron shot. The thing is, I adjusted, and got better from there. Funny how Jim can watch my practice swing and anticipate my mistake. I do think with my driver, I know 'strengthen grip will fly straighter', 'make sure your swinging inside path' helps. For irons, I can correct striking by making sure practice swing takes a divot in front at full speed.

Hoping to play today. Hoping to do my first FULL 18 today. Haven't decided on courses yet... lots of traffic I can see at certain courses. Northwest looks busy for a 40 degree day. Needwood too. Weird. Thinking Laytonville again, but try to get through the whole course starting around 1pm. We'll see... maybe show up around noonish, and get a good warmup in and then hit the course. Pretty damn excited for this, just hoping I can play alone. I know this is a social sport, but hate getting paired with randoms as you never know what you'll get...

Expectations on today. Average just below double bogey would be really good for me. A 1.8 would be great and a 104 score, that would be around my best. A 2.2 would be average = 111. If I hit that average with a few mulligans, I would still be very happy, especially at the white tees (vice gold). A bad day would be 2.7, probably means I'm playing tees too far back. Tees will make a difference, and I'll see how the warmup goes before making a call on 'from where'.

To get to 1.8, I need to limit those misses short putts and terrible short game shots. Keep it slow... dependent on the course conditions.

A few notes... I got that chipper coming. Figured it's a good addition to the bag. I can pitch decently, but I think it will limit some of the sculling

My driver should arrive FRIDAY. Super excited. I had to confirm with the fitter that we didn't go with the XF. Dude is giving me confidence in how I hit it. Says that will be a driver I can use for a lot longer, and I can grow into it. I hit it well for my swing and lower the spin rate.

When I hopefully get the driver working over the next week... if it's everything I dreamed of, I'll pull the trigger that first week of January on the rest of the upgrade.

So lets count it up... Driver (1) , Irons 5-9 (4) , Hybrid (1) , Wedges (3), Putter (1), Chipper (1) == 11 clubs. I probably add either a hybrid or wood and I'm done for a bit. Play 11-12 clubs at this stage is good enough. Likely pick up a new bag with a little better organization.

item.title: An average outing at Laytonsville
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I scored what would be a 109 or 110. I finished 15 holes before the course backed up too much. 2.1 average per hole over par. Not terrible, but I really think I'm 10 strokes better than this when I putt well. I went into this thinking a 2.2 would be an average day, and that's where we ended up. Really was hoping to make a jump. But will have to wait.

My putting stunk. Plain and simple stunk. I think NOT using the perfect putting mat on the regular is having effect. Not enough 2 putts, way too many misses short and long setting up a poor second putt. This tells the story of today:

Short game was decent. Pitch shots were getting me in playable positions a few times. I tried that 5 hybrid putting and failed somewhat. I pitched over a couple times. Each shot was a little better.

Driving tee shots were decent. I don't count the mulligans, so there are a few more shots that went right. There were more of those early than late. Improvement.

Says my approach shots were trash. I agree, but I don't think it was as terrible as this shot chart shows:

The center one seems like it wasn't that far. There was a lot of shots on the fringe. There were plenty of bad iron shots though, where the ball traveled nowhere. I tend to miss left and short. Bias right and a club up.

Last I'll take a look at some distances.

So I think that's about accurate that I am driving about 193 per the average.

I think the hybrid is about 150 playable. Should probably be 10 longer, but whatever.

The irons are a mess. 7 and 9 played the same today. I know 110-120 on the 9 clean is about right. Add 10 yards for each of the next few clubs. The means my 6 should be playing 140-150.

item.title: 2022, and Goal setting for 2023
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
2022 is almost in the books. 6 more days, and probably one more golf outing. Two if I'm lucky, zero if I'm not.

Overall, I set the bar pretty low for 2022. I really started this in July with semi-seriousness. I hit a par, and a birdie in July and August, the later which has not been repeated since August!

I got sick in September and Late October which kept me off the course for a bit. I did hit most of the scoring and goals. The only one not hit was the 'Play 18'. Almost got there this past week, but only 15. I consider it mostly done since it was on a full length course.

For skills goal, it's a mixed bag, and hard to evaluate. Skills are a constantly developing thing. I think I will rework this for 2023.

So for 2023, I had these goals set before , and I think they are easier than I thought.

  • Score 3 over par per hole (~125) by end of June
  • Score 2.5 over par per hole (~115) by end of August
  • Score 2 over par per hole (~105) or below by end of September
  • Score 100 or below (~1.5 over par) by end of November 2023
  • Score 1 over par or better on one of the short 9-hole courses.

So looking at those scores. I think we already regularly score in the 115-105 range. I've hit the 2 below par a couple times on 9-hole courses. Outside chance of me breaking 100 early next year if the weather cooperates.

So redoing the 2023 scoring goals

  • Break 100 on 18
  • Break 90 on 18
  • Break 46 on 9, without any mulligans (Northwest 9)
  • Break 40 on 9, without any mulligans (Northwest 9)
  • End season consistently shooting in the high 80s to low 90s. Stretch goal to an 18 handicap
  • Get through 9 holes without shooting worse than double bogey on any hole
  • Get through 18 holes without shooting worse than double bogey on any hole

I think this is doable. I know how a lot of the path to get there, and just need to practice like crazy on both long and short. I think we could see sub 100 scores in February if we have a mild winter.

Now for the fun ones for 2023, the stat goals:

  • Ego goal, 250+ yard drive on course - Push goal would be to hit 275+
  • Birdie a Par 3, a Par 4, and a Par 5
  • 2 putt or better 7 out of 9
  • 2 putt or better 14 out of 18
  • 7 FIRs streak
  • 7 GIRs streak

General

  • Play at least 3 new courses
  • Get kids out with me more
  • Find some my age playing partners

I like this , and will update the page soon.

item.title: PXG 0311 Driver First Hits
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I got my first bit of range time with the driver yesterday. I ended up taking the kids to top golf, which was both good and bad. The bad being, the tees were not high enough which caused some driver swing issues. The music, the people, the lack of focus.

The good though, was top tracer which shows speed, carry, etc. I wish I had paid a little better attention to speed, but I did some really good 200+ carry numbers that I was never able to achieve with my previous driver.

It took a lot of hits before things started getting good. Towards the end of our time, I was hitting 4 out 5 into the net, with a decent level of dispersion. The slices were still there but got better as the afternoon went on and I adjusted to the club. I love the feel of the club, but the sound left something to be desired. Not sure how I feel about the feedback the club was giving me, as I had a few shots I thought I hit decent.

The mishits weren't all terrible. Once I got use to it, it was more like a 150-yard hook than a slice. The hook didn't hook as far as the slice. Current play stats below, should be able to play Thursday Friday this week to get some new stats for comparison.

item.title: I hit 270+ yard drive
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
14th hole at Blue Mash. Of course at the last second, I decided to not take my watch, otherwise I'd have an accurate number. I hit it square, and it flew, hit some frozen ground and had a really great roll downhill, maybe 30 yards. The hole from the green tees is 326 yards.

The purple X is roughly where I landed. I'd say 30-40 yards off the green, putting us just short. So estimate a 286 yard drive! I then of course went to pitch and hit it right in the sand trap. Hit out and then 2 putted. A could have been birdie with a great drive turned in to a bogie.

By comparison, I played this hole last time with Jim and I ended up in the sand trap in the middle. Probably 150 yards.

A few more observations from today. My short game, while having moments of brilliance, is mostly horrid. I can't seem to hit a pitch correctly. Zero consistency. Hitting the hybrid seems to be a better deal for me.

Aim is still bad. Sometimes you just skip this most important part of your routine when your thinking about setting up your swing.

My approach irons are probably the weakest part of my game. I hit a few clean, but for the most part you never know what your gonna get when I get up to the ball. Fat and thin, totally inconsistent.

So lets rank things cause I like to do that sort of thing.

  1. Driving - you hit long and straight, and now hit it REALLY long. If you cutout the slices (from too steep a swing) you tend to be pretty good.
  2. Putting - inconsistent, but moment of brilliance where you can 2 putt about every hole. Struggle from 4-7 ft misses where you should be shooting 80%+
  3. Short game inside 75 yards. Again, you never know what your going to get here. I hit some good shots, but lots of junk
  4. Irons and Hybrid- what at one time was my best clubs, are now the worst. I hit fat and thin . I hit all over the place... Aim is terrible.

item.title: Initial Driver Numbers, not my best today
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
First 9 holes recorded with the new Driver at Northwest. Performance Average 226, and a 246 yard drive recorded! Things were going way right for most shots, but otherwise pretty darn good.

Old driver prior, longest shot was just short of 200 yards. Performance average of 190.

The 25 yard performance average doesn't fully show how really longer this driver is. On hole 6 a month ago, I hit 190 on hole 2, today I hit 246. 56 yards longer. 9th hole. 223 yards vs 166, 57 yards longer.

So your at least 36 yards longer, but probably 50-60 yards longer on well hit shots.

Now the bad. I played terrible approaches today, and a bunch of really bad holes. Putting was decent, but not great.

  1. Took easy with the driver since it was really slicing at the range. 177 yards. 7i went 134... but ended up a little right and down the hole off the green. A good pitch and a 2 putt made for a decent double bogey start.
  2. Long drive of the day at 246. Good 7i shot on the green. 2 putt... this was awesome.
  3. Another long drive, over the fairway and almost into the creek. PW on to the green was a little long which set up a 3 putt for bogey. You were on in 2 though!
  4. Disaster strikes. 207 yard drive (although not counting the mulligan that I hit prior). I get lucky that I found the ball, I've got a chance, so I 7 iron it out . It's a good ball but ricochets off the tree backwards on to the green. Then things get ugly. I take a penalty coming over the creek, and then play a terrible short game trying whatever I can ... nothing works, 8 and that is genorous (except I still 2 putted)
  5. Really pissed me off. My 9 iron ball flight was kind of low and left. I thought I landed it on the green, but instead ended up with a penalty, but saved it with a putt
  6. My nemesis. I popped up my drive, and it only went 159. I really wanted to get it over the creek at 200. Hybrid... in to the pond, Penalty shot, goes errant. I play a 9 iron shot that goes left, but my PW does well to get on the green. I 2 putt to save face.. another genorous 8.
  7. This should have been better. 192 yard drive, that went right (again). I play the 7i, with a remaining 127 yards, and end up hitting it 158 in my little punch out. Pitch over and then chipper (which was terrible all day). 2 Putt.
  8. A shitty 5. Decent hybrid on to the mini-fairway. I try the chipper and fail, try again a little better, 2 putts in.
  9. Tee shot slices right again, but 223 yards (and uphill). A good 9i punch 75 yards, the chipper on, and 2 putt for bogey.

Holes 1,2,3 and 9. If I played everything that well, I'm scoring 1.25 over, and scoring in the mid-90s. Everything else was pretty much trash. I should be 3-4 on those short par 3s. Blow up holes on 4 and 6 will ruin your scores. Poor short game all over the place easily losing 5 strokes per nine holes. Missed irons are just embarrassing. Clear where the work needs to be done:

item.title: Equipment conundrum
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So after seeing what a new driver did for me, I'm highly considering updating the entire bag. Yes the drive is still slicing, but when I'm hitting it well, I'm about 240-250 straight. Getting consistent with that is saving a stroke on most par 4s, and 5s. I could see it on Hole 2 and 3 yesterday, where it was driver , and easier iron shot or pitch. I saw it in my lesson with a couple good drives that setup decent 2nd shots.

So that part of the equation taken care of, I turn to irons and wedges. So right now I'm headed to the 0211 with stiff shafts 5-SW, 8 clubs. 99 a club, and adding a 19 degree hybrid (roughly a 3 hybrid). This totals me up to 1072. A good setup, but I'm weighing it with option 2.

I stick with the iron profile we fitted, but go 5-9. 99$ a stick. I then go a little crazy, and get some premium wedges on a special for 7 for 1400. So I get 3 wedges that retail at 500 for about 200 each. Then I get my hybrid, and possibly a 2nd hybrid and a wood. 6 clubs. I take a look at a mallet putter (apparently, they make one of the best). Now I'm only up to 6 clubs...

Alternatively, I could go, 3 wedges, 6-9 on the premium irons, and just buy my hybrid outright.

Lots of choices and cost optimizations now...

item.title: Fun, but mediocre evening holes
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
My son is really loving the golf and so got another few holes of practice in tonight. Laytonsville. Score 40 on a par of 28. 12 over thru 7 holes. A 103 equivalent sounds good, but thinking about the mulligans I took (too many), and how terrible my short game was. Ugh...

Let's start with the driver again. A lower average thrown off by a bad drive on 2. My long drive was bit shorter at 226. Some bad misses off the tee, but not all that terrible when you hit it right. Still need more good than bad. I'd love to throw out the mulligan slices once and for all.

Putting was decent, small sample size, but lots of 2 putts, and some really nice close putts.

Approach was the usual mess of 'I don't know if I'm going to hit it right, so everything falls apart.

The Rundown:

  1. Good hole bogey. 212 yard drive into the bunker. PW to green, but a distance. If there is such thing as a good 3 putt, this was probably it. Stroke lost: 1 putt. Best hole of the day for me.
  2. Terrible drive miss hit, but it still went 157, so I played it. Hybrid miss hit, but then a great approach with a 9 iron. I 3 putt again, but not a terrible 3 putt. Stroke Lost: Approach 1,
  3. Hybrid off the tee. A bit more line drive than arc, but playable. 140 yards. Pitch over, and on ugh. Good 2 putt. Stoke Lost: Wedges 1
  4. Long drive of the day, 225 uphill. Bad approach, 7i mishit, 77 yards. Bad pitch wedge into the bunker from 50 yards out, SW out and over, SW over again, SW on. 2 Putt. Strokes Lost: Approach 1, Wedges: 3
  5. Bogey, 9i was hit well enough just off the green. After the misery on previous hole, I went for the hybrid to tap on to the green. It worked, but not enough distance control. I 2 putt for the bogey. Strokes Lost: Wedge 1 (if I had hit a proper wedge and then 1 putt for par)
  6. Driver Slice, but played 193 yards. Hybrid sliced; Hybrid sliced again! 8 Iron up hill, best approach shot of the day... 107 yards up a big hill. Pitch wedges on for a 2 putt. Best wedges of the day too. Strokes Lost: Approach 2
  7. Good drive, I think this actually went further than the 193 the shot scope gave me. But all good. It landed just left off fairway. 9i approach landed in between the bunkers. Not a good approach, properly hit this should have landed mid green, pitch wedge was okay. 2 putt for a bogey. Not a bad hole.

I replayed 4 from a closer tee, and got a 7 again. 6 was a bit of a mess as ball visibility became an issue.

So as I count myself, lost strokes:

  1. Putting: 1
  2. Approach: 4
  3. Wedges: 5

Shot scope against 20 HDCP says:

And for the year:

So prioritizing. Work on Wedges and Irons. You get that down, you'll have some good days in 2023.

item.title: Another terrible one - Blue Mash Front 9
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I seem to be moving backwards. I hit incredibly well on the range, and then get to the course and it becomes total dog s#$t.

I've been struggling with my irons. Nothing new here, but I got to the range and was on fire. Everything was going straight, and my contact was clean. Simple 3/4 shots with good tempo. Granted, it was on mat on top of grass.

Out on the course, it all fell apart. I think a lot of it had to do with the hybrid. The hybrid was just way off, lots of miss hit, and shorter hits. I have very little that works at 200 yards, and nothing consistent in the 150-80 range (and closer). I'd be happy if I got the same shot trajectory through my irons and hybrids, but sometimes it's a balloon with a little draw or slice, and other times it's a line drive pull. Probably poor contact.

I think the mat is part of the problem. Poor feedback from fat shots on the mat. The other problem is that I am able to dial in a club giving me a false sense of security, but then when picking up a new club it gets to shit. Need to practice like you play. Hit a driver, then a hybrid or 7 iron. Hit a pitch. Repeat. Go to different flags. Switch up the irons on each fake hole. Give yourself time and practice setup.

So the score was a 58 over 9 holes at a 36 par. 22 over, a 116 if I played 18. Part of that was giving myself an 8 on hole 7 with a lost ball (that I thought was my best shot of the day, but couldn't find the damn ball as the sun was going down).

Lets start with 'strokes gained' analysis. So the mulligan data is not in there, but I'm now tracking in my spreadsheet. I think as I get better with my driver that number will come out a bit better. I am confident that I can reduce my slice and reduce the mulligans to 1 per 9 holes. Need to get a bit better going in to out, vs out to in. I know the feeling when I lock in.

The short game here was a bit of a surprise. I used the chipper once (and it sucked), the pitch wedge was decent a few times though, but there were still holes where I went over and back. I used the hybrid a couple times on those short shots too, equally bad.

So what to work on this week:

  1. Practice like you play - Driver->Hybrid/Iron -> Wedge -> Repeat
  2. Pitch and Chip shots - working on the feel and variety of options
  3. Irons, 3/4 shots holding wrist (this was amazing on the range). Dial that in, for accuracy of aim.
  4. Driving more in to out, reduce slice
  5. Putting - practice more within 10 ft.

So I won't go thru the whole course review, but I'll give some highlights and lowlights

  • Hole 2 - Couple slices, put one in play at 180 yards. I counted 1 mulligan penalty here. The hybrid from the rough cut the distance in half, 122 yards, but didn't land fairway. 8 iron went 96 yards, where I was hitting it 130+ at the range. Pitch on, 2 putt
  • Hole 6 - Par 3, probably best of the day. 8i off tee, 102 yards, ends up short. Two pitches, first one goes 10 yards, second goes 24 yards for a great single putt in. Cut out that stupid putt , and you might have par'ed it.
  • Hole7 - Hit was I thought was a decent drive, but only measured 150 yards sliced in the woods. I then hit what I thought was a great recovery shot with my 7i. I thought it had a chance to get on the green, but I could no locate it afterwards... low point of the round.
  • Hole 8 - Decent drive, but didn't go especially long. 210 yards, but landed towards my aim point. This a shorter , but tough par 4 as you have to come uphill. I shanked the 9, then didn't put enough on the PW, used the chipper to get on. 2 putts. Not terrible
  • Hole 9. It's pretty dark, but I somehow hit the driver 213 yards and on the fairway. Now we have a problem. I should be hitting fairway wood here, especially on a par 5, but I don't have confidence in that club at all. So I go hybrid, and I slice it 103 yards right. A second hybrid shot slices as well for 87 yards. Then best approach shot of the day 133 yards with my 7 iron just off the green. Pitch over, and 2 putt.

My standards rise each time I go out, and my scoring becomes a little more strict each time. I was admittedly pretty deflated by my performance, but had pretty good fun with the older kid. I can still play poorly, and have fun. He hit a couple bogey's so was proud of him.

item.title: Another subpar outing
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
11 holes Northwest. A 111 equivalent. Some rough spots, but the short game, normally my biggest weakness, was really good. Better decision making, and only one or two shots that I didn't like all that much.

Putting was really where the strokes should have been better. Greens were tough, but way more 3 putts than 2 putts. Driving was terrible slicing things off, and lots of poor shots. I was definitely slicing at the range, but got it going towards the end. Then I had a bunch of poor shots. I was coming up way shorter than I had been... A 180 average today, with a 198 long. Yuck...

Approaches were better today, but not great. I had some really great shots with the irons today, but it was offset by plenty of bad. Inconsistency is my biggest problem.

Some noteable high and low

  1. Hole 3 - hybrid off the deck only went 124. I kind of expect to get 150-170. My pitch went a perfect 53 yards to 23 ft of hole... 2 putt. Bogey
  2. Hole 4. Took 2 drives. The second one went missing but REALLY flew. I mean like 300 yards flew, but it was lost. So I ended up playing a penalty shot, and did well with a 7i approach, which went the proper 125 yards. Then I used the chipper thing, and got me in range for a 2 putt.
  3. Hole 5. A double, but not terrible. Driver 187 on a poorly hit drive. I'll take that. Then I attempted a 3 wood just off the fairway. I thought I hit it clean, but it only went 115. Then a hybrid that I slammed 151 yards, and then did the hybrid putt trick to get on and start playing (it didn't do that well. 2 putt.
  4. Hole 6 - took the 3 wood off the tee. It went a measly 137. my 53 sand wedge full shot was great though and put me in middle of the green. I 3 putted.
  5. Hole 9 - Another dissapointing sliced drive. Losing distance on these, 171. 123 yards out all uphill. I go 6 iron this time, it's been decent for me today. 88 yards just off the green. Chipper, then 2 putt, Bogey. So I want to play a couple more.
  6. Hole 10 - A poorly hit 156 yard drive. With nearly 200 yards remaining, I decide to give the wood another try. I hit 108. Boo. 9i ends up short, but not terrible. Chipper thing on and then 3 putt. 3 Putts killing me today.
  7. Hole 18 - I skipped around. Another 150 yard junky drive. Hybrid terrible (82), 7i terrible (55), 9i good (82 yards), but lands bunker (was trying to avoid the on the left). SW out of the bunker was good, but then made a terrible 3 putt. Way over estimated my first putt.

item.title: New PXG clubs arrived, and more a coming
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So this may be a rather long post, covering a few topics

  • PXG 5 Hybrid, 0311 XF (25 degree) bought used
  • PXG 0311 Driver is slice central
  • PXG 2022 0211 XCor2 Irons on the ay

So lets start with the hybrid. Received today from PXG express. The hybrid cost me 110 + tax, shipping was included. Packaged well, and was in fantastic shape for what they described as 'good shape'. It had a little cosmetic wear but that was it.

I had hit the 19 degree hybrid during my fitting, and really liked it with a UST Recoil 75 Dart shaft. I had some balls really flying. This one at this price with a Projext X EvenFlow Riptide 80 - 6.0 was just too good to pass up. Even had the grips upgraded to Golf Pride mid size which felt so good.

So first hit with the club on a monitor, 160 yard carry without much effort. Everything was pulling left, unlike my typical slice. It just felt so damn solid, and was able to work it to some more straight shots. It was super forgiving at everything I threw at.

I've only hit off the mat at this point, but the feel and flight has it now as my favorite club in the bag. I will never touch my old 5 hybrid again! It's convinced me to finish out the bag any way I can with this club at 19 degree, and take a flyer on 0311 XF 3 wood. I will find these used and buy. Right now PXG has them at 250 through the site new + 30 shipping. I think I can do a little better. The 19 degree one is out there, but it is a different shaft that I haven't tried yet. I will find these at a lower price within the parameters of what I've hit in the next few weeks and I will have the bag.

----

Next up, the 0311 Driver. What started as an amazing flight that was going pretty straight, has turned in to slice central. I checked the weight setting and it's setup for a draw bias. I might take the head off and make sure it's setup correctly there. It's been super frustrating. I'd say 3 out 4 are pretty heavy slices. It's really robbing distance. I haven't seen many 200 carries with it lately.

I'm not sure exactly how to describe the feel that's working for me on this club now. The best I can do is 'coming through the ball'. Slower tempo seems to help too. This one is going to take some more time.

----

Last up, I've ordered the 0211 Xcor2 irons. I'm convinced given what I've seen with the hybrid today, I should see a nice result. The clubs should be here hopefully by Jan 20. With any luck I might see them monday or tuesday next week.

item.title: Filled out the bag
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Over the next 2 weeks I will be retiring all my Wilson Pro Platinum starter clubs for a mostly PXG bag. The only two hold outs are the Ping putter and Wilson Chipper.

So I was able to upgrade everything with a mix of used and new clubs. How this will workout. Will be interesting, it's a large blend of shafts in the woods and hybrids. No club is like another. Possibly even a few different lengths. I'll go through the bag upgrades and the cost of each.

  1. Irons - Replaced with new 2022 Irons on promotion. Cost was $800 with shipping and tax on a $99 a stick discount. I am going 6i -> Sw, including a gap wedge, so going from 2 to 3 wedges. 1/2+ and 2 degrees upright. Should arrive mid next week.
  2. Driver - Replace with the 0311 9 degree Driver. $350 for the driver with shipping and tax on a $300 promotion. It's a beast when I'm hitting it well. However my driver slice needs to fix. This just makes the slice go further at the moment. I just updated the hosel setting, it was turned a bit the wrong way I think. Will hopefully have a good effect when I get back out there.
  3. Hybrids - 0311 XF 25 Hybrid (5), and 19 Hybrid (3). Bought used $270 total with shipping. This marks a huge discount from the original price I was going to pay for just the 19 hybrid was going to be 330 dollars + tax. Even at the current price of 250 a stick, still looking at 560 + tax shipped, so this is a steal. I have 2 clubs now, but maybe not the most ideal shaft setup. It's still all stiff at least. I do worry that the 25 hybrid which I hit so well at the range may overlap with the 6 iron. A 22 may be in order in the future.
  4. Wood - 0311 XF 3 Wood on it's way as of this morning. My latest purchase is $150 shipped. Will probably arrive early next week as well. Shaft is normal length.

So total upgrade cost right now stands at $1520. So going from 500 clubs to 1500 clubs will see if it makes a scoring difference at all. Fortunately, I have partially subsidized this cost through an employee benefit. Add in another 200 dollars for the Ping Sigma putter, and the Wilson Chipper and my bag cost is $1700. Golf is not cheap.

I think the only change I'd like to make now is a new bag, and a push cart.

item.title: Tuning my PXG clubs - 3 out 4 arrived, lessons
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I checked my new driver again. Looking at the chart below, the driver was tuned to 'Big Minus' shipped. That's -1.5 degree loft, and -1.5 degree lie. I believe this is more of fade bias, not the max fade bias, but headed that direction. I've moved it to standard which should be the most draw bias , and checked that the weights were setup the same. I've also read somewhere less loft is usually more slice, and I was at the lowest loft setting for the driver at a 7.5 degrees.

If I get out there and I'm all the sudden hitting fairways we will know.

I double checked the 5 hybrid I received, and it was set standard. In my time at the range, it was headed left. A little bit of a pull.

I received my 3 wood today. It came in with the correct standard hosel setting. I have not had a chance to hit it yet, but it will be another piece of the puzzle. With any luck, I will get the 3 hybrid tomorrow and that will be good. I hit that 200 a few times during the fitting. Looking forward to getting out there and seeing how things travel. I do say, I love heading to top golf for this, as I get ball flight, etc now that they've installed the top tracer in all the bays. I will be there Thursday and should have all my new clubs by then.

I would have played today, but I definitely have some hip soreness in my right hip. Not terrible, feels more sore than injured, but needs a bit of rest.

Now.. with all these new clubs I worry that my swing is still changing significantly. I still tend to come in steep, so hopefully the clubs will help a little with that. Excited though that all my woods are adjustable, and I can probably tune them up right. I like to tinker. I understand the basics of it now, so I think I can get things right.

So in my lesson, I really worked on the irons. My wrists were not turning over at all, but I was still releasing the club too early. I wasn't extending my right arm enough leaving things bunched up. When I started turning the wrists over... things would go left again, but ball flight was straight, and I could feel when the club squared up. I am super excited to lock these feelings in and hopefully get a bit better in my approach.

item.title: Hampshire Greens 1st time.
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I played Hampshire Greens for the first time. My normal course was too busy, so I drove 5 minutes down the road to a less busy course. This course is more difficult than Northwest or Laytonsville in my opinion (slope rating for the green tees was 121, which matches up with Northwest's 121 for the white tees)

Unfortunately shot scope didn't upload my scores, and also I didn't keep my scorecard as well as I usually do. I left a couple holes unmarked, and took a best guess at a couple more hoping that I could go back and see the shots in the app afterwards. In the future, I'll pay better attention to detail.

6 bogey's. The rest were double or worse. I'll cap some highlights

  1. Hole 1 -Great first drive, and on the fairway right in front of the green on my 2nd shot. I'm thinknig, this could be a great day. I finished it out with a 3 putt, for bogey. Was happy with this start.
  2. Hole 2 - A Par 5 I scored an 8, but might have been worse. Drive right, then I don't recall with a 3 putt.
  3. Hole 3 This was actually a decent hole. Hit right just off fairway. Two more shots on to the green, and a 2 putt
  4. Hole 4 - A bogey on a medium par 3 I'll take. I hit in to bunker on first shot, and then took me two out, and then single putt!
  5. Hole 5 - A decent drive, followed by a decent 2nd shot that left down a hill. I hit a shot over the green just to the fringe, and 3 shots from there for a 5 on a Par 4.
  6. Hole 6 - was a par 5 where I lost some balls. I didn't end up scoring it, as I took too many drops
  7. Hole 7 - A weird dogleg, where I sliced in to a better position, but ended up hitting a crap ball and then recovery. The recovery was good, but a 7
  8. Hole 8 - best I remember, I didn't hit green, and had some sloppy short game
  9. Hole 9 -- too many drops again and I lost count. It was like a 10
  10. Hole 10 - Fun one. Hit right (again) from the tee. Hit a decent approach, and then a some better short game with a 2 putt for a bogey. Feeling good again
  11. Hole 11 - Went right -- messed up a shot out of the rough, then I'm on and 2 putt.
  12. Hole 12 - A 7 on par 5, but didn't count the mulligan.
  13. Hole 13 - I hit the cart path on the drive, and bounce bounce bounce. I wish I got that recorded.
  14. Hole 14 - Par 3 A good shot from the green tee. 7 Iron I think just over the green, another to get on, and then 3 putt.
  15. Hole 15 - Drive was slicey. Apparently I hit a nice 2 putt though.
  16. Hole 16 - Damn difficult hole, I actually hit some good shots, but ended up a little short of the green
  17. I tried to play 17. I failed horribly.

My 103 score is not indicative. I'd say it's more like a 113 missing the 2 holes with lost balls.

Anyhow... was fun playing with the new hybrids, but actually had some contact issues out on the course. They did a little worse than expected given the range time, but not terrible. The fairway wood was hit once, and wasn't terrible either. Not as long as at the range, but played longer than the old 5 wood

The slice on the driver was still present after the tune up. Not quite as bad, but still some nasty slices today. Same on the hybrids, but again not quite as bad. Range time was really good. Lots of really straight shots.

Irons come tomorrow... lots more golf this week.

item.title: The bag is upgraded!
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
All clubs are in! The irons arrived today. Ignoring the Wilson FW Cover, it's all PXG clubs, a Ping putter and a Wilson chipper.

So a few observations on the new irons just from looks and swinging them in the house

  • They appear to be about .25 inch shorter than my old irons. Old irons were +1 inches, and these are +.5 inches. Difference in manufactures I guess
  • They are supposedly raised 2 degrees upright. I have no idea how to measure it, and didn't notice much a difference comparing old vs new
  • These things are way heavier compared to the old irons. I remember liking the heavier feel during the fitting, as it allowed me a better sense of where the club was. True Temper, Elevate MP 95g, Stiff, Parallel. I think the other shafts are all a bit lighter than this. Will see how it plays
  • The 6 Iron length (38.625) looks like it's about the same as same as the 5 Hybrid (39 1/4). The loft is actually a little lower on the 6 iron. This could end up overlapping, but only time will tell. For now both stay in the bag
  • Glad I didn't go any lower , the 3 Hybrid is at 19 degrees which matches the 4 iron.
  • The heaviness of the steel makes the whole bag pretty heavy. There is a lot of heft to my clubs now.
  • They are so shiny... hate to ding them all up.

Besides the new clubs, I'm back in debug purgatory with the shot scope stuff. I love there product, but sucks that this might be the 2nd defective unit I've gotten. This time I got way more rounds... but still not great. I don't like the other options that are out there. When Shot Scope works it's phenomenal. Acros costs too much, but apparently only slightly more accurate, and can have similar problems. Golf Pad's price is better, but you need the cell phone near, and read lots of not registering issues. They have a belt buckle thing, but doesn't seem as user friendly. So this story will continue.

item.title: Gear Nut - Shot Scope, PXG Clubs and what's next for me.
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I've unfortunately turned in to a bit of a gear nut with golf. This probably just means I'll spend way more money than I should at my skill level. I like to shop, I like the idea of optimizing my clubs. I'm not at a skill level where it matters so much, but it's kind of fun, and I can afford it.

So let me go through a few topics.

Tracking

I am currently using the Shot Scope, and when it works I believe strongly that it is the best price performance in the market right now. At 150-200 dollars on sale, you get a product that tracks shots very well without much user input. The watch gives you quick distances to the front, middle and back of green. I'm not good enough yet to care exactly where the pin is. It does a good job marking the pin location with the pin collect feature you use at when you putt in. That is the only time you need to manually put anything in the watch is during that pin collect.

When it doesn't catch your shot, or catches an extra shot, it's really great software makes it easy to correct. I like to review my round right after I play, and find it easy to remember what happened on each hole, and where the mistakes are. The accuracy seems pretty damn good to me, although I've read reports from others that Garmin and GolfPad may do a better job (this makes sense since Garmin has been in the GPS game a long time, and GolfPad uses the phones GPS).

The downsides now... the big one is that the watch has failed me twice. The first watch stopped reading tags after 2 rounds. The 2nd watch I got 6 rounds in and then it had the same behavior. Sucks that I missed some stats when this happened. I had become so reliant on it working when it did fail, it was disastrous for me as I hadn't been doing a great job tracking my score that round.

Really that is my only downside to the device. The support team has been super responsive, and has offered to replace my watch a 2nd time. Maybe there was a bad batch, but they seem to be willing to make things right.

The tags are easy to use, and when it works it's great! The stats are awesome for strokes Gained, showing you where you are struggling most in a round or over several rounds.

The competitors are Garmin (with or without Tags), GolfPad (same), and Arccos. I've read that Arccos software is great, but the tags get damaged and fall off. They are expensive to purchase and require a monthly subscription. GolfPad has 99 dollar tags, which is a good model, but requires cell phone to stay in pocket. I was considering giving this a try , but don't like the idea of having to pull out the cell phone to see distances. If you don't use the tags, you can manually set the club, but again, involves fumbling around with a cell phone during a round. A watch is really better in that situation.

Garmin has tags, and some pretty extensive golf watches. You can entirely do manual shot tracking with Garmin, and there watches are pretty awesome. I hate the idea of having to select each club before the shot. It's an extra step that slows you down. There tags are 300 bucks. They look good, but not sure what your really getting for the premium price. I do wonder what happens when you lose a tag with a 25-30 dollar replacement fee. That's a bit ugly. I've read mixed reviews on the Garmin software for golf. I even tried it manually on the course one time, but I failed quickly as I was more focused on my game than the cell phone.

PXG Clubs

So still figuring out how all these new clubs will perform.

I've had the Driver the longest, and when I hit it well it's great, but I'm losing a lot of balls at the moment. Setting it to standard this past week seemed to help, but there were still plenty of shots going right. It's a swing thing that is exacerbated by the length of the driver. I plan try to set it out of draw bias, and into the 'most forgiving' bias and see how we do. Hopefully will have some feedback on that today. I am highly considering only playing it in very wide fairways, and switching to my 3 wood if I am hitting that more consistently.

The woods and hybrids are so new, and I've had so few shots with them, it's hard to tell if they are working or not. They are doing really well at the range, but I haven't been able to get a good feel for them yet on the course.

The irons are a complete unknown. I will hit the them for the first time tonight, and I'm uber excited about it. I'm very optimistic, that my 7 iron length will go from this:

To a much higher long and playing average. I think the 130 could easily be a 160. Will have to see if I can consistent with some distances before the spring. Also need to figure out if I have overlap or gaps that can be adjusted for.

The last bit is the 3 wedges that came with it. I'm guessing I can get more accurate with the new wedges, but that's going to take a bit more time. So many shots I hit with the wedges and need to get in the practice area for hours to work on!

Putter and Chipper

Let's start with the chipper first. I am leaving it in the bag for now, and find I use 3-5 times when I'm out playing. I like it for bump and runs in the fringe, or just on the fairway to the hole. Versus the 5 hybrid, I'm not sure how much of a difference it makes. I need to spend a lot of time figuring that one out. The new 5 hybrid has a much more solid feel to it and I feel like it can play a bit longer and more versatile from different lies. It doesn't feel as accurate right on the fringe, or rough around the green. I don't have enough experience with it yet though to make a determination. More time in the chipping area practicing.

The putter I can already say will be the next thing I really experiment with. Mallet vs Blade. There seems to be so much happening in the putter market. The TaylorMade GTX with the sliding weights looks really intriguing for me to delve in to the mallets. I did forget my blade one day, and played with someone else's mallet, and I liked parts of it. I felt like more accurate closer in where I've been strugling (the lag works, but not the 5-10 footers)

Balls

I started with Taylor Made Noodles as my primary, and experimented with a bunch of different types of balls. I found lostballs.com and figured this a good way to go. I got a bucket of Bridgestones that are supposed to help the ball fly straighter and had a moderate compression ratio. I also bought a bucket of taylormades that was less than 50 cents a ball. I'm losing so much now, makes me feel better using these found balls.

The Noodles and various other inexpensive balls I've been playing have been good too. The Kirklands which are a bit more premium but found on sell for just over a dollar a ball have been good too, but I'm trying to get cost down to less around 50 to 75 cents a ball at my current stage. When I start losing less, a dollar or so seems reasonable.

Other - Bags, Tees, etc

I'm giving myself the 'break 100' you can get yourself a new bag. For now, I'm sticking with Wilson bag that is adequate. As long as I organize things correctly when I start, it is a perfectly capable carry or cart bag. I've been looking at a few of the more premium bags, so when I do get there, I will spend a little for something nice.

I do want to get a push or pull cart and give it a try to see how we do with that. Need to find a course that can rent, and see how I like it before purchasing. If I love it, could consider one of those ones that follows you around. Love the idea of walking without pushing or pulling anything.

Tees, I've kind of settled on those plastic tees that cradle the ball. They are only difficult when the ground is frozen. They aren't inexpensive but they help.

So a long post covering all my golf equipment. This is part of the fun though. Evaluating, replacing, finding deals, seeing where you improve.

item.title: PXG Irons first impressions and Hip Pain.
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I hit Top Golf with the new 0211 irons (kid has an after school activity right near Top Golf, only reason I go there). My first impression was, this is going to take some time to get use to. It wasn't like during the fitting where I immediately was striking the ball better. These clubs are heavier, and feel considerably different than the old irons.

One good thing about top golf is that you get ball speed, carry distance, etc. It does seem like they have the carry distance tuned to what floor you're on, so you're not getting a terrible impression that you're carrying the ball 10 yards further than you expect because you're hitting from 50 feet up.

It was raining, and I'm working on a lot of stuff with my swing at the moment, so caveat that. The general feeling was is they were carrying about the same as my old irons, however I think the ball flight was a bit more consistently straight (again, working some things with the swing). When I hit the sweet spot on the iron, it did have some really long high flying hits with the 7 iron, but not really reporting carry of more than 120. More range time required, and I'll get a better idea from hitting at Northwest as I know where each club was landing at that range.

I'm really working on a few things at the moment.

  • Getting that wrist flexion, waiter holding a platter, movement at the top of the backswing with my trail arm.
  • Getting some more turn, where I feel it my lat, without overswinging to high
  • Coming down from the inside and squaring the club face
  • Extension with the wrists by turning them over so that I get that whip through the ball.

When I put it together with the coach, it was feeling pretty good, but yesterday not so much. Monday at the range I felt like I kept the feeling, but now it's a little lost.

Not sure if it was the rain or, my hip, but the longer shots weren't really flying either. The hybrids were going a little longer than the long iron. Still finding the 5 hybrid the best club to hit, the 3 hybrid a little tougher to hit.

The fairway wood off the tee wasn't bad. Distance on some shots was really good, making me think I may play a few rounds just trying to hit fairways with the fairway wood.

The driver was still slice city. I know how to get in to a better feel with the driver to hit more straight, but it doesn't always translate through.

This brings me to the next thing. I really want to practice a lot right now, but I have this pain in my trail hip flexor. I would love to take the afternoon and do 2 balls over at the Notherwest 9, but the hip is not cooperating. One ball with the fairway wood, one with the Driver.

I know this will recover and get better, but I need to lay off a bunch of stuff for a bit and take better care of it. I need to get the heating pad on it, and more consistent anti-inflammatory.

item.title: Irons and Hybrids
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
