So I hit my irons again at top golf with the kids. I'm having trouble adjusting at the moment. Really got myself a bit frustrated. The hybrids on the flip side, I'm hitting pure, long, and fairly straight.

Lets start with the good

  • 5 Hybrid. Most consistent club in the bag at the moment, My favorite shaft of the bunch, the Project X EventFlow Riptide 80 - 6.0 Stiff . I'm really able to snap that club. Very consistent 150 yard club. Slightly left bias
  • 3 Hybrid. This club just feels so different. I am way less consistent with it, but I am pretty long when hit well. 170 Yard carry on several shots. It's a slight right bias, and can slice when not hit well.
  • 5 Wood. Slightly longer, I think I actually have good gaping here in these clubs which I was concerned about. This could end up being a really good club off the tee. Still working on it though.

Now for the less good

  • 9 Iron - 105-110 Carry. This is actually pretty good, and was getting decent ball flight with this iron.
  • 8 Iron - 110-120 Carry. Inconsistent. I hit this a bunch during the lesson, and it was doing pretty well, but way off today.
  • 7 Iron - 120-130 Carry. The clubs carry a little longer, but I hit a lot more poor shots as I start moving up the irons. Very inconsistent ball striking. I'm not getting the whip in my swing that I was with my hybrids. I did hit some nice pure ones , but not enough.
  • 6 Iron - Was not pleasant today.

The Wedges on the other hand, the feel I had with them during my lesson this past weekend was really good. Was able to dial in shorter wedge shots much better with the Sand and Gap Wedge. The Pitching wedge felt good too.

I do think these Irons are a bit longer than the old Irons , but I wouldn't describe them as easier to hit. Probably just need to put in the work.

I really came to range today with the hope that I would be whipping my wrists a bit better, but the only thing that seemed to work was that feeling of whipping it from my back swing. Anyhow, that's the story. More work to put in.

item.title: Still haven't played new irons. A Sunday Bag? What would I play?
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I have 13 clubs in the bag now. Crazy. It's pretty heavy when walking with. I'm really looking forward to playing a course with the new clubs even though I'm having trouble with them. I haven't had a full range session with them, and hoping to get that in next week without the kids.

So my previous set was 10 clubs that I would carry, but I am considering a few courses where I should carry less.

I'm thinking of Needwood, and the Sterling Par 3 course, and what I would carry there. Needwood only has 2 par 4 holes, and I could get away with not carrying the driver. So for that course and the Sterling one without anything longer than 200 yards I would likely bring:

  • 5 Hy - my favorite club at the moment, and pretty consistent
  • 3 Hy or 3 Wood - Maybe the 3 Wood if playing needwood, but the 3 Hybrid at a par 3 course with no need to hit longer than 200.
  • 2 Irons, 2 Wedges = 4 clubs. Definitely the SW, and probably the PW. The 9 , and 7, or 8 and 6. The gaps are so incosistent between my clubs, that I really don't need to drag a ton of irons around.
  • Putter

So 7 clubs total to carry on these shorter courses rather than carrying my whole damn bag around. Possibly adding a chipper in there too. I have this Gap wedge at the moment, and don't think I will find much reason to use, unless I start seeing consistency in the irons, and I have good full swings that are dialed in with them.

Thinking also for carry on my favorite Northwest 9

  • Driver or Wood - Might even get away with just the 3 hybrid off the tee which could be fun . The wood isn't as long, but there is nothing really that requires a long drive at Northwest except for 2nd hole. Most greens should be reached with a wood or hybrid + another hybrid shot.
  • 3/5 Hy - If the 3 hybrid gets better I would bring that
  • 2 Irons and 2 Wedges - Again SW, PW, 9, 7.
  • Putter

So 8 clubs here. 9 if you drag along your chipper. Probably just use the hybrid instead of the chipper in those situations.

So I really want to buy either the Loma XL Sunday bag or Cobra one. Looks like the perfect bag for these shorter walking courses.

item.title: Fixing the slice with Rick Shiels
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Trying to fix my slice this week. Found this series to be pretty good, as it reinforces some of the things I've been working on with my coach. Being a good student I wanted to take some notes. The images were taken from the video below, so reference that for first hand information

(17) THE COMPLETE FIX YOUR SLICE GUIDE - YouTube

What causes a slice? This pictures below

The club face at contact aims further right than your swing path. Swing goes left, but club face is open to the right

The fixes - first get the ball going left:

  1. A Strong Grip - nothing new here, but for me just to keep checking it and making sure your grip is right. This alone typically helps me a little, but not enough to get things going left.
  2. Backswing - NO CUPPING of the left wrist
    • Halfway back (image below, see club face pointing slightly down towards the ground)
    • All the way back BOW THE LEFT WRIST - this is what Jim has been on me for months. I need to ingrain this one. I think this will have the most effect on the swing
  3. Follow Through -
    • Don't try to add loft through shot, counteract by getting the club face to rotate left (Image below)
    • Get Arms to cross over rotate around the body - cross the arms over. This also I've been working on with Jim. He refers to as releasing the club,

At this point, hopefully I'm hitting more left. Now Rick wants you to change the path.

  1. Ball position forward with slight body tilt - you've been doing this pretty well from the start
  2. Right shoulder back to get in to a closed stance (this is something else Jim has been on me for)
  3. hit inside of the golf ball by - turn the ball to 7 o'clock with your closed club face.

Strike location on the clubface

  • Striking in the heel will lead to more curvature right.
  • Toe will typically go left
  • Athletes foot powder to see your strike point

item.title: More practice, irons coming along
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I practiced at TopGolf again yesterday. Will be the last time I go there for some time, at least at that price. It's great, because you get carry and distance on real ball flight. This is great on a half price Tuesday, or an AM session, but not so great on a Thursday night.

At any rate, some numbers. Lets start with the wedges which I took poor notes on. These are carry distances, and really need to be sussed out with the shot scope in performance.

  • SW 50-70
  • GW - 70-90
  • PW - 90-110 - Probably a good 100 on average

Those are guestimates after my warmup. I did record a 110 on the PW. The height on these shots was good. Still pretty high arc for me.

Now getting down in the Irons, the 9 Iron was great, and everthing else was still kind of hard to hit.

  • 9i - 118-138 - 125 Average
  • 8i - 115-118
  • 7i - 127-135
  • 6i - 130-145

So, happy with the 9 iron. I would say a 125 average is probably about right for a clean hit. I think with a bit more time, I can target these averages. I expect

  • 9i 125
  • 8i 135
  • 7i 145
  • 6i 155

I feel pretty confident with the 9 after yesterday. Setup and practice swings are key with all this. The slower and more you paid attention to your setup and rehersal, the better things went. The 8 was terrible, but think I can get there. 6-7 were VERY incosistent.

Now the hybrids

  • 25 - 140 average - a bit of a surprise as this always felt a little longer, I think you can hope for a 150+ here. This club will roll out a bit more than the irons
  • 19 - 160 - average - same as above on the rollout. Felt good, but as the clubs got longer, the slice came in to play.

The woods and Driver I'm not really sure on the numbers, but longer than all the above, but less consistent is dispersion.

The best part about yesterday, were these checks

  • Backswing check to wrists bowed
  • Backswing check to more back than up
  • Light swing check brush ground and focus on release
  • Medium swing check brush ground with release
  • Quiet mind and go

When I hit the irons pure, man, it was great. Good solid striking. Still need to work it, but it was huge improvement on a couple weeks ago.

The Driver early started out straight. Adding swing speed threw things off, but I know the procedure, checkpoints and feelings. I finally feel like I am at a point where I understand what's going on, and adjust my practice to improve!

That above statement is huge. I have paused on lessons, as I know where I need to put in the work. On the flip side, the lessons were starting to be a bit of a chore to schedule. They were still super valuable, but I needed to spend some time fixing things myself now with a better understanding. I have the tools.

I know I need a lot of range time, but I have an itch to play, and will surely play this weekend.

Goals to head in to spring with some more consistent distance and dispersion. I'd love to see 3/4 or more of my shots being well hit within distance and dispersion

item.title: Just more practice
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I thought I might play today, but the unusual winter warmth made the courses just too crowded for me. I know it usually works out okay, but I didn't want to have the stranger experience today.

So then. Good practice with the irons. I am getting more comfortable with the new irons. It was bombs away on the down slope with the hybrids. Decent off the tee with the 3 wood. I mean, really really nice ball flights. The driver had some slice in, but worked it out to go left and some straight shots

So funny thing happened as I hit through a 110 balls.

  • Irons start straight, with a little bit more draw to slice as I get down to 6, and 7 iron. PW-8 was pretty high straight ball flight.
  • Hybrids hitting well, a few shots that draw a little, a few that fade a little. Good dispersion
  • Wood off the tee. Slice, but then start working it back to center and have some nice balls
  • Driver, slice, takes even more work to get it back to center and then going left.
  • Eventually Drivers, Woods and Hybrids are all pulling left! I'm not even sure it's a pull, but everything is going left. This about 60 balls in.
  • Towards the end, I head back to the irons, and guess what... they are all pulling left.

The instruction from the other day was working, However, I think I may have gone to swinging too much around the body. I think my wrist cock was better, but yea, this was some good stuff.

I thought about it awhile, and decide to stop there. I knew a round while it could have been fun, would have been me working to try to get back to middle, and could have been a disaster.

The other interesting thing with the irons was that I was getting really long with little effort and clean strikes. Felt really good like I was releasing well.

item.title: Got another putter...
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I threw another variable in the bag. On the strength of this review, and the price being relatively low, I thought it was worth a try to see how I do with a mallet vs blade. A good way to get into mallets and test out.

On the putting mat downstairs, good feel for the shorter putts. I can see how it does well on the shorter putts, and this has been my larger problem as of late. If I'm to be honest about it, anything that is longer than 2 feet is usually a struggle.

On average PGA Tour pros make 99% of 2-foot putts, 96% of 3-foot putts, 88% of 4-foot putts and 77% of 5-foot putts according to strokes gained pioneer, Mark Broadie. From 10 feet their one putt percentage is 40%, 23% from 15 feet, 15% from 20 feet, 7% from 30 feet, 4% from 40 feet, 3% from 50 feet and 2% from 60 feet.

Random search

3 to 5 feet is a huge problem for me. Granted, pros at only 77% a 5 foot. So what's reasonable for an amateur, who knows. Clearly I shouldn't be 77% , but if I make half I'm 2 putting more often than 3 putting.

You can play it 2 ways, how close can you get it from 10 feet on longer. Your not going to make many 10 foot and longer... maybe 10-20% at 10ft.

To state the goal pretty simply, 10ft and longer, get the ball within 5 feet for a >50% chance of making a 2 putt. Which putter are you better within 5ft (guessing mallet given struggles of late), which are you better at distance control?

If I am to be even more specific about where I struggle on putting, it's when the greens have nasty inclines in them. Small inclines I can deal with,

item.title: First Full 18 -- Scored a 99 at Laytonsville
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
First... allowed some mulligans, and took some extra shots, so this isn't a legit sub-100 score. Perhaps, the real score was more like a 105-110, but still, not bad for the first time through 18 holes.

I birdied my first Par 4! This was the highlight below.

A really good drive although a little left 207 yards, so decent distance for today (long drive today was 215, not my best). The 8 iron played just about where I wanted it to 114 yards on the green. Setup an 18 foot putt. Spent some time setting up and sunk it!

Putting had not been good. Greens were running super fast, and my putts were really rolling long, especially on the front 9. I hit a really good (single) on 11, think I was around that 10 foot plus range. I hit another good putt on the following hole on 15.

I had another couple birdie opportunities, one I really messed up on the prior hole (Hole 13). I hit a drive that smacked a tree, and decided to play. It was 144 yards just off the fairway. I then hit a beautiful 7i 138 yards, 18 feet left of the whole. The greens were evil though, and I missed long leaving a 4 footer down hill, which I missed to 3 putt. So the birdie opportunity became a bogey. Overall today, 7 bogeys, 9 doubles, one triple and the birdie.

Short game a putting was pretty bad today. Lack of practice no surprise. Happy with the end result though.

item.title: One good hole keeps you coming back for more
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I'm itching to get back out on the course! It's so funny how one good hole leads you to chasing that feeling. That birdie has me wanting to rush out this afternoon and see if I can repeat!

It wasn't just the birdie, but it was a few other great shots, that I can relive in shot scope (so glad that is working again)

  • Hole 4 - The 208 yard drive uphill. Didn't even swing for the fences and got distance and kept it on the fairway.
  • Hole 8 = The 215 yard drive (uphill again!), left you 60 yards to the hole
  • Hole 9 - The save from the trees after slicing the ball 175 yards, with a 135 yard hybrid just off the green.
  • Hole 11 - The 1 putt after playing out of the bunker. You hit over the bunker, and came back around and sunk a 10-15 footer.
  • Hole 13 - The 7i, 138 yard shot. Yea, I followed it with a 3 putt, but man that just felt so damn good to have the first birdie opportunity of the day and a perfect flight on your iron.
  • Hole 14 All 3 shots on the birdie went right. A drive 200+ , a 8i 114 yards right at the hole, and a perfect long putt .
  • Hole 15 - The 5 hybrid, 157 yards just off the green. The chipper to one putt was perfect. This hole, was actually played really well after slicing the driver some and using the GW to punch out to the fairway, otherwise this is a par.

Chasing that feeling, and the weather is so good today, I want to do 9 this afternoon if I can. Will be a stretch.

One other note... the new putter. I played with it on the green, and I had a lot of trouble with the stroke and feel with it. It will take time to see if it's usable, but as of now, not a good purchase. Gave me more confidence in my Ping putter, and made me want to use it even more. It's nice as a backup.

I can say after Saturday's gaming that my Ping is definitely better with my distance control. Perhaps you could develop that with the other putter, but that is only useful if it's really better for the shorter putts.

item.title: 2 More Scores
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So played twice over the weekend!

  1. Laytonsville, another 99! Front 9 felt really good, back 9 was rough. Walked it
  2. Northwest, a 50, at Par 34. Not as good, with some terrible putting.

So lets talk highlights from yesterday first:

  1. Par on hole 1. I think that's a first on this hole that I've probably played 7 or 8 times now. I hit an awesome ~200 yard drive in the fairway. I then hit a 7 iron 161 yards over the green (more on this later). Chipper on and a putt. Exactly how every hole should go.
  2. I hit the green on both par 3s (Holes 5 and 8).
  3. Driving with the wood was really consistent. 164 yards on 3 and 4. Probably should have stuck with it on 6 and 7.
  4. Hybrid and wood play for the most part was good. Distances were good. The H19 off the tee at 163 yards on 8 was a great shot, although would have liked about another 5-10 yards roll on it. The hybrid 19 although came off sliced, went 142 on hole 2. I also hit a decent 3w on 6 140 yards, although I'd like that to travel more in the 160+ range. IIT was a tough lie though.

Lowlights from yesterday:

  1. Hole 2 was a disaster after a great hole 1. I felt so confident with my driver, and then slice-a-rony happened. A good 2nd shot was followed up by some terrible short game. SW over, then LW over, and over again for an 8!
  2. Very incosistent with the irons. A 161 yard iron shot that I pured went over the green on that par. An 8 iron on the following hole went 78 and then 89 on slight miss hits. I do think my 9 iron on hole 5 going 111 is right where I would think, but then I came up short on 6 with an 83 yard strike, and repeated the same mistake on the next hole

Now on to Laytonville. Played this alone, and had massive fatigue from walking the first 9 holes. I think I need to drop some weight. I do get a lot more concentration when playing alone and my result tends to be a little better. Managing a kid makes the game harder. So highs and lows:

Highs:

  1. Par on hole 2. A pedestrian sliced drive 160 yards just off the green. A decent 8i 112 yards and a spectacular chipper shot that landed 2 ft from the hole!
  2. 9 boogies! I try for boogie golf and did pretty good with this Saturday.
  3. Short game. The wedges and the chipper served me well, and I played to just about my 20 handicap.
  4. Putting was good on the front 9
  5. The front 9 scored a 46. That is a best.
  6. Driving was shorter but more fairways (although this made little difference on the back 9)

Lows:

  1. Popped and sliced too many drives. I need to work on this further. My distance has receded over the last several weeks.
  2. Fatigue walking on the back 9. I need to lose some weight and get the cardio back. I use to be a runner, this should be easy
  3. Hip pain. My hip was on fire at the end of the round.
  4. Putting was crap on the back 9. Lots of missed opportunities. Distance control is the problem. I try to measure and feel, and it just is up in the air. I know I miss long more than I miss short, leaving me with a hard 2nd putt.
  5. The final hole was a nasty 8 triple bogey struggle. I just was done... even though the weather was beautiful and the sun was setting picturesque.
  6. Iron play was inconsistent again.

So a few themes coming out of the last few rounds:

  1. The very short game with the chipper is actually pretty good, except your distance control like the putter leaves you 3 putting more than you would like. The wedges from mid range are decent too, but any other type of wedge shot is a struggle
  2. Irons, you never know what your going to get distance wise. Lack of consistency. Working on some tempo and thoughts might improve this. Hard to play the game well when a 7iron might go 170 yards or 90 yards.
  3. Putting... distance control needs work. Reading greens needs work. Short putts need work. It comes together at times, but I think the distance control at this point will pay the biggest dividends
  4. Driver. The shot scope misses a lot of my messes! It doesn't count all those that I shank off. The pop ups which I sometimes play, and the distance seeming to drop from a couple months back. I went from a 226 performance average to 200 average since I got the new driver. Might be the hip fatigue, but likely something in my game. I'd set a reasonable goal of about a 230-250 drive by the end of the year.
  5. Hybrids and Woods actually play decent. Decent mid range but still lacks consistency.
  6. Fatigue plays a role. Drop weight, gain cardio. This will improve everything.

item.title: I love the shot scope... when it works. Goals for March
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Just taking a look at the last few rounds from the shot scope. That thing is gold when it works properly. Fingers crossed it stays in sync. Last round, I think I only had one correction.

I really like how they gamify goals in the medals section. A few medals I've gotten:

  • Birdie
  • Break 100
  • Break 50 Front
  • Break 50 Back
  • 200 Yard Tee Shot
  • 4 FIR in a round
  • 2 GIR
  • 20% Green Success
  • 36 Putts

To go after next:

  • Break 95
  • Break 45 on Front or Back
  • 225, 250, and 275 Yard Tee Shot -
  • 6 FIR+
  • 30% Green Success
  • 32 Putts or Better

I can't include some of the distance to hole, distance to putt. Those numbers just seem a little off, or at the very least easy to fake on the shot scope. Just including the number of putts per round is pretty good.

Biggest disappointment right now is my driving distance falling off a cliff. After hitting that 275 yard drive, and then a 246 in freezing cold weather (that one was measured), my performance has gone to crap! As you can see below, the P-average is just dropping. I get the average being on the low end, but that average going down almost 50 yards! WTF... I mean even the 205-215 P-average would feel about right. What I'm doing wrong, who knows.

Then of course all the other problems... Iron consistency, putting, short game, etc. I really like the decisions I'm making with the chipper right now, and love that club. I made 2 mistake with it over 27 holes this weekend when I came up short on a shot and didn't get on the green, and another when I over shot it on a down slope... tough greens.

item.title: Taking a short break
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I'm trying not to swing for a week or two to see if I can get my hip to recover. That includes swinging in basement working on things. This is going to be tough with 80 degree weather.

I think if I can get this hip back to normal, I can actually get more practice in more regularly. As it stands right now, if I go to the range, I'm usually in pain for a day or two afterwards. I need to get the inflammation down, and then get back to it slowly.

item.title: Hip recovery -- still on break
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Hip is recovering. I took 2 days worth of NSAIDs which didn't seem to do much. I've not been doing any stretching of the hip over the last several days. I do a bit of mobility, moving it in to the position where things tighten up, but keep that to a minimum. The more I move it seems to loosen up to a point, and then goes back to painful again. No rolling or massage either. No weight lifting with lower body, and no incline walks as well.

I wrapped it with some of that spongy sports wrap for compression last night. That might been helping. It's hard to get compression in the right spot as the pain is about 3 inches below where the hip joint points out in the front. I also have been doing heat, seems to help a little. Sitting seems to not help.

As it gets better, I will try adding in each piece of the puzzle. This has basically been an issue since December and continued to get worse. It will be nice to feel like you can swing hard again without hurting this.

In the meantime, I've been doing a bit of putting on the matt, and that's about it. I think I'm pretty much decided that I am not a mallet putter guy. I like the mallet putter that I bought, but I can't seem to get use to the feel of it. I switch back and forth between my blade and mallet, and the blade seems to fit my stroke better, and I can feel things better. Still experimenting, so I can't say 100% settled, but I like that I can play with both now.

Been watching videos, Danny Maude now mostly. His take is less technical, but he seems to be a popular one for a lot of golfers. I like it so far, but can't say I've been able to really try much of his stuff yet. I do find you can find certain things that get repeated by all the golf pros out there (and I should do some study on that).

Found this one on wrist hinge today, and seems to be

(25) PROPER WRIST HINGE IN GOLF BACKSWING - YouTube

item.title: Putting, hip recovery, and maybe a simulator?
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I continue to rest the hip. I've done a bit of indoor swinging of the clubs, but not much. I'd really like to have zero pain in the hip while stretching to know I'm good to resume. Then take a lot of care in warming up the muscles before hitting. I may need a bit more time with massage, and I continue to do some medial glute work. Also cutting lifts on the lower body for at least another week. Hopefully all this will lead to a good return.

So with that said, I'll I've done is putting on the putting matt. What I've learned... you got your putter right with the Ping Sigma 2. That thing is great, and just works in my hands. I think as long as I continue to groove it when I'm not playing it will serve me well out on the course.

So of course with this obsession I'm already looking at a simulator to practice at home. I have this issue though that ceilings are too low in the basement. They are almost good on the main floor, but not quite there for a driver. In the garage I get up towards 9 feet+ and I seem to be able to follow all the way through with the driver. Garage is the best for room. Basement is best for setup tear down.

I would love to turn our basement guest room into a sim, but there are some limitations there. I think I could get away with irons , but not anything longer than that. It would cut cost too, but I think the 6-12 inches extra I get in the garage makes a big difference in not pulling swings.

The garage is good because of height, but would require movement of one of the door openers to the back (500 bucks - day job). Then would need to probably get a drop down screen. I found one, but it's 2200 for the screen, plus another 2K for a skytrack (because you'll need to set it up on the side to have enough room in either situation). Total cost is around 6K with getting proper matts. I could potentially just invest in a matt and screen for practice and see how I like that. That would still require about 600-700 in matts, and another 400 for the golf return. Still need 500 for the garage door fix thing and probably some lighting work.

So ballpark. 1500 for practice, 5500 for a full simulator. At least though with the practice if you spend well on that matts then you could reuse that.

Just a bit of a dream right now... but still have some money to spend.

item.title: Practice area coming along, and hip recovery
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I ended up going the inexpensive route to build up my garage practice bay. It actually turned out quite good.

  • 4 Anokey golf nets @40 dollars each. I have 2 for side netting, and 2 in front, with one of them coming over for some ceiling protection. 160 dollars
  • Hardware. Bought some 15 foot cable from Harbor freight for about 12 bucks, and some additional hardware than ran about 25 dollars including a bunch of carabiners, hooks and turnbuckles. All in total, lets round up to 50 bucks in hardware.

So that is 210 for the netting enclosure, and it's pretty big, and seems pretty safe with double netting in the area hit the most. Compare that to some of the 600-800 dollar hitting nets, and I feel pretty good about this.

Flooring

  • Cheap 25 dollar turf rug from home depot in the front.
  • 210 dollar grade B mat
  • 130 dollar insert from bullseye.

Flooring total so far... 365. Add another 210 for the netting, and we are 575 for a fully functioning garage practice bay.

Now the sim part, which has not been purchased yet. I plan to purchase the MLM 2 Pro as soon as I can get my hands on one. That's 700. Add another 300 dollars for Awesome golf, and that's 1000 more. I have computers and extra monitors lying around so that cost will be covered... possibly a bit more for a few more extras. I can justify a 1500 dollar purchase as about 10 to 15 trips to top golf. I just love that I can work on my game multiple times a week without having to drive to the range anymore. This will hopefully pay dividends.

My hip on the other hand... I hit a few shots today, and I'm not sure if that was the issue, but my hip started immediately hurting... danger danger danger

item.title: Garmin R10 it is
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
After much debate, I realized I would be waiting for the MLM Pro 2 for several months, and I am ready to get started now. So I went over to Dick's and bought the R10. 550 dollars.

After going through a bunch of reviews, for the money it just seemed to be a great deal, and probably similar accuracy to the Rapsodo (although I expect Rapsodo to do a bit better given early reviews). I also have a bit of brand loyalty to Garmin as they've put out good products I've used in the past. Running metrics... Garmin is the best. Workout watch, I've been using a garmin for about 7 years now.

So lets go through the setup now and costs associated. I haven't actually put much of this in to practice yet. I have yet to purchase the GSPro or Awesome Golf licenses yet. So current total spent is 1232, with another 600 coming for software.

  • Hitting Bay Total Cost: 637
    • Aoneky nets. Got 4 10x10 nets, 2 for main area to ceiling, partially doubled upped to protect main hitting area. $160
    • Various Hardware including turnbuckles, hooks, security cable to suspend nets from. Combo between Harbor Freight and Home Depot. A cheap 25 dollar astro like turf carpet. $100
    • Rawhide Mat Grade B - Seemed best bang for the buck for a basic mat. I plan to cut, and use with a hitting strip. $205
    • Bullseye hitting strip - 12x24. $130
    • Shag Tube and Rubber Tees $37
  • Simulator Hardware -$595
    • Garmin R10 - $550
    • Level and Protector -$45
  • Software - 600
    • Awesome Golf $350
    • GSPro $250
  • Electronics
    • Old work Surface Book 2 laptop with NVIDIA graphics card $0
    • Old TV Or budget new monitor 300 dollars

I have an old 50 inch plasma, but the thing weighs a ton, and is super thick. Would rather just shell out a few more dollars for a thin 4K display.

So if I buy the TV, I'm in about 2100 dollars. Feel pretty good about that as the kids were into it right away before even putting Awesome Golf on the screen.

Now if I could just get my hip back to normal so I could play every day and start improving.

item.title: Initial Garmin R10 impressions
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
In no particular order:

  • Distance seems to be pretty accurate. Maybe even a little long on the irons and hybrids so far.
  • Direction is good , but wonder if I am still slicing particularly on the longer clubs. Apparently lack of side spin matters in the Garmin, but perhaps if I continue to pay attention to face path stats I can get a better sense of what will happen vs what it tells me.
  • Missed shots are rare, but they do happen, I'd say maybe 2%-4%, and it's mostly just overall bad shots.
  • Bluetooth issue showed up once over this first week, when my son brought out his laptop and had it too close to the unit and was having trouble holding connection.
  • I dislike having to use the phone to the link to Awesome Golf. Apparently GS Pro can work with a direct connection, but for the kids for now it will be awesome golf
  • Awesome golf is pretty much what you would want in a product. If it were less than 200 dollars it would be a no brainer, but it's pricey for what you get (4 courses a range, a few kids games and a few other features). The thing is, it just works and isn't buggy so I will pay for the license.
  • I hate that my garage rails are in the way, and will end up spending at least what I spent on the sim setup to raise the rails.
  • Makes me want to play golf outside less now. Not great side effect. I do get a chance to play more without having to drive though.

On the accuracy front. It seems to be great for someone at my level. I really get punished on my poor shots, and I like that. I'll take the 5/25 degree hybrid as an example. Average on course for that club is a 145, with a performance average of 124. A little shorter on average on the Garmin at 135, but it fits with my inconsistency.

The long shots... I've hit a 157 with that club on course. During that test I hit a 161, and earlier I had the Garmin read a 188 on that club. I smashed it, and while 188 is probably not playable distance for me, a 160ish is.

Another example... hitting a lot of 8 iron. Lets say that 8 iron is a 115 club for me. I'm getting the same numbers on the Garmin average with a 116 average (this includes bad shots), with a 131 long during test (and 144 long overall).

So I think I am starting to get a sense of distance in these clubs. The distance spreads are atrocious though. For the 5 hybrid, I hit two 161 yards, and then a 118, 108,121, and 138. I can't hold it now, but I can imagine at some point those numbers will creep to something consistent.

8 Iron spreads were better, but still could go 10+/- either wayt.

Down to the pitching wedge, the last one tested, I was the same sort of experience. Occasional great strike, mostly bad to average. High of 133 yards, down to low of 73 yards. Hard to play when your ball striking is inconsistent.

Really looking forward to hitting a real range and getting out sometime soon to play a real course. I imagine my short game will be trash, but hopefully will start striking the ball better in the next few weeks...

item.title: Golf Sim updates
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Loving the golf sim. Stands up and tears down quick. Seems to give accurate distance numbers. Punishes my poor shots, and rewards my good shots. Gets me practicing almost daily.

The dislikes. Indoor Swing Syndrome, exacerbated by garage rails and openers. The tendency to go for distance over clean striking. Not being able to swing driver (yet). The gaps in the net. Skyed shots

So I have a list of projects for the sim, in what I think is the right order

  • Extend top net another 2 feet. I have had some skied shots with both the driver on mishits and wedges. I think taking the top net out another 2 feet can solve this.
  • Closing the gaps. I'm still having issues with gaps in the nets and a few balls slipping through particularly on the bottom left now More clips doesn't necessarily do it.
  • Replacing the right side hook with a hook and turnbuckle. This is just lazy.
  • Build out a place to store the mat on the side wall. Easy sto-a-way.
  • Garage track remediation. Finding from just left of middle to stand, keeps the swing way under the track. This is okay, but doesn't help my son. Removing my wife's side garage door opener would let me swing through a bit more. I can also cut about 12 inches off tracks and set rails back a little further which might help.
  • Mount TV . No point in mounting or buying a TV until this is done. Laptop is annoying because I can't really see it from the distance I'm at.
  • Chalk lines for placement, to keep things consistent once you have a decent setup.
  • Leveling of mat so it's not so uphill.

Long term...

  • Perhaps eventually a projector and ability to hang a screen over the net. Depends on how much use I'm getting and if the above actually remediates the indoor swinging thing.
  • Perhaps different mechanisms for hanging the nets on a pulley system perhaps. Would be fun to see if you could get that to work.

item.title: Sim updates - Swinging easy
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
The other day I put together my list of things to do

  • Extend top net another 2 feet. I have had some skyed shots with both the driver on mishits and wedges. I think taking the top net out another 2 feet can solve this.
    • Done - Fixed the top part. I had several errant balls that were caught by the raised net yesterday. I redid the whole netting structure, and was happy with it.
  • Closing the gaps. I’m still having issues with gaps in the nets and a few balls slipping through particularly on the bottom left now More clips doesn’t necessarily do it.
    • Mostly done - Fixed the gaps , but still a few spots of concern. No issues yesterday
  • Replacing the right side hook with a hook and turnbuckle. This is just lazy.
    • Done - fixed but at the expense of losing a bit of slack with the turnbuckles. It works well though.
  • Build out a place to store the mat on the side wall. Easy sto-a-way.
    • Still thinking about this one. Can't seem to figure out the ideal way of doing this. I'm ready to start parking my car again in the garage and the setup supports it , except for the mat at the moment. Hooks in to the mat seem wasteful, need some sort of drop in type thing. actually think there is a good space, just need to move some garage things around again.
  • Garage track remediation. Finding from just left of middle to stand, keeps the swing way under the track. This is okay, but doesn’t help my son. Removing my wife’s side garage door opener would let me swing through a bit more. I can also cut about 12 inches off tracks and set rails back a little further which might help.
    • Quote incoming. The initially 5K to basically redo the entire garage is not working for me. Got another guy out here yesterday to quote just one replacement on one side. I think when all is said and done it should hopefully be about 1200 dollars including cutting some of the garage track excess.
  • Mount TV . No point in mounting or buying a TV until this is done. Laptop is annoying because I can’t really see it from the distance I’m at.
    • Also getting closer... gonna wait for garage to be complete first.
  • Chalk lines for placement, to keep things consistent once you have a decent setup.
    • Getting closer, this appears to be dead center middle of the garage, nets are slightly right biased.
  • Leveling of mat so it’s not so uphill.
    • Thinking through all sorts of ideas on this one, nothing sticking yet, but likely just cardboard folded right.


So a couple of areas of concern with my swing. I've been really hitting the ball with as much power as I can. Instead yesterday I tried to do just easy swinging, and concentrating on power sort of later. Basically just really trying to stay loose. I can't seem to find it right.

The really concerning part was now I'm coming over the top according to the club path. The day before I was reading all negative club face path , and yesterday it was all positive. Possible setup issues with the Garmin is likely.

item.title: Sim update and Swing updates
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
What's left to do:

  • Purchase and mount a TV
  • Method of hanging mat

What was done in the last week

  • Garage remediation - had them raise the rails slightly, and added one jack lift. I can now swing through better, but it's still not perfect. My swing has changed some and find longer clubs hitting the ceiling on the follow through (not on the back swing)
  • Extend the net. This is a continual process. I still think I have one more go around with this.
  • Purchased GSPro - it is as good as advertised, and I haven't even played any courses on it yet just a few holes in practice mode.

So the good... I can swing my irons fully without worrying about hitting anything as I come through. Hybrids are good too... but I may be stuck playing par-3s. I can't imagine I'll ever really be able to hit driver fully, and I cut the 3w a bit short. The more I follow through lately and come up, the more danger I am in hitting the ceiling. This is due to some swing changes.

So now for the terrible swing updates. I've started changing things up quite a bit, and I'm not sure it's been for the better. I am more doing a 3/4 swing and just trying to be consistent with my ball striking.

I am trying, without much success yet, to focus on using my body to square the club. I am trying to not muscle it. This is leading to the ball not going as far, but this needs to happen to get where I want to be. An easy swing with the body rotation.

Striking has been a bit better, but it degrades over a session. I need more practice and more breaks. Fitness and weight have become an issue. And the lingering issue with my hip.

item.title: Still waiting for the hip to get better
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
It's taking way longer than expected for the hip to recover. It's killing me with this perfect blustery 60 degree weather that I can't get out there. I've got this great garage setup to practice too, and I can barely use it. Its been almost 2 weeks since I've hit a ball. Stretch, roll , etc. It gets better and worse over and over. Walking seems to be the biggest irritant. I always feel like I need to roll in to it and beat the hell out of it, but it seems to only hurt for days after that. I do 'light' stretching. It still stays tight and painful. I wrap it, seems to help, but temporary relief. Sometimes feels like I could play with it wrapped.

I can only imagine what things will look like once I've gotten it right. Can't wait to swing free, especially pain free.

item.title: Wasted spring, hip update
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I've wasted this spring with this hip injury. We've had some of the best golf weather thinkable, and the last time I played was in February. What a disappointment. I remember that last 18 and being able to barely walk on the 18th. Can't let that happen again, need to keep the body mobile and healthy.

So the hip is slowly recovering. It's really hard to figure out what is working and what isn't. Alot of 2 steps forward one step back type stuff. I continue to do mobility work. No heavy leg work, mostly single leg stability type stuff. This morning it feels pretty good, but who knows where I end up at the end of the day. It's a tricky balance I've been playing.

Once I am able to get back to it, I've got the garage setup and will put in the work. Really will work on cleaning up the swing once I can move freely through the hip again. Work on the swing, and then a few driving range + short game practice days and then back to the course with as many holes as possible with late tee times. I think I can still get myself averaging in the 90s this year. Especially if you can make the garage work a regular scheduled thing.

item.title: Still no golf
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded: I am still recovering, both hip and elbow. I am so frustrated, but I have to really wait. I did a few balls at TopGolf with family. Of course I wanted to hit it far, and this wasn't good for my hip. Gotta recover before you can rip it again.

item.title: Monthly check-in of no golf
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
We are now well into 4 months of zero golf. I have had hip improvements, but I still don't trust that a day out on links sets me back to square one where I was 4 months ago.

At this point, I'm waiting till I have not even a twinge of pain. I have had some really good days where it felt like I could have, but then it comes back a bit. No straight line recoveries. The good news is most of my elbow pain is gone now. With the exception of my right quad, my body feels pretty good.

I am keeping my fingers crossed I'm between 2-4 weeks away from being close to 100%!

item.title: It's August... still no golf, still nasty hips
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I thought things would be good by now. Definitely have improvement, but still have issues with my right hip. The pain is different

I've been watching this guy, and gotten some good tips when I get back to things. Allowing me to get fundamentals first. Weight forward, arms straight, don't mess with your wrists.

(1) The Golf Swing Lesson You Always Needed BUT NEVER HAD (You Missed This!) - YouTube

Hoping to take my return to golf with a chance of getting back to some real basics and move forward from there.

item.title: I miss golf
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
My hip is still messed up. I've tried a bunch of different things and nothing seems to stick. It gets better, than worse, better than worse. I really miss being out there golfing. I haven't been on course 7 months now. I've hit balls a few times and paid the price with additional hip pain the next day.

I started a new workout protocol that is no longer focused on the rehab. We'll see how it goes, and maybe ignoring it for awhile it will just get better...

Regards,

One Frustrated Golfer

item.title: My monthly ode to missing golf
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I officially have missed the entire 2023 'season' of playing golf. My last round back in February of this year.

Some mild progress on the hip, but I still think the swinging is a bad idea at this point. I'm keeping on some rehab exercises, and hope that sometime this winter I can at least swing in the garage and start getting ready for a 2024 season.

At this point, just want to get back to swinging well, and hopefully scoring in the 90s when I'm able to get back out.

item.title: Hit golf balls today
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
For the first time in many months, I hit golf balls again. I did a hip warmup before leaving, and everything is feeling okay so far (except for an ankle injury I'm dealing with). 

It kind of started as expected, I couldn't even make contact with the ball. Then, it started coming back with the 9 iron. We were at TopGolf bottom floor, so I can believe my yardage. Consistent yardage with the 9 about 130 yards carry, great ball flight! 

Then playing the hybrids saw some great carry crushing the ball, with some rollout to the back fence line --- 200 yards. I still had it. Inconsistent, not ready to play, but I can still smack it. I couldn't hit the driver worth crap, but it's not a good place to practice there as you can't tee it up to proper height. 2 weeks consistent practice and I think I could try 9 holes. A little putter work in the basement, and your good to go. 

If the hips hold, I think I might just be weeks away from playing again! I am apprehensive, I'm on anti-inflammatories for the aforementioned ankle injury, but could this be the return...

One thing of note... I hit it well when I wasn't forcing things. So close...

item.title: A negative hip test
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded: This will be quick. My hip felt great when I was hitting. The last 2 days have been pure hell as I've been in near constant pain. So there we are... back to the drawing board.

item.title: We played!
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
15 Months and 13 days since the last time on course. Took the kids to Needwood for a fun 9. Hit a few good shots, and lots of terrible ones. It was an experience. I know I'm going to have to go slow if I want to keep playing, so maybe once a week with some swings in between. Right now the hip is fine (only 2 driver swings), but we'll see tomorrow. It's less swings than going to top golf or the range.

Highlight of the day was the 2nd hole, a really easy Par 3 , that I could have birdied. I hit within 5 feet, but it's been so long since I've putted I couldn't sink it.

Actually, the big highlight of the day was my son sinking a 20 footer on the 6th hole.

Just a few observations

  • Layoff, led to lots of misses, poor contact, poor
  • Irons felt pretty good despite this. A few really good iron shots.
  • Hybrid was all over the place, but okay.
  • +18 over 9 holes --- double bogey golf
  • One par, 2 bogeys, and everything else bad. Didn't include the penalties ... probably lost 6 balls.

I missed it. Would love to play more, but again going to take it slow. Next up will be a little practice, slowing things down and then Northwest. All dependent on the hip does over the next week.

item.title: I'm slicing again
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I'm back, but at the range and slice was a little worse than I left it a year ago. I had about a month of hitting the driver pretty straight in winter 22 but now it's back. So many anti-slice options out there, gotta go back and watch the danny maude stuff to. I think his loop thing is worth trying

Hank Haney Fixes A High Handicapper's Slice LIVE (youtube.com)

  • Strong grip
  • Reverse Loop and back turn
  • Reverse loop turned 45 degrees from target to
  • Turn hands down earlier (this might be enough for you)

Other than slicing, the big thing is : STOP TRYING TO KILL THE BALL. Let the club and momentum do the work and things tend to do better. You actually hit most of the clubs minus the driver pretty decent.

item.title: Playing again - River Marsh
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Not a lot, but I am playing again. While on vacation I took the boys to play at River Marsh. We got 12 holes in. I scored a 67 over 12, 16 over par. It even says I birdied a hole (which I don't recall, I do recall par'ing a couple holes).

I now go out and just have fun. I don't keep a scorecard, but just play the holes and let the watch keep semi-track of what I'm doing. I hit more penalties in a round like this. Without the penalties, I hit in the mid 90s, with them, I'm hitting in the 100s. Reduce the penalties.

Interesting enough... I had more issues with the irons/hybrids than the driver this last go. Was basically hitting some okay drives (slicing, yes, but not as bad). I was having trouble judging the iron shots.

Irons were either too long or too short. I can recall a shot I hit perfectly, right over the hole and the green. It was a 9 iron on hole 9. 100 yards to hole, I thought perfect, 9 iron should be right. I make great contact it goes 130+ in to the rough. So frustrating.

Also hit some great drives that just sliced a bit and were lost in the rough. Fortunately had some wide fairways this go around and it wasn't too bad. Needwood is tough because the driver fairways are narrow.

I'd love to see my driver get back up to speed. 227 P-Avg, vs 194 P-Avg this year. I blame it on slice entirely.

Putting can improve dramatically with just a bit of putting on the mat, and some time at the range on the putting green. Iron game needs work on real grass.

item.title: If you were to play with less clubs, which would you leave at home?
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So thinking about what I'm carrying right now and what would likely be enough. Right now you are carrying -- 4 Irons, 3 wedges, 2 hybrids, 1 wood, 1 driver, a putter and a chipper. That's 13 clubs, and I think I could probably get away with between 6-8 on a normal day.

So easy enough on the irons... you don't need 6 thru 9. You could just bring 9 and 7. 2 Clubs down.

Wedges - you could take that down to 1 or 2. So 1-2 clubs down. I'd say you could probably just bring your Gap wedge and that would do it, or conversely, bring the sand wedge and the pitch wedge.

Hybrids and Woods - So you can probably get away with just the one hybrid. But which. The wood is always tough to hit, but you do use it off the tee when driver not going well. I feel like I hit the shorter hybrid better than the longer, so I could go with either. Down 2 clubs

Must brings -- Driver, even when your not hitting it well you still should be teeing off par 4s and 5s.

Putter for obvious reasons. The chipper is a nice to have, and I tend to use it several times just off the green. I could probably get away with using the hybrid the same way.

So lets total it up , minimum 6 clubs

  • 2 Irons
  • 1 Wedge
  • 1 Hybrid
  • 1 Driver
  • 1 Putter

So the adds in order you would add it:

  • I'd say add chipper on a normal day for 7.
  • Next I might switch to PW and sand, so 8 for that. This is probably where I would most likely play. 8 clubs!
  • Next is a toss up depending on course, to 9 or 10:
    • The Gap wedge - it plays a role when it matters, when your near the hole.
    • Add the 8 iron. You don't need a 6, as the hybrid pretty much covers that distance
    • Add the wood or longer hybrid. Granted this club seems to make the least difference at the moment, so you pro

The only real decision to make here is on the hybrid. Just going by stats -- the H25 (shorter hybrid, plays only 4 yards shorter, but averages longer in real play. Not alot of data on this, but that is more like a 5 iron, and has most flexibility.

The irons 9-7 are almost interchangeable with the data. The long hits do tell something. 111 on the 9i, and 161 on the 7i. Performance average has those gapped at 25 yard - 105 to 130. PW to SW would be 103 to 63, which is a 40 yard gap. So now, I think I would take a third wedge to try to fill that gap.

An example on a 400 yard, par 4 -- Drive 190, leaves you 210 to whole. You hit a good hybrid for 150, which leaves you a wedge away... wedges matter. So I play 9 clubs, all wedges.

item.title: Northwest 9 - First Eval in a long time
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So a few things first. I can't play a ton, it takes the hip still several days to recover depending on how much I hit driver. But I can play, and I don't play half bad when I do.

My driver is still slice town, but everything else is decent enough to play fun rounds.

So this isn't exact. I did not count my penalties/mulligans, so I think this is 2-4 strokes higher. But still had some decent holes. The hole 3 and hole 5 pars are good. I don't recall whether 3 was a real par or not. I think it might have been, as I hit to the right side of the green and then two putted...

Hole 1 - Can't recall if I dropped or not (leaning not, but the tee shot was terribly sliced with the hybrid. A fat 7i, and then a good gap wedge shot of 72 yards got me on, but then a 3 putt (which I thought was 2). I thought this was Bogey, but lets say double.

Hole 2: Another sliced drive, didn't hit it hard, and only went 159. Surprised it was found. Hybrid shot was poor 128 yards, but moved things. Gap wedge lined drive for 88 yards, not a good metric there, as when I hit it right it pops up and lands softly. This one rolled over the green, then used my chipper to get on for a 2 putt. Happy to 2 putt, to go double bogey here.

Hole 3: Decided to tee off with the hybrid 19 since the creek was down and the driver sucked on the last hole. Hit a nice 156 yard shot downhill to avoid creek. Probably a little too much loft off the tee, but it was straightish. Now the next shot, I pulled an 8 Iron and hit it uphill 129 yd. This is a great shot, 2nd best of the day. I think I was surprised to see it landed green right side and I was able to 2 putt for a PAR!

Hole 4: Hybrid 19 flew well last time, why not do the same here... 150 yards again downhill off the tee. Avoiding the creek. A little left. This is where the decision was a bit ugh. I took a 7 iron, and hit a decent shot, but didn't have the cleanliness or power of the previous 8i shot, and it ended up 10 yards short of the green, where I was hoping to at least match the previous 8 iron shot. This is where it got pretty disappointing where I went from par to triple bogey. I chipped over the green, then chipped on poorly, then 3 putted. Ugliest hole of the day, despite a decent approach.

Hole 5: Gap wedge 90 yards off the tee, should have gone PW, but was nervous about hitting over the green. Hit a great 2 putt! Messed up shotscope not registering the 2nd putt as a really short one screwing with my stats

Hole 6: I hate this hole, but was feeling pretty good. I decided to give the driver a shot, and to attempt to clear the 160 yard creek. I cleared the creek, caught a great wind and the thing just flew! If i see the stat sheet it says 280. I found a ball on the green. It might have been my ball, as I was swapping out a few from my pocket all day, but I probably really didn't hit it 280... maybe 220-230, but we didn't see the ball in the tress. From their I play a poor short game with a 3 putt.

Hole 7: I Mulligan'd the first ball, but retrieved it, hit a second off the tee nicely with the H19. 167 a little right. Sand Wedge on (I muffed one, so I really didn't par this hole, and I took a mulligan). Sandwedge 45 yards and two putt. So really double bogey, but otherwise when you hit right, it went pretty well.

Hole 8: h25 Off Tee. IT went 126 yards. So frustrating as this really is a 150 yard club. The H19 would have been too long if hit cleanly. A bad sand wedge shot, followed by a good one led to a 2 putt and double.

Hole 9: Best shot of the day. Terrible driver! Sliced right popped up, 115 yards. I said screw it and decided to play it. Stepped up with H19 which I had been hitting well, hoping to advance just off the green. I hit my shot of the day a 205 yard that carried at least 180 of that. It rolled nicely on to the top of the green. Left a really long first putt, which left me 8 ft, a miss on 8 and then tap in. Bogey, but a good recovery.

This was a lot of fun. My son hit some good shots too, which makes it all the better.

I'm not going to bother on too much strokes gained analysis. Putting numbers are way off for this (it thinks I made some long putts, which I didn't). Short game and approaches are the weak areas and need the practice. Driving with hybrids is decent enough, driving with the driver is still a mess.

If I could practice daily I would and I think I could get sorted, but between work, working out and injuries, I relegated to at most 2 times a week.

item.title: A horrid 7 holes
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
They weren't all bad, but mostly bad. First time playing Crossvines (aka Poolesville).

First the good:

  • Par on a Par 5 --- Granted, playing forward tees with kids, a 390 yard. Saved a terrible drive (142 yd slice), with a 210 yard Hybrid shot and a nice sand wedge on to the green. Long birdie putt missed, but was able to 2 putt for par. Last hole of the day and it was good.
  • The drive on 6 @ 175 yards actually stayed straight (felt like I hit it much further than that)
  • A 160 yard 7 iron shot that stayed on the green. However I three putted, which ruined this hole for boogie.
  • More 2 putts than 3 putts...

The bad:

  • Hole 2 , a 9! I haven't had that much crap in a long time. Poor drive, 119 yards, a missed H19 shot (83 yards), followed up by a well hit one that ended up right (178 yards), then Gap wedge short to the bunker, 2 shots out of the bunker and then a 3 putt!
  • a 9 iron 163 yard shot that went over the green on 6 (I think it bounced over and down an embankment.
  • Lots of miss hits. Irons going longer than expected. Hybrid misses followed by good shots. Tough short game (wedge 50 yard in ) play.

Finding some reliability with my hybrid 19. Driver is problematic still. Putting is blah, and the irons are unpredictable. 163 yard 9 iron, and a 79 yard nine iron. A 160 yard 7 iron that probably my shot of the day. Wedge practice is needed. Those distances were rough.

item.title: No opportunity to practice
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I've been so excited to get back at the golf, but have had zero opportunity to practice of late. I have not set up the mat in the garage either. That would probably do some good for 'contact', but I haven't felt like recreating the whole setup.

Also, it does take a couple days for my hip to feel right after hitting balls... especially driver. I think most of the hip issues are coming from driver. Anyhow... might bring clubs along and stop at the range on the way home tomorrow

item.title: Northwest 9 - 50
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I counted a few penalties this time. So 2 good holes, one okay, and 6 not so good holes.

Lets start with the good and okay:

  • Hole 8 was your best hole today. I hit what I'll describe as an okay 7 iron. 7i 135 seems a little hsort for me, but it was raining, and I hadn't been really clean on the irons today. So good decision, I'm about 8-10 feet from the hole. Birdie chance just missed, easy tap in for par
  • Hole 4 - hybrid off the tee, that was hit well, but didn't get the distance I expected 157. Really nice 8 iron across the creek, just missed the green by about 2 yards. Chipper to mid green and 5 foot par putt.
  • Hole 7 was an okay one. I do wonder sometimes if the yardages are right. Shotscope says 131. Sandwedge on and then a 3 putt.
  • I'll mention driving the ball 225 with a pretty significant slice on the final hole (the only hole I brought the driver out for.

The bad:

  • Hole 1 - Bad tee shot, bad iron shot, good Gap Wedge. Good putting
  • Hole 2 - Hybrid 19 okay off tee, but went a little to far right. A bit of a mess getting it on the green with a mix hybrid and wedges ... A bad 3 putt
  • Hole 3 - This was actually a decent hole if you throw out the penalty . I hit a bad 9 iron, take that away , and the next shot was a good 9 iron 100 yards landing softly uphill. on the green with a 2 putt.
  • Hole 5 - A disaster... I forgot some clubs on the prior hole and had to run back... I choose poorly with the gap wedge, and then hit it poorly leaving the ball short. My chip on missed pretty pretty bad, and then putting was shat
  • Hole 6 - Always a mess... I played it really great from the start, hitting a beautiful H25 180yds. Then I hit a perfect H25 for the approach with 150 yards uphill to the hole... but I hit a tree, doh.
  • Forced to go 8i at 100 yards out, and then I come up just short... your still okay, but then it took 4 more shots in the short game to get it in ... there again bad short game
  • Hole 9 - A drive that was actually playable . Punch out with PW is actually good, but then the sand wedge flies over, and the sandwedge back on is no good, and then a 3 putt. Short game again.

So much to work on. 150 yards in seems to struggle a lot. Hybrid play is decent enough, but not consistent. Still need to figure out my driver issues. Then around the green... needs a lot of practice... Chipping and putting.

Hitting the ball kind of funny too, too many swing things going on for consistency.

item.title: Almost 9 Laytonsville
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Got out there again. A few observations before the score

  • Score is really a few strokes higher than this. I didn't count a couple mulligans
  • I play from forward tees with the kids. This is good , as I need the shorter course as my drives are just not cutting it lately.
  • I am managing the kids , keeping them positive, and not paying much attention to my game, but more or less just 'play practice', and not caring how I do. I like when I hit good shots, but don't get too bent out of shape with the bad.

Thinking I should move this to good, bad and ugly

Good

  • Hole 5, Par 3 -- I par'ed it. 100 yard hole, tee'd off 9 (on a good day the wedge will get me 100). Didn't hit a great shot, but landed on the fringe. Really good 2 putt here to get it. Very long putt from fringe, leaving a 4-6 foot putt for par.
  • 3 Bogey's - 2, 7,8
    • Hole 2 I decided to try the driver,sliced a little but not too bad, 193 yards. Then I went PW with 90 yards remaining and came up way short on a bad shot. The sand wedge was better (I might have came out of the trap on that) . A 2 putt!
    • Hole 7 - One of my least favorite on this course. I popped my driver shot, and it only went 108 yards. Left 185, Bad H19, only 120 yards, then gap wedge got me on fringe from 75 out. 2 Putt was able to save a disaster again. Hey... 2 putting seems to be a key here!
    • Hole 8 - Last hole of the day. Decided to try the 3w off the tee. Bad idea, only 127 yards, slight slice right off the green. Then 7i up hill, 152 to hole, Lands short 50 to hole, and then I sky it over with the gap wedge over the hole, but hit a nice chipper on to the green for a 1 putt!
  • So putting helped scored today

Bad

  • Hole 1, breakfast ball, and just not warmed up. A really bad 8i shot out of the rough, lack of wedge control
  • Hole 3 I hit 2 balls off the tee, I should have played the first ball as it landed closer to the green. 8i only 102, on a hole that was 138. Good Gap wedge on , bad 3 putt.
  • Hole 4 - Par 5 , a decent drive followed by a decent fairway hybrid shot. 190 yards fairway, then H19 154 yards (not best, but good enough), then 8i 104 yards, then gap wedge too far ... That's the shot that could have saved this hole, but instead you were far enough way to three putt, and double bogey

Ugly

  • Hole 6 - Par 5, always been a tough one where you go down in elevation and back up in elevation. I hit a decent fairway drive here, but the rest was ruined by poor play. 217 yards, leaving 190 remaining. H19 should get me most of the way there, but I mishit, and only goes 94. Then 9i problems, only 83 yards miss right. Then Gw over, and Gw on. So 5 shots to get on green, and your ruined by a three putt.

The problems

  • Driver slice is still a problem, but progress with some playable drives today.
  • Hybrids were hit and miss. I was so on with the Hybrid at northwest the time before, and sucked that I wasn't able to whip it like I did there
  • Swing is just all over the place --- too many thoughts while playing, and not enough just doing it. Need to get swing right
  • Irons , especially 7-9 were absolutely terrible, no consistency, no differentiation between these clubs
  • Wedges are a little better , but these require feel when say 60 yards or so away. Chipper has been decent for just off the green but need lots of practice here
  • Avoid 3 putts more often! You've improved, but still not great.

So basically your entire game needs work. I think if I just focus on some iron play we can make some progress 8i through GW ... must practice to grove the swing before play. If you do that, I think you can fix the hybrid/driver issue in the round, or at least hit it well enough.

item.title: Back to golf -- Observations coming back on the first 55 holes
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I am back, lets cover some stats. I'm no longer doing these in a spreadsheet, just relying on ShotScope to keep track

  • 6 Rounds
  • 55 holes (avg ~9 holes per outing)
  • Average +14.7 per 9 holes, or 1.63 over par per hole
  • Average about 102 on 72 course
  • The one birdie is questionable, as it was the first time out, and I don't recall the hole well.
  • Pars are good, and feel good that there are quite a few legit holes in there

Some observations:

  • Playing closer/short tees is fun
  • Tee shots are still all over the place, missing right more often than left. Playing the hybrid more off tee and shorter courses has given me a

The Weakest to Strongest:

  • According to ShotScope, the weakest part of the game by far is approaches. I just flat out miss on the approaches. 59% of approach shots miss short.
  • Next is putting. It's improving some , but still needs a fair amount of work. Too many 3 putts or worse. I will say, I think I'm not setting up approaches and short game to enable enough 2 putts. The likelihood of 3 putting when your 30ft + out is high.
  • Next is the short game, which I think falls in the same category. I do okay under 25 yards, but not great in the 25-50 yard range. So basically good with my chipper right off the green, bad with the wedges in that mid range
  • Tee shots are actually seeing a very 'slight' strokes gained. I think part of this is the effect of taking mulligans off the tees not showing how really bad my driver and other long clubs are. When your taking multiple shots off the tee for practice, it hides deficiencies.

What do you need to improve

So many areas here to improve in. I think the biggest bang for the buck right now is working on 7i - Wedge and getting consistent with those. A bit of work with the driver to straighten out could play dividends, or keep getting solid with the 19 hybrid. Having the driver start producing better 225-250 yard drives straight would allow you to play some longer courses.

Short game and putting. Just keep at it, this can be a strength as you kind of know what your doing. Just have to eliminate the mistakes.

So I think you need more range sessions per week, without getting your hip all jacked up... and then short game sessions. Hard to find the practice time, but that is the way to get better. I also think sufficient warmups could help before playing. It does seems to take me about 50 balls though before you figure things out on the range.

item.title: Another 8 holes -- minor rant
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
First the minor rant on slow play. I suck, but I play fast. If you suck ,you can still play fast and not hold up groups behind you. My kids can be slow at time, but never should an adult play at 15-20 min per hole. 10 minutes guys and gals. My kids can do it hitting on average100 yard drives and 70-80 yard irons... you can do it too. Move up, drop balls when you hit in the rough and keep moving forward.

Last night we knew we would have trouble as the 5:50 tee time, didn't get the go ahead until 5:53, but then took another 2 minutes to tee off, only to take 12 practice swings and barely hit the fairway... I get it, I've been there being the new guy, but no excuse. Then it was a long slow wait for them to clear the fairway for us to tee off. We hit the green (and it was 3 shots for both my son and I), and they were just teeing off. What were you doing for the last 5 minutes... ugh . We finish hole, to find them hunting for balls in the rough. Another wait to clear the fairway. I hit rare 240 yard on this hole, and nearly hit them as they were moving to the green... but after a 10 minute wait I didn't feel that bad.

So we ended up skipping a hole , hole 6, which is a terrible hole anyhow. I played white tees, and played pretty terrible . Score doesn't count the lost balls on 7 and 8

The good - Birdie's, Pars, & some Bogey's

  • Hole 9 - Hey, I parred it. Terrible drive that popped and only went 137 yards. Great hybrid show with the H25 (5 iron replacement), and goes 161, with a nice soft role on the green. Had a small chance at birdie putt, was like 15-20 feet. Missed but kept the miss within 2 feet!
  • Hole 2 - Mentioned above, 240 yards off the tee. Granted downhill. Tried a shorter backswing which worked here. I left the ball 130 out. Why I a hit a 9i iron here is beyond me, I hit the 9i, not cleanly and went 93 yards. Nice 40 yard sandwedge shot and some good lag putting led to a 2 putt, and a bogey.
  • Hole 4 - H19 off tee, 197 yards (downhill). Right where I wanted it... probably best shot of the day. Left me an 8i, roughly 120 yards out. I'm thinking par or birdie, but I hit the 8i off (irons are really struggling), and then I had to wedge on. 2 Putt was good.

The ok - Bogey+, but with some decent play

  • Hole 5 - Par 3 PW, 97 yards, but not hit well. I am on the green though, and then I 3 putt
  • Hole 1 - A decent 190 yard drive, leaving 165 to hole. The hybrid 25 (5) didn't work here, poorly hit and only covered 91 yards, but the PW worked and got me on in 3. The 3 putt here was painful though as I missed a medium length putt that would have made this a 'good' hole.

The bad - Bogey+ and bad play

  • Hole 3 - Good with the Hybrid 25 off the tee, 151 yads, next shot was actually hit really well, but a little right coming up the hill, I hit a tree and ricocheted in the creek. Don't hate this shot, but it was disappointing. I took a drop and sand wedged on... this was good. But then I took 3 putts,
  • Hole 7 - 2 terrible slices off the tee, this sucks. Lost balls. I dropped roughly where I hit, and hit a great PW approach to another terrible 3 putt.
  • Hole 8 - Par 3, I fell apart here (only to get it back on hole 9) . Hit two balls in the water... that's 4 lost balls in 2 holes!! I finally hit a decent shot off the tee, but it slices in to some trees off the green. (141 yard hybrid). I SW, then PW (shotscope didn't pick up the extra shot). I went over the green from a non-sand bunker. What a freaking mess. I 3 putt to top it all off. The scorecard says 6, but it was a 7 , and four over!

So overall, problems are the same. Was a bit better off the tee today with a warmup, but it fell apart at the end. Hybrid Play was decent, Driver was okayish, nothing sliced too bad, but not opportunity. Take away mulligan lost balls. Iron play was lackluster again. A little better with the wedges. Putting was blah , 4 2 putts, 4 3 putts.

I think focus on keeping the ball in play, minimizing the mulligans. I think you could gain a few strokes now with better iron play. I am just not hitting the irons cleanly at all. More range time... Short game wasn't actually that horrible today, except for 8. A few really good wedge shots. Some luck though.

Ankle hurts a lot after playing, hip not as bad.

item.title: Distances Today - Gapping?
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I've got some decent data through 63 holes of play this year. Trying to gap this at around 15 yards for my very high handicap.

  • Driver - 202 yard average. Long is likely in the 240-260 range, but yea this
  • 3W - Unknown, taken it off the tee once, and not played since
  • H19 - 185 yard club. One of the best when your hitting well, tends to stay low and rolls. Long 210 with this one. 180 and up yard club
  • H25 - 158 yard average, 181 long. 155-180 yards club. When your this far out, your usually a couple shots, but yea, this should get you there. Overlap with 6 iron, should probably play hybrid.
  • 6i - 145-160 yard club too chickenshit to play this. Never been a good club, but it's probably should be your '150 yard club'.
  • 7i - 143 yards average, 160 long so lets just say 130-145 yard club
  • 8i - 120 yards average , but less data on this club. 132 long. I think you could make this 115-130 yard club
  • 9i, 103 yards with a 163 long. I feel like I hit this club longer and have a better chance at making a good shot. S I'll move this up a 100 to 115 yad club
  • PW - - 86 Yards - 85-100 yard club
  • GW - 79 yards - 70-85 yard club
  • SW - 50 to 70 yard club

Let me rewrite this:

  • H19: 180 yard up
  • H25: 155-180 yards
  • 6i: 145-155 yards
  • 7i: 130-145 yards
  • 8i: 115-130 yard
  • 9i: 100-115 yards
  • PW: 85-100 yards
  • GW: 70-85 yards
  • SW 55- 70 yards (full swing)
    • Both Gap and Sand use shorter swings below 55 , Gap usually better on this

So that's it for now. I imagine I could be about 10 yards longer on the irons when I start hitting them right again. The hybrids same. I think eventually you'd like something closer to a 10-12 yard gap as you get better.

It actually looks like my averages are pretty average all around. https://www.golflink.com/instruction/average-distance-each-golf-club. I read that article after I did this, and most of distances fall right within that first chart in the link. Pretty average, I'd say, kind of in the mid-hitter range.

item.title: What's going on with your swing
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
You started the year pretty decently, but some bad habits have crept back in during rounds. Particularly it seems like I'm coming over the top more and slicing. I had a moment early/mid July the hybrids were really doing well mid-round and at the driving range. Straight with lots of power. If I could find that through the bag with some consistency, I would really have something.

So what is it. The good

  • Keeping weight forward helps, that video on keeping things simple, weight forward chin to shoulder backswing
  • The thing thought and practice of down (shallow the club), then around. Perhaps when shallowing I'm chopping down too much, but we'll see. I think perhaps pointing the club a bit more flat could be worth a shot here , dropping the club in to the slot a little differently.
  • Length and arm straight - going as far as you can while keeping the arm strength, but not overdoing it. You have enough power without requiring a long backswing and you have to keep remembering that
  • Staying loose and practicing loose. Letting it flow seems to keep you on track. Confidence breeds better shots

The bad:

  • You get in a habit of coming inside
  • Tensing up - lots of just bad hacky shots with too much tension.
  • Cupped wrists. During my lessons instructor keep trying to get me to bow more, I think because I was so cupped in the hopes that it would just flatten things out.
  • Your not getting enough lift on any of your shots, too many thin and fat leaving lots of line drives. Okay with some of the longer clubs.
  • The inconsistency leads to inconsistent yardages, and inconsistent play. I can line up a great shot, but I'm playing a 30-40 yard gap on whether I hit it properly or not. If you can just hit more often on the course without all the shanks, tops, etc

Feeling a bit beat up at the moment, so taking a few days before playing again. Maybe Thursday.

item.title: Strike a couple things in the last post
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Lets try to keep things simple. Keeping things simple seems to be paying the biggest dividends. Back to watching a lot of Saguto's stuff, and I just like his approach. It's less handsy, more flow, more simplicity. Just do this thing and other things fall in to place.

I was watching yet another YouTube guy doing that thing with shallowing the club where you turn the club more perpendicular to the ball to get rid of slicing. That's his swing... not mine. I saw about 10 different videos on dropping the club into the slot. There doesn't appear to be any consensus on this. What worked for me was just breaking that part of the swing into the slot and then running the turn. Practice a bunch and then start swinging. That seemed to start providing a better swing path overall. Less over the top. I

Another one is watching the videos of all the pros bend in the down swing. Again, not something I should be thinking about at this moment. Just get contact right.

I discussed the cup wrist thing too... I understand what that might have been doing, and maybe that's a thing for me, but I think I need to be careful. I trust that it was shown to me by a pro, but I also developed a lot of hip sway with the instructor, so who knows. I like now how my swing is more turn with the hips, but it's a bit out of sequence I think.

Focus less on power and more on consistent contact. I've got so much strength in my upper body that this all should fall in to place if I try.

Hip is doing okay, no big issues. Ankle is the larger problem right now. That persistent sprain that I got last year, keeps creeping back. Golf is the worst thing for it. It's the lead ankle, and I tend to torque in my swing... no good. I can't win with this injuries.

item.title: Short shutdown (hopefully)
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
2 Things..
