Most important one is I need a brief shutdown on swinging because of the ankle. It's really aggravated, and need a rest. It may be 2 weeks, it may be 3... if it doesn't improve it's a trip to the ortho. I may be able to do stuff with Kino tape, but that's a TBD.

On the injury side... the hip however has been excellent... hope to keep it that way

Now on the other side , swinging. I had a really bad time last time I hit balls. Slice central, especially with the driver.

What I noticed whenever I go back and I watch the Saguto videos and try to incorporate his stuff, things just go better. His latest video on weight forward seems like gold. I remember doing this to start the season and how good things felt. Sort of simple golf swing turn and swing with weight forward. I have so much power in my shoulders, this should be a good thing for me. It's apparently a little controversial his advice, the doctrine has been more about weight shift.

Basically, whatever works for straightish ball flight and decent power from about 100 yards out... then that will allow you to focus on the real scoring parts of the game again which is short game and putting.

item.title: Stack and Tilt?
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I've been through a bunch of different things as of late, and I've come upon the 'Stack and Tilt' method. I got there through Tom Saguto who's content is really great, and much more fun to watch then a lot of guys. He doesn't call out 'Stack and Tilt', but his approach seems to be pretty close to this, and he simplifies things. SIMPLIFY THINGS.

This is definitely different than some of the other things I've watched in the past. The way he is communicating things is answering a lot of the questions I had, and simplifying things for me. Again, I remember the first few times I played and watching his stuff and taking it to the course and feeling like, I'm not that bad.

This swing is different, and the big thing I am taking through my walkthrough today is my hands , and getting hands down... not flipping. I really got pretty good at flipping the wrists and doing all sort of funky stuff, but I believe that led to lots of inconsistency.

=================

I'm going to start things off with someone else's perspective first.

First part is control the low point, hit the ground in the same spot --- The most important thing when your learning.

Weight to the left in setup -- weight is always moving forward.

#2 Power - Move the club and hands around the body on plane --- turn the feet out

#3 Curve -- this is beyond you right now , but angle when contact in stance by moving the ball around. So you can control the ball by the placement in stance, pretty cool.

Basically every other video here calls out each of my faults and fixes them in a simple manner... I captured some of my favorites here, but keys are

  1. Weight forward at the start,
  2. Shoulder to shoulder (shoulder pointed to ball, move your other shoulder through). The hips will follow the shoulders and your swing
  3. Hands down -- this is new today, but it's basically drill to stop flipping and get crispy
  4. From above, contact ball divot
  5. Tension free ,
  6. Duck feet on setup
  7. Tilt!!! Tilt down
  8. Swing under the stick (shallow) for the over the top thing (this is not new for you) \

You can watch the videos over and over to get the finer points, and those matter... it's good reminders, but this is still all pretty simple. Now all I need is for my ankle to heal, and to start smacking balls again.

item.title: This is/was me
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Another great one for me... trail armed tucked, keep wrist angle through impact. Get through impact without flipping....

Same thing instructor showed me... but never any confusion about flipping in this video.

item.title: 63 holes in to 2024
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So not a ton of numbers to analyze yet. 63 holes over 2 months (June-July). Only 7 outings, and took the month of August mostly off because of the ankle.

What the numbers say and don't say.

  • You didn't lose much in the shutdown in 22. Your putting and short game are not terrible
  • Your Strokes gained off the tee is deceiving because of the mulligans your not counting. Get rid of this, and it's not so bad. But it really is pretty bad at the moment.
  • Your approach game which feels like it isn't that bad, is really terrible. I suppose your only remembering the good shots. I think some it is bad tee shots and playing from bad positions, but a lot of it is inconsistent iron play and distances. It's the old, you can't rely on your distances so you club up and down and have all sorts of problems. Very few greens in regulation.
  • Your best round was the 2nd one at River Marsh. That one felt pretty good, and wide fairways helped. I think I took some drops. Scores tracked are likely around low 100s, but show a little lower because I sometimes penalize myself and sometimes don't.

So it's still the same place you were

  • Fix the slice off the tee. If your real tee shots were as good the score you'd be fine.
  • Work on getting consistent with the Irons, distance etc
  • Keep working on putting and short game . Putting has been pretty strong, but the general slow improvement is working.

item.title: The only thing that matters at this stage...
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Is when you hit the ball you hit fairly consistently with a decent amount of aim.

I've gotten hung up on different things in the recent past, like 'how I should be swinging'. The truth of the matter is though, the 'how' only matters if the result is good and consistent. It's easy with all the youtube, instagram , etc stuff out there on swing mechanics to get caught up on what's right and wrong.

What's right... what moves the ball consistently right now. As a high handicapper --- good consistent contact, with consistent distances through your clubs is what matters. Your confident enough that if you can just keep the ball in play you'll score. If you cut out the shanks, slices, pushes etc, the rest of the game is fine.

It then comes to the short game, which you can manage right now... but if you really had the basics of the swing down, you could start focusing on that short game more where you can gain strokes... Your losing more strokes on your shitty swing than you are because of your short game at this point. Short game because of the lessons I have some decent play... yes, I make mistakes and lose strokes, but it's more manageable than having a ball fly off in the rough or out of bounds hunting it down and taking all the fun out of the game.

So this feeds into me trying this stack and tilt thing. Golf is so damn messy, with so many opinions. It's so religious. So I am trying this... I think I've seen some decent results when I was paying attention. I look at stack and tilt vs alot of other swings (more weight shift), and yes there are differences, but they aren't huge when you get things right.

I think it's really just about learning to make good contact, and perhaps a different process of building up your swing. Some of the same drills and concepts are still in play (ie, my wrist in the back swing, using a stick to work on not coming over the top, removing the chicken wings , etc).

It's all still kind of similar. Yes the fundamental of weight more left at address is of particular difference in the setup, but if it breeds consistency versus a loss of minor distance, then who cares. As I've also come to learn... better contact leads to better distance anyhow.

So I need to stick with it for a bit, but biggest concern is the driver slice at the moment.. and that I think is the hardest one to fix at the moment. I still remember the feeling of coming more around the body and smacking it back a few years ago. I was hitting lots of 200+ drives a couple years ago, and now I'm just slicing everything

Looking back at some of my lessons... and I think I can apply this to what I'm still doing with stack and tilt... hands back at top of backswing. My swing plane was decent, but because I never got back enough there was no room on the swing but to come over the top.

So #1 drill should be with the alignment sticks and working over the top still. Biggest source of issue right now... and all your trying to do is solve the 'keep in play' issue.

item.title: Notes on striking course
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Setup

  • Weight forward at start
  • Toes a little (or a lot ) duck
  • Hands a bit forward at address
  • Elbows together -- right arm will fold and unfold.
  • Body to golf ball -- spine tilt down through the golf swing
    • Slight hinge and wrist, drop from the waist down to ground

Checkpoints

  • Make sure front shoulder down towards the ground
  • Left shoulder under chin, swing the shoulders body follows . Weight never moves back
  • Finish with club shaft angled down
  • Arms straight through impact
  • is the weight forward at follow through
  • Are the elbows together at follow through
  • head in place -- same tilt towards the ground
  • hands behind right bicep --- don't move up to backswing then down -- wasted movement

Drills

  • Short 'unit swing' - 1/4 to 1/2 to 3/4 swings controlling contact -- weight forward, club angled down towards the ground at end , let the shoulders tell the body what to do
  • Anti-sway. Setup with right foot back, narrower stance, big toe inline with heel, heel stays down, knee straight whole time. No pressure on back leg
  • The under the stick to 'un-steepen' your swing. Use a basket to hold up.

item.title: Slice to Pull
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I went to the range. I followed my instructions, and things were good. I was at a grass range so I got a lot better feedback yesterday. I would say my percentage of bad shots was a bit lower. Better contact overall.

Now the problem, had WAY more shots going left than slicing. Didn't seem to matter the club, irons through the driver everything going left. So a few things I'm reading:

  • Swinging too far across the body
  • A grip too strong to combat a slice
  • Setup position too far forward of center (or maybe I'm dropping my trail foot back too far)
  • Over the top

So I think step 1 for me is to weaken the grip just a tad... just move it a bit closer to neutral, but probably still pretty strong. I think step 2 is to watch my alignment at address. Step 3 is check to your positioning related to ball, and step 4 make sure I'm not still coming over the top. Perhaps I'm holding the wrists a bit long too. It's the golf swing, so many things going on. I'm gonna stick with Saguto and his instruction and just see where that takes me.

I think we can see from this diagram, the most likely scenario is your getting your club face more closed now, but the club path may be a bit too inside. I don't think I'm hooking (or if I am hooking too much), so I don't think I've got the club path going straight and overly closed face... but it's hard to say. If you follow the chart above, It's possible club path is the same, but I've just gone from open club face to closed club face. Now I just need to get it in the middle.

I really was focusing on 'coming around the body' more yesterday, and that was helping. Also getting my hands to a position behind me.

The nice thing... My driver was probably going straighter than I've seen it since coming back. Was nice to not see a slice even if it was going left. I did have a few really nice ball flight crushed drives that went nice and high!

The ankle is so-so today. Definitely a small step back even with it all wrapped up. But totally playable. I hit around 100 balls, and I'm not limping any worse today. A good 9 holes will only see me hitting 50 balls... so yea, lets do that!

item.title: Can't win...
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So no golf yesterday. Ankle was still a bit funky, but the hip after the range session was an absolute mess. It's better today, but not great. Perhaps the swing change aggravated it. Perhaps hitting a larger number of balls (closer to 100 than 50 you typically). Also, not stretching as much as you have been, and a slight change in your supplementation.

At any rate, it's my birthday and I want to try out my swing change on course. So I'll be stretching and giving this a try a bit later. Since I'll be going it alone I haven't decided on a course.

Of the county muni-courses I've done, in order of favorites:

  • Northwest 18 (I think I've only made it 13 holes) - Always liked how open this course was, big fairways. Not as challenging as the 9 on accuracy, but more challenging on distance. Need to play the full course at some point.
  • Laytonville (All 18) - Only full 18 I've done, love and hate some holes. First birdie here on a par 4. Love the start of this course par 4s on both front and back 9s as a forgiving warmup. Hate 4-7, stretch up and down. Back 9 is a bit easier.
  • Northwest 9 - Best 9 holes to play in county. Played it so many times. Lots of water which can make it a bit more expensive. Can be slow with lots of players learning like me. Hole 6 is a very difficult hole -- maybe the most difficult hole I've played.
  • Hampshire Greens (think about 15 holes, not quite 18) - Really like this course, but the way I've been hitting, I fear hitting the houses a bit too much, otherwise it might be at top of list today. Fun course when your ready again.
  • Poolesville (only made it 8 holes) - I look forward to doing this one again. Had a similar wide big feeling like Northwest. It's just a bit further than the rest.
  • Needwood 9 - So this was the first 9 holes I ever played. I have a love hate relationship with it. I hit my first par 3 birdie here, but I've also come to really dislike the 2 par 4s on this course. The first 2 holes are so simple, then that Par 4 dog leg is an ugly difficult hole. The following par 3 is a water hazard hole with lots of danger if mishit. The next hole is super simple, and then a couple interesting par 3s, then that evil blind par 4. Anyhow.. this one only in a pinch

Honorable mention:

  • Blue Mash (played mix of holes) - Not part of MCG, but a public course in MoCo. It's nice, but usually at bit more expensive, and not sure worth the price lift.

Still left

  • Sligo Creek 9 (another shorter course) - Think this one would be fun with the kids ,
  • Needwood Full - Always seems crowded. This one eventually, but would love to be paired with non-randoms if I do this one.
  • Little Bennet - Further drive, heard very hilly.
  • Rattlewood - Even further
  • Falls Road - The idea of playing in Potomac makes me vomit a little. Can imagine you'll get a fair amount of douche-baggery

Then you have all the Frederick courses, and a few closer PG courses (College Park).

item.title: Good weather, poor etiquette and slow play
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I decided to go alone, and consider it a half success as I got 6 holes in 1:15. I have to say, I miss playing in the winter when nobody is around, and look forward to this winter to pick this back up again.

Okay, so the day starts with an older gentleman coming up the wrong way on the cart path as I'm ready to tee off. He warns me to play slow since there are two groups of 4 that have things backed up. I kind of figured when I booked, but I ignored my better instincts and carried on.

So I take my time teeing off. When I finally do, I slice the first couple balls... ouch, I thought I fixed that. 3rd ball I got on track, right down the middle. 186 yard, very very average kind of drive. I'll take it. I then go 7i, and shank the first one off just a little (it wasn't that bad actually). I took another shot, and that landed just off the green, where I was able to chip on and 3 putt. So double bogey if you don't count the mulligans

I practice some putting, and started to feel much better after a bit of practice. I had time, the guys in front of me were not teeing off yet. No biggie, but it seemed that they were waiting for the group in front to clear the hole. I figured backed up , this is okay.

2nd hole, good 223 yard drive --- pretty straight, if not a bit left. So be it Again, 7i, two shots. Second one was hit nicely for a 156 yard shot that I played. Then pitch and 2 putt bogey. I'll take that.

3rd hole. More mulligans with the hybrid , everyhing going left now in the trees. Some are kind of hook-ey with the hybrid. Not great,. 7i this time coming up hill, but I lose the ball as it bounces off the green. Pissed me off as it was pretty good hit .

4th hole. I'm starting to get a little annoyed with the waiting for group in front to clear green before teeing off... don't people know as long as you can't hit them, you can tee off. I gave them a bit of grace, as I think they didn't want to be pressuring the slow group. So whatever... more putting practice, and I needed it.

So 4th hole, more hooks left. Ended up playing the 8i from about 152 yards , hoping to come up a little short on green. Wrong, I hit it well... bound to happen, and it goes 161 yards (uphill). More practice putting, and now on to the next hole.

5th, the par 3 ... waiting waiting patiently. They are slow now. I hit a 9i perfectly... too long, but it still hits way back on the green. I decide, to play a 2nd ball with the PW, perfect 109 yard shot, a little long still. Okay, Iron is admittedly feeling good now. I've got momentum. I ended up 3 putting, very difficult downhill putt.

I pull up to 6... I know they can't clear the creek, yet their jerking around, so I give up, decide to skip to 8 as I can see another giant group coming up 7. In this situation, I would have done the right thing and asked if they wanted to play in with me... no offer, so fuck em, and go around. I'm usually not shy about asking, but these guys seemed a bit clueless.

Go to 8... another slow foursome hunting balls, playing slow. So I'm like fuck it... I'll just ride around these guys and blast one off 9. I got a nasty look, and a wtf my way. At this point... a little pissed so I blast 3 drives for practice, and take the 3rd. There was slice a hook and a decent 210 yarder. I play that one, but I shank a 9i and then have trouble wedging on as I'm rushing. I think the fools behind me who couldn't drive the ball 150 yards were waiting for me to clear the green and cursing me. I was in no danger of any of their 4 some hitting me. So anyhow, I putted in with my Gw for 2.

So two decent bogey's and a bunch mulligans. You can't count this for anything, but I think your back. Now you just need less crowded days and better etiquette.

Iron game felt a little better with new swing motions. In general, the shots were good enough. I'll probably throw this in the spreadsheet, but this was not a good outing and your working on a swing change, so here we are.

item.title: Why I hate the sim
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I practiced in my 'sim' today. I have some issues with my little garage sim.

  • It takes too long to setup -- 10 minutes at least to get nets and mats, etc all ready to go
  • It's hot as f* in my garage -- yup, it's hot. Perhaps it's better during winter time
  • It's up sloped slightly
  • There are garage rails that get in the way (although I think if you line up the ball under the rails you effectively avoid this -- except my son doesn't because of his too steep swing
  • You don't get a good feel for direction. You get some feedback on ball flight, but it's not great with the Garmin R10. Distance is also of issue
  • Indoor swing syndrome.
  • I can't hit my driver worth a damn inside, and my feet come off the mat.

So that's pretty much it. I'd rather hit the driving range and feel more free. It's better practice to see the ball fly. I should just stop on my way home and make the one driving range a good stop 3 days a week until you start hitting the ball better.

I do think, I only really need to practice 3-5 clubs. A mid/high iron (like 7-8), a hybrid and the driver. That covers most my distance shots. Practicing with the wedges is almost like a separate session.

item.title: Range Session - Great Irons, bad Driver
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So out of the sim, back to the range. Took me some energy to get there... but I did it!

So when I got out there I was really hitting wedges through about 8 iron super well. The Saguto stuff was really good. I mean, wedges were hitting the island, which is 120 yards! 9 irons were stretching to 130-140 at times. This is with range balls too! Lots of straight ball paths, tended a little left more than right, so all good... only a few slices all day.

The hybrids were okay... some pretty good stuff, a bit of trouble launching, but in general it was a lot of playable stuff. Again, not much in slice land, less than 5% overall the day... and I usually knew it when I hit it.

Now the problem. Popping the driver. I'm hitting the driver all wrong right now, and I'm not entirely sure why. It may be setup or something else. The best I was doing was doing like a half driver swing and it was going about as far as my 8 iron.

The 3 Wood was the same... same issue. I was either popping it or getting lousy distance. Basically anything off the tee was trash!!!

I've got a charity scramble coming up, which is motivating me to work on my game some. Either going to play or practice again today... Need to work on putts and chips a ton this coming week!

item.title: Another overly rushed range session
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I wish I could slow down sometimes. A very busy range yesterday, and on my way home, made me go super fast through a bucket. I hit some good balls... feel like my irons are pretty solid!

The driver is still tricky, but contact was better today and hit a few decent 200 yardish drives with the range balls. It's a bit disappointing, because my hybrids are almost as long (sometimes longer)

I few observations over the last couple sessions

  • I am noticing a lot of that 'coil' feeling in my swing of late. When I get it right, the ball can really go
  • Yesterday was more right bias then left, but I think that had to do with where I was in the range (against the left wall)
  • Driver is different than everything else, and it shows.
  • Thinking go slow in the back swing worked
  • Thinking around instead of and 'up and down' helps with the over the top.
  • Mishits are still a thing.

Anyhow... part of me wants to play today, part of me thinks I should rest. If I could convince a kid, then it would be good, will keep it light and fun.

item.title: Scrambles, drinking, building golf stamina
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I did my first charity scramble yesterday. It was fun, but introduced a new concept to me... 'drinking on the golf course'. I think it actually helped relax me for a bit.

Anyhow, same sort of problems drunk or sober. I sliced my first drive, but was actually pretty good after that with the slices, there were a few more that I sliced off with other clubs (irons, hybrids), but in general I hit it much.

Over 18 holes, the driver actually started being a decent club for me. Fortunately I was playing with an ex-baseball palyer that was murdering the ball, had 300 in him on a lot of drives. I was pretty happy the few times I landed 30-50 yards behind him in the fairway. Had some really great fliers... but also plenty of bad shots.

Hybrids were weak, I think I was pushing, slicing, toping all over the place... I usually have a tracker, but not today. Irons were also all over the place. I hit some really solid shots, but my distances (as they've been), have been all over the place. No consistency with my speed I think. I can crush my 7-9. At this point, I mine as well just play the 8, because any of those clubs could go between 80-160 yards.

My short game was absolutely awful. I had two good holes chipping. Putting was kind of all over the place. Difficult greens, lots of really difficult putts. I didn't hole a single long putt... had been a strength, but it's fallen off. Need work on the lag putting again.

I am super sore today... I haven't done 18 in 2 years. My ankle is complaining this morning. MY hips a little, my back a little. Rest up , hope to get the kids back in to it this week.

item.title: Needwood Exec 9 again
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Back at the first course I ever played. It's a mostly Par 3 course that isn't super interesting albeit a couple holes.

So yesterday was all about a decent approach game, bad putting and a few mulligans that ruined good holes. So the usual breakdown

Best Hole(s)

  • Hole 3 - A 'fake' birdie. I hit two drives, and two approaches, but when I hit it right, it ended up birdie. 183 yard down the center drive, 84 yard gap wedge and a 1 putt, from about 15 ft.
  • Hole 5 - A 'fake' par. First approach shanked out of bounds, but second was a 103 yard pitching wedge , with a good two putt.

Okay Holes(s) -

  • Holes 1 & 2 , both hit the green, but putting was sucking so I 3 putted. The greens were not easy.
  • Holes 4 and 6. Did not hit the green, but still managed bogies with some decent chip and putt play.
  • Hole 9 - Same deal, missed green (way over more on this later), and then chip and 2 putt.

Bad Holes

  • Hole 7 - you four putted after hitting the green. Really tough green
  • Hole 8 - this one wasn't really bad, I had a great drive 225 yards, and a decent approach that went just a little right and long. Not sure exactly what happened after that, but it looks like I 4 putted from the fringe after a chip. I vaguely remember going around the hole.

Take aways:

  • Your iron and wedge distances are really unpredictable on full swings, let's break it down
    • GW 93, 82, 84
    • Pw 92, 103
    • 9i 140 (downhill)
    • 8i 126 (slight uphill) , 138 , 159 (uphill slight)
  • So given above, the 8i deviation on the 8i is just all over the place. I caught the ball good on the last hit and I probably carried the 140, and then bounced the extra 20 , The 138 was a nice soft land and should be about your carry , the 126 I caught a little off, but not consistency. The 9 goes downhill 140 a little long, but yea, that's probably about right. The wedges were actually good on full swings, the deviation was at least playable.
  • Your putting stunk big time. You need to practice more. Your chipping could use some work. The 3 putts killed you
  • You hit both FIR and 56% of GIR, that's got to be some kind of PR.
  • If you cut our your mulligans you actually golfed well. Makes you want to play again today!

item.title: Mulligans, consistent scoring and having fun
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So really wanting to play some more now. I really would like to track my progress a bit better, so this brings me to a discussion around mulligans.

I get a false sense of 'how well I played' as of late because I take a fair number of mulligans (as high as 1 per hole some days). As someone who is really in a learning/figuring out your game phase, perfectly good for me to take a shot twice. It really built a ton of confidence for me when I missed a shot, and then a 2nd shot was really good and played that rather than trying to play some awful lie, or taking a drop somewhere. I need the extra stroke to figure things out at this point.

A really good example was my 'double mulligan birdie'. First tee shot sliced (was first driver of the day), second was really clean and straight. Played the 2nd of course. I had around a 90 yard shot, of which I hit over the green with a bit too much power and landed in a bush. I took a second and ended 15 feet from the hole. I sunk the putt... still felt great, even though it wasn't a real birdie. I hit 3 good shots, the way you would like to play most of your holes.

I think I took another 1-2 mulligans on that course... I can remember I shanked one 2 holes later, and then hit a nice green. Pretty sure it was 3 mulligans for the day...

My point on writing this... I really just need to track this stuff now. The watch does a great job tracking for the most part. A few corrections, but it's usually pretty spot on as long as I track my putts right (I too often do the putt collect in the wrong location, which makes my putting look better than it was).

The goal would be to drop scores and mulligans over the winter, till you get to playing with only 1-2 per 18 holes while getting that score solid in the 90s. Your almost hitting well enough again, that you might get there with just a bunch of short game practice. Honestly, going back to Jim would be a good

So the rule from now on with your scoring --- Keep your score, track your mulligans, but definitely take them so that you can actually work on your game when on course rather than just playing all the trash you hit. Try to limit them 5 per 9 holes for now

item.title: 6 Crappy holes
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I was feeling so good about my last outing, I wanted to get back out. So I rushed down to my the course this afternoon, and played 6 really terrible holes. There were no good holes, everything was double boget or worse

Bad

  • Hole 3 - Miss right with a 6i (lost again), then Sw, miss to bunker, SW (good shot on). Then a 2 putt, made a really fantastic 1st putt here, almost hit from 17 ft.
  • Hole 4 - Probably best hold of the day as I didn't lose a ball here. Drive sliced, but playable at 171 yards. Hit a nice H19 184 yards, LW on. Now had I 2 putt here I would have been super happy, but I missed bad and 3 putt again.

Worse

  • Hole #1 - Breakfast ball sliced, second shot sliced, I gave up finding them, 3rd shot was playable, but I still couldn't locate. Estimate about 225 downhill (I actually don't recall whether I found this one or not, and played where it lie), I then hit across the green, haven't done that in a long time. Lost the ball again, required to drop , hit my pitching wedge, probably my best club... and damnit, the grip snapped off it!! I didn't even take a big divot, it just purely broke. I made a 3 putt.
  • Hole #2 - Another trash drive, but at least I didn't lose it. I shanked it 111 yards... ugh. Then 7i comes up a little short, SW on, and 3 putt.
  • Hole 5 - because I lost the tee shot , I mark this one terrible again. More slicing off the tee... I thought we fixed this. H19, and H25 playing crappy. Skulled the SW LW to 2 putt, for another double.
  • Hole 6 - hybrid off the tee 164 yards, but lost it again. Sand wedge on (this was a nice shot), but then another 3 putt!

Takeaways

  • You played terrible, even with the mulligans this was pretty bad. Take away the good, the nice putt on 3, and the decent approach on 4.
  • You got thrown off by the slow play in front of you again ... how the hell is it this slow at the end of the day. I don't think it was the guys in front, but the guys in front of them. I think part of it is being a single you can play fast, but 2 or 3 play that much slower in front of you. Anyhow, it threw me off just a little. And then the guys coming up behind me... where the hell did they come from.
  • Your slice is back bad. Really had trouble keeping the drive in the fairway. It was slice, or fix the slice and your too far left. Ugh... no good drives here
  • You only hit 2 iron shots over 6 holes. Everything else was wedge and hybrid. So different.
  • You didn't have a tag on your 'replacement SW' , so numbers are not as accurate.You need new wedges (and you were just getting really good with them)
  • Back to the range again I guess...

item.title: Range session
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I did a range session yesterday, observations

  • You need to practice more. Your consistency was about on par with prior range sessions. Pretty even mix of good and bad. The bad yesterday was not as awful as it has been, but still enough misses to give you pause to go back to the course. A fair number of the misses were still playable (fats and thins).
  • Usually some clubs go better than others. Wedges thru 9 are usually pretty good. I struggled with hybrids and driver yesterday. 8,7,6 irons were fair, but inconsistent, with the caveat, I was actually hitting the 6 iron okay yesterday which I haven't done.
  • Slice was less prevalent on drives, but you had plenty of pop ops. Driver is still the hardest club to get right. Swinging a bit less power and turn
  • Your biggest flaws at the moment seem to be chicken wings, follow through, and hip turn. Man, when the hips come with me, it just feels so good, but I think I was mostly shoulders yesterday. I am trying to follow my guy, but I think I need to focus a little on getting my hips turned through the swing. Tempo is probably an issue, I need more video to start working on things. I caught myself swaying at one point, and fixed it quick. I am getting much better at feeling what I do wrong.
  • Hitting a jumbo bucket ruins me for the next day's workout. It really sucks that I don't recover from that, but it is more balls than you hit during a round. HRV down, RHR way up after a range session. This makes me think I am working too hard as usual
  • I feel like I've got a good whip or sling of the club now. I also do better with coming around my body versus up and down.
  • The 'pump' rehearsal of shallowing the club seems to help
  • Not a ton of spin on my iron shots, unless I slow my swing . Just an interesting aside, as I notice this on course too. If I try to smack it, it ends up bouncing long, a bit more finesse especially 9 and lower I can get some spin and land it.
  • I good 7 iron shot for me is around 150, I stuck several 7 and 8 irons right by the flag. Not as confident I can do that during regular play.
  • Driver was really hard to track last night. I was popping some up, but I think I hit a few clean. I know there was a slice or two in there, but more often when I think 'go around your body', your more likely to miss left than right.

Tons to unpack here... I just need to hit more is where I am at the moment. Probably more off the grass to get things right. You need like a week of hitting a 100 balls a day. Perhaps it might be time to park outside and keep your net up for a week and work on things.

item.title: No Range No Golf -- Thinking about updating the sim again
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So work and other stuff busy, no time to golf. The ankle is still keeping me away a bit, which really kind of sucks.

Got me thinking about updating the sim setup again. The one decision I really hate that I made was not getting proper tracking for the nets. This was not a good decision. Setting up and taking down the nets is a PIA. What is kind of a clever setup, still kind of sucks when you just want to get out there and hit balls.

I am starting to look at launch monitors where I can place the monitor beside the mat. There has been a ton of releases since I first purchased. Looks like I am anywhere between 1000 (Square) to 5K for the Garmin R5. I am leaning towards something in the middle like the Bushnell, but I know I am not going to do anything until after holidays. Skytrack and others are in the mix too. I just want something that will punish my slice or hook... direction and shot shape is more important than distance. The goal of the setup will be 1) to play courses and have fun , 2) setup better striking when you play on the course.

I figure if I do this, I've learned a few things, the trickiest is how to get a good hitting area that can support myself and my boys. Make sure everyone's swing can be full and clear (but maybe not driver for my large frame, but at least the boys could). That way everyone can have some fun. I am highly considering go all out and getting the projector this go around. The wiring situation worries me most about all this, how do I get this right. The ideal place is right side of garage because power, but the garage rails get in the way of myself and my son sometimes. I think you need a cart of some sort to pull out.

As I imagine it, the best spot is still right side of garage, because wiring is easier. This will mean you need to move the garage jack-shaft to the middle though. And this just kind of sucks as that adds $1500 and the space over there is tight.

I think some other stuff has to happen first , I have a list of home improvements that must be taken care of: Roof, bathroom window, some dry rot, etc before I can think about any of this... but it's fun to dream. I need to get the ankle right too to make this thing worthwhile.

item.title: Lots of range time, no real golf
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I've been going to the range, and have had a mix bag experience. This is two experiences one week between each other.

  • Last range session was pretty bad, I was hitting all over the place, misses/bad shots were probably 35% -45%. Driver was fairly long when hit well, irons were fairly short. 8 Iron shots probably about 110.
  • Prior range session was dead on, hitting long and fairly straight, misses were fairly consistent , and I'd say, I was in the 10-15% range on the misses. If I could hit like that every time. 8 Iron was going 140+

So what explains that 30 yard difference, and massive inconsistency.

  • Was pretty fresh for the one session, felt drained and sore on the other.
  • I was alone during the better range session.
  • I got in to a groove quick on the first...
  • Hip has been very achy 2 days post range sessions in the hip, still need to figure this out. I think the hip problem made me change my swing on the 2nd

If I had a session like I did the previous, I feel like I could go out and score around 100 or less (depending on putting). The second one, I'm losing a lot of balls. Even some of the drives on that second one that went long they would move left or right far enough where they wouldn't be playable.

I am ready to get out there and play, but it's been a struggle to find the time. Kids have been less interested. Last time we waited till June we played for the first time in Cambridge. Fun wide course, and hoping that we can repeat it again this year.

item.title: Looking over last years rounds
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
It's getting me excited to play again, especially when I look at the last 'good' time I played.

A few summaries of 2024:

  • I only played 11 times. One 18 hole scramble was not tracked
  • Most holes tracked was 13 at River Marsh which was fun, but not particularly great.
  • Between June 1, and Oct 24, I played 9 holes roughly ever 2 weeks. Not a ton of golf.

I still got a bit better if you don't count the last round! In my all time records, my 'best front 9' was considered Needwood on 10/20. That was a plus 9, and I remember playing pretty well with Greyson along with me and a really nice couple. Not a hard course by any manner, but I hit some really good shots that day.

I only played 6 times in 2023, before shutting down because of the hip thing. The prior year in 2022, I played 25 times between July and end of year as I was learning. Roughly once a week into winter.

I think if I could play pain free, I would go back to a weekly round, perhaps just get up insanely early once a week and walk northwest on a Saturday or Sunday first thing. Got to get the hip straightened out before taking that on.

item.title: Pretty sure it's time
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I am starting up again. I missing a wedge that will arrive tomorrow, but I am 90% sure I will play 9 holes today. I'll even wait out slow players if it comes to it, but I'll play 9. I have the itch... the body isn't in the best shape , but it's good enough to get out there and play.

It will likely start with Needwood 9 again. My driver is doing pretty well, but I only get 2 shots at it on Needwood exec. If I'm up for it, I'll do another 9 on Sunday at Northwest where I can at least get 6 driver holes in.

I am going to be coming in kind of cold, haven't hit for almost 2 weeks, but whatever. You'll either find your swing or not. Trying to move to a more fluid swing, but don't think you'll get a chance to do much on the course today if you go. My putting is probably a big hot mess since I haven't practiced at all. Same goes for the short game around the greens.

Let's wrap the ankles and start golfing again! Stay in your game, and take it nice and easy and keep the balls in play.

item.title: First Round of 2025
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So first a bit of disappointment... I don't have a score. The shot scope tracked my day, but failed me in the end, and the round never synced to the phone. I see no history. I really love tracking my shots with the Shot Scope, getting some distances and evaluating my game, but instead this time no data. I think this happened once before. My need a firmware or software upgrade (app) to get things working.

So now, instead of the usual , I will give my best memory (I didn't keep a scorecard). I did keep track of drops and mulligans, so I'll cover those.

I'll just relive the holes in order and see if I can come up with my 'score'

  1. This was the worst hole of the day. I struggled off the tee with my 9i, and then went wedge, and wedge till I got on. 3 shots on, and then 3 putts. 6, or +3
  2. This is one of the short par 3s, less than 100 yards to the hole. I went GW, and it went long, I was not getting the loft on my clubs like I have been at the range, and it went bouncing 120 yards or so. Terrible, I took another shot just to get a feel, and that didn't go so well. I second shot was on to the green with a wedge, I think I was fringe, and then I 2 putted. Putting actually was a good thing today (wish I had my stats). Lots more 2 putts than 3 putts. Anyone, so will say this was 2+2, for a +1 (your at +4 now)
  3. So not a bad hole, I hit a near perfect center of the fairway drive. I wish I had stat on that, 200 or so. I didn't kill it, just took it nice and easy. Just straight nice high ball flight. Great. Then I tried to hit my new PW on to the green. Again, I'm not getting flight, I am hitting line drives... it blasts over the green (80 yard shot travels 100+) . I take my first drop here (even though I found my ball), so I hit the green, and then 2 putt again. Nice long putt on the 2nd their too. So we'll mark this a +1 (your now at +5, with one drop)
  4. 9i misses green right, but not terrible. My shot went over, hit the guys bag and stopped it which happened to be great. I'm on the fringe, and I 2 putt again. Another +1 , your now at +6 with one drop/mulligan
  5. Easiest hole, but I still screwed it up. Irons still not getting the air, going long. I'll give this one another 2+2. So +1, and your now at +7 with one drop/mulligan
  6. The first hole I ever birdied, was not kind to me today. I took 2 mulligans, and a drop on this one, starting to get a little fatigued. My 2 mulligans are off the tee, but my third I hit soft, and it doesn't make it to the green, but lands in the sand trap, I get out of the trap, but I over hit and have to take a drop. I then 3 putt. So this is a terrible hole. +3, your now at +10.
  7. Best hole of the day, I think I hit 7 or 8i hit green right side. Nice straight shot, didn't quite have the loft I wanted, but I'll take it. I then 2 putt. Par, still at +10
  8. Driver twice today, and both times nice and playable. Not as long on this one, but I kept it straight and right in the middle of the fairway. What was even better was hitting the next GIR, again, nice and soft on the right side of green (not a big target either). Almost though I might get an eagle for a second as the ball bounced in front of the hole, and them skimmed by the flag. I couldn't save par though, as I 3 putted, for another bogey +1, and now at +11.
  9. Same problem I have on this hole, I always end up long. Once again, my 8i flies over over the green (probably 150+), I have to come back, 2 to get on. And then a 3 putt I'm guessing ... at any rate, it was a double and now at +13.

So if you score like I did, you actually played better than ever. The putting was very good. I am going to keep two scores this year, a mulligan+ score, and one without (The score I've been posting prior to 2025). So I scored a 42. My adjusted score with the drops+mulligans, I moved to a 47. These are still very good scores in the scheme of things. Putting did you right today.

Your score at @72, would be a 98 not adjusted (I like that), and a 108 adjusted. Not bad for the first time out. I was really encouraged by my putting (lots of 2 putts), and my 2 driver hits.

Your short game wasn't terrible, you did okay getting on. If your body cooperates, you might repeat it tomorrow (or mid week). It's unlikely, but you never know. I really want to give NW a try now that the driver performed so well. I need to sleep hard now and let the body regenerate.

item.title: Score Tracking for 2025
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I think I've come up with a 'best of both worlds' way of tracking this year. I believe it will show improvement in a way, while not killing my ego entirely. Before I get in to the scoring, I want to go through the evolution of this

I think early in year 1 (2022), I started tracking every time I even whiffed at the ball. I saw my scores go way down after some lessons, but I think at that point I started giving myself a free ball here and there , but I was still pretty honest about my tracking.

In late 2022 after I got the shot scope, I think is where I started to track less and less my misses, and just keep the normal shots in the Shot Scope. It made for a good analysis of my clubs without the misses, and a clear walkthrough of a hole, which was nice, but not entirely accurate. By 2024 this was full habit. I distinctly remember the 'birdie mulligan' hole that I had that year. I denoted it, but I know it wasn't a true birdie, as I hit 2 tee shots. Even though the 2nd tee shot and follow on wedge shot were good.

So I like tracking progress, but you have to be honest about progress, and I hadn't really been with not really counting bad tee shots, or the occasional drop. This inflated my scores some a bit, but it was suspect because there was a bit of good and bad here. You might hit a few bad tee shots and recover one day, but you might instead play a bad tee shot the next. How do you differentiate if your not tracking.

So here is how I am tracking this year:

  1. You are likely to have Provisionals from the tee, and this will include shots like you had yesterday, where you basically miss hit. You don't play the mis hits if it doesn't travel at least past tee boxes, and run a provisional. The provisional is tracked separately, your not adding it in the shot scope, but you'll adjust score at end of round.
  2. You hit in to the rough and can't find your ball, you take a drop , you don't mark it with shot scope, but you'll adjust score at end of the round.

Each of the above will considered another stroke. I started tracking this kind of late last year, but wasn't adjusting my scores.

This leaves last years scores looking something like this. The scores will likely be tighter in some instances.

What is pretty cool is I asked ChatGPT what this would like over 20 rounds, with the gap closing in, this is sort of a projected version of what I think would happen (funny, it got close the first time, but then timed out or something,AI got confused, but eventually came up with this):

item.title: Planning out more golf
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I'm all in. So want to continue to get tuned up and see if this is really the year of golf for me. So I am already planning my week around a few golf outings. I've spent some time this AM trying to get my shot scope back from the dead. No luck so far. It's like it won't allow it to save firmware/courses/etc. It's like it's got a write block on it, so I am likely just gonna go pickup a new tracking device. I like the V5, as I prefer the physical buttons and round face of the new ones. It's 1209 right now, and may be worth picking up if I find out the watch is still not working this week.

Anyhow, I'd like to paly Wed or Thu, Friday or Saturday, and Monday this coming week. I want to to just keep at it. I could clearly use the swing practice with the irons, but it's messed up from the mats, so I don't want much time doing that anymore. I need to work on getting the ball back up in the air, and taking a divot. Driver seems to be reasonably on, hope it stays that way. Short game could use a ton of work, ie, inside 50 yards, but not your putting. I have no idea on the hybrids/woods, as I haven't hit them yet.

I am encouraged that I started the round so poorly, and was able to get better as I moved through the holes. This should be a lesson... don't let the first 2 or 3 holes guide your day. Just fight through it, and see if you can get on track. So the plan this week if the body holds up:

  1. Wed or Thu- Play NW 9 holes , or try the 18 late and play about 9.
  2. Fri/Sat - Open up to play anything just see if kids want to join. AM, PM , doesn't matter.
  3. Mon - River Marsh afternoon hopefully with the kids.
  4. Wed (technically I might still be on vacation), if we're back maybe an early round at crossvines or something like that, depending on how the body feels

So that's it


As I was writing this, I got it to update firmware on my V3 shot scope, so maybe there is hope. Full watch reset, reconnect Bluetooth, and it finally took a firmware write, but updating courses still doesn't work, which makes me think it won't complete writing the round at the end of the day. I unsubscribed to all courses and we'll see. Again, when this thing works it works like a champ and the stats are pretty damn good, rarely misses a shot, but when it doesn't what a frustrating mess. Perhaps, 'subscribed courses' isn't really necessary. Thinking about it, you might not get accurate numbers while your out there (i.e., if the course moved, but it should consolidate everything correctly once it uploads to the phone as that would have the updated course materials, and then you should see where things landed.

item.title: Moving from Low 110s, to Low 90s?
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So realistically, I'm scoring in the low 110s (low 100 to high 90s on a good day). I want to move my scores down so that I am scoring consistently in the low 90s. I am asking Copilot and it's giving me some tips that are actually really good. I'll infuse a bit with my own voice:

  1. Risk Management & Course Strategy
    • Eliminate Penalty Strokes: Use safer clubs off the tee (e.g., hybrids or 3-woods) to keep the ball in play. Fewer lost balls, OB shots, and hazards mean fewer extra strokes. For me this means use Driver when it's working, but don't try to kill it. 200 yards is fine if you keep it in the fairway. The theme here is 'No Hero Shots'. You are capable of making a good shot here and there, but you need to pick those opportunities carefully. If you see water, make sure you come up sufficiently short.
    • Smart Shot Planning: Before each hole, decide your “safe zone” strategy—target areas that leave you with manageable approach shots rather than chasing difficult pin placements. Sound advice, but lack of consistency is a killer, so even when managing, your chance at a miss is high
    • Consistent Pre-Shot Routine: Develop and stick to a routine that guides your club selection and shot execution, ensuring the same smart decisions each time. This foundation is critical because minimizing mistakes directly removes stroke losses from your game. For me this means loose swings to the side, but once you get over the ball you only take the one shot.
  2. Short Game Mastery
    • Putting Efficiency: Practice lag putting and work daily on creating a smooth, repeatable stroke that eliminates three-putts. Consistent, confident putting can shave valuable shots off your score. No 3 putts, duh. If I go by the last round, this isn't a problem right now. Your lag putting was spot on. What really helped was 15 minutes on the greens prior to the round.
    • Reliable Chipping and Pitching: Focus on simple, reproducible shots such as bump-and-run techniques to ensure you’re up and down around the green. Emphasize contact consistency over complex tricks. I'm decent enough in the fringe with the chipper, that helps shave some points, you are missing practice time in that slightly longer (say, 10-20 yards from the green), and some of the near side bunker work.
    • Pressure Drills: Create practice scenarios that simulate on-course pressure to build routine and confidence on short game shots. Since many excess strokes come from a subpar short game, refining these fundamentals can yield immediate benefits. This is just reinforcing some dedicated time practicing the short game with a bit of extra pressure
  3. Data-Driven Practice & Analysis
    • Track Your Game Metrics: Use scorecards or digital apps to record fairways hit, greens in regulation, and putting stats. Over time, this data will pinpoint where you’re losing strokes. This I'm good at. It was obvious from the last round it was Irons, where we struggle is you fix one thing and another part of the game starts suffering, and it's a constant whack a mole.
    • Target Weaknesses: Identify recurring issues—whether off the tee, around the green, or on the putting green—and tailor your practice drills to address those gaps.
    • Regular Review: Set aside time after rounds to analyze your performance. Experiment with small changes (e.g., different tee clubs or green strategies) and monitor the effects. A data-driven approach ensures your improvements are focused and measurable, turning adjustment into habit.

item.title: A not so great round at NW, and more Shot Scope woes
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I was so excited to get home and review my round. I synced as I walked off the course and saw my score in the Android App. It gave me a generous 49, but then I got home logged in to the Shot Scope portal to only see one hole!!! What the hell. Reached out to support, but the shot scope has been a lot of trouble. I don't care about missed shots, I can correct for that, but whole missed rounds, and before that not registering clubs.

When it works it works great, but when it doesn't it's total crap. It's like their is no software QA on this stuff, and older versions of the watch are just an absolute mess.

Alright, without the details, on to my analysis. I am going to go hole by hole to see if I can consolidate my score

  1. Best hole of the day probably. First ball was a breakfast ball. Second ball was a 175 yard drive up the left, hit well enough. 2nd shot was either PW or 9i, and I actually ended up getting to GIR. I marked a 5, so I think I may have 3 putted, or maybe it was a chip and 2 putt, at any rate. Score was a 5 with one mulligan marked. (current +1, 1 mulligan)
  2. Another mulligan off the tee, shanked left. Then I went for 6. a good drive (maybe 250 downhill), and iron shot that came just off the green (9 or 8i I think), and then it was a bad chip and a 3 putt. So short game not good here, but a 6 wasn't terrible on this hole as the putting despite being 3 wasn't terrible. (current +3, 2 mulligans)
  3. First bad hole. Good off the tee, nice and center. I shanked an iron on the 2nd shot, and then follow up mulligan I ended up getting over but well short, took another shot to get on , and then I'm at 6 with one mulligan (current +5, 3 mulligan)
  4. Okay, this is where the mulligans started getting bad, 3 mulligans taken here. The actually shots you played were good though. The hybrid landed a little off the fairway, the 8i from across the creek to the green was a great shot, putting was a bit terrible though, 3 putt, and I ended up with a 6. (+8, 6 mulligan)
  5. Another bad tee shot, followed up by a great straight iron shot on the par 3. This was a virtual par if you dont' count the first errant tee shot. (+8, 7 mulligans)
  6. Terror hole... Taking 2 mulligans here off the tee with the hybrid... what the hell happened. THe 3rd shot was great though. I hit it right where it should have gone. 150 yards left with another hybrid, came up short, but not terrible. Had a bad shot to chip on, and then another chip. Another mulligan for 3 here, so total 7 with 3 more (current +11, 10 mulligans)
  7. 1 mulligan surprisingly, just off the tee, hit the driver too far left. The next shot was a pop up driver, but went 100 or so yards, setting up a decent hybrid shot, and then a decent wedge shot on to the green, +1 here, for not a bad hole (I wish I could see if this was legit). (current +12, 11 mulligans)
  8. 1 mulligan again off the tee. Second shot was good, 3rd shot over and then 2 putt for bogey. Not bad (current +13, 12 mulligans)
  9. A disaster, mulligan 1 from the tee shanked off. Second shot decent. 3rd shot 9 iron over the green left, never had that miss before. Then I couldn't hit a SW and was basically done, call it 2 more mulligans, and a 3 putt for a 7...

Finishes the round at +15, and 14 mulligans/drops

Lets do the analysis. Score without the drops, 102. Not terrible. Scores with the drops, 130. Terrible. Got to cut down the mistakes (off the tee). Short game was brutal today, lots of misses and extra strokes. Irons were okay, better than it had been. Heat played a role today, it was hot and sweaty.

A couple other thoughts post a day. If it had registered, I think the drive off 2 would have been close to 250. My hip/quad is a wreck today, one day post (and 2 days post a range session the day before). If it were not for the quad pain, I would play a lot more.

I'll categorize the problems:

  • Lack of consistency on tee shots, and iron shots, too many mistakes that are unplayable
  • Short game (inside 50) - those short shots to get to the green are not great. Chipping on even with the chipper was bad in this last outing. Could use short game practice time.
  • Putting, I will list as not a problem , as it's about average for my game.

item.title: River Marsh take 2 - 18 holes, and what I recall
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So the shot scope is definitely a no go. It uploaded 3 holes , although seemed to be good recording throughout the day. It's either a new shot scope, or acros, or something else for future tracing. Again, so good when it works, and I really missed some great stats on this trip!

First, the themes and then a play-by-play

  1. Too many mistakes off the tee... I lost a lot of balls, hit a lot of provisionals. I was really driving the ball well on many holes, but enough of them were 2nd or provisional shots.Plenty of iron shots went bad too
  2. Putting was better, a fair mix of 2 and 3 putts. The 3 putts were absurd distances, there were some mistakes and some easy putts missed, but I made it up with several good putts (including a couple for par).
  3. Short game was a little bit better, You got a bit better with the SW and dialing in distance... you did have times going over the green, and you also sculled a few over. This is definitely an area to continue to work on to save strokes
  4. Irons were inconsistent... I have an inconsistent bag too,

I'll do a rough estimate, but I didn't even right down holes 16 thru 18. I was dealing with emotions from my youngest, and kind of hurt my forearm on one of the late holes, so the last few were pretty bad, But I'll try my best to score the whole thing for a rough average. For the purposes of measuring mulligans, I won't try to count, and just use a 1.5 per hole. I had some zero's towards the back 9, but I know I made those up on the last 2 holes...

  1. Par 4 , shot a 6. 3 Putt, 1 mulligan (which really stunk, because the mulligan was my provisional, and I didn't find the better hit ball. So good drive, I remember my second shot being a poor one, but my third was good enough to hit the green or just off the green, and then a 3 putt. Double bogey not bad on #1
  2. Par 4, this one I actually barely recall, it's weird. I hit a very weak tee shot I recall, and then I hit an iron that ended up just around the sand trap, and then I wedged on. I scored a 6. 4 to get on, 2 putt (+4)
  3. First Par 5, okay, I think this is the first one I felt like I played pretty well. I hit a decent drive that landed center, and this is where I think I'm driving the ball 200 plus on most holes here out. Drives were high, long and straight, with the exception of a few that shanked or sliced out. Anyhow, this one requires you to cross some marsh, which I did, I think I got on in 4, and then 2 putted, but I scored it a 7 so something else happened. +2, (+6)
  4. I am pretty sure this was the only one that the shot scope picked up correctly. Drive, 242 straight on the fairway. 8 iron 157 to a 3 putt... well, that seems a bit sketchy, but I do recall this hole, and hitting a nice iron shot. So this one is your first bogey (+1), for a total of (+7)
  5. Another Par 5, again, I think I drove this one well, and then played well enough. Looks like my issue here was a 3 putt, for the double. (+9)
  6. A Par 3, and I marked it par. I definetly remember the mulligan here, but I do remember chipping on , and then putting one in. I'll go with par here (+9)
  7. A par 4, I have it marked 3, but there is no way. I do recall, hitting a good drive here (looking at Grint's overhead for reminders of the hole), and a good iron shot to get on, lets say I two putted it and that's another par (+9)
  8. Another par 3, and I have it marked par, so we'll go with that. I was getting better at this point. I remember hitting a decent iron that landed just off the green, and I think I two putted from the fringe. Stay at (+9)
  9. I have this marked single bogey, but I think I will mark it double, because I'm recall this hole well enough. Great drive, although might have been a little off fairway, and then hit a hybrid just in to the left corner. The PW over bounced off the green though. It was a good shot with a bad bounce, the ball was not found, I dropped and then 2 putt. So good putting again, but I think it's fair to say you were at least +11 at this point (+11)
  10. I remember this being pretty diastorous, I marked a 7 (+3) on Par 4. I hit a good drive, but the follow on shot went in to the marsh OB, I ended up taking a drop on the other side, which played tough. (+14)
  11. I think this one played well for me. I marked it a 4 for par with no mulligans, so I am going to go with that. Good drive, I think iron'ed on and then 2 putt. (+14)
  12. Says I par again, but I don't recall this one well. good hole here, and I didn't take any mulligans. I honestly don't remember this one that well, but I think I drove a bit right against some housing construction. Then I took a couple more to get on the green. , putting was 2, I'll keep at +14 here.
  13. +2 here on a par 3, so you know you scored it right. 2 putt, but some struggles getting on the green (in 3). +16
  14. +2 on a par 4 here, 3 to get on , 3 to putt, if I see the read. +18
  15. A par 3, you most definitely pared. You even traveled over water on this one
  16. I stopped scoring here, but I think I can surmise well enough. I think I drove the hell of this one, and then struggled a bit when I got close to the green, hitting over then back on. My putting was good, I am going to score this a +2 since that is about what I'm averaging. +20
  17. Over the river failure. I was exhausted, and I'm just gonna max +4 on this hole. +24.
  18. Last hole, dramatic long par 5 up to the hotel. I drove it in to some trees, and took a bit of relief to get it out. I think it took me either 4 or 5 to get on, and then 2 putt for another +2. +26

So overall you'll go +26 on a course score of 70. So that's an adjusted '72 score' of 98. Using my 1.5 mulligans per hole, I'm at a 125 for the 72. I played better the prior year, but it's tricky, as I'm a bit more honest about the mulligans now. I think it was close, but I think you can take some solace in driving the ball decently. Iron play improving, putting improving.

Your body isn't totally wrecked either. Your forearm is a little rough, but that's really about it. I'll be happy if my hip cooperates over the next few days and allows me to think about a weekend round!

I think both boys also parred holes which is exciting. I mean legit pars. The 12 year old smashes his driver, the older one is too steep and has trouble getting the ball in the air, but he plays without getting too emotional now which is impressive!

item.title: Next watch
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I really did love the shot scope, and sad to see it go, but it is time to move on to the next watch. I am disappointed because I'll be losing that automatic detection that worked so well for most of 2 years. I didn't hear back from support after a week, so I give up. On a good note, when I had issues a few years back they sent me new watches and tags under warranty. They had to do it twice though as the 2nd didn't work, and the 3rd finally did... serious manufacture issues. Also on a good note, there stats are really good. The reason I am moving back to Garmin, is just that I trust it more. I've had so many issues, and so many missed rounds and stats with basically zero rhyme or reason to it. Did the hardware go bad, was it bad connection between phone/watch. IT's too hard to tell, and there is no feedback as to why. Too bad...

I am going to switch back over to Garmin products. More reliability, but more required interaction. For each shot I'll need to set my club... this is a major annoyance. I could eventually get the CT sensors (maybe they will come down in price at some point). Currently sitting at 269, lowest 249. A purchase for the future if you really hate setting the club on each hole. I imagine they will be near in reliability of the shot tracking with the current tags I use (those are pretty good, less than a 10% miss rate when it was working).

So now I'm on to which watch. Do you buy a golf only watch, or upgrade the whole package. A few options

  1. Epix pro 2 - this is a mack daddy watch with all the bells and whistles. 689 Saphire addition on sale, almost 1/3 off! PRetty impressive discount. More features than I need, but I do love my garmin for workouts . I use it on walks to track. I use to run (not anymore), and this would cover all those things...
  2. S44 - this is the latest mid-range golf watch. Looks pretty good at 299

S50, and S62 are out... if I'm getting a watch that does more, I step up to either epix or fenix or one of the other premium.

item.title: A terrible turn
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I don't know what happened, but my game which stinks pretty bad, got a whole lot worse during my last few outings. Let me summarize:

I went to the range after about 2 weeks of not hitting about 1 week ago. It was a bad experience, I was in a bad mood, and had a difficult time hitting the ball straight, making contact, etc etc. Slicing, hooking, etc, it was all there.

I went to the range 2 days ago, and it was better, not where I was earlier on in the season, but it felt good enough. So I took one of the boys out yesterday, and it was a bloodbath. I couldn't hit crap. Especially as things wore on, I don't have a score, nor numbers, but I do have a decent memory, will run through the holes. The number of mishits and mulligans was higher than it ever had been.

  1. Bad drive slice off but in play, poor iron contact, followed by more poor iron contact where I missed green right... chipped on and played it out. I scored this a 6
  2. A bad first tee drive, and then one that flew far enough, Iron shot misses right, chip to 2 putt, for a 5 (not including the mulligan off the tee)
  3. This was actually a good hole, that could have been great... I hit a bad drive (with hybrid), literally one of those 'to the next tee box' kind of drives... I hit a couple more when I started slicing it out... so I played the poor shot because it was in play... I then hit a good hybrid down in the corner right in front of the creek. Next shot was a perfect iron up the hill, but landed just long off the green. I then hit a chip with the chipper from about 25 feet that hit the pin in!
  4. Really falling apart here.... just all over the place, same experience as previous hole, can't get the hybrid right. I then hit down in the corner, have to take some relief. I pop the ball over, chip and putt. Lots of mulligans here, and pretty frustrated with the number of mulligans you hit so far.
  5. I hit a straight shot right at the pin. Funny thing, saw the hole punch right next to where my ball landed... pin on another day it was an easy birdie, if not a hole in one! I then proceeded to 3 putt, for bogey... no mulligans on this one, so I'll take that
  6. Really terrible... I slice 2 balls, and hit another way left. I can't keep it in play. I have trouble with the irons before finally getting one to move towards the bunker... just so many bad mulligans. I then do the whole chip and putt, which was not great.
  7. Worth mentioning, my 80 lb son bombed a 180 yard drive from the 'ladies tees', coming up about 15-20 yards short of the green on a par 4! He struggles with the short game, but off the tee he is great. Me... I hit a bad drive, and then another bad drive... I played something that was probably 100 yards just past tee boxes again. My next shot was good enough and ended up green right, and chip and putt
  8. I hit 3 balls in the water from the tee... I ended up playing my sons ball, because I was struggling. IT was a good lesson for him, I stayed positive as I shanked ball after ball.. .maybe it was the heat.Chip and putt was not terrible, needed the practice.
  9. Decent enough drive, son really bombed it too, and almost out drove just teeing off 10 ahead... what happened to my drive. It was such a source of strength in Cambridge and earlier in the year, and now it went back to crap. Anyhow, I then started hitting across, and iron'ed over the green, chipped and putted... painful.

So what happened... poor contact, heat, lots of mistakes. Still had a couple good moments, and I'll use those to keep going, but what a mess this was! Was doing so much better keeping my ball in play off the tee, but it went off. Iron play was a mess, and short game was just about adequate. I think I started over thinking the swing, instead of '1 or 2' things. I got up there and had a million thoughts, and wasn't able to clear it.

Usually it's the go around the ball instead of up and down that has been helping lately (especially on drives), but I couldn't quite get it right. Anyhow, I might take a week or two, and then give it a go again...

item.title: Switched to Garmin
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I bought a Fenix 7 Pro Solar. I haven't done a round with it yet, but I started playing with the golf features that I could.

I'll do a full comparison of the shot scope after I get 9 holes in. I did try to track with the app the other day, but that failed miserably. It's too much to try to grab your phone after every shot.

So how I think this should work on course:

  1. Autoshot - so my watch supports this feature. It looks like they are doing some smart detection when you swing. It says 'speed and impact'. According to copilot it uses a tri-axial accelerometer and a gyroscope to measure speed (this could be interesting stat), and then it says a shock wave travels up the shafter into the wrist for a 'sharp spike' in acceleration to detect the impact. My guess is they use an algorithm smart enough to figure out which was practice swing vs real swing, but also should be able to get some misses with the data. I had movement at location X, and then went to location Y.
  2. Club selection. Without the ct10 sensors, looks like I'll have to put in my club at each swing. I've opened the app on the phone, but hard to tell how this will work. There is an option to 'measure shot' which confuses things. Directions just say lead wrist watch it will detect. It says it will prompt after you swing. After you have a certain amount of rounds, I think it might suggest the club, and hopefully you just confirm that you
  3. Short Game (Chip and Putt) - no idea how this will work right now, asking copilot. This is why I guess they recommend CT10 for short game clubs. I imagine this will take a bit of work to get down. Hopefully it does the 'select 1,2,3 or 4+_' on putts when you reach the green. With shot scope those stats were never quite right, but I knew how many putts I took. Detecting a chip to the green will likely be something I need to put in manually. This is one of those things, if they make it easy and intuitive enough, should be able to get it down easily. Garmin has typically been pretty good at this

Off Course. This is where I think Shot Scope really had a superior experience, but what I can tell with Garmin so far from logging in to the app :

  1. The score for the round looks easy enough ... it includes GIR, Putts, Fairway (which I entered manually for a few holes last time). I can't
  2. It has a a graphic that shows 'off the tee' , which looks to plot what you've done. Right now it says filtered 'all clubs', with no option. Hopefully that becomes a drop down of club selection. Approach looks to be a similiar. Chip and Putt has an advertisement for CT10 sensors ... lol
  3. Course Stats --- so we'll see how this goes, but I think that will likely fill in if you finish all holes. Hopefully it will give you partial, even if you do say 7 holes of an 18. This just looks like it will be a summary page from the documentation. It looks like the Hole Stats are interesting if your playing the same course over and over, will get you an average per hole which looks nice.

So what's I'm really uncertain of, and hoping the experience is good with Garmin, the auto shot section. I'm not finding a ton of images, but this one looks right!

So it's not a pure overlay of overhead imagery like Shot Scope. That's minus one for Garmin (I think). It appears it will show up over this more computer graphic of the hole. What I do like is that it has edit/add shots. That will hopefully allow you to adjust if you missed a shot, add the missing chips if those are missed, etc. I think there is something to be said in this view, you will likely always get the same hole orientation view (bottom to top) vs shot scope which goes left to right (except in edit)

The historical shots is also pretty intriguing. Would be interested over time to see how we performed on certain holes. This would be nice to have right now.

I will say, shot scope when it worked worked so well. Their stats were amazing, even for a hack like me. I could see after a round how I was doing.

I really loved with shot scope, the lack of input required (you only needed to put you putts in end of hole) and it got everything else. The interface on the web was intuitive enough to easily update post round.

I really liked reliving the good holes from the watch, and I did learn from the stats where I should focus practice more... not that I can't tell as of late that I need more focus on short game and irons (at least up until last week).

Speaking of which, I pulled up shot scope, and I remember birdie this hole a couple years ago, alone on the course in the cold first or second time I did 18 at laytonsville

OR paring a par 5 after struggling early in Poolesville.

This fake birdie at Needwood (I remember the random couple we played with, and how I looked like a gamer for 3 holes). This was late last year.

item.title: First time out with Garmin -- mixed bag
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I think there is a bit of learning curve on playing with the Garmin Golf App/Watch. Let me give my thoughts so far

The good:

  1. The swing detection for longer Wood/Iron shots works pretty well.
  2. It caught the bad shots, which is actually a pretty good situation. It didn't count my double shots (ie, if I took two shots from the same location)
  3. No glitches, only user errors, ie problems I created. .
  4. The option to penalty was quite clear/

The okay:

  1. Scorekeeping during the round was alright. I found it a bit clunky, and hard to go back after you've committed. I think in time this will improve as I get use to the controls. Overall it was an okay experience that I think would get better with more experience. You basically say how many strokes, how many putts at the end of the hole.
  2. Post editing. Yes, you can post edit. It's easier from the computer, but I think this should probably fall in to the not-so good category. I need to give it some time though, just like shot scope there is a learning curve here. It's probably good enough for here

The not so good (but maybe can be corrected)

  1. Club selection -- it was non-existent during this round. I think there is an option or something I need to do
  2. When doing my post-edits, I can change the number of putts. It's two separate screens. It also couldn't figure out where to do this on the phone at all.
  3. Chips and putts. This was as expected. Hard to track once you get in close unless you have sensors on the putter/chippers.

Let me give an example of this last one...

Not a terrible hole, I hit a good 8 iron to the green (one of the few of the day). But then I 3 putted. I actually think it someone figured out based off my walk path where the ball landed... it did land left side of the green bunker. So this one it got, but the others I had to correct for not hitting the green.. because I think the chips were not registered. I guess I'll be buying one of there small sensor packs in the near future.

So no club stats wasn't a big deal today. I'm still hitting the ball kind off terribly. Hoping I find my way back to the driver from a month ago... man, what a difference from 250... need to spend more range time... I think the stretching was helping. No slices today, which was interesting, just bad hits, and lots of stuff going left. We'll see if we can get back on track.

item.title: Turn on Club Prompt! CT10 small set - and a review of my terrible round
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I played with the watch some, and figured out that I need to turn the 'Club Prompt On' Great! I'll see how that performs the next go around.

I am highly considering getting the CT10 set of 3 to try out. The only issue I'm having is that I think I might eventually buy the whole set. It's 25 bucks a club vs 17.50 a club. There is also a tag that's like the shotscope (ct1), but says you need to tap it to register. I may give manual selection a try before going this route.

I didn't do a run down of the last 9 holes. It was a fun set. I am really struggling though, last two times have been rough. I drove the ball so well in Cambridge, and since then it's been a big struggle. Irons have been equally inconsistent.

I'll do my good, okay, terrible again

Good:

  • Hole 3. Despite a terrible mishit drive, and going over the green, you bogey'ed this hole.
  • Hole 7. You once again got a GIR. I think it was a 139 yard 8 iron (slightly uphill)

Okay:

  • Hole 6, I think it was an 8 Iron, that traveled 123 yards (this time slightly downhill). At least it got up in the air. Missed the green, but didn't miss terrible. Was able to chip on, and then 2 putt for bogey. That isn't terrble

Bad:

  • Everything else was pretty bad.
