    • Hole 1 a bad tee shot, struggled to get the ball moving to the hole
    • Hole 2 - easiest on the course, missed right in to the bunker, came out and 3 putted for a double
    • Hole 5, missed green again, this time way right, with a chip and 3 putt. (3 putts were bad this day)
    • Hole 8 - a pure disaster. Terrible off the tee, pushing the ball all over the wrong place. Lots of junk until I finally hit a clean iron 110 yards to the green... I put a score of 8 here, was pretty bad
    • Hole 9 - couldn't hit worth a damn, ended up dropping (I found my ball , but the shot was impossible) so I gave myself a 5, but probably a 6.

Total was a 46! I adjusted up 4 mulligans and penalties (not very high because i often just played the bad shot).

I didn't track the prior 9 at Northwest, but my scores have been trending in the wrong direction. I just feel like I am close to making a breakthrough. When I hit driver and irons well enough, and I don't 3 putt, I feel like I've got a pretty good shot... just that lack of consistency is killing me. It doesn't even matter what club, it could be any club and I lose it.

I honestly think... if I just played a little more, I could figure most of this out on the course. The only thing I can say is that the range time did improve my driver quite a bit... but I'm not sure if that was luck + feel or something else.

Anyhow, hope to get 9 holes in 2x a week now, and see where that takes us.

item.title: Massive heat wave == no golf. Another broken Club!
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So a massive oppressive heat wave, combined with a ton of work, left me with zero golf the last 2 weeks until yesterday's range session.

I can take one major lesson from yesterday's range session. Shorten your swing, and don't try to hit the ball hard. The only thing you should be trying to do is hit the ball right, even with the big clubs when you need distance. 30-60 yards shorter on the driver doesn't matter , keeping it in play is all that matters. 9 iron going 140 vs 100, doesn't matter. Keeping it in play and where you want it to go.

I really get in my head at the driving range, and hell it's just fun to whack the ball far. It's fun when I get in a groove and can hit my 7 irons 150+. None of this translates to the course though --- well, it does, but like every 5th shot.

Once I started just my quick short shots, and yes, again pushing my weight more forward to the left on setup (or earlier in the swing), things started improving. You have more misses left, but yea. Just happy that I found the driver again after the last couple times out I couldn't make it work right. Doesn't mean it's good enough to play, but at least there is hope.

I did receive my ct10s, haven't got a change to play them yet. Update when I do.

I lost another club! I broke my 8 iron on the backswing. Same sort of thing that happened on the pitching wedge. This happened as I was shorting up my swing. I am getting a lot of force in to the club at the early part of the down swing (which I'm not sure is good or not), but anyhow, broke at handle again. I cut it open just now, no rust, not sure what the issue is, no rust evident.

I think maybe I am too rough with the clubs sometimes... but then again, I'm not sure. Perhaps I left my clubs in the car one too many times (I mean sometimes you would drive to work with them to play after work). I have plenty of times grounded these clubs, so yea, I play pretty rough. The 8 iron (second to break), was my second most popular club, after the PW which broke last year.

At any rate... it's making my consider another set now... I liked the Maltby I purchased, but it was still a bit on the short side, wanted something a little in between that size and what I have now (which are just a tad longer than I like).

I actually just did some research and found out that there may be an issue with my shaft (True Temper), found others who have also broken shaft in same spot!!

item.title: First 'real' scorecard from Garmin Tracking --
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So this post will cover two topics (1) How did the Garmin perform tracking 9 holes. (2) How I played my latest 9 holes. Both have a lot of good, but probably more bad than good.

First up Garmin. First time I used the club tracking. There is a lot of 'I wish they would implement X' type comments here. It feels like a half finished product on the watch. Here are my thoughts

Good:

  1. It tracks shots pretty well, it only really missed one 'full club' shot today on the first hole. I was able to update it post hole. So whatever it does on that hit detection works very well. Everything from drives to a 30 yard flop it got!
  2. It auto picked up when I hit with the 'chipper' too with the CT10, so that worked out pretty good.

Bad/Ugly:

  1. Putting, even with the CT10 sensors is still a bit messy. It repeatedly got the putting very wrong. I wish it would prompt for 'how many putt's at the end of the hole. This was a much better system on the shot scope.
  2. At the end of the hole the interface to change things is complex, and I don't have it down yet. Maybe I could more easily update the scoring. It just seems overly complicated. Its ask for number of strokes... but it's been counting my strokes... so what if I just upped the number of putts, then shouldn't that just update my score. This is just very un-intuitive for me. Perhaps I will get better at this system over time, but initial thoughts are pretty blah.
  3. The post editing experience is atrocious. You have a separate screen/interface on the web site for adjusting your shots vs adjusting your putts (happens in the scorecard) and scores.. For instance, if I want to add a shot post round, then I go add place a shot roughly on the map and give a club. But to change the number of putts (btw, I can't see the number of putts on this screen), I've got to go back to the scorecard and update the scorecard. This is just a BAD UI decision. When I update the putt number, and you have my shots... why the hell don't you just update my score for the hole!!! I just realized my first update to this was so bad, that I now need to go back to update my score for everytime I updated my putts! IT doesn't happen automatically... So goofy...
  4. Also, I can't seem to zoom in and out either on the hole. Perhaps this experience is better on the phone, but so far what i've seen in the web site is really quite bad.
  5. I've got some stats which is good, but the stats display is pretty lousy. I was terrible off the tee today, and it shows on the chart well. It's just not a great interface again, poor design, poor experience. The approach and chip not so great.

So I am pretty critical. I've gotten to use two systems, and here are my basic pro/cons so far:

  1. Garmin will likely get the GPS right better than shot scope and be more reliable. It detects your contact well (which the tags on the clubs from shot scope were less reliable).
  2. Shot Scope was hands down a better experience on course, especially with the putting feature. Again, this is so far after 1 round
  3. Shot Scope post edit was orders of magnitude better experience than Garmin (So far... still learning)
  4. Shot Scope stats are presented much better in their portal, and much more informative.

So I went with Garmin, and I'm regretting my decision a little. I know I won't have the 'I missed a whole round', or 'I have a dead watch' with Garmin (I had multiple problems with shot scope, they replaced my watch twice), but Shot Scope got the golf experience so much better than Garmin did.

It's all about UI here, and a bit of the on course experience being simplified. Garmin covers a much wider range of products (most of it's watches can do this golf thing), but it really needs some additional work to get right. I do think 5 rounds in though my opinion will likely improve as I get better at using the watch and the app. It's tough with golf as you play for several hours and you want the tech to just get it right.

-----

So now on to my awful scoring!

.

A 49 (this was adjusted multiple times, mostly up, but a couple that were wrong down... don't like this about Garmin), but this does not include my mulligans (although their were less today, they were still out there, it just turns out my 2nd shots were mostly worse than the first).

The good

  1. Hole 4 was decent despite taking a mulligan, I hit a good 5hybrid after a bad 5h from the tee that bounced off a tree. Neither shot was great, but I decided to play the second with the 5 hybrid, and cleared the creek well, got a nice bounce of some canadian geese, and ended just short of the green. The chipper and 2 putt, got me in at 5.
  2. Hole 1 wasn't terrible either, a bad drive off the tee, a poor hybrid shot, and then a very nice 7i to the green (or just off, can't recall), that was a decent play. a 2 putt. If I had just punched it back here off the tee, this could have been a good hole
  3. Hole 9, terrible tee shot 147 yards with my driver (popped up in the air again), amazing 2nd shot with the 3h, 172 yards on to the fringe with a 3 putt. That's not a terrible bogey, and if I could do that on every hole I'd score in the 90s consistently.

The typical bad:

  1. Hole 2 and 3, double bogey's with mixes of good and bad shots. Terrible drive, followed by decent hybrid and PW shots that got me close enough. Hole 3 was interesting with the 9i up the hill a little longer than I though. My shots off the tee and hybrid her were not good
  2. Hole 7 , this was pretty bad drive off the tee, to the wrong fairway for 176 yards... at least it traveled some. I then hit again and sliced it off, so just played my sons ball back 100 yards from the green. This went to green with a good iron shot that made me look like an all star.

Ugly:

  1. Hole 6, always terrible, today was not exception... lost ball in creek had trouble off tee, etc etc.
  2. Hole 8... why this one always troubles me too. I sliced tee shot before finding something to play way off to the right 93 yards out. Missed a PW shot, so took another and then 3 putted... bad.
  3. Hole 6, which is usually a good hole. 3 Putt killed me here, I shanked my first shot (PW) and it only went 54 yards, then took the SW on ... 32 yards, and then 3 putt. Oh wait, that's 5 on the scorecard not 6 got adjust again.

item.title: The inconsistency dilemma, and how to correct it.
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
If I watch you tube, shorts, Facebook ,Instagram, I am bombarded with most well meaning information on the golf swing. The thing is, I can only really work on correcting one thing a time, and most of the time I'd rather just go out and play despite my wild swing inconsistencies.

Why am I inconsistent. Because I just don't swing a golf club usually more than once a week. Ranges are decent toll road + 35 minute round trip away. The outing is usually an 1.5 hours +. I get to play if I'm lucky once a week. If I am doing things okay, and I stay consistent with a range + 9 or 18 holes a week, I start to improve a bit.. Basically , my ball striking gets better, maybe not my swing, but my striking gets better, my putting gets better, I typically play better with more reps... that's a pretty obvious statement. And when I layoff for too long, I play worse.

I think back to early summer when I was really driving the ball well, I was getting lots of range reps. This was good. Now, I am driving the ball pretty poorly because of lack of reps. I found my driver on the range last week, but this week I was struggling. So okay...

The obvious :) solution to this is building the sim. Building the sim will improve the striking with more reps if, and only if ... you use it 3 or 4 times a week. The rub on this though is that it becomes a chore to setup if I do it in the garage, and doing it 3 to 4 times may not happen. Also, my hip (which has come back ugly again), could keep that tampered down.

So I had another look in the garage the other day, and I think I can make the setup work better. Basically getting the swing plane underneath the the middle, but a slight bit more left, to the wife's side of the garage. I'm not quite sure of this, but it felt better when I swinging there. Moving right seems to create a problem as you can't be all the way right otherwise my 'steep' swinger ends up coming right up to the garage rails, and I come around , but I'm left with less room. Getting the ball under the left middle rail seems like it would the right solution, ball under that should you leave you never hitting the rail if you don't come in steep (natural training there, but not too opinionated, you can still be pretty steep), that should leave enough come around for most clubs (driver may be a problem and need to test this). Shanks left are a little close to the window, but that can probably be protected.

So what am I looking at for cost. I had this spec'd out awhile back.

What I already have:

  1. Mat/Insert. THis is decent, need to cut the mat a little better, but it serves it purpose
  2. Nets. May not use in next version
  3. Computers. Maybe have old machines that could run software
  4. Garmin R10 - likely not use, as the behind to net room is just not really long enough. It works, but it isn't great.

What you really need to get upgraded to something more usable

  1. A camera based launch monitor. I could go square for now,
  2. A projector - time to switch out the nets
  3. A retractable screen with side panels. 0 This is a tough one since I do have kids that will shank off, but I think we can get closer to the screen with this.
  4. Some additional setup infrastructure - there could be some power things you need to do to get all this right.

Your looking at several thousand dollars on the screen setup (maybe 2500 with a fair amount of DIY). Your then looking at another 1000 to 5000 for a real launch monito. So you are looking at roughly 7500 bucks for this setup. Versus the range (18 dollars for a extra large bucket). Lets say you need about 50 range sessions to get pretty decent per year at around 200 balls... That's say 1000 dollars... so it takes about 7 years to recoup the cost on here, but you likely get some cost recouped from the tolls and time you'd save. Trying to make my argument here. I think I want to do it, I've completed some of the house stuff that was needed... and the rest should be done in the Fall which is perfect time for this project.

item.title: Sligo Creek - Fun outing, and a birdie!
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So decided to try a new course today with my younger son, Sligo Creek. It's a 9 hole short course, similar to Northwest Inside 9 , with 7 Par 4s (most of them on the shorter/narrower side), and 2 Par 3s.

I'll do my good/okay/bad/ugly as usual

  1. I got a legit birdie on Hole 8. Was with another father/son pair who recommended to take an iron shot first instead of driver. The hole is about 250 yards, so it seemed drivable, but the creek and pond were around the dangerous 200 yard zone. A good drive ends up there, especially downhill. Driver is the dangerous play, so I hit a good 7i, 146 yards, leaving about 110 to the hole. The second 7i (uphill), I hit a little differently, I decided to go at it long, as it seemed an okay play, and I hit it just long, but it came down the slope on the green to almost back in to the hole, left a 2 foot putt for BIRDIE!

The okay:

  • Hole 1 - I hit the hybrid, and not particularly well. I actually attempted a provisional, but that one donked off way right... The 3 hybrid 137 yards is not a good play for me... that's 175 club just a couple days ago. The hole is 261, but I had struggled with the driver Thursday and the fairway was tight. So anyone I followed up playing it a bit short instead of long with the 9i for 92 yards, and then the chipper for 26. If I hadn't of sucked with the 3 putt, this would have just been bogie, and that's what I am trying to play for.
  • Hole 3 - Good drive (209 yards), flew straight. It didn't feel like a strong drive, just a controlled one which I was okay with on hole 3. I then had to hit the PW . It shanked left, I then chippered out. Any hole on in 3 is a good hole IMO, but then I 3 putted. A 2 putt here would have made this a 'good hole'.
  • Hole 4 - I'll take this as a decent hole since I hit a bad hybrid off the tee and recovered. I hit PW that didn't really go very far, but traveled up the hill okay. Then LW for a 2 putt.
  • Hole 6: This is almost good, except I had to take a drop. So it sits here. Driver went slice right, but playable. I took a provisional (because I thought I lost it), and then one easily would have been the drive of the day if I had found it and played it. My 9i once again really clean, traveled too long, and now I'm hunting around behind the hole. Didn't find it, took a less generous drop to LW and then 2 putt. A bogey would have been good here, but it's not a real one (Mulligan on this hole)
  • Hole 7 - A legit bogey this time, Drive sliced 179 yards, so was playing in the rough. 7i centered things back, but didn't travel. SW, played well at 50 to get on for a 2 putt... if I played every hole this well it would have been good.

The Bad

  • Hole 2: Despite me 'scoring' a bogie here, I give it a bad because of the struggles with the SW. The SW has become my nemesis, sometimes great, sometimes awful. IT's from my old Wilson set (lost the PXG one last year). Couldn't connect with it. I actually took me 3 shots, so this one was really a double, but I mulligan one, before the 3rd SW actually got on green and you sunk a decent putt. (Mulligan on this hole)
  • Hole 5 - I 'popped the driver, but it landed decently for a playable hole. Then I did the dreaded 9i should go 110, but I caught it 'right' and it went 134. I really struggled with SW again here, knocked it over, and then knocked it back (4 on). Just realized I marked it 3 putt, so this one should have been a 7 (correcting now)

The ugly:

  • Hole 9 -- saved this for last. Mr. generous snowman 8. Drive was 191(Mulligan on this one too, as the first kind of skidded off so I played the provisional on this). Then I actually shot a good 9i, but that still left a bit to the hole. Where it got bad was the SW again! I bladed it over , but I then recovered with the chipper. Your on in 4... but then the putting was plain terrible. No control, took me 4 shots to get it in the hole.

So overall score... same as Thursday, a 49. But less mulligans, so in general a better outing. A little less struggle overall. I find hitting my irons kind 'choppy' leaves me in a bit on control, and I'm happy with this. I only really am playing 2 irons (9 and 7), and then PW is in there... the GW I think is probably similar to the PW, so I'm not sure what to do with that.

Driver could be better... at least I had some in play today. I know I was hitting it fairly long for a bit earlier this year, but now I am struggling with my swing, so just trying to keep it in play rather than swinging out is fine for now. I'll take consistency and playable balls over distance at this point.

So a comment on the Garmin experience: It was better today, but not quite great. I am still not great with the controls, and it seems too much work when you pass a hole to go back and correct. Navigation is still difficult, but you've only really played 27 holes at this point. It's hard to learn on the fly, but I think a few more rounds and you'll have it down. It's really easy to make mistakes, then they are hard to correct while on the course... Again, should get better in time.

I should also mention my son hit the ball really well today. His putting stinks, but if he had that down he'd compete with his dad.

item.title: 2 days in a row!
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
This is probably a bad idea, but we are playing again today after a great outing yesterday.

Up today is the Crossvines! We'll try to get 9 holes in between 6:30-8:30, then drive back home. We played this course once before and had some fun (it was July 13 last year, day trump was shot), but only got through 7 holes if I recall correctly.

So lthis is way longer Par 4s then I saw yesterday... which means, I'm gonna have to play the driver. Looking at the sheet, I'm gonna play from the White's , first hole is 326, and second hole is 467. Even the red's for my son is 417 on the second par 5, so this should make a challenging start.

Looking at the flyover, first hole is a slight dogleg (and a tigher fairway than some of the other courses we've played. Looks like you are probably 3 shots to the green the way you've been hitting, and should play it easy

Second hole is a pretty straight and long Par 5! Challenge here looks like some bunkers on either side of the green... and of course the length

3rd hole looks like a nice break, and pretty pedestrian 176 yard Par 3... the trick always here is what club ? The right club is probably my hybrid, but

4th a pretty straight par 4... we 369 yards. This is a tough spot for me..and average drive of 200 leaves me 170 out... a good drive leaves me 120 out. A bad drive leaves me 200+ out

5th and 6th are the same experience... All pretty similar straight fairways but not super wide so a little bit of challenge to keep it clean... & is a long Par 5, that I believe I Par'ed the last go around.

Hole 8 , if we get there, over water, so this is challenge... Hole 9 is another straight shot tighter fairway.

Just looking through the back 9 --- looks a bit more challenging then the front. More dog legs, more trees

It looks like this course is going to require some distance, even playing from the white tees, so I'm gonna need to get the driver working. My plan is to start it conservative and see if I can get it going a bit more distance as I move through.

Looking at how I played it last time, my driver really failed me, so it does appear that if I just keep it in play I can do well.

item.title: Crossvines the 2nd time
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
A really good experience this time around, course was in amazing condition. My game stunk per usual, but I'm not too beat up about it. Had a few good shots and more revelations

First off though... the Garmin as predicted is getting better as I get more use to it. I still made a couple mistakes and had smaller corrections, but this time I actually threw the penalty in there.

For the most part, I am playing my first ball too, so less mulligans. I think this is more a luck thing, but also when you play with others, you don't hold up as much, so taking more than 2 tee shots is not so great

Overall, I was 15 over again, a 48 over 8 holes. A rough 108 score relative over a 72 par course. I'll give my good/bad/ugly as usual.

Good:

  • Hole 2- So I hit a decent drive, but it went left again (hook -- this is interesting). 196 yards, so I'll take it. Then hit that 3h, 209 yards on the second hit, leaving it nicely in the fairway. Wow my 3h is great today (more on that later) -- a 9i hit just right for 101 yards, and then a 2 putt this time for bogie
  • Hole 7. I'll give myself a good here, despite a small struggle. , I finally hit a decent drive 226 yards. After the 175 yard on the previous hole (which also went straigtht), it was nice to hit a straight one that went close to where I thought it would go. I however did end up in the rough, and just off a sand bunker. So the 3h failed me here again, a mishit that wasn't all that terrible only traveled 78 yards. But then I hit another 3h, 192 yards (yes this was longer than many of my drives). Unfortunatly, I hit SW over, then LW back on for 2 putt, so a double, but not a bad double.

Okay:

  • Hole 1 - Bogie, well, I think it was, so I am going to give myself it. My first drive hooked left, low distance (again) -- 154. My second shot with a 3h, 182 was great though, with a LW on, but a 3 putt. So 3 on, 3 to get it in... bad putting sunk you here, but really wasn't a bad hole... anytime your 3 on, you give your change for a +1, which is generally what your going for.
  • Hole 4 - I will say this one was okay, but I'm not sure I played correctly. To be honest, I have a 239 yard drive that appears to have gone right this time, I didn't find the ball so estimated, then GW it through some trees to a nice 100 yard 9i shot for a 2 putt. Close enough...
  • Hole 5, another double, but not sooo terrible. Drive was straight but distance lacked (175 yards). 3hybrid failed here and only went 93 yards, then I hit a good 93 yard 9i, but that just missed. So I was 4 to get to the green as chippered on. then a decent 2 putt.
  • Hole 8 I'll give an okay too, despite another double. I hit over water, with a 7i 147 yards. I missed right, but that seemed to be the safer play. My problem shot, and it was a tough shot, was a SW over a bunker to hit the green (par 3), and I bladed it... hate the SW and would like to replace. I then had LW, and then 2 putt...

Bad:

  • Hole 3This one wasn't as terrible as the double score suggests. First shot with 5h this time, only puttered out 76 yards... then a PW for 87, that actually went over. I tried to control, but didn't have good control, had to chipper on (it's a par 3, so 2 on is the goal), and then 3 putt... so yea, not great.
  • Hole 6: Another okay drive, again a little left on this. Almost same as previous hole, where I hit a bad 3h that puttered out only 97 yards (and directionally wrong), then a miss with an iron (23 yards), and PW that lands in the sand trap, then on for 3 putt... triple boogie .

Missed the 9th hole, was only able to hit driver -- but I hit it decent for 210 yards (watch marked it , because I then hit an iron to have the ball disappear off to no where land.

Lets discuss some clubs in general over the weekend and how I am performing

  1. Driver is very inconsistent. I started the year (of course I don't have metrics on this) nice and long and straight. Playing in June I was really quite good with the driver, and I think I was hitting enough 250+. I feel like my average should be at least 240, but I am averaging way less than that (even on good shots). I've never been able to capture a good round where the driver was on... but I do know if I had captured early on, especially at River Marsh, I'd have some good numbers. I need to spend more range time, but definitely the feel of coming around the body was helping. There was something else I was doing though at the range that was really working for a bit, and I haven't really found it again. I could possibly look at swapping driver, but I know I can hit this driver...
  2. 3 Hybrid. Let me put some numbers here: 182, 209, 192, 179. Average ~190 when hit well over the weekend. It's a good club for me that I hit well. Occasional miss hits, but the miss hits still travel. This is the MMT 80 Stiff... and I've been thinking about trying this out with another iron to see if I like it on my irons too.. .maybe move through the entire bag with this shaft. This is a good club for anything in the 175+ range.
  3. 5 Hybrid. It's been better than in the past... it's the 150-175 club. Its that Project X club, and it feels like the length is a bit short (but maybe)
  4. Irons -- and really I'm only talking 7 and 9 at this point. I love my 7i, let me do the same number game: 123, 147, 146, 147, so a rough 140 yarder. The 9i without looking I hit less hard typically and more finese. It's like the 95-105 trying to land it in the right spot.
  5. PW - less than 95, more than 75. The shaft length on this bugs me. It's faulty
  6. GW - not used a lot lately, perhaps a 50-60 should see this.
  7. SW - old club, not a fan, feel like this one I should be replacing shortly but doesn't necessarily need to match
  8. LW - this is the chipper, and I love this club, just rarely makes mistakes, but you can't play it in all situations.
  9. Putter - been better with the putter with more practice in the past. Struggling this year... don't believe my numbers are very good, lots of mistakes...

So have come back around to a few things:

  • I think I play the irons a little longer (maybe 1/4-1/2 inch), if anything I'd shorten up 1/4 inch in my next set of irons to see how we do.
  • I really like the MMT shaft, it's a graphite that feels iron on my 3h. I think that would keep my launch a little lower. I am considering trying an 8 iron Maltby with that for experimentation.
  • If that ended up working out, I'd like just reshaft the 5h to the right size with the same. The only knock I have here is if I go with some new wedges, then I've got a fit problem.

item.title: The right feel?
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Found a couple things at the range today before the humidity got to me.

#1. Loosened up with that drill I saw on Danny maude. Hold bicep 5 on each side moving club, then moving with hips. Right after this I hit 9i on island ( about 140 yards) multiple times. I fell apart shortly after that, but those hits felt pretty good

#2. That feel I mentioned in previous post, I found it again. I can only describe the feeling as holding the back swing a bit , like a purposeful lag, that I feel storing up energy. It almost feels like I'm hitting off my back foot, but I'm not. This seems to lead to some more control with the woods. The only thing is , I don't know how to recreate the feel. I know it when I got it, but not quite sure how to repeat... Needs some more work

Got a bit of swing video. It still looks like timing is off , wish I could figure out more of my faults from this besides my swing being ugly.

Not going to play for a week... Too humid beach week ..

item.title: More range time with some implications
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Okay, so I hit 100 balls today, was by myself so had a better feel for what was going on.

  1. My ball flight with the irons is super high. I know mat's effect this, but I think I have a small issue here. Good thing is that they tend to land soft. The missing 8 iron is kind of a big deal for me, as there is definitely space between the 9-7. The PW is the same length and the GW, but it's definitely a bit longer, but not too bad... I can't hit my old 8 iron, It needs to come out of the bag. I see most guys with these much lower and longer trajectories... I try to deloft the club, but I'm not very successful there... it's interesting I know it's good that I get spin and loft, but I think I'm too high and too far.
  2. I could play a round with SW, GW, 9i,7i,3hy, 3wd (optional),d, p, and the chipper. That's 8 clubs, instead of 14, and I think I would actually play better. The 6i I can't ever seem to hit (without a lot of work), the 5hy is confusing but has been valuable in the past... it's a bit short and not fitting with the rest of the clubs. The PW is so close to the GW, you might not need it.
  3. I hit my driver straight and far today once I figured it back out. I'd say I was hitting it further than anyone at the range (not sure if this is a function of the balls, or just nobody hitting long at the range). I was out by the 225 marker on several shots. The wood was also going well off the tee. It felt like it did early in the season, where it was easy and long. Same kind of hold it back feeling. Wasn't even blasting it hard.
  4. "Stay down", I found myself forgetting to stay down, and that was leading to some bad shots. Especially with irons.
  5. Trying to 'not hit it hard' vs 'hit it hard' today was interesting. You definitely need to put some juice behind it to get it moving, but after a few hits it was getting closer between hitting hard and not as the ball striking got better. I wish you could keep it nice and easy, but I still tend to try to through too much juice at the ball, and that definitely leads to some faults.
  6. I got straighter, and my dispersion improved the more balls I hit.
  7. Another thing I found, stepping behind the ball before I go up to hit, and looking out where I want to hit seemed to spatially get me in a better place... so keep doing that.

So I have made the decision to go full sim over the next couple months. I think both I and the kids will get a bunch of enjoyment out of it. Allow us to practice more easily, and improve ball striking. I'd love to see the kids and I get consistent enough with the 50yd+ game to make our outings a bit more interesting.

I am going with a setup that will have remote controlled screen, with projector and an upgraded launch monitor. All in all, I think I will be about 6K in for this project. I have the money so thought , why not now.

I'm thinking of setting up an auxiliary tv in the room to have football on on Sundays... not sure this will work , as I'm still working through the setup. It does appear that the best setup will be a centered under the middle of the garage with a 94" width. At first I thought I might split the garage, but now I'm reconsidering. By split, I was thinking to bias the left half of the garage to the sim, and the right half to a TV setup. But now I am thinking the 105" length centered might be a better setup. The extra foot seems like a better deal, but will require to do the TV side mounted (which may not fit right with the car).

I love obsessing about these things... will figure a setup out and make the purchase soon.

item.title: The Garage Sim
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I am going all in, but it's way more complicated than I thought. Every time I think I have it figured out, I end up having a new wrinkle thrown in.

Lets start with current setup, and a picture:

I'll just bulletize:

  • R10 launch monitor - it does the job, but placing it way behind left less room. It misses a ton of shots, the setup is complicated (phone to computer nonsense). It's just
  • Netting - again does the job, but not ideal. First off the setup. It's a big pain, I end up running around for about 5 minutes or longer trying to remember what hooks in to what when I'm setting up, getting up on stools, attaching and re-attaching. It's a pain --- add that to removing the cars from the garage, you can look at up to 10 minutes to get everything in place. It's just not great. The netting would occasionaly let balls through if not setup just right. Net side impact is pretty good, and I have sent a few off that direction.
  • No screens. My typical setup was an old laptop hooked in to GSPRO (it actually worked fine with an older nvidia card a couple years back). I kept saying I would move a TV to the right wall, but it never happened.
  • Mat is actually good, I have an insert I cut out since this picture. Needs a bit more work to get it flush (cut wasn't perfect), but that is good.

So I decided this was actually get used way more if we did it right so want to go with the full projector + TV setup. A better (camera-based) launch monitor.

The tough part is the screen, projector and protection areas, again bulletized:

  • Screen - I have come back to a metech roller with Poly Spacer screen. It gets recommended most on reddit as a setup. That part is easy, the hard part is size. I started at just under 9 feet, and now I am looking at 16 feet. So I am buying the argument that wider is going to be better --- it's going to catch more balls, more immersive. But then I end up down the path of 16:9, and 4:3. As I get wider I need more height to get things to line up on 16:9 .. I think I am getting closer, but it also complicates getting the right projector with throw ratio. It's definitely not as adjustable as I thought, and you have to get the research right before purchasing.
  • Baffle - you need this for the screen, something you don't typically think about but need to protect the top and roller. I think I found some less than 100 dollar solutions on this from golf sim sites. (Carls, etc)
  • Gutter (bottom) protection + Weight. 3 things here:
    • Weight on bottom pocket of screen needed (or bungees to wall?) -
    • Lower Screen protection - door draft protection might be good just to lay in front of screen, or some more foam
  • Side/Shank Protection - I am going to budget less here. I found some home theater black curtains. Put it on some track and we are good. The complication has arisen though with the roller being wider than the screen, which leaves a 'gap' that could cause a problem. My thought was get tracking that would push up way in to the corner, and then track it next to the roller working in some. But now it looks like there will be a gap, so need to thing about either just hanging from the ceiling (again, hate the idea of having to get up on a stool every time). I looked at other retractable options, but it seems crazy to spend another 1000 or more , when the solution could be more like 150. T
  • Ceiling - this is another tough one. I need something. Before the net would catch with a bit of slack, and I still had a few fly up... Some have used gym mats on the ceiling, others foam, acoustic tiles, and other materials. I thing 3-4 feet is enough here, but you still want to do something, and the wider I go the more coverage we may need. This one you might not need to get right , right away, but you'll need a solution sooner than later.
  • Flooring - another 'gonna go budget' here. I'm already spending a lot, so horse stall mats seem like the best solution I could later add turf to the mat. Still have some work to do to figure out which ones (3x4 1/2", 4x6 3/4"), and how much (do you need full width of screen, for aesthetics this will be good, but you shouldn't be hitting too many outside of middle 10 feet of screen). Should probably at the very least get 3 x 4x6, but if you apply turf, that could get pretty high, or if just use the cheap emerald turf cut, that would probably work.

The easy parts (or at least mostly decided parts)

  • Likely a BLP w/ club data
  • Mat stays the same (it's good)

So you can see, just not a buy and go but your researching several areas. I think it may be a staged thing now, but the 'big' and fix the rest. Ie, buy the screen first, then the projector, then the flooring then the curtains. Make sure each piece works with the next.

item.title: Garage Sim - Update #1
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I am making my purchases in stages, but I've got my first 1K in to this now:

  • Metech Retractable 158 inch (616.18 w/tax + shipping)
  • Poly Spacer 156x114 inch screen (391.2 w/tax + shipping)
  • Baffle - Carl's Place from Indoor Golf Outlet ($42.40 w/ tax + shipping)

Total was 1049.78. I am budgeting myself 6K to do this.

I am still a little concerned about swinging driver in the Garage, or the kids doing it, but I think we are okay with this

Here is where I am with my estimated notes:

  • Flooring $200
  • Side Curtains with tracking $200
  • Ceiling Protection $350 (maybe high)
  • BLP $2365 w/ 10% Off (still likely to go this way vice square)
  • Cage $150 - protect the most expensive thing in SIM
  • Subscription $500 - this kills me, but I might be able to deduct some from my work plan
  • Projector $1140 - likely a BENQ LH600ST 1080p projector. I am limited options on where I can mount, and this fits with the 9'5" throw for my screen and adjustable zoom. I thought about cheaping out here, but this seems like a reasonable compromise. Still this could be a possible return. Where I want to mount is right between the garage tracks, and it could cast shadows, or not fit correctly.
  • Projector Ceiling Mount $50 - Haven't shopped this yet, waiting to make full decision on this.
  • Blackout curtains for windows - $110, not sure yet, just measured windows, but this will cut light close to zero in garage for projector. Would rather do this sooner than later
  • Total: 6114.78

So that comes in right around where I think. I'm concerned my delay on the BLP and they will put the price back where it was. It seems like a good deal at current price though. The Lpi at $1000 less without the club data, and doesn't have a battery (plugged in the whole time).

There are some other considerations that I haven't fully gotten to

  • Electrical work, which at this point is just me adding some extension cords with power strips. It's getting a little messy though.

Then there is the labor, in order of how I will likely do things:

  • Putting up the Screen - this is toughest part as it's 13 feet, hoping I can hang and then put the roller in place we will see 2-3HR (because there will be lots of measuring. Includes adding the screen to the roller , getting power to the motor, etc
  • Putting the baffle in should be an easy hang - 15min
  • Hanging the Side Curtains with tracking - 1HR (again with the measuring and placing
  • Hanging the blackout rollers - 30min
  • Fixing the flooring to the turf carpet and cutting flooring to size - 30min - 1HR
  • Getting my cut right on the hitting surface 20 min to fix up
  • Affixing ceiling protection - 1HR to 2HR
  • Mounting Projector 1 HR (because I'll be trying multiple locations), will also
  • Software and launch monitor setup 1-2HR

It's a multi-day job likely, starting with hopefully the screen this weekend, then I will work on the curtains, then the projector & flooring, then the

Last thing up will be the ceiling. I have a few marks, they aren't bad, but I think it will likely be the using it before I actually finish that part out. Likely going to with gym tiles, but not sure how I want to affix to the ceiling yet.

item.title: Garage Sim Update #2
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
No work has begun, as I hurt my back and need to rest for at least one more day. I can't put the roller up anyhow, since it hasn't arrived.

I do plan on rounding out all the purchasing today. I have decided on curtains, but not the tracking . It will be easier to see when I get the screen up, but the way I imagine it now is some tracking that comes from behind the screen around (slight J shape). Only out 5 feet.

The window curtains may or may not purchase later.

I've purchased the ceiling tiles and hardware to mount -- largest part of the job, and will start on that as soon as I get the screen up. Ceiling tiles, then baffle, might also need some foam attached to the baffle.

That leaves the rest of the big purchase which is the BLP, Projector (3600 total), that I will likely make today.

The flooring can be covered last, as I think that is just a couple local trips to pickup mats and staple some fake turf too. Also will need that weight for the bottom of screen or protection at the bottom. This will all play out as I get things up. I may need to put a gromet in the screen and use some bungees to attach to wall while in play. Will have to be careful not to try to pull the screen up when attached.

item.title: Garage Sim Update #3 - Netting down, square ordered
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So first off, I've decided on the budget build. I am trying to do the upgrade under $3500. I have enough pieces received now that I can start building.

So purchases since last post:

  • I ordered the square (along with a protective case and TPX balls). This actually is costing less than my retractable screen. The only thing I didn't like about the square is that it won't work well with the garage open during daytime. I could see this being a small problem in the future, but with winter approaching likely not. Square was 740.94, TPX balls x36 were 89.03, and protective from frugal fixer , 69.5. Likely get most of this early next week
  • Because I can not have light, next purchase was Blackout Roller Curtains from Amazon , 125.06. Arrives Sunday, likely install next week.

What's left:

  • Projector - I found a Benq TH671ST an hour away for $600, but haven't pulled the trigger because the 2 hours of driving isn't worth it. Same rough cost on ebay... There are a couple of other BenQ projectors I've been looking at, but I notice not everyone advertises the correct model, and there seems to be some confusion on specifics (specifically the LH600ST, I've seen as both WUGXA, and WXGA) . Anyone, still working through this, I will also need some sort of protection around this. I've seen a few viewsonic x2 variants for sale as well, but mixed reviews on how they work. I really would prefer to have something with both horz/vert keystone. The TH671ST has only vertical. I also will need a mount for this, along with some protection. Thinking through options on that such as the metal baskets I've seen online or mounting some polycarbonate under garage rails if it goes where I think it will.
  • Flooring - Still likely stall mats, and I'll likely do this last. Putting some turf on top
  • Curtains - Damn, have I ever shopped for side curtains. It's either too small, too light, not sure of tracks. Because I have a very wide screen, I am less concerned about have this day 1, but to finish it out with the flooring is likely 2 weeks out.
  • GSPro... Excited for some of the courses in there.

To do list:

  1. Install the screen. This will be the hardest part of the job , motor + roller + screen attachment. But once you have this your good...
  2. Install the Foam panels on ceiling. This will likely be the second hardest part of the job just because you have like 18 panels, 4 screws a panel attaching while on a ladder. Not fun...
  3. Install the baffle -- buy and attach foam if you think necessary...

Once that's in place, we can run some tests, and do some further measurements...

Then

  1. Install Blackout Roller Curtains - Will need to install prior to setting up square
  2. Setup Square, with protector, and balls. Measure out and marking for proper distance and mat placement. This involves a lot of things, setting up software, computer etc etc. I will likely for now just use my work computer until I decide or a more permanent solution. It's
  3. Buy GSPro
  4. Install Projector with projector mount and protection
  5. Finish out with Flooring and Curtains

Project plan in place!!! Now that I have all this, hoping to have the full setup in place in about 2 weeks.

Things I might be missing... a spotlight for the hitting area. Laser Alignment (although mostly reading this is unnecessary).

Exciting little project... but unfortunately has kept me off the golf course...

item.title: Build Progress - First snafu of the build
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I had my first issue in my build-out. I ordered a screen that ended up being too large for the roller. A bit of miscommunication with the vendor, I should have double checked what they were advising me,. Anyhow, the vendor is making it right. The screen needs be in somewhat shorter than the roller!

So the Metech roller was harder to install than I thought. I spent a good half an hour pounding two pieces of the roller together. In retrospect I saw a tip on using some silicon lubricant, and that made things go quicker. Should have done that, but it's done now. I went to install the screen on the roller as a check before installing the brackets. That's when I discovered the issue with the screen.

I did install my two pieces of 1x4 to the ceiling, and that seems good to go, so brackets go up on there. I'm not sure how to get a good measurement on the bracket placement though. I think all I can really do is get it up, and leave some play in the bolts before tightening them up. The first one doesn't need to be precise, but the 2nd one will have to balance on the ladder while we lift and measure to get in place, and then eventually tighten it up. I may try that on Wednesday or Thursday.

I've already received the square... it came in like 2 days despite a bunch of places saying out of stock. Haven't opened it up yet. Some 'nearly mint' TP X Pix balls also came from lostgolfballs. My blackout blinds are also in the garage ready to install. I am only lacking curtains + flooring to get to the done state. May add some additional lighting to the setup for

item.title: Build update
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
More construction than a golf update.

I haven't had a chance to work on things this week, but plan on an easier workout and then spending some time installing things today. Here is my construction plan for the weekend:

Today:

  1. Attempt to hang the roller. I may need another ladder, or something tall to rest the roller on. Like a saw horse, but really high... I'm almost tempted to roll my fridge out because that would do the job, but might need to get creative ... perhaps a temporary sling using some of the bungee cords hooks that I have. This would make sense, and give me more flexibility and getting in in place correctly!
  2. Install the blackout curtains - this should be easy , except for the cleaning portion. Fingers crossed

Tomorrow:

  1. Baffle & Ceiling tile - this will take an hour an or two . Think the tile goes in first and then hook the baffle. Perhaps do this after the next trip to lowes or home depot. Should probably add some extra foam to the back of the baffle... whatever is cheap. It just a bit of extra protection
  2. Go get flooring - mine as well get this done, it's pretty straight forward, but involves me driving 30 minutes. Also involves getting more 'turf' carpet to attach to the floor.

Sunday:

  1. Install Screen - supposed to arrive by end of day
  2. Test! - determine whether additional side curtains will be needed

I made a mistake by ordering these light to socket things from china, and won't show up for another 2 weeks... so may need to just suck it up and drive back to lowes this weekend (They have the same thing)

So the lowes/Home Depot list

  1. Light Socket to 3 prong
  2. Foam for the baffle
  3. Floor tile - artificial grass
  4. Carpet Tape
  5. Separate trip to Tractor supply for mats.

This gets us to test, still have the all important finishing the following weekend (but may wait in hopes of getting the right projector at right price for prime day)

Finishing:

  1. Projector and mount
  2. Build cage to protect projector
  3. Pin light
  4. (Optional) Add additional Strip lights garage for finishing

Software

Going to wait to purchase GSPro... took a look a the square stuff, and it actually seems pretty decent. I think we will be just about centered to the screen too, so should produce a decent experience.

Just writing through this helps get the build out right.

item.title: Build Update - Roller in place
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So yesterday I installed the Metech roller. This was going to be the hardest part of the job, but didn't end up being too bad. I ended up using hooks and a bungee cord to keep the roller up while I installed the motor side. That worked great. Motor side went in fairly easily as I measured out roughly where to install on the 1 by 4 I had installed last week. See picture below

I then installed the second bracket using the roller to check the measurements. This was a bit tougher to get in place, mostly just tough getting the bolts to catch with the pilot holes I drilled so I could crank in.

I pulled down on the installation after completed with some bungee cords and everything is solid to the ceiling. Not impressive without the screen and a projector, but the roller install itself in the next pic:

Then added the blackout curtains from amazon. Hard to tell right now, but they should do the job.

So that all went pretty well. The screen is still expected to arrive on Sunday, and that should get us to the initial testing phase, or at least a yes or no on whether it's safe to hit. Some concern without a panel on the left side, a VERY errant ball could escape and hit the window. I feel like this would be quite the issue if it happened.

So what's up next:

  1. Ceiling tile install - May be easier than I thought, just some measuring and then go to work I think. Baffle should be simple a couple of the dry wall hooks through the ceiling tiles. Adding some foam on the back of the baffle, not sure how I will secure this, but that will part of this job too.
  2. Cleanup of Garage -- needs more cleanup than initially anticipated.
  3. Fixup mat - I need to cut about another 1/4 to 1/2 inch out of the base mat, so that the filler goes in properly. This is always a pain, even with a sharp razor.
  4. Floor mats - won't be getting today. Have a tire issue and the idea of driving further than comfortable is a problem.

I skipped ahead on the launch monitor and software. That is basically ready to go, I need to install on a laptop, but it's really a good system they setup. I played with their swing stick just to get a feel for the software. No problems with the protector and reading the ball (so far), but the ball is still stationary at this point, but I get the green light for 'ready' to hit in multiple modes. Even in my not purely dark office.

Right now the software I count is 20 18 hole courses, with another 7 on the way including a 27 hole course. With the included credits, we would get 18 full rounds for 3 people (55 rounds!). If we played twice a week and did 18 holes, that would last us 2.5 months . MY guess we'll get closer to 4-5 months on that 1000 credits as not everyone will play every time! But even if you used max, you'd be looking at about $175 dollars a year.

Doing the GSPro comparison, $250 a year, it comes out just a bit more. I can see us switching this up at some point. I like squares model so far, but love the idea of playing some of the local courses I've played (and not played) on GSPro (River Creek, Needwood, Falls, Whiskey Creek). Would be fun to build out some of the local courses around here too...

item.title: Screen Sized Right, Screen in place - Charity Scramble in a week!!
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
This keeps growing and changing as I get further down the road.

I got the screen in place. It's a perfect fit now, and rolls up just fine! The projector is on the way tomorrow, I have someone delivering off FB marketplace

Today I bought some rebar and some foam to stuff in the bottom of screen to weight it down a bit when playing. It looks like a pretty tight squeeze, so that's going to be a bit of a mess.

Still haven't done the ceiling. I have decided that I am going to use 8 tiles to start. I can always expand, but don't think I will need. 3 rows of 4 tiles, so the width is 8 feet, the dept is 6 feet. I can always adjust this out by adding 2 feet on each side if I want, but it seems overkill. The baffle will go over (and around), making that pretty easy to get in place.

The problem I've identified now is on the sides. It's a bit of a larger issue than I though since I see a gap to the window for a very wayward shot. Not likely, but not out of realm of possibility. It also gets complicated because ideally you want the curtain to come around and out. The rest I can kind of deal with as we move forward. A golf ball in to the wall on the right is not a big deal... it's just the garage drywall... however, I think it would be nice to put some curtains on either side.

So while writing this I think it's decided the curtains will be necessary. I've also decided that I am going to put some recessed lights in to replace the light bulbs, and maybe put a small cage around for protection.

Also, was about to order the stall mats, I should have pulled the trigger, but uncertain whether I need 2, 3, or 4! I need more measuring, likely it's 3 with some cuts on the 3rd.

All this said... the projector comes today, the mount, etc. etc. There is still a ton to do, but I just found I'm doing the charity scramble on Monday! I thought I had a couple weeks, but nope.

----

Update 10/1:

So I started putting the ceiling together yesterday, then a kid got sick and had to run to the doctor... so I can't seem to make any progress! I am also feeling a bit under the weather, so sensitive to that as well.

I also realized I made a mistake on the rebar and insulation. This isn't going to work, and either a weighted battle rope or sand filled old hose seems to be the better option.

So now the order of operations :

  1. Ceiling tiles up
  2. Projector mount and test
  3. Electrical mounting (but this somewhat depends on what you need to do with the curtains.
  4. Measure out a proper hitting location and purchase stall mats for the area. Attach old/new carpet to stall mats with tape. Tape up your setup

Those 3 things will get you to a working simulator , but then you need to prioritize

  1. Side Curtains (protect the window)
  2. Weighted rope/hose for bottom

item.title: I put in a few hours on the sim yesterday, here's what I accomplished
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
• I hung the ceiling. I still might add some more tiles to it go wider, but I think I need to a few more things in place before doing that. It's fairly easy once you line up the tiles and borders (which can be tricky even on the ground... must line up before mounting. This took about 1.5 hours after measuring to the center (even though it looks offset here), and then attaching up the ceiling . I had the kids hit some balls, and the ceiling already caught... it slowed the ball way down and no issue what so ever. This was a good decision.
    • I got the projector mounted and installed. I used a cheap amazon mount, and everything kind of came together. I ended up going just outside the garage track. I tried to get it inside, to ensure that I could get full width, but it was too dangerous from a shadow perspective. Attaching the mount wasn't simple... another 1 by 4" attached to studs with 2" wood screws and mount attached. It's not perfect, but it works well. Probably still need a bit of tuning, and there are a couple retaining screws I have to do today.

    What I need to do now

    • Figure out a better system for the baffle. I used drywall hooks to attach, and then smacked the baffle and it came crashing. The added tension on the baffle made anything additional come crashing down. I also need to attach some foam to the back. Perhaps just some glue
    • Order Track and curtains --- pain in the ass, but needs to be done. May either involve using velcro to the screen, or mounting around at curve. Either way I've got tracked picked out and ready to go... Need to measure height to ceiling again. \
    • Flooring.. .a trip to Tractor supply to purchase... wish I had gotten on sale on Sunday, but now realize I need 3 full mats to make things look right.
    • Wire up - I need to tie off power cables and probably purchase proper extension cords. In the amazon cart now.
    • 2x Recessed lights - but may come later. Just unplug for now.
    • A DIY Cage for the projector with wire

    On the tech side:

    • Where the hell is the computer going to go? For now it will be a chair, but need to come up with a system for that. Bluetooth keyboard mouse or golf controller. Perhaps a cart. Do I want to add a dedicated PC.
    • Maybe a TV mounted on one wall...
    • GSPro...

item.title: It's up, some first impressions
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I did a little test run last night with the kids. Moved the mat slightly closer to the screen in the hopes of catching more errant balls, used my work laptop and played 2 holes and some range time. What we learned.

On the setup:

  1. I need curtains, and I need the baffle. Balls go everywhere. I should have known this from the last go around. Several balls made it behind/around the screen on errant shots. Saturday...
  2. I need a hose filled with sand to weight it down at the bottom and adjust the height slightly.
  3. I really need flooring. Nothing like balls bouncing at you off concrete floors. Makes me worry about the projector
  4. Projector needs a cage, anything and everything can happen. This should be pretty easy though.

On the Square:

  1. Pretty good first impressions of overall experience. It was just plain fun. We only played 2 holes, but it played like we play when out on the course.
  2. When it's on, it appears to be very accurate. We used the provided balls and I would say things seemed pretty normal for ball flight. I was getting some indoor swing syndrome and felt short on everything, but that definitely felt like a swing thing and not a reader thing. Slices felt sliced, pushes felt pushed... Straight felt straight. No club stickers on yet, but I like what I saw.
    • It punishes bad shots I also noticed. This is a good thing too, as it will force us in to less mistakes hopefully.
  3. It had trouble reading off those bird-tees with my son. It missed a fair number of shots. I didn't setup as well as we could have. We may not have been level, setup was rushed, it was just good enough. There is a little bit of sunlight seeping in from the garage door. We had enough missed shots to give pause, but I think refining setup will solve this in the long run.
  4. The square software is really good for something that is essentially included with the device. I think it works out to a penny or two a hole, that's a pretty good go. Again we played only two holes. Some play notes:
    • The aim function right or left worked just fine, and then setup for a straight shot. That's going to throw aim off over time as it doesn't force you to square yourself in other directions. This is normal in indoor golf though, and can be compensated some by actually working some aim on shots.
    • My son hit his 7 really well, and his ball flight was straight and consistent when his contact was good. There is hope.
    • I don't like that it doesn't keep your shots in a database somewhere. Perhaps I missed something in the play menu though. Would be good to save off for analysis.
  5. My old laptop did not work, and not sure why. I think it had something to do with how it was sending the signal on the HDMI at a higher resolution even though the laptop resolution was 1080p. Would still rather that be the dedicated laptop for this... so ordering some additional cable, and will play around with it some!

Given the setup, I do really like the square software, but I definitely see room for GSPro and maybe Awesome Golf in the future. All are good products.

item.title: I went to the range
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Despite having an indoor sim that gives me stats galore, I need to hit the range today because it's been more than 30 days since I played.

It really showed today. Irons and wedges were okay, woods were terrible. I could not hit driver. Where before I was say hitting 50% fairway, today is would have been like 10%! Driver can be so good some days, and then like today nothing was working. It always feels like I have a missing 'feel', when I find it sometimes it holds , and sometimes it doesn't.

I fear that I won't be hitting a ton of driver in the sim because of space concerns... I swung it fine, but I worry about the follow through. I am cool just hitting woods off the tee, and working that in the 200 range and then working on irons for a long time.

Excited to do more with the sim, but I think I have two outdoor golf days this weekend. Tomorrow a short 9 hole, and then Monday 18 holes. Then finish out the sim and get a Thursday night golf thing going...

Left for the sim... Time permitting tomorrow I will add the first curtain, and cut some of the ceiling tiles to fit in. I got a couple of pieces of wood to run the curtain track over. If it works, I will buy the other curtain track and be done with this.

I have a couple of lights to install to, and I think some metal grate above that. It's a tricky little installation on this.

The baffle too... this is all still work on the ceiling. Then I need the tractor supply mats. Hitting myself for not ordering the 3 mats when I had a chance to get them delivered!

The project goes on and on... probably need a full 10 hours to finish everything up including some additional orders.

item.title: Couple more build notes & off to golf Laytsonville!
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I get to play today, but spent a bit of time doing some more sim buildout.

A couple of notes on the buildout

  1. The track I bought from amazon for 25 dollars was just fine. Running straight track from the gap just above the screen roller is perfect. I may not have installed the framing or track perfectly square, but it's fine.
  2. The curtains I bought were trash. I think I paid 35 bucks for a set of 2 96" x 52" --- I think it's about 3-5 inches shorter than advertised. What a pain, I will likely return, and just go extra long. I don't like the material either, they aren't very heavy. I'd like to add at least another 2 feet worth of length (so like 76" vice 52). I'll leave in place for now, but ugh.

You can see in that photo I Velcro together for a nice clean finish here. This will work with any replacement too.

So the other thing I am planning on doing this weekend is additional ceiling tiles, which is tough. I need to replace the lights first, and then I need to do a whole bunch of measuring. It's such an odd structure and will take some work to get the measurements right. The new track may also require us to cut a side short.

So off to a course today that I am very familiar with. Will likely get 9 holes in, and I'm looking over the GPS flyover... I'm going to play blue or white....

  1. I've slice in to those trees almost every time I play here, might be good to hit the wood (which was straighter off the tee yesterday). If I can turn it in to a 150 yard or less iron, then I'm in good shape.
  2. Same sort of thing... aim a little left (I know you've flown it too far left in the past), this one is a little
  3. If you play blue, your 179 on a par 3 which is a tough shot for me. I can get there with my 5 hybrid, but that isn't reliable. White at 152, is more reasonable, where you can try the 6 or 7 --- maybe I'm making my decision
  4. Par 5.... up hill, should at least try to hit the driver up the hill and hopefully your nice and warmed up by now.
  5. Easiest hole on the course... 8 iron... oh wait --- I don't have an either. Will be force to 9 iron 130 yards.
  6. Another par 5 -- hopefully get a bit of practice on the driver again. Tough as this one is a valley, you go donw and up. Perhaps the hardest hole on the course (they rank 18 harder, but I disagree)
  7. Careful again -- go wood or hybrid to iron. Water to your left, driver too unruly here.
  8. You can think about driver again if it went well on the par 5s as it's straight up a hill.
  9. Same issue --- but this time your going down the hill

Your likely done here... I doubt anyone will want to play the Par 5 here... I think the key will be -- don't try to smash the ball today, just hit it nice and clean...

item.title: From frustration to a lipped out Eagle, back to frustration!
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I could not hit the ball today. Too many thoughts especially early. I could not hit the woods period. Tried the wood instead of the driver == failed. Tried the driver on2, failed. Played my older sons ball the first couple holes. Ahh hell, let me do the writeup...

  1. Can't even freaking hit the ball with the wood. Decided to play my older sons ball which wasn't a great shot either but was at least on the fairway. 2nd or 3rd shot I flushed over the hole, clubbed down and then came up just left. Don't remember the putting,... not a hole even worth counting.
  2. Hit driver, left, then left again, I'm losing balls massively. I play my sons ball again.. this time I hit a decent approach but lose the ball in the rough on the right. This is frustrating (I actually hit a good ball.
  3. I hit 7 iron off the tee maybe, but it goes left again. Yea, your missing left now more than right. Its the right distance , with the wrong aim. But at least I'm cleaner hits. I SW on I think for 2 shots, and then 2 more. My younger son is having a meltdown and trying to manage his emotions.
  4. I decide I'm playing so poorly, I move up a tee to play with kids. I hit a massive drive on this Par 5, up in to the left rough. If my watch had actually recorded things, it would have be 250 yard or so drive. (351, so I think it left with my ~100 left, but watch wasn't working... more on that later). I hit a perfect 9 iron, I'm maybe 8-10 ft from hole! Not bad at all... I go to putt, for a technical eagle... it lips out, and I tap in for birdie... I like playing the kids tees.
  5. Decide to tee up at the 100 yard tee, instead of the 130. I hit a good shot , it's off the left of the green though, I chip on and putt out for par. So birdie, par... not bad for 2holes.
  6. Back to a struggle... can't get the driver moving (took 3 shots). When I finally did, it was more of a old style, not a lot of hip swing... but the ball moved. Then I played a great shot with a hybrid... but I lost the ball... I hit a good SW to get on, and then putted out... don't recall the score, says a 6 but in reality much higher.
  7. Good drive, but in penalty area. Iron on decent shot, and then putt out, minus the penalty it was a boogie (but it was a 3 putt)
  8. Driver goes left, again... left. I need to stop over thinking the slice problem. I had a bit of trouble wedging out, and then a decent 2 putt.
  9. Down the hill, good drive this time I think I missed right finally. Then a couple wedges on and a 2 putt. So a 5. I'd be happy to do 5s all day.

Overall, fun to play from kids tees. Easier lower pressure time. Higher pressure trying to manage the emotions of my other junior who was playing poorly today. My older junior was doing really well. He got on the green in 2 or 3 on several par 4s. He hit a legit approach shot within 5 feet. He par'ed a par 3.

The almost eagle was fun... wish I had sunk that putt, it was really close.

What does this say for playing monday... could be ugly, or great. Play relaxed and just hit the ball and you should be fine. Think about your swing and your dead.

item.title: More progress... can see the finish line (next week?)
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Forgot to post this the other day... So finished the ceiling tiles with semi-recessed lights. I didn't want to replace the whole box on each light so I eventually found these 12 dollar lights that fit in to existing junction boxes (not sure I have that name right). You can see in the picture, worked out pretty good. I could possible add a layer of lexan on top of these... but the lexan would actually cost as much as the light. We'll see how things go, if we get a hit we may have to go that way.

So now what's left

  1. 1 more track and hang curtain + velcro. I will likely return the curtains for something heavier in the future, but until I figure that out, will keep going on this. Annoyed sizing wasn't right.
  2. Flooring. I am leaning to start with just stall mats on the floor, 3 across for 12 feet. That will solve the bounce problem. I suppose I could get a 4th, and cut it to the edge, or use it for additional hitting area.
  3. Attach wiring properly. HDMI, Power, etc, cable ties, sticky's whatever else I have around
  4. Figure out the issue with the connection between the surface 2 and the projector. I think the surface 2 will run things fine, and I'd like to make it the semi-permanent solution. GSPro I recall ran fine on it when I used it before, slightly slower than the other laptop, but eventually we can purchase something else.
  5. A quick fold up stand for the laptop. ORdered on amazon
  6. Battle rope to put in the bottom! I have 2" rope that ways like 30 lbs, so that should keep things stead, and also adding a pillow to stop puts
  7. GSpro ---

Some optionals:

  • Laser off the square for centering
  • Point light for the hitting area.

I played my scramble, mix of good and bad. Played with a guy with a sim, says he hits 300 balls a day... it makes a huge difference. I hit meh, some good balls for me as usual. A few greens, and just missed greens. A few good drives, a mix of bad drives. Playing with a few good players is a wholly different feel.

Actually got a couple good tips

  • Not staying down is a problem again
  • keep the putter a bit lower on my strike provides a bit more control.
  • I'm really flippy again...

item.title: Done?
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I think I am pretty much done with the initial build now. First let me list off the problems

  • Bounce back from the screen --- I added the heavy rope to the bottom which evens out the screen, but now bounce back has gotten a bit worse from the screen because it tightened up.
  • The foam installation on the top didn't work. It was a hack and you likely need to drill again. This can wait for a bit.
  • The bounce off the stall mats is better, but still pretty bad. I laid the turf carpet on it, this helped none. It's better that concrete by I would say 50%. I want it to just die, even if it comes 5 feet back. I've read carpet padding might help.
  • The crappy curtains actually keeps thing contained, but still could use a little longer and will replace at some point.
  • Perhaps could stand to be another foot or so back from the screen
  • Indoor swing syndrome... I have it bad... I can't seem to swing freely, despite knowing I have room. I don't think we have an issue, as my son's shots are going about the right distance, and I do have an occasional good strike that just comes up a bit short, but overall it's been a bit of a mess to get use to. Time should heal this. I'm really stopping my swing early which is causing issue.

What I still need to do:

  • Figure out that area between the screen roller and ceiling.
  • Cut the piece that's rubbing against the screen as it rolls up and down.
  • Figure out the carpet thing.

item.title: Initial distance comparisons
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So today I played some holes, and things felt a little better. I did not hit driver, played the kids tees and hit the hybrids off the tees.

So I know from previous rounds, a well hit 3 hybrid was hitting anywhere between 170-220. I think I might have kind of replicated it finally today, but it still feels like good shots are about 10-20 yards short on that club.

Same for the 9i and 7i. I think what I would typically see on course would be about 110 on the 9i, but a clean shot could go 130+, the 7i , I think clean it's the 130-140 yard club, it also felt a little short. I will say as I got more comfortable in the sim, the distances started looking a bit more accurate.

I think on the long end I'm going to be challenged for a awhile. Can I hit a 200+ yard drive in the sim? So far no, but I haven't tried that much. Still getting use to thing.

What I did notice was that instead of trying to hit the turf, I'm now trying to hit the ball (if that makes any sense). I had to compensate some for lack of turf, and my hitting strip + square was really punishing the fat shots (like it should). So as I was hitting through the ball it was doing better. I was letting my body spin a little out on the follow through too and that seemed to help me feel and exaggerate the turn some.

I can see how in the long run, this immediate feedback can help you work through things.... much faster than on the range. I am starting to come together with how a practice routine my look once I get the right things in place.

Ie , lets try to work, 50, 75, 100 yard spots and work that to get a tight dispersion.

item.title: Sim stuff getting better
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Figuring a few things out. Played by myself for the first time this evening and allowed me a bit more time to adjust things. Jumble of notes here:

First off, I added a 5% boost, and this seemed to get things a bit more in line with my expected outdoor hits. Granted, I was hitting the ball harder than I should tonight. I saw the 3 hybrid go in the 170 yard range tonight, 9i, were about 105-110, 7i were a bit tricky. Most importantly, I learned a couple things... 1 is that I can start a session and export to csv in the app. This should help analyze what's happening after the fact and adjust.

I also attempted the target alignment. I was noticing some not so straight shots, that felt more straight. It seems my miss is more left than right lately (this is also true at the range... so probably correct). I also miss right, but that tends to be more a bad slice hit. Anyhow the alignment function didn't seem to work right, so will try again tommorow.

I noticed hitting down on the ball doesn't seem to work right now in the sim, I just need to make a solid strike through (like I'm not taking a divot). I'm not sure how this will translate on the course. Time will tell. I still chunk the turf on shots, and it punishes like hell. I feel like I'm just trying to smack the ball in the center, it's hard to explain, but it seems to work.

I raised the LM up another 1/2 inch or so tonight. No better results, still have my missed reads... about 1 in 10 this go round which has been the experience. Most of the misses were bad shots.

I don't like that I can't export a game -- I'd love to see a shot by shot, that would be pretty easy from a programming perspective. I did 5 holes tonight, and just wanted to keep going. Long game was actually okay this time, but figuring out the chipping and putting is proving a bit of a challenge. It's like learning a different game. You can't feel your way through a chip or putt which is hard to do. Shorter putts I can kind of estimate. The chipping game is really hard, seems to be better to drop to drop one on the green from the rough versus chip. The chipper did not work tonight.

For the most part, I was hitting well enough over a 5 hole game. It was fun, could have kept going easily... Par'ed a couple holes, but also double bogey a couple times. It seems to go one way or another. This is actually fairly accurate to my game right now. I can imagine a week of playing 9 holes a day and you should do better on a course. That is what I would like to eventually try if the body cooperates.

Paying attention to ball speed trajectory and other stats right after the shot can be a really helpful thing. I think slowing things down some, I'll come back around to swinging slower but further here... but I think that will be in combination with working different things. Tonight I really noticed width = higher ball speed. I don't need to swing harder, just get wider.

I learned tonight, I can probably run all this on my tablet. Will try tomorow, if my body is not a total wreck after working out.

I found out I can hit my wood to the ceiling on a follow through. Driver is exceedingly hard to hit in the sim.

I found out a ball hit the right way can make it through the gap.... this was a first and kind of sucked. I still got a read!

I think the most important lesson tonight were:

  1. The indoor game is very different, and you will play differently inside versus outside.
  2. Your probably not going to hit a lot of driver inside, but that should be okay... Driver is something to work on specific range sessions then... get good with the wood off the tee, or maybe get a mini-driver.

So I can anticipate a progression here...

  1. You'll start dialing in the 150 yard in game a lot, while using hybrid and woods off the tees to play holes.
  2. You'll greatly improve the iron game and striking. I see you'll be good through the irons and hybrids... but the driver , chip and putt will not move at the same speed.
  3. You'll start figuring out correlation between certain techniques/feels and ball speed and flight. This is the learning process.
  4. You'll take it to the course and adjust or get very frustrated by the lack of carryover from sim to course.
