... then you'll buy new clubs, because your missing matched PW/8i, and your SW is off. You'll buy a mini-driver because your driver is too long in the garage. You'll do this in a month on black friday!

item.title: The new goal
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Okay, so a couple new goals here centered around sim golfing...

Overall, your trying to practice to get your swing better, that's great, and every warmup will be a work around fixing up a part of your swing or game.

The real goal is to get a consistent 9 holes under 48. That is a mid 90s score, and that is a push for you. No mulligans. We will track this one by one as you move on down the scoring list, and then will see if we can translate to the course once achieved. I'd like the goal to be in the sim to actually get it down to a mid 80s score in the sim. That would be scoring 43 or lower per 9 holes.

Not a lot of 18 holes... but 9 holes should take about 45 minutes not including warmup. An hour practice a day. See if you can work it down.

I'll start a spreadsheet with the info. This will be on the 'lady' tees (because eh, no driver), 5% boost, and concede putts within 4 ft for now. Basically playing smart golf avoiding mishits, get to green in par or better strokes. That's the game right now

item.title: Played 5 holes...
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So realizing I have to change my previous goal. You may not get 9 holes in every session.

Yesterday I played 5 holes. I felt like it was once again a good representation of my game. I went bogey, bogey, birdie, bogey, and then quad-bogey. I registered this as the first go in the spreadsheet with a score trending at 94.

So what I've been doing is using the hybrid or wood as a driver. Going to stick with this for some time. I play from the 'forward'/'lady' tees. This seems fair, and probably good to stay at until you consistently score under 90. Then you may want to figure out how to get longer off the tee with a mini driver/2 wood type thing. Until then this is your setup.

So the disappointment lies, that even with good hits on the hybrid (which I've hit 200+. Looking at stats from August I hit 3H 182 and 209 on consecutive holes. Late round I hit it 192 yards. I will say, the 9i is close to what I play it at about 100-110 yards, however on a good day I can easily carry the 9 130-140. It ends up a little short in the sim, but this is okay. 7i is sort of the same thing. In general though, I think we are close on the irons with the 5% boost, but a little short on the woods (one day was better than another). The woods feel like clean hits and should fly 180 at least. The game in the sim is a bit different

So what happened on these 5 holes. Decent hits off the tee, but they were only going 130-160 (again wish I could export data to check these numbers) . Next shots were similar typically 3h on the Par 4s and 5s. I was getting on the green, and having various luck with putting. A good birdie putt on the Par 3, a mix of 2 and 3 putts on the others. Was pretty fun all around. Last hole was a wreck. I took a mulligan off the tee trying to hit the wood. Decided to hit it again, and still struggled. The mulligan was a better shot. I ended up struggling getting the ball to fly from there. This is typical of my game, a few good holes and then a disaster. When I finally hit the green, the difficult putting in. Maybe this will be better in gspro?

Bringing me to my next topic. The lack of ability to add/remove players mid-round is a bigger deal than I thought in Square! Kids coming and going is a likely occurrence.

GSPro is almost perfect, except it won't give me the club distances so I will have to take notes on this instead of exports... I am about to make the transition again, unfortunately I think it might quickly lead to buying another PC . I vaguely remember it working okay on the old laptop, but not great... worth going though this process again, but will just stink if I have to purchase more hardware.

Also, recovery sucks after working out and golfing in the same day.

item.title: Lots of holes, lots of info - GsPro playing now
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I played a bunch today. First time I actually really got to work through things with the sim. Just some bullets to start

  • On good hits, I am experiencing a fall off in distance which seems to become greater as you move up the bag to longer clubs (but I haven't actually proven anything yet).
  • My garage floor slopes up about 2%. (Could also be described as a 1 degree incline up). This may be causing some issues, it may be showing launch up a degree or two. Even at the max on the 3 hybrid, Chat-gpt would anticipate the launch monitor to read a longer hit.
  • There might be issues with the case
  • Indoor swing syndrome doesn't seem to be a thing. I can tell when I've hit cleanly, especially on the 3Hy, and I would expect that thing to go 175-210 yards each time.

So we have a bit of a mystery that I am trying to work through. I am not so worried about my mis-hits, they seem to track in the equally bad as direction as I would expect. The club in and out, and all those things seems to be right, and seem to be reflected in the ball flight path (ie, I can force myself in to a more in to out path and I see the flight change).

I can only suspect that I have an issue around ball speed or spin that is causing this.

So I decided to just bite the bullet and get GsPro today. I knew I was going to buy, so today was a good day with some time to play. I could do a whole post on Pros/Cons on GsPro vs the native software, but I'm going to save that till I get a bit further in to GSPro.

So first I played a few holes on a course I've played a bunch --- actually I think it was the first course I ever played, which is the Needwood 9. This played interesting... Triple, par, Triple, Double Bogey. So nothing too exciting here, 3 par 3s, and one par 4. It was pretty accurate , except the tree sitting right in front of the yellow tees. Putting has conintued to be an issue, and figuring out the green speeds... this was true for the entire day.

Then I switched to supposed Kapalua Plantation Course. It was supposed to be on the easier side. So I captured a shot early on, I think it was 3 or 5 hybrid, I think it was well hit. I ended up with 105.9 yards carry game, and 109.9 carry raw. Total length was 113. Ball speed 87, and total spin of 6308. This felt off...

So another capture (this is before I started messing with settings, I'm certain this was a 3hy I hit 145.8 game carry, 141 raw, and total 151 length. This was one of those pureed shots that I would have though traveled 200+

I get through 9 holes. I birdied one hole, but everything else is atrocious. I have 10s and 11s in the car. I 'm playing tees that are supposed to forward, but it says black in the scorecard. I'm at a 63 after 9 holes! I find alot of the issues are around putting and chipping (but more on that later), and of course not getting any distance off the tee. I had one good hit, but averaging 110 yards off the tee. Even on a bad day, I'm much better than this.

So I pop up a different course, and keep trudging along but start playing with settings again. I'm getting worse, but mostly because I didn't have a birdie --- I've got a 60 through 7 holes... wow. Again this is much an issue around chipping and putting, but a fair amount is the, hey I can't get down the course at all!

So I start playing with some settings, and find a boost setting in GSPro. At first, I think okay let me play with this some.

I'm going to give a few hits and different percentages. Unfortunately I was tweaking this a ton, but I think I settled on something like between 1.2 to 1.35 being about right. The clubs are best guesses.

So because I did this early today, and writing at night, I can't remember exactly how I had these setup. I need to play around with this.

So I think I moved around down from 1.35, down to 1.3, I believe the last show was 1.25.

So I am roughly 25% off? I can't be that far off. I have real metrics that show my course statistics. I know the 3 Hybrid goes a lot longer when I strike it right, that's the easiest one to see.

So I think a few things we need to test, roughly in this order.

  1. Test with and without the cover. Test also with the replacement piece + cover if the first has issue.
  2. Test comparison by trying to level the square further.
  3. Test comparison with the Garmin R10. Setup with your phone and just get some data from the range at the same time.
  4. Possible look at testing with a shim solution that at least squares the square flat?
  5. Go out and play again and get some more distances with the Garmin to see how your doing (in a few weeks) and compare your numbers again.

And how to test:

  1. Test with 3H, PW, 9i, and 7i. You hit the best of your clubs. Driver is too funny to really test right now.

My big concern here is that the boost feature may not actually fix the problem. Lets say my 9i is going 95 in the sim, then I'm hitting 118 with a boost. Say the the 7 is going 105, which would go about 131 with a boost. Probably okay, but not great. Now lets say that the 3 hy measures 115, now your getting 143 carry at the 25% (but it feels like up here you need more like the 35%).

On the flip side, now I have an issue on the short chips and feel. This could potentially mess with your game tremendously if your not cognizant of what's really happening. Say the PW, and GW are pretty close to there numbers... then we have an issue with half shots going way over. You basically have no feel for practices the mid-range (80 yards in range)

item.title: Swing Stats
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So if I'm going to start working on my swing in the sim I need to start from a spot where I know I am getting consistent numbers. So I have a bit of an experiment I am setting up

First off, lets take a look at 4 clubs I can generally hit pretty well:

Apparently WordPress doesn't want to cut and paste excel today, so bear with me here... The third column (which for some reason won't let me edit the upper right ) is estimated roll out

So what are my stat distances, I took performance averages from Shot Scope Course data, and combined it with some Garmin Course data (which reduced most of the performance averages down some). I think the sample size is good. I removed the clearly poor shots from the Garmin data, I can remember my bad shots pretty well.

I had Gpt5 estimate my some average carry and rollout numbers from these. I think it's close enough, if we are trying to get within a +/-3 to 5%.

So now I have some old Garmin numbers (I'm going to collect this data again, so it matters less right now).

I believe these are carry numbers, 3 hybrid 154, 7 iron 111, 9 iron 106, and PW 92. It's just some data from a spreadsheet, so again I need to rerun this data. The old garmin R10 data says

  • 3 hybrid - 5.8% short, So this is looking better
  • 7 Iron - 15.3% short, Cleary had some bad data here
  • 9 Iron - 3.8% longer, looks about right, proof that you can get longer carries with good strikes inside on your shorter irons. 9 is tricky, because when I flush, it goes 13+
  • PW - 1.1% longer - Not a good data point as this was actually a different club, but the threshold looks right.

Now the assumption right now is

  • Garmin appears to be longer than square? Anecdotally I can say so far this appears to be slightly true. More so on the higher end of clubs. This could be an issue with:
    • Case - Test with and without case.
    • Alignment - testing raises up the Square, and making sure the bubble in centered
  • Outside appears to be longer than inside
    • Not a terrible surprise, but right now square numbers are going way low, and it's messing with me.
    • Comparing with R10 live will give some validation on speed, etc.

So this should lead to a fun little experiment and then a post on reddit or elsewhere.

item.title: Swing stats
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I did the first test. Interesting stats, and still don't have the answer for on/off. Anecdotally it seems like I read it longer with the case on then off.

Funny thing first, Square is longer than Garmin in this experiment. Ball speed significantly faster with Square.

Distance across the board is longer with Square,

  • 9i - Carry 3 yards
  • 7i - Carry 8 yards
  • PW - Carry 6 yards+
  • 3 Hy - Carry 15 yards+

Translated in totals too. Spin rates were lower on the square. Garmin had higher launch angles by about +2 degree (8%). Apex was within 5%. Club path had Garmin more in to out, Square more out to in.

I tend to be going slightly right, which is a bit interesting as the misses felt more left lately, but I actually believe that I am going back more right again. PW had a much larger spread on the Square , which is also interesting. I must have hit a bad shot or two.

These sample sizes are still pretty small still. I'm hitting better and it's make me wonder if I am doing something.

If look back to my chart on playing distances I'm seeing some funky stuff too. Largest deviation is in the 7i (Again, might be a sample size issue and some bad shots.

I asked GPT to resample with the top 3 shots. I get it down to something that is starting to look a bit more reasonable.

So the further I go down this, I am starting to see a more consistent ~13% deviation between what the square reads and what I actually hit on course. The other question will then become does this translate over to GsPro the same as it captured in square.

On that, I played 10 holes more... I attempted ultra high, and my compute basically died... dropped back down the high, and all was good. I am medium to high on the old laptop, and this is fine.

So on the course, set thigns up this way.

  • Red tees (again no driver)
  • Larger 10 foot zone for putts
  • 1.05% boost this time (things were still short but felt closer!)
  • Quad Bogey max (did not reach this)

Course was Arizona National.. Was pretty fun. 4 pars, 1 bogey, and 4 dbls, and one triple. The triple was because bad putting . GIR, and FIR were good with the hybrid. This is more like my scoring.

So testing forward. You need a GSpro test without boost. Your played today with a 5% and that helped, bumping it up to ~13% may put you in roughly the right spot.

Feeling wedge shots is the tricky part with all this, and that has been a lot of feel so far, but I've done well.

item.title: Still calculating...
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So looking at my limited analysis from the other day, I was looking at a 13% boost. I'm now thinking that number may not quite cut it. Looking at total, which seems more realistic compared to playing data moves up to 16-18%. GPT says it thinks 17-18%.

I'd rather start on the short end, so I think we will try 1.16 and see how that feels. I will get some time tomorrow in the sim. I will likely focus more irons this next go around and getting consistent numbers to play with for them. I'll also try a few tee'd up wood shots to see if that starts to produce a more playable round.

Then I'll play another 9 at the 16% boost. Going to continue on the red tees (no driver yet) , until I'm consistently scoring in that lower 90s, then back to whites where I normally play. At some point your going to need to get 200 yards+ out of the driver consistently.

I don't have good data on cover on / cover off yet. I did hit some shots yesterday but only on the early shots did I notice a deviation. It went away very quickly, and I couldn't readily see a difference. Rather have it on.

Look forward to a couple weeks of rinse and repeat. I think my striking is getting better already with just more reps. I'm still hoping to baseline, and then build the plan to get better.

item.title: Raw Carry, Carry, --- a 99 in Tahoe and more
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I took some more data points. I did about a 50 ball warmup before playing.

What we learned this time. I was pretty sure I turned off the boost during the range session.

I practiced the 9i a bit to warmup. It went well enough, kind of crazy that I got to a point where the carry was reading 120-130. I was not consistent, but ball speed in the higher 80s was producing this. First off I put the new clear polycarbonate shield on, and my first thought was ... this feels better and more real. A 128 yard 9 iron is a nice shot for me... I've done that some

I then worked up to hitting the 7 iron. This is where things started looking a bit weird to me. I think I may have had an elevation adjustment, but not sure that accounts for the drastic difference between raw carry and carry in GSPro. So the 7i started first couple shots hit really good. 153, and 154 carry (162, 163 distance). So I know, when I'm hitting well this is good. Thr raw numbers however were quite a bit lower... we were seeing 24% lower , 123, and 124 yards. So that deviation was huge, but also, yea ball speed up around 94-96 mph. Some good clean strikes, but, longest beeing 162 yard 7i. When I think about hitting my 7 in Olney, that means I clear the island, and that's not a normal strike. My average here was 146.33 through 8 balls, including a couple mishits. Take those out and you get to about 150 yards distance. That's kind of insane in comparison to what you 've been seeing. But compare it the raw of 109 yards. Weird hug?

Now to the 3H, which I've been hitting really well. These carry and distance numbers were looking good. 183.2, across the good strikes. That's inline with what you have seen. Carry numbers were high, long was 209.3. These are good numbers. The raw carry was a mere 115. Wow, maybe you shouldn't pay attention to raw carry?

On to driver and wood off some tees just to see things. I thought these were not great, but actually... I hit a 241 yard drive in the sim, with a 188 yard carry (low launch angle) 152, and 208. Interesting stuff, ball speed as high as 113. So this is starting to look more normal

I tried the wood, thinking this might be good to try to tee off with. 211, 214,208. I thought this might work... but it didn't translate to play.

So clearly I need to practice more, and these practice numbers coming from gspro seem way closer to my real numbers. Granted, 5000 ft may have causes this, but at least we are starting to get a real feel.

I then started play, knocked the boost up to 1.16. This was kind of funny, because I think I started hitting it shorter after this. Not terrible, but just not like the crusting in the first part of the session. I played a full 18 holes ... crazy. Took less than an hour.

I played the Tahoe pro -am course. Recognized some of the holes. It was fun, but tougher than other courses.

So 48 on the front 9. I set the stimp down, played on red tees again (5474 yards). I took about 5 mulligans. A 99 with 5 mulligans is about right with my skill level t a slightly higher tee. I set the boost to 1.16, and it played kind of how I thought it would.

The front 9 actually went pretty well. I was getting to green, but struggling in the short game with GsPro. It felt actually pretty real to my golf game. A birdie on 4 was a nice surprise. I think I hit a PW or 9i right in the gimme 6ft . I parred another hole. It all felt pretty real, despite being a bit rushed.

I had some disasters though. I hit into areas I couldn't play from, and had to take a couple mulligans. I had trouble figuring out how to get some of the short shots in the right place. I think it happened on the back 9, but I got stuck in a sand trap and took 3 tries to get out. Same thing coming short from the rough on to the green. That is the struggle in these rounds so far. But I feel like it's kind of playing like my game again.

I saw a lot of bogies, those I'm pretty good with, some with 3 putts, some worse. It should actually be pretty straight forward to get some better distance control near the greens and start dropping strokes.

Longest drive of the day was 186.1... This is also a bit funny, I though I hit the 3H in the 200 range a few times, but didn't get the same range numbers despite the boost. Overall though the clubs felt close to how things play. This is all super fun... and yea I got 18 holes in an 54 minutes. Crazy!

So adding to the stat sheet where I am trying to drop scores... I can see easily from today I could drop probably 3 or 4 strokes from putting, another 5 to 7 with a better short sim game. You should be able to get in to low 90s at these settings in a few weeks.

The other thing I am noticing, is you can probably at least get the wood as a driver. You need to practice this, but it's possible. You tried to play it a couple times, but you either skyed it, or you hit the tee and the ball plopped on the ground.

I am just really jazzed by what felt like realistic numbers from the sim today. 183 average on my 3 hybrid, is right in line with my 184 playing average. 7i 146 yard average is in line with my playing average. 9i, same thing 108 and 109!

Thought about posting this, but I need more data and time: Tonight I got distances in the GSPro range with my Square Launch monitor dead on to my course distances. I am not quite sure how I achieved this with the number of variables I've been tweaking, but I am super excited to see things that meet up with my expectations and my course numbers. I'm not a good golfer, but I hit my 9i, 7i, and 3 hybrid pretty good, so I've been using those to test and adjust in the sim.

Tonight , the 3 Hybrid range distances, and 9i were within 1 yard of my average playing distance (as recorded on course using a Garmin Watch, and a Shot Scope before that), and the 7i was like 4 yards over my playing stats. So really close IMO.

I originally started out with the Square software and their driving range. I was getting lots of short hits, especially as I started moving up in club length. It was pretty frustrating on the range. The 3 Hybrid and 7i were coming up around 25 yards shorter! the 9i, was like 15 yards short (total distance and carry).

I purchased GsPro earlier this week, but used the range for the first time tonight. The numbers were very different. I had previously used a boost in GsPro too, but turned that off for the range tonight.

What I was noticing though was the Raw Carry direct from Square was quite a bit lower than the 'GSPro Carry' . I do have some elevation set (maybe that's what did it?). What is GSPro doing different so that my carry is anywhere between

I played 18 holes after the range session… and I will say, it felt pretty much like my terrible golf game. The bad shots were still there, but the good shots felt well… good!

item.title: Raw Carry vs GsPro Carry
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Playing with GPT and my numbers to try.

For the irons, it is apparently a spin issue. High spin shots don't get rewarded with extra carry. That's what GPT tells me on the raw side. A 8i with 6800 rpm and 22 degree launch will project around 150 yards, the model assumes lift keeps it in the air longer. The raw carry game is only 122 yards. Interesting

So my lower launch angle is a bit low ~18 degree, and I'm spinning a ton for the launch rate. GSPro model assumes a more aerodynamic lift, my backspin is high in the 4500-5500 range. It's saying my strikes aren't efficient with the large gap between raw Carry and Carry

The modeled carry

Swing adjustments to improve efficiency

  1. 7‑iron / 9‑iron
    • Goal: Reduce spin slightly (to ~5,500–6,000 rpm) and launch closer to 19–20°.
    • Swing keys:
      • Ball slightly further back in stance to lower launch.
      • Focus on compressing the ball (hands a touch ahead at impact).
      • Avoid “adding loft” with scooping — feel like you’re trapping the ball.
  2. 3‑Hybrid
    • Goal: Launch higher (18–19°) with less side spin.
    • Swing keys:
      • Tee it slightly higher on range mats or play ball a fraction forward.
      • Feel a shallower path (less out‑to‑in) to reduce fade spin.
      • Smooth tempo — hybrids punish over‑aggression with spinny fades.
  3. Driver / 3‑Wood
    • Goal: Neutralize spin axis and optimize launch (Driver ~12–14°, 3W ~14–16°).
    • Swing keys:
      • Focus on center‑face contact (use foot spray or impact tape).
      • Slightly upward angle of attack with driver to reduce spin.
      • Keep shoulders square through impact to avoid big path/face gaps.

So this is actually pretty good... #1 feels about right, I always launch way high with the irons. With the hybrid I tend to hit a lower shot. Looking at the numbers though, I seem to mostly be in the range they want. Side spin seems larger problem ,and out to in on it and getting in to some slice territory . So my old out to in need to go more in to out (and I've gotten better at exaggerating this, but at the cost of other things.

I feel like I have a fitter with me when analyzing this information. It's suggesting go heavier on the club, more towards the players realm. Intersting I went down the path of building a maltby iron to meet this.

Maltby TE+ Pearl Custom Irons is where I ended up at 123 dollars a club!

It gave me a practice routine to help with the ballooning. IT actually directly hits the problems I think I have.

Irons (7i, 9i)

  • Problem: Too much spin, ballooning flight.
  • Keys:
    • Hands slightly ahead at impact → de‑loft, reduce spin.
    • Ball position just forward of center, not creeping too far up.
    • Feel like you’re “covering” the ball with chest rotation, not flipping wrists.
  • Drill: Low‑flight challenge — hit 10 balls trying to keep peak height under 70 ft. This forces you to compress and reduce spin.

Hybrid

  • Problem: Side spin tilt (+10°), low launch.
  • Keys:
    • Ball slightly forward, but sweep through (don’t chop down).
    • Neutralize path: your data showed −8° path at times. Work toward −2° to 0°.
    • Feel like the face is “square to path” longer through impact.
  • Drill: Alignment stick gate — place two sticks 3 ft down target line, 1 yd apart. Start ball between them. This trains start line and reduces face‑to‑path mismatch.

Square to path longer through impact is an interesting one... I've seen this gate drill before too. All super good stuff, I need more data to fully work this out.

I think I finally have a way though to produce swing changes! The iron fixes will come later, going to improve my swing some and then work on the next set of irons and wedges.

item.title: It was the boost...
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Okay, mystery solved. Some how I had the boost setting stuck the last time. I just hit a bunch of balls, and now I'm seeing boost vs unboosted 7i. When boosted, you go 22% longer, without the boost the spin numbers do effect the ball flight

Played around with some ball flight things like in to out and out to in before my back started killing me. This was a not so readable chart that showed by club paths,

What my new GPT coach keeps coming back to is the Face to Path with +-2 degrees produces the best hits. Suggests that I use a gate to work through to help with that strike pattern, and also gave a tip to angle out the left gate a little to promote a more in to out swing.

Angle of Attack -- Irons sometimes get too steep which adds spin . Not always, but it's happening. Hybrids and woods should be shallower. My angle of attack doesn't change much between clubs.

Dynamic loft. Work on delofting irons.

Foot spray for location . Here is the cut and paste of what I'm getting :

Impact Checklist

  1. Face‑to‑Path
    • Goal: ±2° → straight, efficient ball flight.
    • Outside ±5° = big curve (hooks/slices).
  2. Swing Path
    • Goal: ±4° → playable draw/fade.
    • Beyond ±8° = dispersion explodes.
  3. Angle of Attack (AoA)
    • Irons: –3° to –6° (downward).
    • Hybrids/Woods: –1° to –2° (shallow).
    • Driver: 0° to +3° (upward).
  4. Dynamic Loft
    • Irons: deliver slightly less than static loft (de‑loft at impact).
    • Hybrids/Woods: don’t add loft — keep it neutral.
  5. Spin Windows
    • 9i: 7,000–9,000 rpm
    • 7i: 6,000–7,000 rpm
    • Hybrids: 3,500–4,500 rpm
    • Driver: 2,000–2,500 rpm
  6. Strike Location
    • Centered contact = consistent spin and launch.
    • High/low face strikes = ballooning or knuckleballs.

. Face‑to‑Path Control

  • Alignment Stick Gate Drill
    • Place two sticks just outside the ball, parallel to target.
    • Swing through the “gate” without hitting them.
    • Helps keep face/path synced.
  • Impact Tape or Foot Spray
    • Mark strike location and pair it with GSPro face/path numbers.
    • Reinforces how centered contact + neutral face/path = best shots.

Swing Path Neutralization

  • Exaggeration Drill
    • Hit 5 balls intentionally in‑to‑out (draw), then 5 out‑to‑in (fade).
    • Then hit 5 “neutral.”
    • Builds awareness of path control instead of letting it drift.

. Angle of Attack Training

  • Tee Height Drill (Driver)
    • Tee ball higher, move it forward in stance.
    • Feel like you’re “hitting up” through the ball.
  • Low Point Awareness (Irons)
    • Place a towel 4–6 inches behind the ball.
    • Strike ball without touching towel → ensures downward AoA.
  • Hybrid Sweep Drill
    • Place ball slightly forward, feel like brushing grass level.
    • Goal: shallow, not steep.

4. Dynamic Loft Management

  • Punch Shot Drill (Irons)
    • Hit ¾ swings keeping hands slightly ahead at impact.
    • Trains de‑lofting without flipping.
  • Neutral Loft Drill (Hybrids/Woods)
    • Focus on “covering” the ball with chest rotation.
    • Prevents adding loft at impact.

5. Spin Consistency

  • Strike Pattern Drill
    • Use face spray to see if you’re striking high/low.
    • High = low spin knuckleball, low = ballooning spin.
  • Tempo Drill
    • Count “1‑2” in backswing, “3” at impact.
    • Smooth tempo reduces spin variability

6. Centered Contact

  • Gate Drill with Tees
    • Place two tees just wider than clubface.
    • Strike ball without clipping tees.
  • Impact Location Ladder
    • Intentionally hit high, low, toe, heel, then center.
    • Builds awareness of strike location and its effect on spin/launch.

item.title: River Creek - High Score
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So a few problems playing today. I started the day without the boost, and getting frustrated. I was playing with my son, and despite hitting some decent balls, they were coming up WAY short. Finally figured out my profile was set back to no boost. Before that though, I was killing the ball trying to makeup distance. Not good

So after that's fixed, I'm playing alone, and just decide to do a quick 9. I decided to do River Creek a course I've played 2x before. It plays exactly like I remember each hole. Really great actually, down to the greens that I remember. Pretty impressive.

So I forgot to set a few things up... and there are a few issues. I played the white tees, but again, I'm playing with a hybrid as I can't seem to figure out how to hit anything off a tee inside. I'll come back to that in the future, but yea, bummer.

So anyhow, I didn't set the mulligan, I didn't set the stimp (8 was fine though), and I didn't set the gimme up (also fine), so it was 5 ft.

Where did I leak this time:

  1. Short game chipping --- this is the largest problem. It's almost the closer you are to the green, the worse this situation is. My chipper doesn't read well, so I'm chipping with various clubs, and it's pissp oor.
  2. Penalties - hitting in to water
  3. Bad shots - lots of balls that ended short , lots of fat shots that I couldn't recover from. Inconsistency from wooods -> 9i.
  4. Putting - not terrible today, starting to get hang of thing
  5. Distance off tees - I rank this last, but even at 5900 yards, playing driver would help tremendously. It's nice to play the 3 hybrid, but I wasns't hitting it great today. I believe the longest drive (180 yards) came with the wood (not teed again).

So much higher, but a rushed 10 holes. It did feel 'real' though. Take out one really disastrous hole... a 10 on 2, couldn't get out of a sand trap would have gotten you down to a 108, which in my mind would have been closer to what I could score now. I was at a 115 projected.

I'm ready to hunker down and start practicing more at this point. A bit more practice then play... lets see fi we can figure out where the leaks in the swing are.

item.title: The swing rebuild
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I've known for a long time that I muscle my clubs. I am not a 'pure' athlete, but I am basically strong enough and athletic enough to use a ton of muscle to get the ball moving.

I can put a lot of muscle behind the ball. I asked chat gpt based on my lifts, and I get an answer that I am the in top 5-10% of strength of men my age (49), and in the intermediate to advanced level for people who train my age. Big bench, pullups, deadlift, etc. I lack some flexibility, but clearly strength is there. This is doubled edged sword because I can get the moving, but I use a lot of my strength to do this. This also leaves me beat at the end of a session. I work too hard for the very average to below average numbers I get in ball speed (club speed, distance, etc)

So what gives. I think it was natural to use my strength to get the ball moving, and that has actually worked for years. Granted, I have some aches and pains because of it. Lately I've been watching a lot of Danny Maude. Been really focusing in the videos he has on using momentum in the club, and this is my first area of focus.

So now I have a place to practice that isn't as hard to get to as the range, and every time I hit the course I am not trying to rock the ball long down the fairway. I've got some space and time to work on things, and the ability to be consistent about it. As hard as it's going to be I am going to stay away from the distance numbers for a bit, and focus on both form and contact.

"Don't collect tips, collect swing drills"

So, I'm watching these videos, and I am starting to get a collection of drills. Whether these drills actually work will to be determined, but I think I have a sense of where to step back to, and then going forward I have enough knowledge to keep things going in the right direction. I will stick with Danny, Paddy, and perhaps a few others highly vetted instructors over time.

So lets start with tip 1, which I actually did in a range session and saw results. I warmed up with the bicep hold thing from Danny. I noticed right after that the good hits were going far, but with a bit less effort. Not exactly max distance, but close to my max distance, but less effort. The problems starting coming in when I just kept going and the strikes became inconsistent, and I started reverting in to muscling it.

The first 3 drills come from this, and I've been doing this whenever a club is around This Is How I Build The Easiest Swing In Golf

Drill 1 - Bicep hold - hands

  1. Bicep hold left - Works on natural movement through the elbows. You start with just elbows, and then get the turn and hips involved
  2. Bicep hold right - Same thing opposite side. Focus up and down --- turn creates the round, the arms create the up down
  3. Take that feeling to hit the ball. Hold the bicep and swing, and then grip the club with both hands and swing .... DONT TRY TO MUSCLE IT

Drill 2 - The Matt Foley move

  1. I call this the Matt Foley move. Practice rotation in the hip. Backwards / forwards
  2. Lead leg straightens, back leg flex
  3. This helps with ball first contact
  4. Hit a few balls there and compare with previous step

Drill 3- Pressure Shift

  1. Learn the feeling of the golf pendulum.
  2. Learn the timing of the golf pendulum shifting weight back and forth
  3. Start with pendulum down to swinging with rhythm.

That's all something that you build build build, until it becomes natural. These will stay in the practice until your swing continues to look like this.

----

A couple more notes -- don't know if I will like this one.

The Greatest Golf Drill I've Ever Seen & Works With Every Club

Get more consistent. Danny wants you to tighten the screws (it's the bicep drill , but different)

Table Drill:

  1. Keeping the arms connected to the body, you have a table slightly lower, and your just angle the table down a bit at a time and work on your turn. Focus on keeping the arms

Arms now... and you've worked on torso (Graham Walker). Your basically using body for part of the arc, and the arms for the second part of the arc.

  1. First you pitch the club up with the wrist up from to get the correct postition.
  2. Kind of figure out where you need to be start and end

-----

item.title: First 100 shots with purpose
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I had a good range session, hit 122 balls through the bag, like a large range basket working on the things from the videos. Overall, I think it worked pretty well.

So I really felts like I was doing some good things, and honestly getting out of of some of the issues I was having.

Pretty amazing how feeding the csv to copilot and what I am able to get out of the data. So I'm going to start with some known basic observations before digging into the data

  1. I did a better job of turning the body today. I did start muscling it more as time went on, but I think I was pretty good at staying loose.
  2. I was very Out to in according to the monitor. That pattern leads to slice. It was actually a bit better as I got further in to the bag, and sped things up. A bit more turn, and club a bit further behind me seems to help this.
  3. Working on some speed 'feels' prior to the swings really helped. I know I wasn't working on speed, but the pendulum feeling was part of the work. That throw the club out first feeling a couple times produced some of the longest hits.
  4. Had a lot of flow tonight, and was feeling a more controlled path. Think I made progress.
  5. I need to record myself swinging though to get some better feedback to what's going on. Only so much you can do with feel

So into the numbers as analyzed in copilot. I had it crunch quite a bit, and I think copilot is failing in memory now as it's hard to read.

Some of your carry numbers were really good, if I look at the good. 9i distances were peaking around 110 or so, which is inline, but I was not swinging super hard, I was using the momentum, so a big difference. My dispersion was starting to tighten up. You could see the slower swings this was very true, as you had misses, things went off.

7i, I had some really good hits, raw carry in the 100s, adjusted in the 120s up to 155 (with a 93 peak). I am throwing the club, but dispersion is a problem here more.

I can hit the 6i again after all this work. And it travels longer than the 7. The speed is higher, and everything is good.

On to 5 hybrid, the thing is moving pretty good, adjusted Carry 142, 3H, up to 154, and 3W, 164... this all equates to hits traveling another 20 yards on top of those carries. Even the raw carries were reasonable here.

Here is the problem, and I think you want to work on it this way. There is swing practice thoughts for part of your session, and then 'hit it consistently' as another part.

I think a fair number of my bad shots are fat. Lack of turn is still a problem, but less a problem now. The bump whether legit or not helps psychologically right now without messing things up too much.

You are missing an important part of the game evident by the 9 holes you finished up with. Your short game is atrocious in the sim. Anything within about 70 yards is dog shit. You don't know what clubs, how far, etc. Bump and runs suck, too much or too little. You need to practice this too to lower scores.

You did this Top of the Rock course... Not bad except for when couldn't figure out a hole and keep hitting over or under it around water. PW sucks right now with control. Putting is getting better from a sim perspective, but don't think that will translate much. Your score on this 3 hole par course was 104 equivalent, so not terrible.

Something went wrong with the mulligans again in gspro, need to pay alot of attention at setup not to f it up.

item.title: Practice Schedule and next steps
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
This week we will continue with the drills from the last go around. Will focus around 3 facets: 1) Irons/Woods full shot swings, 2) Short game, chip and putt, 3) Course management 9 holes.

Mostly your working on the swing right now. It's effortless power is the focus right now, swing easy, good contact, ball flies. You want to start to decrease the number of bad shots you make ...

  1. Do some warmup shots half shots PW, 9i.
  2. Staying loose and swinging the golf club like it's a pendulum. Continue following Danny's instruction on this. Nice swings, especially since we are sore today
  3. 50 to 100 balls working on striking the ball.

Short Game practice

  1. Start with Op 36, since this will essentially be a short game practice at 25 yards. See if you can work this up
  2. Focus on those short distance shots. Pitching and putting

Course management 9 holes - Energy permitting

  1. 9 hole practice to keep track of scores.
  2. You need a list of good courses around similiar difficulty to keep good track.
  3. Focus on not blowing up in holes. Keep playing shorter tees.

Longer term,

  1. You'll likely need to work on tee shots outside more than inside. You still may be able to simulate this winter, but it's going to be a challenge.
  2. Work up the Op 36 to higher levels. This should keep you focused on the

On the swing, the theme's right now are effortless power with Danny, and better striking. Goals are with new swing

  1. Swing with less muscle, use the pendulum
  2. Measuring, >85% 'good shots' with the iron, >75% 'good shots' with the woods. This means your swinging less hard, but getting things clean ... when you get there it will be time for new clubs. Good shot constitutes a tighter dispersion, lack of hooks, slices, pushes, thin and fat, etc. A bit left/right is fine, dispersion tightening will come along with this. It's about good contact greater than 85%> with iron. Holding to that number will keep your practice in line and keep you from trying to kill it each time.
  3. Distance eventually ... with the new power sources, find more distance (beyond what your doing now) with the new swing. This is seperate measured practice that you roll back in to your current practice. You'll go find the right Danny videos on this.
  4. Work on keeping on plane, I-O preferred, but O-I is okay, as long as the club path is in that close range (I think less than 2 or 3 is what your after)

Goals with the short game:

  • No more chipping over the green --- at least in GSPro, your going to get on,
  • Control putting distance, will take time in GSPro, it's a different game, but hopefully you can find a way to equate it back. Get consistent with your putting stroke.

----

So provided that to GPT, it reminded me I need a swing camera and software of some sort. Kinovea will start with a cheap camera. Want to make sure I'm not looking like an idiot and where faults may be coming in with the new swing. This is probably a priority as you feel like your doing right, but don't have a ton of feedback.

I'm looking through the Danny videos now for a progression on the swing. This shouldn't be a static thing, should adjust to where the problems are (again, you can start looking at faults and adjust to that)

item.title: Some good , some bad
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Okay, start with the bad first. The swing session was not good... just lots of fat shots, I'll have to analyze but I felt shorter today, and just overall sluggish on the ball... lots of all over the place. Not swinging through and muscling more than I should. The other bad was on the course, but will share that at the end.

Now the good... first op 36. Level 1 failed... because of one blow up hole where I think ended up in water or something. At any rate, I actually mark this as good, as this is great practice at 50 yards! I was only 1 stroke over, so more to come on this. Like this short game practice. I need way more of that 50 (and then 75, 100, etc). IT was a challenge, but not too bad.

The other good... playing Junior Tees at River Creek. It's a fun course, and intermediate challenge. So fast too... 14 holes in 33 minutes. IO scored a 75, over a Par 56. That is a 96. So yea, I felt good about that. Granted I'm hitting a 3 hybrid without a tee off the deck to tee off, with a good driver I think I play this pretty well.

No mulligans on this, and I took penalties to top it off. Only 3 double bogey+ out of 14 which is a win. Keep playing Junior tees to gain confidence. 3 Pars and a birdie, not bad at all.

Now the bad part, on the last hole I ended up having a blow up and just quit. I was doing well up to that point, so I'll just take that. I know this course now pretty well, it's a fun one, and the first repeat on GsPro. I think I'd like to go back to Arizona National again, as that one was also on the easy side.

So sucked that the swing stuff seemed rushed today and not good. You really have to slow down to make progress. You seem to be moving the hips after or too late in the swing. It takes time.

Scoring is all about the short game. You have to pitch, chip and putt right. This is tricky in the sim, but you'll get there. Ops36 is the way!

item.title: Op36 -- first 3 levels
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
The boys and I are playing through Op36 in GSPro. It really is a decent bit of fun, and really good practice. I passed levels 1 through 3 today, but not super happy with the scores. I think we could do much better.

Level 1 was fairly straight forward, I had a few problem holes, but got through smoothly the 25 yard challenge. I hate that I was doing this flippy gap wedge shot on most of these holes, but it worked.

Level 2 is 50, some how before it let me skip to this. I scored a 32. 6 holes for 3, 1 4, and 2 5s. Not bad. I didn't like what I was doing here either, I stuck with the gap wedge, but I was missing a fair amount on the half swings, trying to control things. I was ending up short, and doing the wrist flick thing again with the gap wedge, which was working but not a shot I care to repeat on course. Bad practice.

Level 3 I thought was going to be 75, but is actually 100. I was in for 34 on this one. Okay, but not great. 100 yards for me should be a clean but not hard 9 iron. Because of some troubles, I averaged 83, coming up short a bunch of times. In for 3, on 5 of the 9 holes (more than half). So felt good about that, had a bunch of trouble on one hole. I am getting much better at judging putt distances in the sim. Not great, but good enough.

So I thought it was a good idea to have my boys try this out too, I got one son through level 1, and into level 2 before a blow up hole. The other had a blow up hole to start not having played in a long time. Hope I can get him back and not frustrated, always hard managing temperament.

I'm excited to play level 4, a little less level 5. Level 4 is the 150 yard holes, that likely means either 3 or 5 hybrid the way I'm swinging right now. A 6 iron is possible, but the 7 is short. The 200 at level 5 would be 3 hybrid or 3 wood. I feel pretty good about finding a rhythm at 150 yards, and that seems like a really good practice range. Moving up to 200 is going be tough, but maybe that's the right play. I would love to get the kids to the 150 level, and see what they can do. Force them to hit a hybrid or wood inside to get use to that .

All good practice, game is improving ever so slightly. Makes me want to do this every day through winter and see where we end up.

item.title: Op 36 - Obsessed with getting better
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So granted, really frustrating round today. I tried the ops 36 level 4 which is 150 yards out. I am keeping this in my log as all Par 3s. I did not get to 36 through either 2 tries, but I did improve by 2 strokes and I think I can get it next go around. I got a 41 on the first, and a 39 on the second.

So the problem today, 150 for me is not 7 iron, it could be 6, but I've always hit the 5 hybrid better. So I said, yea, lets go with that.

So a club that is usually pretty okay for me, ended up being a HOT mess today. Everything pushed or sliced right. Everything going right, and it felt right. And short. Lots of fat shots, but just nothing going anywhere. Trying to keep the swing thoughts from the videos I had been watching. I think I took the concept of swing easy a little too easy today (more later). 95 and 108 on the two rounds for average drive. Again, the 5 on the course is my 150 yards or so club. These are not good numbers. Longs were 131 & 125.

My 9 iron in contrast was going 83 yards yesterday. Given the number of fat shots, that is actually probably right... the 5 hybrid should at least be 40-50 yards longer. Crazy side spin numbers on this too.

A little bit of good --- The 25,50 and 100 games helped tremendously as I was able to keep getting the ball on the green and score, even if I was averaging 2 shots to the green. This test at 150 yards to get a 4 is basically a test to bogey a medium to long par 3 repeatedly.

So back to my 5 hybrid, right right right... everything moving right. I can see the ball flight too... terrible. Even in practice prior it was going right. And my power is nowhere to be found, I start reverting after some good swings in practice.

So after all this nonsense, I go back and check my notes . One thing for 'efffortless power' was to swing back hard creating momentum, and then try to to take that through. So I try a couple shots, and BAM it's working. H3 is hitting fat, but I am cranking some good shots. Average on the H3 is up to 114, but it's going straight. I hit one 171 carry pure, and a couple in the 145 range.

Then I'm like, okay can I do this with the H5. Sort of , more bad shots than good , but I did manage to get it in the 130-140 carry ,which is about right for a 150 yard shot with a little roll (maybe a little short). I am able to carry it 167 on a good strike. The momentum thing is working!

Now I'm like, let's try this again --- lets try to do this where you are averaging 125, almost 30 longer than what you played the start at (and 20 longer than the second go around). Alas, the square did not want to cooperate... brings me to two things

  1. I need to start using the GSPro beta with square support. Apparently this works better than OpenAPI --which now seems to get stuck . I can see it's likely a dev issue of either a timeout or not tracking the when your supposed to be hitting or not. Something is weird, and it doesn't work quite right. At first I thought the API connect was the way to go, but it seems really flakey now. It can work for a long time, but then it goes back
  2. I am getting tired of the long load times, laggy play, and the semi- shitty graphics already. I have a 4K tv that I am likely to hook up. I suppose running at 1080p a bit higher would be okay, but right now things are so damn slow on the old laptop. Today was weird because it seemed to get bogged down out of nowhere. Probably needs a reboot. It's not really sustainable long term though. I need a dedicated PC this winter... likely will build something that is 4K compat feed that to the TV and downsample on the projector. See how that looks overall...

Further frustrating, I'm looking at some numbers over the past week...

H3 Avg Carry a week ago was 166! Today is was 114. That was after you started hitting it well. H5 was 150 carry! , today it was 124. What the hell happened. 50 yards on the Hybrid 3, and 25 yards on the Hybrid 5. Wtf...

This golf journey is crazy, but your starting to get better striking and cause and effect as you work through these swing changes. I've already played more holes (117 vs 71) on tracked courses this year. I'd love for the chart to start converging down to lower scores overall. I'd like to see scores in the 80s and then take this back outside. I feel like consistency and a few weeks could get you there.

item.title: Wednesday notes
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Just going to bulletize these notes today

  • Op36 forces realism on. So 150 is a tough one to play. That's a perfect hit 5 hybrid, and a sometimes 3 hybrid. I got close today, and was only 2 strokes off. It's fun and good practice
  • Playing without the boost messed some shots up later. The 40- 60 yard in shots I had dialed in with Op 36 (no boost), but yea, they fly a bit longer with boost turned on.
  • I played Porky's , because the name was funny. I probably should have picked easier (difficulty 5.6) greens were difficult for me, but it was a good challenge, I scores a 102 equivalent with a 5 gimme circle and that included a hole where I went from one bunker to another back over.
  • This felt pretty real once again playing forward tees and using the 3 hybrid to tee off. I didn't hit the 3 very well today.
  • Practice was pretty good, but didn't translate to play. I think the Op 36 lack of boost threw me off, and was hitting the ball too hard.
  • Will be REALLY curious when I hit the range next how far the ball is flying. So far I have a feeling that I will be killing the ball, but my dispersion will be all over the place.
  • Noticed a lot less 'misses' today. I can only think of 2 or 3 shots today that were 'pure' misses. Most everything was contact, although I went right a fair amount today. Your hitting the ball more cleanly now, so that is good... Plenty of fat shots, but most of them were playable, just steals distance.
  • Capturing length of course is good, keep doing this. Once you consistently can score under 90, then you can up the distance and try to throw the wood in, and then once you can do that you think about moving to a driver or mini driver.
  • My biggest problem is still hip turn and generating power from the legs instead of the shoulders. Perhaps this is leading to my preponderance of fat shots.
  • My bag is so odd right now... PW different than iron, 3 and 5 hybrids, weird length and different shafts... wood is a different shaft too... so swinging lots of different feels.
  • The closing the face drill I worked on today with Danny at the beginning of the session , just getting the ball straight worked pretty good... could probably do that more.
  • Need to continue to work on hip turn, and staying relaxed.
  • I'm throwing the club back hard now to get momentum, think that is not so good long term.

So hoping to get rounds Saturday, and maybe Sunday. The hip doesn't hurt from playing, which is pretty awesome now. I need to practice more than playing, but damn is it fun to play. I need an outdoor session to see how the ball is flying too.

item.title: Saturday's 19 holes
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I think I'm getting better, at least at Sim golf.

I played the first course I ever played on today. I scored a +1, which is kind of unheard of. No mulligans nothing, everything was pretty clean. A birdie, 6 pars, and 2 bogeys. I would have been even if I hadn't of overhit the green on 9 (which I also seem to do in real life). It's funny for the courses that I play, how accurate the shots are. I felt like I was actually hitting shots that I had shot before.

Distance seemed to be on point, again, longest club I'm using is the 3 hybrid right now. I need some work to get the wood going correctly. Another problem is between GW-PW-9i, which to use when, but I chose pretty well. I don't even both with the SW at the moment.

So 2nd course, I played Domaine LaForest. Was interesting, I ended up with a ~102 score, but I can blame that somewhat on some bad holes. I had a 10 (I didn't max quad), and just had trouble chipping and putting... lost a stroke coming out of the sand, lost several putting on that one. Would be nice if GSPro had a hole by hole export with maps... that would be fun.

On the skills front, the one thing I'm going better lately is backswing with momentum that is turning around and hitting the ball longer. I still have trouble getting the hips to turn correctly, but I think I'm feeling through things better. I feel like I am a month or two away of consistent play in the SIM to something quite a bit better.

With an upper body workout scheduled for tomorrow, I think I will not do as well, but hoping I can get another 18 holes in... I'd like to see if I can replay the Tahoe course or Arizona National, as though two I think I did decent 90s on. I get the feeling the Domaine Laforest was a bit harder, and had some really tight fairways that I had trouble navigating (and some terribly difficult greens).

item.title: What's effecting the score vs what's effecting the swing
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Really itching to hit some balls today.

So making improvement in multiple areas at once. My swing is one part, but those changes take longer to move to the 'course' play. Course play has been all about short game and getting on from 50 yards or less, and then getting putts in , in 2. So lets talk sim short game first

  1. Putting is becoming easier, you basically aim it and have a bit of distance control and try to get within the ring. Your just getting a better feel at this , but I fear none of this will translate to course. It's a different game putting in the sim.
  2. 50 yards in -- I am getting better with the sim. Chipper when appropriate (it spins a lot on the ball) when just outside of, or on the fringe. Coming up, from below the greens close, I've got a shot that pops up and lands softly sometimes. 50 yards out, I've got about a half swing Gap wedge that I am getting a good feel for. Again, lots of fear that this that everything in this 'feel' range will end up 10 yards short in real life... can't wait to test though

On the swing... lets talk about what's working

  1. Momentum. Everything is momentum. Momentum on the back swing is really helping, not trying to control that thing up, but rather being loose and fast on the back swing fires some rockets.
  2. Thinking about club head position. Short shot practice with good contact. You should probably just do this for 30 minutes each day
  3. The bicep hold and pendulum drill
  4. Not thinking, just hitting
  5. Rehearsing impact positions -- hand in front, hips turned

What's not working well

  1. Your still too fast overall
  2. Your hips don't clear properly, and your sequencing is off (or gets off when you start playing for real).
  3. You still default to muscle (but I feel like it's muscled less now, so that's a win).
  4. The table drill didn't help me.
  5. Your all over the place in dispersion and you still have a wicked slice, and produce too much spin on many many shots. Maybe this will be better at the range and on course, but still working to reduce spin and more stable swing plane (less i-o, %, more o-i if possible).

So again, really itching to practice play today. I would do this 2 hours every day if I could, but alas I can't. It's very hard to just practice and not want to jump in playing holes. You need to work on the swing, but the realism of playing a course feels like better practice.

On the sim, it's great, but I'm already in the what would make this better mode. Let me list off in order I think of priority

  1. A better computer setup - I'm using basically the oldest nvidia card you can find in a laptop that's about 8 years old. This is probably the most expensive of fixes (at least 700) but has the most payoff. Still a question about permanent in garage or laptop, or something small that carry in and out. I think I prefer the permanent, but that means cleaning it at least once a quarter and mounting it properly.
  2. Lighting - whether it's rope lights or some lights that point away from the hitting area, this could be much better.
  3. Flooring - this is still a bit of a mess. The floors are okay now, but the setup is not ideal. I also wonder if my hitting strip is hiding my fat shots (although saving my elbows and wrists). At any rate, a bit of carpet pad and putting the fake greens on, a better hitting strip might be in order too.
  4. Hanging the TV - This is free as I've now moved the hanger rack to the back. I just haven't decided on which of the tv's I want to move. 65 " seems overkill, the 50" seems right, but seems like a waste of a pretty good TV.
  5. A bit more garage organization - I'm spending so much time out there, and already moved some things around, but a good thorough cleaning would be pretty awesome.

The last two I need to stay away from, as they

  • New LM - yea, I love the square, but the Eye Mini looks intriguing right now. I don't need it, and I am good for now is what I need to tell myself. This is a next year upgrade, not a black friday upgrade
  • Well, when you get a PC, then you connect the PC at 4K to the TV you've hung, then you have a 4K display, but now your projecting in 1080p.... lol, I know I know... but someday.

item.title: Best front 9, disastrous back 9
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So did the Wynn golf club today. Tighter fairways, took 2 mulligans on the back 9, and had a blow up hole (5 over), and a couple pretty bad holes (3 over back to back).

Let's start with the front. I scored a 40 on a par 35, 5 over is pretty good for me. Also remember, no driver at all here, largest club is a 3 hybrid (which averaged 170 yards from the tee today).

I had a really nice stretch to start with the exception of hole 3. I went par, boogie, +2, birdie, par, par, then 3 bogies to start. Putting was good, short game was good, no big mistakes except on 3 (and I don't recall what went wrong there, but think it was putting and still getting a feel for distance.

I was fine until hole 11, and then I had a disaster, I got a penalty which I took, and then another one! Two shots in the water before getting a 10 on a par 5. I recovered well with a par on the next hole. I followed up the next few holes with bogey, then 3+, 3+. More of an issue with short than long game. A few bad shots I was able to recover, but you lose more strokes close than far. Definitely had at least 2 occasions where I went over the green, and a few more where I should have gotten closer to the hole. It's a mix of bad play, and not getting the right distance.

So the swing things are working okay, I'm still not getting much of a hip turn, it's frustrating. I am hitting the ball pretty far though with momentum back and clean hits. Biggest miss continues to be fat. This just steals distance, and doesn't necessarily mess up my round too much. Only a few shots that were bad. I think I'm fat, because I'm not turning through.

On the good side, I kind of know how generate power a lot better than before. It's less a question about how the power is generated, but more if I am going to translate that squarely to the ball.

item.title: What to practice next
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Drills that are working

  • Bicep hold
  • Waggle to feel momentum
  • Natural momentum in back swing, (use the body)
  • Rehearse the impact position (hands in front, hips turned)
  • Soft to increase momentum

Drills next up

Want to spend a lot of time just hitting 1/2 to 3/4 swings maximizing performance in that hit. It was a drill from Danny, and I really liked the concept. If you can maximize on that 1/2 to 3/4 swing (you have numbers and can watch things). I can also check the swing path in this.

Danny actually suggested in one video to do a like 1/4 swing and learn the feel of hands in front. I think this would be super valuable... so trying to do this today. I've been rehearsing downstairs, but need a ball to make it right. The hands in front is a tough think

I got some spray, and can evaluate where I am hitting on the ball.

I'm still getting that fat miss and the suggestion is to get those hands in front, so that will be the focus today after warmup

  • Keep loose
  • Use momentum
  • Focus on hands in front of club head.
  • 1/4 to 3/4 swings, working on max distance on those.

I'll do another 18 holes today too...

Depending on how things go, may actually take this outside this weekend and see how the ball is flying.

item.title: I thought I was playing terribly, but...
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I ended up scoring a 87 on the Falls Road course which was of similar length as the Wynn I did earlier this week.

So lets start off with the bad. I was trying some stuff with the swing early as I discussed, and I was just really making poor contact. Lots of fat shot, and just not good contact. I wasn't quite sure what was happening. Even on half swings I was having some trouble. Really trying to swing through the body, and just playing with different variables and seeing how they effect things.

At any rate... contact was bad, warmup and practice was just bad. I started on the Arizona course, but after 2 holes I was was like 8 over, and I decided this would just be a warmup. So I switched to the 'local' course... and I started pretty poorly, but decided best to get a score and stick with it. I started triple bogey, double bogey, but then had a nice par/bogey/par/bogey pattern. Front 9 not particularly good, scored a 47.

Back 9 things really improved, par par, bogey, bogey, bogey, par, birdie. I had only 1 double + over the back 9 for a 40. Today it was all about the mid range 30-50 yard shot, and getting the putt distances close to right.

Here is where things were really off though... my 3 Hybrid that has been my go to 'tee shot' for these shorter courses was a 150 yard average today. I was averaging 170 earlier this week. I can only imagine if I had been hitting it solid, I think I would have dropped a few more strokes.

Basically every club was coming up way short today. It's good to see you can still score even when not hitting those clubs well.

I do have concern, that I am learning a different game in so many ways. I am very concerned because I haven't played a tee shot since I've started this. Every time I even try to hit off a tee in the sim, I hit the tee, and the ball just goes down. What gives?

On my swing... man I wish I knew what the hell was going on. I thought I had made some really good progress last go around... one step forward, 2 steps back. This is golf though, and nothing quite new. I do wonder too about the shoes I was wearing, and attempting to turn.

One thing of note, I've been playing around with taking the club back a bit from outside to promote that out to in swing. I couldn't get much distance that way, but it seemed to create a more repeatable flight path with less deviation. What didn't work was thinking hands in front, that just ended up thining and fatting all over the place.

Perhaps I should watch the videos right before playing and do the exercises right after. Will hit again tomorrow and Sunday, and I'm sure by then I'll be having a different experience.

item.title: Struggling downtrend
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So another round and half today. First round, Wynn again, 18 holes, I scored a 93, which is one stroke worse than I did the previous go around. I actually think I did better than this as it may have registered a couple extra strokes on hole 3.

This time the scorecard was more balanced, a 46 and 47 on the front and back. 1 birdie, 3 pars, and 7 bogey's. This is pretty good for a 4800 length course.

Again though, the driving (3 hybrid) distance was way down. It felt a bit longer today, but clearly I've changed something and lost some distance. My form got worse as time went on.

I then played Shadow Creek again... I should not play this course, it's really hard. I failed miserably. Part of it is the extra distance at ~6200 yards, and the other part is just the course is harder for whatever reason. It doesn't look hard, it just plays tough. I shot a 62 over 10 holes of a par 40. That's a 112 equivalent, and I took a couple mulligans. I played 15 holes of this course before and I scored at 128 equivalent, so dropping 16 strokes seems pretty good.

So I'm still struggling with the swing. I actually hit some good shots in early practice, but then playing on course fell apart. I need to likely just spend time refining things now and then see if I can get better course play. I do a pretty good job in the sim now of getting 'close to , or on the green', and then getting in in 2-3 shots. 50 yards out is improving. Getting there too is better.

It would be really nice if I could hit off tees in the sim... I can't seem to figure it out. I'm all over the place with my irons and 3 hybrid still... contact is a bit better, but it's not great.

I need to stick with a practice thing and work it to exhaustion, instead of immediately heading out to play a course and letting the bad habits creep in. I was doing a weird jump back thing with my legs today that is probably awful. I should probably try to hit the range and see how things actually are playing with the last month of hitting. It's been probably 15 session over about 30 days now since I finished the sim. Did I improve?

item.title: Terrible putting sinks the score (again)
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Last two games, 78%, and 57% FIR, but a 9 and 6% GIR. That is problem 1. Problem 2, putts... 2.1 and 2.3 per hole. Better scores, more 2 putts than 3 putts. Poor short game. 2 blow up holes of quad bogeys.

Long game was fine, a couple of misses here and there, but I really struggled on greens. Felt like one of the early courses I played. I felt pretty good off the tee. Iron game was pretty lousy, short or long. Course was Whiskey Creek, and Junior tees, 4300 yards. Still keeping things generally in the 4000 to 5500 range, as I only play a max 3 hybrid.

Today I actually got a few off the bird tees, but still struggling to find some sort way of consistently hitting of a tee in the sim. It's just not happening at all. Not sure if it's me, the sim, or something else. It is pointing out that it appears I am hitting too low on the face of most clubs (duh, fat is your miss).

Had a decent warmup session today , spent a lot of time on half swings, and just trying to finish properly. In general, just working on more momentum, less effort more distance. It seems to be slowly helping, but not improving contact/misses yet.

Consistency is not a thing because every variable I throw in to fix, tends to send things somewhere else. Should spend more time practicing than playing, but playing is much damn fun. I can see though if you could just get on the green more, or closer to the pin when your chipping you could easily cut a 5 to 10 strokes.

Putting will continue to be hard to judge in the sim. Longer I play though, the more I get to know about how much backswing I need to get a distance. This will probably never help in the real world, but I can simulate getting scores down.

item.title: I feel like I'm getting worse
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
1 month in, and I feel like I am getting worse. I had a moment where I did Wynn, Falls, Wynn, and the '5 over' 9 that made me feel like a new player.

So today's scores, a 105 over 12 East Lake (random choice)_. And a 96 on what I will call 'long needwood'. Long needwood kind of proves though that my short and Iron game are failing me as it's mostly par 3s.

Most of the time, I can guarantee the 3 hybrid to go 150-170 yards off the tee, to get me in position to make shots. In practice today the 9 iron was pretty hot, and the 7 was not so hot. The short game again was mostly atrocious.

Best shot of the day was my first hold that I birdied (I think the only one of the day). I hit a 150 yard out of rough to within the circle.

My shots are all over the place, especially with the irons. I get messed up with my tempo and what I'm trying to do. I have this flick shot I have to play alot because my GIR is so terrible. Putting is pretty tough too.

I'll stick at it, but I think I need to really commit to fixing the swing, and I think the next step is some video analysis to see where the faults are lying.

item.title: That's just how golf is
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I played Arizona National GC again today. Last time, I went through 10 holes and scored ~101, today I scored a 90. Improvement, right.

It really helped that I finished it with a birdie par birdie. I hit had a couple of really nice recoveries. Surprisingly 3 triple+, and mostly due to short game mishaps. Putting was fine.

I drove the ball really well today too. 170 yard average. 213 long. That's about what I would expect, I'd love to get about 180 consistently with that club, but not quite there.

The majority of your mistakes that lose strokes are 50 yards in. The next up is the inconsistent Iron play, and then probably the weird putting. If you miss with your longer clubs (3 and 5), the next shot is usually recoverable. So maybe this is progress. The Irons bug me, because my misses are so bad. I hit over the green a couple times yesterday with pure flushes, and then I'll fat the next 3.

Stance seems to help me some, bending a bit there are others

item.title: A few observations
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I am probably a low 90s in the sim on a good day, and low 100s on a bad day on the courses I've been playing.

I've played 319 holes,

  • 13 birdies, 9%
  • 63 pars, 20%
  • 104 bogey, 33%
  • 2+ , 139, 44%

I think there is a general good trend here

The orange series normalized for Mulligans is what matters here.

The two really good scores, one was a simple 100 yard challenge, the other was that insane needwood 9 where you almost made par. The observation here is: as you worked on that short game with the ops36 challenged, you really were able to score for a short bit!

So you should probably do the ops36 challenges at 100 over and over again .. .problem is still that you can't get the bump there, so you end up being off. I want to practice with real numbers, but I am convinced that I am hitting the ball much further than it's actually telling me. I honestly think I'll play a round and the 3 hybrid will go 200 plus on the good, and 170 on the bad. We'll see. I think the 7 iron and 9 iron will be a bit closer to what I'm seeing in the sim with the

---

So I started this post before playing my 18 holes today. I played Wolf Creek, which is a course I know well from playing WGT computer golf. Well I think I found my favorite course! I scored a 40 on the front, and a 46 on the back, 3 mulligans. So adjusted score, breaks 90 on a legit course that's over 5000 yards (played again only with a 3 hybrid off the tee).

So it helped to actually know most of the course. I knew the basic strategy, although still made a few mistakes. The biggest was getting stuck in some sand that the machine wouldn't let me out (I actually took a few extra strokes here).

You can see, I par'ed the first 4, before a disaster hole where I tried to clear the mountain on the way down and hit a bad shot.

Came back down to earth on the back 9, a little trouble on 13 and 14, but in general bogey and golf.

This was super fun, ball was flying. Shot shapes were good. I did stick the greens to more forgiveness today, but didn't notice much.

Where di I lose strokes... short game again, and iron game mid distance. Getting 200 yards on a lot of drives today minus a few misses. Hit a lot of fairways and stayed out of trouble mostly. It was the chipping and putting that messed things up.

So many misses with the irons, too long or too short. I don't need to be precise with the hybrids, I just need to move the ball and keep out of trouble. With the irons it's all about aim, and I fail here. I ground a ton, and then I hit clean (and it goes much further). Need to work on that more.

This is by far the most fun course I've played. 40 minutes 18 holes. Of the courses I've played, my current ranking is

  1. Wolf Creek GC
  2. Arizona National GC
  3. Wynn
  4. River Creek
  5. Edgewood Tahoe

Honorable mentions right now are Needwood (because of the novelty of it being my first course), and Falls Road (because it's close).

I am excited too because I am getting the new laptop today, and should be able to play these all without the insane choppiness and delay I currently experience.

item.title: A technical post
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Not a golf technical one either, but a 'tech' technical post.

I got a new laptop, super excited. It has a new fancy 5060 Nvidia RTX card in it, a bunch of RAM, i7, etc.

I setup, added about 70 courses from my list (of which I'll probably end up using 20% of). I ran it on the laptop and was amazed at the speed. Everything ran so damn smooth all the way up to Ultra! I was so excited to play, but life and events kept me out of my sim until last night. I hook everything up, and bam I am getting worse choppiness than I did with my 1060 on medium.

Quickly realize the laptop went to the integrated graphics chip or some nonsense like that. Surprisingly the thing ran at all. I disconnected the projector, still same experience, then rebooted... hey everything is running great again. Turns out when I started this adventure, the graphics system on the laptop was doing the weird thing of trying to display correctly, tanking the performance down to unusable.

So turn the setting to force the NVidia GPU --- back to running nice and smooth again, but then I hook through the projector and it forces it in to two screen mode. So this is partly on me, this would likely work, I can run the app on one screen and then the laptop drives it's laptop screen. That would be fine, but I really liked in GSPRO being able to pick a location with the mouse on the screen and aim for that point. It's really helped last few rounds, so wanted to recreate that experience.

So run into another problem when you attempt to duplicate screens. You need to hit lowest common denominator in resolution and refresh rate. Okay, no problem, set the main screen to 1920x1080 @ 60hz. Plug in projector, and then everything goes crazy. You get a mass of flashing, and then it eventually returns to original setting when you unplug. Turns out as soon as I plug the projector in, the system wants to default back to the 165hz on the laptop screen.

Tried a bunch of different things. Kept setting manual then back again and it wouldn't 'stick' . I tried this CRU utility that allows you to get in to the meat of your video config, but that caused problems because it was overly configurable. Chatgpt described as a nuclear option. Idid make a change but ended up reverting everything.

Also on the technical side, I really needed a swing camera, and now that I have a laptop that could likely run swing analysis while playing I bought a cheap Global Shutter camera, that I'll attempt to mount on the wall. Hoping we will be able to see some of the poor mechanics I've started developing (swinging through I know is a big problem, likely hips turn after you strike, and I just need to see that). It's amazing I hit the ball as far I do with such poor mechanics.

item.title: OBS Studio works, my golf swing doesn't
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So first the good technical. OBS works great, it's an extra step to get setup, but all works well. My new laptop performs great on every course.
