Now, today. I started off hitting some irons, and it was actually really good despite a bunch of recent struggle with the irons. I was hitting it further and doing well. I then went to play 9 to 18 holes, and had another terrible outing. I picked a random course, and bam hit a really bad score.

So what happened.. .a few things... I couldn't hit tee shots, so I was taking an extra stroke to get to each green. Short game was really off. I'm finding I am missing with the chipper again (I think I may have worn out the groves, because I can't get it to spin anymore). Iron shots after good practice started going wrong. Just overall terribleness, after playing reasonable last week (adjusted scores of 96, 92, 94, and 89! This was Riveria over 9 (57 over 9) for 114. A couple of +4s really did me in , and no pars, and only 2 bogey's.

So I went back to practice the hybrid, as it usually was a strong part of the game. On a 5000 length course, I can usually get par4 in 2 shots. So I am hitting the hybrid, and I can I tell I am hitting it poorly, and it's going like 120 yards... if I hit it decent, I might get a roll with 140-150. I'm not whipping it. My swing is back messed up again.

I'm usually good on a self correct, but yea, nothing. I finally as I hit for a bit, found that 'whipping feeling', and was able to start cruising the ball down the course. It was still pretty ugly, and shorter. The night before I hit some balls, and it was cruising 170-200. Really just a weird experience.

I will say, a couple things on the setup that I need to setup. Move the stimp back to 8, which gives you a more realistic feel. I was averaging a 2.1 putt per hole. That is pretty good compared to real play (where I'm probably closer to a 2.5), but in sim play I aim to get it under 2.

So back around again. Sometimes I feel like trying to make these swing changes things will start to move the wrong direction. I had this really nice down trend going last week, and now back up again. I think I need to just replay the courses at the same distances I did and see where we land.

item.title: I need a heater, and I need to swing easier
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I am shopping for a heater. It's usually about 20 degrees warmer than outside in my garage, putting it at a balmy 49 degrees at today's 29 degrees. It's been a constant upgrade to the sim. There is always something we could do better, or something that could be corrected slightly.

Right now the top wants are

  1. A small space heater.
  2. Protection between the screen &
  3. Fixing the 'power issues' with proper plugs
  4. Hanging up a few more garage storage options, so I could actually park my car in again.
  5. A proper cart for the laptop
  6. Fixing the tracking on the side curtains on the right side. Super annoying that is blew it up one day

A camera is on the way too... that was a big want as it gets me to the most important part of all this. I want to fix my swing. I am realizing I've come to a certain point where I can't any longer with the way I'm swinging now. I am strong, but stiff, so I swing hard and it's not producing a ton of speed.

I need to just use my body and momentum in new ways. I watched another video (I know , I know), about turning off the shoulders and arms. Along with just drilling half swings using the body to move the ball. I feel like I just need to drill for weeks on this. It's always so hard, because as soon as you start 'playing', you want to hit the ball wrong again. Drill, drill, drill is the next step. Make it a reward if you start hitting better by getting new clubs

So here is the deal, going back a few sessions.

Let's say your average carry on a 9i is around reading (raw) around 80-85 yards. 7i is about 100 (raw) , and H3 is about 155. Again those are the raw numbers that I believe are short (I think on carry, I'm 15% longer, and correct for that even with my shitty swing). So lets set a goal to get within 10 yards (with your 15% boost), to the low end of a 10 Hdcp.

9i would be about 135 (so about 115 raw on my monitor), 7i would be about 155 (so about 130 raw carry on my monitor). My 3 hybrid say 200+ total, so a carry of ~170. So that is a significant distance move, probably too big a move. Let's see if you can add 20 to 25 yards to your 'raw monitor carry' on each club.

So raw on 9i, you want to get to 105 to 110. 7i you want to be 120-125 raw carry, and the 3 hybrid. Lets put that at 175-185. Get those goals consistently, then you can buy yourself some new clubs.

item.title: More data points
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So today I tried to just 'swing easy'. Did I hit the ball long... no. Did I have a bit more control, maybe a bit.

I scored a 96 (with 3 mulligans) on River Creek. It's another 5000 course. Was really struggling to get any sort of distance from the hybrid today (133 off the tee), but the goal was to just try to keep thing nice and easy and in play.

So I started with lots of 9 iron drills just trying to hit half shots, focusing on rhythm, using my body, and swinging through. Some success, but not great. I was kind of hoping that I was going to have one of those 'ah-ha' moments, where I slowed down to make it go further. Nothing of the sort, just slightly better contact. I think it helped the short game if anything, as I had some better feels when I was playing.

So after swinging the 9 and 7 for a bit, I went out and played a round. I started off pretty good, with a bogey, bogey, par. I mulligan'ed a bad shot that went in the water. After I hit 3 mulligans, I decided to stop. If I take away the 4 holes, I was basically playing bogey golf. One really bad blow up on hole 10, where I scored a 9. I was rushing a bit, and that made it suck. It's much more rare for me to blow up a hole these days.

What was missing today --- distance, everything was short. Taking an extra shot to get on the green. I did however because of that have some nice chips that went in to the 6 ft circle. So that was a positive. Front 9 was a 46, back 9 was a 50. Around what I scored last month the last time I played this one, but I played junior tees last time.

Anyhow... back to the swinging. I've been studying, watching and working on feels. Realizing that this is going to take a bunch of time to really get right. Some of what I did in practice made it's way to course, but the frustration of not hitting long got me back in some other ways.

Hoping to play a bunch through the week and weekend. Keep working on the swing... I need to look at the stats, I could see some of these half swings were actually traveling , just not quite where you want (I think good 9i, were carrying just shy of 100 raw... 7i not as good).

item.title: Distance back, but short game off
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I did a quick lunch time practice session. Hit a bunch of 9 irons, and kind of found things again. It's a big work in progress.

On the good side, the 3 hybrid was back, and hitting long. I was muscling it, but it felt good, so whatever.

I asked for a random course and got Sanctuary Moon. It was really well done, ton of fun. I ended up rushing things, and also had an issue with the projector making game play a little off. The course was really fun though, so take the score with a grain of salt. I started off really good, first 6 holes were pretty basic par, bogey golf. Then I blew up on the last few. Over the green in to a trap and back again. I really need to work on the game with the chipper and the sand wedge. That is probably 8 to 10 strokes right there.

This one really doesn't count that much, but it is a data point. I've now played 355 holes, including the 9 just now on sanctuary moon that I have tracked. I think I am approaching as many indoor tracked vs outdoor tracked holes. I need to slow down and play within myself. I know I can actually do well here, if I play my game. I scored an 86 just a couple weeks ago on a not so easy course.

item.title: Well, I'm an idiot
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So GSPRo through a portal actually collects analytics on all rounds, I can see my scorecards and statistics. I've been taking dumbass pictures after each round, and all this data is here. It even tells you where strokes grained/loss.

Strokes Gained, Scoring, putts, greens, etc. I can tell from yesterday's swing easy round.. I had a very high strokes gained from 'off the tee'. Lots of mistakes and short hits. Today t was fairly even across the play, strokes missed approach/around green, and slightly less putting and off the tee. Makes sense

Unfortunately I'm split between a couple accounts, but I can scroll through. In every round it's 'approach to green' where you are losing strokes. Even on my best card (30 on a 29), I lost most on approach to green. See this over and over again.

Now I really wish I had been selecting my clubs when I play, would give me a good view of what I actually did per club (instead of the guessing I do now). I suppose it will get it right now most of the time if I put my distances in correctly.

item.title: Had an 'ah-ha' moment.
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I need to dump data before I get to what caused this, these are straight numbers

i9:

  • Raw Carry 111,108,108,105 = Avg 108
  • Game Carry, 132, 130,127, 124 = Avg 128
  • Total Distance 142, 133, 129,126 = Avg 132

i7

  • Raw Carry: 144, 121,120,119 = Avg 126
  • Game Carry: 172,152,149,149 = Avg 155
  • Total Distance: 180, 152, 149, 149 = Avg 630

These are exactly the kind of hits that I am trying to get to in a post a few weeks ago. I suggested Raw Carry between 105 to 110 on my 9i, and 120 to 125 on the 7i. If the game carry equates to what is actually happening I'd be on cloud 9.

So my usual experience as of late is a lot of fat shots. I've complained tons about this. So I caught a video over the last couple days from Danny Maude on fixing the fat shot. The big thing was to reverse the club momentum by "dragging the club" back. I really had to exaggerate this a ton to get the feel and rhythm right. I actually had to start the feeling dragging back in front of the ball, and then come back around. A bunch of rehearsals in to dropping in the slot, and bam. I'm hitting with little effort, and a ton of distance

https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1DHLF2hoT5

About halfway through he does that exaggerated movement. THere is more in this video than what I just posted, and more to work on, and I'm going to have disect this one a bit more, but just that one movement has got me crushing the ball, and making more room. I noticed less fat shots with the irons.

Now on the flip side, I played a round afterwards (Wynn), and scored my worst score for that course. Bad short game (again), and bad putting . I scored 10 strokes higher than the last 2 times I played, but I was working on this new feel so I'll take it.

So I think I finally have a partial fix to my swing. I am flowing, and moving through the swing. Felt better than I have in a long time. Would love to see this on video (likely soon).

I need to figure out how to recreate this over the ball though. I can't have my swing go forward back forward in the future. At any rate, more practice tomorrow.

item.title: Sim fix priorities (again), and the swing issues
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
This is basically a rehash to organize my thoughts...

Sim priorities --- likely tackle later this week or weekend coming up.

  1. I need to fix the wedge issue, I have a problem with balls slipping through the 'gap'. I think the right fix is to either add net that extends through the gap and hangs down a bit. A bit of concern though is that if it roller catches it it will start bunching up, so it's an experimentation thing. I like that we basically catch the balls with the foam ceiling tile already, I just need a bit more work to get this right. Other option is more foam and the baffle. Foam behind to catch, more foam in front. Saw some egg shell stuff that is like 20 bucks may be worth a try
  2. Heat - at below zero outside, garage is getting down to 50 and below, and making it less comfortable. I don't mind the cold so much, but my kids don't want a thing to do with it.
  3. Buy another plug for the ceiling mount that sticks... Check the power in the corner to see if that is a better option?
  4. Mount that ladder on the wall with another bracket, it's just sitting there right now.
  5. Cleanup all areas -- -you've created kind of a mess, this is part of an overall cleaning that will be happening.
  6. Camera setup. I've got the camera and lens seperate coming (I made a mistake when ordering and didn't get the lens, but foudn a better used one, so hopefully this week
  7. Floor control... coming now soon.
  8. K2 tee system --- looks like these are a go to, I keep losing the birtees --- i just paid 65 for tees... geez
  9. Displayport to
  10. Better laptop cart --- maybe after Christmas, see if you can find something used on sale.

Swing thing -- a bit concerned about the swaying that this my introduce, but distance and fats have been an issue https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1DHLF2hoT5/

Gonna take notes on this video, because it really identifies my biggest swing flaw.

  • At 1:00 minute, he describes why I go fat. Club releases early, and grounds early, wrist is straight at impact (casting earlier in the swing) . You want the usual hands in front with shaft lean, without making it complicated.
  • At 2:00 - your flicky, and fat and thin, because you flick it on the way back, and you flick it forward. Reverse the process
  • You do the opposite of what you think --- instead of in a position of wrists in front to start, you do the opposite,
  • 2:45 --- drag, you drag the club away on the back swing, instead of flicking the wrists back
  • Drag so you can lag
  • Part #2 -- Rotate the body on the way through
  • Work the heels to create the rhythm to get momentum -- back heel (while moving it forward), front heel (as you go back), then push the gas, (and back heel will come up)
  • Don't try to get hands in front, you'll get choppy.

When you created a rhythm here, shots went well. Bigger problem was you were swinging forward back forward again, which reduced some control because your not use to it.

item.title: No better, no worse
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So a little stuck as I work through this swing change. I think the swing is getting better, but my game is not. Here is how I think the scores went down last time:

  1. Ops 36 - after working through that for 3 or 4 days, I scored an adjusted 2 over par.
  2. Stimp on 10. I keep forgetting to reset to 8. This is losing putts and made a difference last time
  3. Rhythm - I got into a rhythm, especially off the tee.
  4. Short game was a little better, and more consistent.

What's happening now

  1. New Swing is causing unknown shots, off course.
  2. Short game fell apart, putting has been poor too
  3. Not playing as much, and it's cold out there.

So I went from solid 90s, back to solid low 100s. Part of it is also I'm not giving myself much in the way of 'bad shots'. The mulligans I'm usually only taking because I want to practice a shot. I'd like to see analysis of this last round. I think it's still 'irons', being the biggest problem. You don't put yourself in scoring position ever. Best I did was a couple sand saves that stuck the green.

The strokes gained were

  • 15 on the approach
  • 7 around the green
  • 6 off the tee
  • 5.6 putting

Your biggest problem here too was you scored a 12 on hole 7, not even a high index hole. Say you triple bogey it for a 9 like the 3 other 'bad holes' --- that cuts 3 strokes and your at a 97, shave a stroke or two by lowering the stimp and your back around the mid 90s, with the opportunity to score.

Raw Carry on the 7 and 9 were not as good today, but the swing was flowing I think a bit better . This still needs a ton of work. I need to the camera feedback to see if there is something really wrong here, but I think I am improving here. I'm not analyzing the numbers at the moment, but I know I wasn't quite as long today, I was high 90s raw on the 9i, which is good .

item.title: Still stink
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I'm working through this swing change focusing on the pull back. Yesterday I hit the ball a bit better, but still not quite where I was before this. I shot a 102 on Edgewood. I think the first time I played that course was about the same, perhaps a little lower. There are some challenging holes on this course.

I feel good, as I finished the back 9 with a birdie, and several good shots. The front 9 on the other hand was utter disaster, with a strectch, of +3, +3, +3. I'll take bogey's right now all day long, and the occasional double (5 of them yesterday), but those holes where I go 3 or 4 over really kill. GsPro showed this round as a stroke improvement (assuming because the higher slope rating).

On the data side (and I prefer using the raw to measure how I'm doing, but the portal seems to report the boost).

  • I9 - Raw carry topped at 105, high 90s were good shots
  • i7 - Raw carry topped at 110, but didn't hit a lot of shots
  • i6- rfaw carry topped at 122. Also didn't hit many shots.
  • h5 - raw carry was less at 118 top, also not a good sample size
  • w3 - couldn't hit,
  • h3 - topped out in in the mid 126s, also small sample size.

Let's look at course, carry, I'll take 84% to account for my boost.

  • H3 - my driving hybrid where I hit most of my tee shots- average 124, max 160
  • i6 (usually don't play this much, averaged carry 73, with a max 137
  • i7 - max 100, average 87

So what does that tell us... Averages skew down with bad shots . 7 was very incosistent, 6 actually played a few good shots with which is rare, but the hit a few bad ones

Basically , you can't play golf with this level on inconsistency. The 3 hybrid is actually probably the best club even though you tend right a ton, and sometimes end up short.

item.title: Another couple rounds
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I played Wolf Creek yesterday. 94, although took a mulligan. I did a few holes of sanctuary moon too, but probably shouldn't have as I'm blasted today.

The 94 was a good score, however less than a month ago I scored a 86 which was one of my best scores.

Over all these courses, I've been trying to find a way using rating and slope to come up with a fair baseline score. My first few attempts at SAS (Slope Adjusted Score) has been a little frustrating. My first shot at normalization ended up all over the place. I basically used a typical SAS with my 'adjusted to 72 score). This messed with the Par3s and because I was trying to base it off my '72' score, it was a weird score.

A little work with Chat GPT and I get a better picture. The blue line is the Slope Adjusted scores. The Wynn scores (That were low) were not as impressive as we thought . I should probably not include the par 3s, they seem to have artificially low scores

So here we are with a actually the last couple 'real rounds' , looking decent enough a bit below your moving average line. Just a tad below 100 --- that seems about right the way your playing. 96 = 98.8 SAS, and 97 = 99.5 SAS. Edgewood Tahoe was a 98.3, despite the 102 score. Harder course... makes sense. So all those scores are bunched.

The 106 on Wynn was punishing last time you played, with a SAS of 119. The two times I played Sanctuary moon too, put me at much higher scores.

Overall though, this is fairly meaningless until you figure out what it will translate on course. Your striking is better, but still not consistent.

It's clear what works

  1. You get consistent 3 Hybrid for your 'tee' shots. --- You could probably gain strokes if you figured out how to hit either the wood or driver inside and gai
  2. Your short game is doable - you could probably use new wedges, but that is another conversation.

What doesn't work

  1. Irons, anything 110 yards in should be scoring shots, SW-9i, is the problem. You clean that up, you gain 10 strokes easy. About 40 yards to 110 yards

I think it seems fairly easy that you could control the driver and keep it in the fairway and you start hitting it say 250 combining that with decent iron play, you could actually do the longer courses and start scoring. Driver needs to start practicing to see if we can hit it. If anything, that will translate to course the best of all clubs.

Then just getting consistent with those irons --- I think it doesn't help that the PW and SW doesn't match the GW,or 9i. I'm missing an 8i. It screams you need new irons, but I want to workout the swing before I do that.

item.title: Another low score
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I finally had one of those rounds where most things went right. I scored an 80 on Wynn. It's an easier course (slope 100, rating 62.4). But I'll take it. 10 over. 10 pars, 6 bogeys, and 2 doubles. Stayed out of trouble. Made a couple of 'hero' shots (putts and chips) and in general didn't make mistakes. This is the key to golf... don't need to hit it long, just score.

Was really fun. So this time, things were a bit different from the 'strokes gained' perspective. Now I'm positive on putts... I putted well. I am basically even around the green (chipping and the SW were really good). Approach to green -11, highest again, and off the tee I have a -5. The minus 5 is probably because I had at least two misses, and wasn't quite as long as I usually am. I only averaged 158 with the hybrid, but that was enough for usually decent second shots.

Sort of interesting, Hybrid is slicing a little bit again... longer club = slice. You can see in the scatter plot how I bias right on the on the hybrids...

The irons bias left.

If I take my 'good hits, I'm hitting it around 175 with the hybrid.

So the irons continue to be a problem. I don't even hit that much when I play these rounds. 1 shot with 6,3 with the 7, and one with 9, 2 PW, 2 GW. That's only 9 shots in the that approach category. The 7 I creamed on one hit it so pure, it went 150 yards... which is at the long end of my shots. I then hit one 97 a few strokes later. Harder to score when you get that. I've gotten really good feel with the SW now though, and so can usually hit the green 50 yards out.

So that was fun, will the next go be as good...

item.title: 86 on Sanctuary Moon, 88 on Wolf Creek
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
A silly course, but kind of fun to play with the kids. I took a few mulligans, but mostly because of bugs, so I think this evened out well. The SAS on this one scored at a 93.8, the prior was a 91.9. I attribute most of this to better short game play, and less 'blow up holes'. This score was all despite getting an 8 on the first hole (granted, I got a 'fake' birdie on 6 where you basically drain down a hole ...

THis is the chart, scores going low again. I think I'll play something more challenging today to not get too excited about this. Goal for the new clubs again is 'lower 90s'.

Of interest

These course stats are more valuable. The irons were not terrible. I like that the 1 PW went 10 yards short of the i9, but that club went 110, to 122. The i7 saw the biggest dispersion 93 on a bad shot, up to 142 on a decent shot (I remember getting frustrated again by this not being consistent).

SW has been super good, you just have a feel for it in the game now. Same with the GW a little longer. You can usually hit the green.

The Hybrid is of most concern. I can hit it long, but I am trending way right again. When I was hitting it well last month the chart looked like this (these are actually all H3 shots, just read as Driver before I was selecting)

That's about right. Less clustering on distance, but more of a 10 - 15 offline, less tendency right. That is a good thing.

Of interest, I hit a i9 with ball speed around 90 mph during warm up. Some of what I am doing is working

I need to start working on the wood and driver to see if I can hit it indoors and start getting 200 yards or more. I think this will actually pay some dividends when getting back out on the course. I have really struggled hitting off the tee... not like how that saying usually goes, but like physically can't hit a tee shot in the SIM. Have to be super relaxed.

---

Just adding to this post. Another score, and they keep dropping... sort of. Today I decided I wanted to see if I could hit the wood off the tee and gain a bit of extra distance. It didn't workout that well, but it wasn't terrible either. Look forward to seeing the stats when they refresh here in a minute.

The 88 was actually in line with other scores... I did an 86, 96, then this 88, although the adjusted score for the mulligans (I did take a couple), is 90 or higher.

Same problems I've been having. I'm started to slice more and more. It's weird, because I don't think it's a club path issue with the new swing (because I'm out to in). The thought is now, the face is still open to path. Chat gpt thinks this could be my body is turning faster than the arms now... I doubt that, but need a swing video to see it.

Okay , shots came in. Weird thing happened here, it didn't track my 3W as a a 3W. It was a bit more even left/right. I think my Wood actually tended a bit left. The irons were actually about equal 10 yards left/right.

Putting struggled a bit today. 34 putts. There were easily 3 or 4 mistakes in putting this time around. Probably only 1 or 2 'real' mistakes on chipping.

Profile is looking pretty similar. Your green approach is not good.

You figure that out, you drop your GSPro scores down about 5 to 10 strokes... and you hit a mid 80s average. I feel like you probably need to get down to around high 70s though, before it starts to make a dent in your real game though.

item.title: Wynn -- 83 Felt good, till
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
... till I realized I scored an 80 the last time. Still, this one was a weird one. I played really well on the front 9, minus the first hole being the only double bogey. A little bit of rust on that one, and a small mistake coming out of the bunker. I birdied hole 8 (a par 5) which was pretty good, it being a longer hole (430 yards).

Back 9 was good, except I did not mulligan a ball I hit in the water, and scored an 8 on a par 5 (the only, triple of the day, but still..). A couple bogey's, 3 pars... 10 over after staying 3 over on the front.

So I have now put a string of 4 sub 90 rounds together over the last week. Am I getting better at golf, or better at a video game?

My other chart tracking things. I think the blue line is probably the most telling of these. I filtered out the Par 3 here, and we get a bit of a more of a story to tell here.

So the blue line represents the SAS adjusted @ 72 score. Basically taking the mulligan adjusted score and applying SAS to it. I rarely take mulligans anymore, and usually only if the game glitches. Maybe 1 a round now.

So if you pay attention to the blue line now, you see in general a downtrend. Some highs and lows. If you take out round 33, which was just a 3 hole blow up sequence, you've been in a steady down trend this month. I noticed my first really good score, is actually not that great, just a good score on an easy score (first time under 90 on an easy course). I then got a 95. The one that was actually good, and dropped the blue line low was the first time I played Wolf Creek well. Funny that I followed that up with one of my worst scores. That little run of bad scores in the 100s punished things.

Then I've had this last 8 rounds which looks really good. Take out the one bad score on the 'easy' Star Wars course, and you see some major improvement.

I think the average on the grey line is being influenced by some of the incomplete and lower scored Par 3 rounds , that are filtered out from the chart. At any rate, I like what I'm seeing.

I still know where I can fix my game --- irons, and now getting off the tee. I think some new wedges would help too. I noticed from the data, that I actually hit the wood long when I connect, it is probably the right club to work on to see if you can get just a slight bit more distance off the tee. I wasn't hitting it hard, and it was traveling in the high 170 range.

So also of note, had another adult in the sim today that actually had a bit of golf experience and commented on how I was stopping my swing short. It's gotten pretty bad in the SIM, especially when playing (not practicing). It's partly a control thing,

item.title: Arizona National GC - Scores keep going down...
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So playing 3 days in a row definitely has it's perks. Today was another good low score at 83. This round was a little different. I decided I want to work on my Fairway Wood off the tee to see if I could get a bit of distance. Because of that, I decided I would mulligan any really bad shots, because I still need more practice with that club, so the usual no mulligans, was actually a lot of mulligans. However, when I did hit even a bad shot (and there were a few) that traveled, I played that shot.

So stats for this round:

The big difference here... 7 of 18 greens. The first couple of holes were rough too, because I missed long with long iron shots (more on that later), but overall very pleased by this. I basically knew my irons during warmup were traveling a bit further, so I clubbed down some, especially as the round went on, and was able to hit the greens pretty well:

What's nice about that chart is that your irons while you could see good and bad shots, the offline was much tighter. Within 10 yards.

I had a couple of misses in the short game, but also had some really phenomenal shots. The putting was I thought pretty good, not many misses, good distance on most. Most holes are a 2 putt.

On the tee, it was a different story. I found another bug so this chart doesn't tell the full story. I believe they are mixing my Hybrid 3 with Wood 3 shots. Either that, or it's just dropping all the Hybrid 3 shots. So the story is, I can geta bit more distance on the W3 off the tee. I had a shot that carried nearly 200, 220 total. Good shots roll a bit more with the wood, it's a good 20 yards max longer. This is good... but I'm not consistent off the tee yet. That's probably another week or two of work. My goal is to get the average distance on that club above 200. The Hybrid 3 does a good job on shots about 175-185 when hit well, although occasionally I'll hit shots over 200 with it. At any rate, there is some work on the long end now.

So right now, short game good... putting good. Iron game improving, and need to work on the hitting off the tee in the SIM with the wood consistently. I also need to work on the slice with the hybrid. Can't forget I also need to work on swinging through.

Excited to actually play a round one of these days... i mean a real one outside. Maybe next week?

item.title: Pinehurst 2 - a frustrating 92
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So a month ago, I would have been pretty happy with a 92. Today, on what should have been an easy course, things fell apart a bit.

So what happened. I think first I need to recognize that yesterday I played about 5 strokes better than I usually play. Today, I played 5 strokes worse, and hence my SAS was about 10 strokes higher (87.7, vs 97.7)

I am surprised on the strokes gained. Today I thought I lost the strokes with a couple bad plays out of the sand, and then also off the tee. Approach was still bad, but I though around the green would have been lower, and I thought putting would have been closer to 0.

I think I really lost some momentum off the tee. I practiced the wood, and it was slice city. I know what the numbers are saying, but I still can't quite figure out how I'm not closing the face. I know I've moved from an over the top move to the exact opposite, and I'm too out to in now. This is causing 'slice city'. More analysis coming.

At any rate, my rolling average is down to 92.2 now over the last 6 rounds, and a 94.3 over the last 10. Your below 95, this is good. I think I can get this below 90 if I keep playing easy courses.

-----

So now notes on my swing. Before the ChatGPT recommendations , I think it's important to mention I've gone from In to Out, to Out to In. I just really need to get it back on center now that I know both feels. Here is what Chat gpt is saying about my practice and round. I think it's pretty dead on.

Your arms are stuck behind you in transition.

This forces:

  • Shoulders to open early
  • Path to go left
  • Face to stay open relative to path
  • Slice pattern

And when you try to fix it:

  • You close the face
  • But the path stays left
  • Ball pulls left

This is exactly the same pattern across both clubs.

These are the feels that directly attack your pattern:

1. Arms fall first

Let the arms win the race in transition. This softens the left path immediately.

2. Knuckles down earlier

This closes the face relative to the path without flipping.

3. Chest stays at the ball a beat longer

Prevents the shoulders from ripping open.

These three feels fix:

  • Path
  • Face
  • Sequencing
  • Start lines
  • Spin axis

Across every club.

Your club path is consistently:

4–7° left

And your face‑to‑path is consistently:

+8° to +15° open to the path

That combination produces:

Pulls when you try to fix it

Slices

High spin axis right

Start lines that drift right

----

The fix:

THE PRACTICE ROUTINE (30–40 minutes)

This is the routine I’d give you if we were standing in your sim together.

1. Warm‑Up: Rebuild the Sequence (5 minutes)

No ball. Just motion.

Drill: “Arms Fall First” Rehearsal

  • Take your normal setup.
  • Go to the top.
  • Let the arms drop straight down while your chest stays quiet.
  • Then rotate through.

Do 10 slow reps, then 10 medium reps.

Feel: “Arms win the race. Body waits a beat.”

This is the #1 fix for your left path.

2. Face Control Reset (5 minutes)

You need the face to stop staying open relative to the path.

Drill: Knuckles Down Early

  • Make half swings with a 9‑iron.
  • Feel the lead‑hand knuckles rotate down earlier in the downswing.
  • Ball should start slightly left and fall right.

Do 15 balls.

Feel: “Knuckles down before the ball.”

This fixes your face‑to‑path numbers.

3. Path Neutralizer (10 minutes)

This is where we fix the –6° left path.

Drill: “Chest at the Ball”

  • Hit balls with a mid‑iron.
  • Feel like your chest stays pointed at the ball longer in transition.
  • This prevents the shoulders from ripping open.

Do 20 balls, slow to medium speed.

What you’ll see: Start lines stabilize. Spin axis shrinks. Ball stops starting left.

4. Combine the Feels (10 minutes)

Now we blend the three pieces into one motion.

Drill: 3‑Feel Integration

Before each shot, say the sequence out loud:

  1. Arms fall first
  2. Knuckles down
  3. Chest stays at the ball

Hit 15–20 balls with:

  • 7‑iron
  • Hybrid
  • 3‑wood

Goal: Start line within 5 yards of center. Spin axis under 15°.

5. Pressure Reps (5 minutes)

This simulates the “on‑course” tension where your sequencing breaks down.

Drill: Random Club Challenge

Pick random clubs:

  • W3
  • H3
  • I7
  • I6

Hit one ball each, no do‑overs.

Before each swing, rehearse the arms‑first move once.

This is where the change sticks.

item.title: Cameras, clubs, and a short break
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I took 2 days off... can't believe it myself. I love playing in the SIM so much, but it was grinding on me a bit. Elbows and hips were bugging. Now knee is bugging from lifting.

So the ELP camera came, and worked this time. I haven't tested it with kinovea yet, but can tell from just plugging it in, lighting will be an issue. I saw the directions for setup, and hopefully won't be too hard. Look forward to a bit of analysis today, even if it's limited with the knee.

So in other news... I took some of my free fitness money and bought a couple clubs and a new hitting strip. So first the clubs. I did a lot of GPT chatting with my numbers and club specs. GPT strongly recommended to me after lots of back and forth and questioning to not do a lie angle adjustment, and that was exaggerating my current issues. I did a lot of back and forth on shaft, and ended up with the MMT like my favorite hybrid. Went with the heavier shaft. For the iron, I just had them build a single test club. Built an 8 iron with a 90g MMT shaft. I figured 8, because it was missing, and a good balance between what I do with the 9i which is a bit more stable, and the 7i which is all over the place. We'll see how it goes. The head is a KE 4 Max... I debated on going with one of the more expensive ones, but GPT plus a ton of research convinced me these could be good irons for a broad range of handicaps. I'm probably heading to about a 20 handicap, scoring in the low 90s if I am being real with myself this year and practice 2 to 3 times a week throughout the year. I can say that the PW I have plays pretty tight and I hit it well, but it does have a bit of a thud when you hit it. It's not huge on feedback, but when I look at my charts it does seem to have better distance and slightly tighter dispersion on the good hits, but the bad hits don't drift right, they drift left more.

I also purchased a SW with a steel shaft from them. Really this is trial run, as I work through how I want to do the wedges. The plan it to love my new 8i, and quickly order the rest of the set to fill it out, and replace the PXG irons. Keep the woods the same, and work towards tightening up dispersion and consistent distance with your irons. I think I've got the right combo to help me get down in the teens handicap in the SIM when I do all this, with the current woods.

I do need to work on driver and wood eventually, but I know what I have I can work with. The only other club I may consider buying is something a little less lofted and shorter to play in the SIM as a driver.

I also (with my leftover money on fitness benefit), bought a gung ho hitting mat. While I like the current hitting strip, I have a bit of a problem as I'm coming off the edge with longer clubs... so I needed something to sit along side. Should arrive in days.

And before I forget, had another upgrade to the SIM. 40 bucks in foam blocks to put around the roller. Should arrive tomorrow, and I will promptly drill it in to the ceiling. Hopefully this will solve the SW high lofted problem.

So I had that session after my last round with GPT with my swing. I'm not going to walk through that again, but I think the suggestions it has been making are pretty good. I tie it back to videos of instructors I like and I think I have a formula. Add in some analysis of videos, and I think I've got an interesting take on what we need to do.

I am considering starting a video series that will walk through my swing changes, and how I am decreasing my handicap using AI tools along with real data and videos to improve my game. I think others might really benefit from what I am starting to discover. A process for improving your gear and game using AI Tools. I could build an APP for it, but the process is likely to change too quickly to keep up. I think it makes sense to start something now, while I'm in the midst of this, so that if I have success, then I'll have a series to show from this.

item.title: 86 on Woodmont North
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So another respectable score. This time took no mulligans, 1 penalty in the water, and still scored under 90! My rolling average over the last 10 is now down to 90.5, and my rolling SAS is at 92.1. Another week of this I could get it to dip to under 90.

The usual disclaimers... I am playing shorter tees, and I'm using a 3 hybrid off the deck for my tee shots. I did not work on the wood tee shot today. I wanted to test without the mulligans on a course that I have not played. It worked out well. Part of the play though is I know my right tendency on the 3 hybrid, and I just play to that. Looks like I was about 15 yards offline today.

Of interest today... played par 3s really poorly. Lots of mistakes there. Had a few good recoveries (A bogey on that penalty hole). I also had a couple of misses, a couple birdie chances just missed. Your play just off the green with the SW and LW was mostly pretty good. A couple mistakes, but for the most part you played it well.

Now on to the swing. Had a really interesting warmup session. Spent a bunch of time before that recording my swing. Three things really stood out

  1. Your Casting like crazy. I tried an exercise where you 'stab' at the middle, and that helped, and may have led you to hitting the ball longer
  2. Bent arm in the back swing. Not great, always been a problem, lots of muscle and lack of flexibility lead to problems
  3. No, or poor follow through. Same old problem.

Before I get too into the numbers, the Kinovea software took some figuring out, but I think I eventually got it kind of right. I need to figure out how to get it to replay back, but enough that I just got recordings was a good thing.

So back to my practice. Spent most of the time shooting 7i all over the place. I started working on taking the club a bit more inside, and starting the swing more with the body than the arms at the start. It actually produced some really good i7 hits... 160 yards +. It felt really good, however was unable to take any of this to the course.

I feel like sometimes the practice just doesn't carry over, and then I end up playing with poor mechanics. Anyhow... I think the video once you figure it out will be key to improving.

item.title: Thrilled with a 92 a month ago, disappointed with a 92 today.
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I played what I thought would be an easy course today. Last time I played it I scored an 87 at the red tees (4404 yards). Today, I played white, at 5200 yards. Not happy with the 92, made a lot of mistakes and didn't have distance when I needed it. Where as a lot of the recent rounds I was flying over the greens, today I was coming up short.

Now, no allowed mulligans as I've been playing lately. I took the Hybrid 3 for the tee shots. So it's not all bad. However the course is rated pretty easy (65), so I should have done better.

A few things stand out. I was rushed a bit, knew I was on the clock. So I played quick. The 37 putts was unusual, didn't hit any good putts, and made several mistakes. Over 2.0 putts per hole, which I've been able to keep down. The GIR was very low 6% (so one hole1), and my irons were not hitting well today. FIR was a bit better at 39%, but not great where I've been about 50% the last 3 rounds, with a higher GIR. Distance was more a problem today, I wasn't hitting the hybrid that great, so I 2nd shots were further than I like, lots of 170 yard + second shots on par 4s today. A few played well, but you were looking at longer path to the greens.

Also short game had a few mistakes worth mentioning.

The good news ... the rolling average continues to fall. Last 10 scores is now down to 90.2 as the last above 100 score comes off the board. However, I know it's skewed a bit with the Wynn score of 82 also coming off here soon.

The bad... my swing is getting worse again. I took some video, saw lots of flaws, but having a bit of trouble pinpointing the biggest problems. Is it the casting, is it your head movement (that is new today), is it your lack of swing through. Is it the bent arm in the back swing. Yet, despite all these pretty big flaws, I'm still striking the ball well, even with my bad mechanics.

The LLMs think the same pretty much. Face control is getting a bit better, but you had more mishits and inconsistency today. Not going to analyze this too much.

item.title: Best score, but on Junior tees
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Played with my son tonight, and decided to do the junior tees with him. Scored an 81, pretty good. I am making up the slope/rating for this one based off shorter courses, but still a decent score for the shorter course. It didn't punish the distance misses like the last round.

Front 9 went +1. 2 Birdies early helped.

Back 9 at 8 over wasn't great. Chalk that up to 3 penalties taken --- 1 a miss on a par 3 (that's hole 14), another 2 in the water. One recovered from the other was a bit of a disaster on 16.

Overall played well enough for a short course. Much higher FIR and GIR than usual. 6 putts less than yesterday too...

This keeps the average low as part of goals, but maybe a bit of a cheat playing under 5000 yards now. My goal really should be adjusted to play that 5000-5500 yards without the driver. It's also deceptive too, because I am using that boost, and I think the boost may be helping more than it's needed now. Only real course place will verify any of this, and that likely wont' happen for a bit given Winter golf times might be hard.

GSPro says I've gone from a 26 down to a 17 now. This is a bit optimistic, but I'll take it for now. IF I go with the average 'score about 5 over what I do on GSPro' , then I'm probably about mid to low 90s on a real course. Of course, that means I would have to work driver a bit and get that going. But driver + hybrid 3 should play a lot of courses.

I did play with the Gun-ho mat for the first time tonight. It seemed like a small upgrade, but useful. More punishing on the fat shots, while also feeling a little more comfortable. Less pain on the fat too. Need to start installing foam that ordered, but looks like I have to cut it some to get to fit. Funny, today was the first time in a long time I didn't have a miss slip through. Not too many high lofted shots...

item.title: My swing is stuck --- literally
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I took some videos last round, and I didn't realize how bad my follow through was really getting. This is a close approximation to what is happening now in the image. IS this indoor swing syndrome and fear to follow through. I'm sure that's playing a role, but I think there is a big sequencing issue, and a bit of a balance problem in the follow through.

If i trust my eye, shot data, and a LLM, 'my arms are late', and that is trapping my body to rotate freely. I stall to avoid the shank, and the club left exits (that's what my data + LLM says). Apparently I've gotten better in the recent rounds.

The data says, I'm producing pretty good ball speed and launch. I'm actually okay at impact. The finish is ugly because I am compensating with a flip (this goes back a long time). I al also believe that there is a balance issue in the finish, and I need to work on that.

Arms late → torso stalls → hands flip → club exits left → finish stops early. Your arms get stuck behind you → your body realizes it can’t rotate through → so it SLAMS THE BRAKES on rotation → your hands flip to square the face → the club exits left → the follow‑through gets cut off.

Basically the LLM is telling me to slow down and work on getting the arms down earlier ... this might not be entirely correct, but it's definitely a sequencing thing.

Balance Fix: Finish Stability Drill

This one is huge for you.

“Hold the Finish for 3 Seconds” Drill

  1. Hit 50% shots.
  2. After impact, freeze your finish.
  3. Hold for 3 full seconds.
  4. If you wobble, reset and try again.

C. Sequencing Fix: Arms‑In‑Front Transition

This is the drill that removes the need for the stall.

“Lead Arm Over Chest” Drill

  1. Make a backswing.
  2. Pause at the top.
  3. Feel your lead arm move down and in front of your chest before your hips unwind.
  4. Make a slow downswing.

This gets your arms synced with your torso so you don’t have to stall.

Just going to work on these for a week or so, and see if I can make improvement.

item.title: Rocky Gap - 86 & GPT lessons
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Hadn't played in a few days, busy work week. Today's round was actually super fun. Really enjoyed the Rocky Gap GC course. Some big fairways, some nice elevation changes. Not a hard course by any means, but a few challenges here and there.

An 86 felts very middling today. I really missed some shots that I could have made. Started with a poor first shot, but recovered from that quickly. Nice to see an even front and back (43 each). The short game was a little worse today, a couple mistakes there. Off the tee was good except for a couple misses.

Biggest misses today fell in to two categories

  • Iron shots short or long --- This happened 70% of the time today, meaning I had to be better with the SW, LW to get on. Today I had quite a few shots sail 10-20 yards over the green!
  • When Pitching and Chipping on , I'm not setup to par the hole. It's almost always a low percentage putt, that leads me to get in the circle but leaves me +1. Lack of distance control in the game is killing me on these short shots.

Improve on #1, the stats say I'm giving up about 13 strokes per round on that would have the biggest ROI. Cut that in half, and your dropping scores by an average of 6 strokes.

Tackling better shots around the green, you probably have 2 or 3 strokes there.

Lastly, you have your long clubs. They are still a problem with consistency and distance. You need to eventually get driver going.

There is another dimension to all this too. How much is the boost really needed. If I look at my carry distance today RAW from the monitor, I was starting to see iron numbers that looked like very real. I came at this at the start that my numbers weren't lining up, but the longer I get into this, the more I start thinking, the boost should be 5% or less. The good news is, once I get things right a little better I can likely start dropping the boost slowly.

I hate doing it, because I know that will start losing strokes. Hoping I can also coincide that with bringing more consistent longer club play in. Perhaps drop to 10% in a week or two, and start hitting the Wood more off the tee. And then drop it more to 5% and down to zero.

So that is part #1. Now lets talk about driving range and swing.

I worked on the dropping hands, and follow through that GPT suggested, and low and behold my shots tended more left than right today. It felt a bit longer too. Yes that's 160 yard i7 carry (again... do you really need a boost). i9 looks similar, even more left. The problem is still, you 110-130 yard carry is not tight enough for a i9. The i7 above included some warmup, but if you took the full shot high end, your even worse at like 130-160 carry.

I will say, my iron hits felt effortless tonight for the distance I was getting. The drills GPT recommended helped. Things may be slowly coming together.

Hoping I love the club that should arrive here soon (8 iron) that I love the shaft head combo, and will be able to order the rest of the set shortly after. Possible I don't love it too and end up hunting a bit more. But I like the idea of starting over with a new set of irons and using that at a 0% boost going forward.

item.title: Valhalla , 95! Puzzle coming together
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So weird round today. An unusually high score in the mid 90s. I thought I was playing a harder course, but the slope/rating at the end did not indicate this, and I'm almost 10 strokes higher from SAS perspective than the last 2 rounds. What happened.

  • I took the boost from 16%, down to 9%. This may have a caused a few strokes trying to adjust to to the 7% less boost.
  • I played the Wood instead of the Hybrid for first shot. This actually probably was a winner.

What caused the big lost strokes

  • 2 penalties in the water (I forgot to turn my mulligan on)
  • A couple of misses over the green in the short game.

So the wood had a really unusual behavior. Everything went straight left. Had to make some adjustments. I usually aim left fairway with the hybrid, but then I started aiming right fairway with the wood. At any rate, lots going on with the swing at the moment, so I don't want to jump to any conclusions.

Here is where things get puzzling. I really loved the 3 hybrid the last couple years. IT was the more 'controllable' club in the bag for a long time. Now it's become this weird right slice machine. I throw the club data in chat gpt, and it thinks the wood has a lower torque shaft and that would be better for me. We'll find out when the test club arrives and we start doing a comparison.

It was nice today though that dropping the boost still felt like it played pretty similar to how you've been playing. You may have lost a touch of feel around the greens, but I think I will stay at this or 8% for next couple rounds , then try dropping to 5. I've got a little bit of work to do to start getting a bit more distance on the W3. If I can get that up 190 or so. Today you were clustered around the 165-175 range, with a few going a bit longer. I think it's possible just need a bit more practice on it. Perhaps actually teeing it a bit for my first shots could help get you distance. Right now it's giving me that as my 2nd highest portion of lost strokes.

The hope is that in the next month

  1. You'll get your 8i test and confirm that it is the right head/shaft combo for your next iron set.
  2. Build out the rest of the iron set, and bring down your dispersion, and actually get some real gaps.
  3. Drop your boost down to closer to or zero.
  4. Work on straightening out your drivers and hybrids.
  5. Start hitting a few Driver shots in the sim

It's also a bit about filling out the bag. I plan on buying a 60 degree if the wedge that comes I like... it's only like 60 bucks, so seems like a no brainer. The rest will be an easy fill out of the bad from GW through either 5 or 6 iron.

LEaving the driver and 3W the same and perhaps mucking some withe hybrids next. I'm excited to get this figured out for spring, and start playing a lot more real course.

item.title: Swing weight shifts
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Because the pattern was really obvious yesterday, I threw all my data including how I had the wood and hybrid 3 setup. GPT corrected things. I'd like to give this a try on the driver a bit later, but it seems that things are bit wonky at the moment.

This is pretty exciting. At least I feel like my swing is getting consistent enough that these changes will actually do something. Swing changes from GPT below:

PXG 0311 XF GEN5 3‑Wood (Diamana 70 Stiff)

Before (your original setup)

  • Rear: 10g
  • Heel: 10g
  • Toe: 5g

What this did:

  • Maximum left bias
  • Fast face closure
  • Pulls and pull‑draws
  • Too much heel + rear weight for your delivery

This was the most draw‑biased configuration possible.

After (your new setup)

  • Toe: 10g
  • Rear: 10g
  • Heel: 5g

What this does now:

  • Slows face rotation
  • Removes draw bias
  • Straightens start lines
  • Keeps forgiveness high
  • Matches your strong‑hand‑torque delivery

This is the correct anti‑left setup for you.

XG 0311 XF GEN1 3‑Hybrid (MMT Hybrid 80 Stiff)

Before (your original setup)

  • Heel: 10g
  • Rear: 10g
  • Toe: 5g

What this did:

  • Shaft already keeps the face open
  • Light toe weight didn’t help stabilize
  • Rear weight made the head “floaty”
  • Heel weight wasn’t enough to overcome the soft tip
  • Result: wipey right misses

This was a mismatch between shaft + weighting.

After (your new setup)

  • Heel: 10g
  • Toe: 10g
  • Rear: 5g

What this does now:

  • Heel weight helps the face square
  • Toe weight stabilizes the face (reduces lag‑open)
  • Reduced rear weight improves timing
  • Should turn wipey rights into straight or slight‑draw shots

This is the correct anti‑right setup for your hybrid.

I moved the 3‑wood from a draw‑biased setup to an anti‑left setup, and the 3‑hybrid from a floaty, open‑face setup to a balanced, anti‑right setup.

Numbers later, see effect...

item.title: Wolf Creek, 89
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Not my best score, but working on things. I'll say I took a mulligan here, and a few penalties. After making the weight changes, and a decent enough warmup with the 3 wood, I decided to use the 3 wood instead of the 3H for my tee shots. This has caused some issues. I had some difficult holes where things didn't work out, and I had some good ones too. Front nine was really nice except for a blow up hole. Back 9 was a bit of a mess.

I had GPT write up a bit on the swing weights. It seemed to have basically worked through the warmup and round. I am starting to trust the AI a bit more. Lets go through the round though.

The front 9 with the exception of of hole 7 went really well. The first hole bogey, but then 3 pars and a birdie. Felt pretty good to be +1 through 5, and bogey on the next hole had me a +2. Then disaster struck on 7, which isn't a particularly hard hole, and I got a quad. I ended the front +6, which is pretty good. I hit a couple of really good putts to save holes on both sides.

The back 9 was bogey or worse 10 through 17. I par 18 to keep it at an 89. I took a mulligan, just to hit the exact same shot somewhere... so not counting that one, as it was actually played the same. Took a mulligan somewhere else where I hit the ball clean with a i7 down, and that ended up in the water. Hated that shot because I knew I should have clubbed down, and of course I caught the 7i perfectly. So I didn't really geta sub-90 score here.

Today, it was the usual misses on approach to the green, but there were some problems off the tee too. Despite a decent warmup with the 3w, I struggled with consistency. Distance and direction were all over the place. The 3W can go further...

I think some of this is related to dropping the boost. I notice this comes through with my data (carry is boosted carry). I dropped the range down to 7% today.

I've played this course 4 times now: 86, 94, 88, 89. Each one has been a bit of a different story.

Starting to create a list of courses I really like, and this is one of my favorites, even though last couple outings haven't been stellar. Plays pretty fun at 5000 yards.

Others that have been good... Here is my list to date

  1. Wynn - Usually pretty fun, played multiple times.
  2. Wolf Creek GC
  3. Rocky Gap - hidden gem for me, really enjoyed this one this week for the first time
  4. River Creek - one of the few I play a bit because I've played in real life
  5. Arizona National GC - was good at 5300 Yellow tees

Those are the most played, a few others I've liked but haven't done well on include Edgewood Tahoe, Valhalla. Falls, Whiskey Creek and Woodmont are interesting to play because they are close, but haven't played IRL. Sanctuary Moon is fun to play with the novelty factor.

Looking at my scoring average... at least in game. I started at a 110 SAS and a 103 average. After a few months... I'm down on to a 94 SAS, and an 88 average. So I dropped 16 strokes off the SAS from the start, and 15 on the average. So pretty close on the easier courses. Getting better, but I really think cleaning up the iron game, and figuring out how to get a bit more distance off the tees will drop me to the low 80s, and the SAS down to the high 80s. Hoping that will equate to at least low 90s when I hit the course in the spring!

Okay, now on to the swing weight analysis. Actually will just make this another post

item.title: Swing Weight Shifts: What Really Happened When I Re‑Weighted My Long Game
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So everything below here was written by chat-gpt/copilot. IT took in a bunch of data and then did the analysis. It did take the data make a recommendation, and then confirmed with further data after the weight changes. I think it over emphasized how much better it is, it was better, but not as dramatic as GPT made it sound.

I’ve been chasing a very specific goal in my long game: get the 3‑wood to stop going left, and get the 3‑hybrid to stop going right. Two opposite problems, two opposite fixes — and both of them came down to head weighting.

This week I finally sat down and rebuilt the weight maps in both clubs. Then I took them straight into a round to see what actually changed.

The results were… eye‑opening.

3‑Wood: From Hook Machine to Fairway Finder

My PXG 0311 XF GEN5 3‑wood came stock with a weight setup that was basically a hook generator:

Original Weight Setup

This is the most draw‑biased configuration PXG makes. With my delivery — forward shaft lean, strong hand torque, left‑biased path — it was a recipe for pull‑draws and snap‑lefts.

So I flipped the script.

New Weight Setup

The goal was simple: slow the face down.

On‑Course Results

The difference was immediate:

  • Start lines centered or slightly right
  • Curvature controlled
  • No snap‑lefts
  • No “fear of left” swings
  • Face‑to‑path stayed in a tight, playable window

For the first time in a long time, I could actually swing the 3‑wood without guarding the left side. This club is officially fixed.

3‑Hybrid: Better… but the Shaft Is Still the Limiter

My 3‑hybrid had the opposite problem. It wasn’t shutting too fast — it was staying open forever. The original weight setup didn’t help:

Original Weight Setup

The rear weight made the head floaty, the toe weight was too light to stabilize the face, and the MMT Hybrid 80S shaft (soft tip, higher torque) lagged the face open.

So I rebuilt it.

New Weight Setup

The idea was to help the face square up and reduce the wipey right miss.

On‑Course Results

The weighting change helped:

  • Start lines improved
  • Curvature reduced
  • Fewer wipey rights

But the shaft is still the bottleneck. The face still lags open too often, and the spin axis still tilts too far right.

This club needs a more stable shaft — something like the Riptide 80 6.0 (which works beautifully in my 5H) or a Tensei Blue 80S.

The head is now doing its job. The shaft isn’t.

5‑Hybrid: Predictable Fade, Very Playable

The 5H continues to be the quiet hero of the bag.

  • Slight right start lines
  • Small, predictable fade
  • Stable face delivery
  • Consistent spin

It’s playable for me — and honestly, it might be even better for my son. This club is exactly what a properly matched hybrid shaft should look like in my hands.

PXG 0211 Irons: The Elevate MP Problem

My PXG 0211 irons with Elevate MP shafts continue to show the same issues:

  • Face‑to‑path all over the place
  • Spin numbers that swing from 3200 to 7000+
  • Start lines that can go left, right, or straight with no pattern
  • Ball speed inconsistencies

This isn’t a head problem. It’s a shaft problem.

The Elevate MP is too soft in the tip, too high in torque, and too timing‑dependent for my delivery. It simply can’t stabilize the face.

These irons are on borrowed time.

KE4 Max PW + Wedges: Stable, Predictable, Exactly What I Need

The KE4 Max PW and wedges continue to be the most stable clubs in my bag:

  • Tight face‑to‑path
  • Predictable spin
  • Consistent start lines
  • No fliers
  • No wipey misses

This is what my swing looks like when the head and shaft actually match my delivery.

It’s also why I’m so excited for the MMT 90 test iron.

What I Expect Next

The MMT 90 8‑iron is on the way, and based on everything I’ve seen, I expect it to deliver:

  • PW‑like stability
  • 9‑iron‑like distance
  • Tight spin window
  • Predictable start lines
  • No fliers
  • No snap‑lefts
  • No wipey rights

If the 8‑iron behaves like my KE4 Max PW — but with more speed — then the entire iron set is getting rebuilt.

And honestly, after this round, that feels inevitable.

item.title: New goals ---the path to lower scores.
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I've got a new set of goals now. I've made some really awesome progress so lets go over that first! My scores since getting the SIM are summarized here SIM Scores – Winter 25-26 – The Iffy Lie

As of today 1/12, I've dropped nearly 16 strokes off the average since the start! 16 strokes in just about 2 and 1/3 months! That's pretty insane. That factors in both SAS and averages, both stats average out to a best of around 16 stroke improvement. That is somewhere between a 15.8 - 16.2 stroke improvement since starting.

Some of this may just be 'getting better at a video game', but I do think I've improved greatly and it will somewhat translate to on course. But first, continued improvement in the SIM is the short term goal. It's easy to predict where the improvement will need to come from. I think that improvement will also have the most carry over to my outside game: Approach shots.

It's all about those iron shots and dialing those in. New irons will probably get me to practice that more. I think I will ignore most other parts of the game as they are 'good enough' right now. I believe there is a full 8 to 10 strokes of improvement available there. That would put me at

  • Average SIM scores around 84, average SAS Scores 86. Goal by about mid-march.

It's easy to game this a bit once you start getting better. You continue to play shorter (5000 yard courses) with your woods. You can expect a bit of uptick which your starting to see right now with a decrease in the boost your using. So much for Indoor Swing Syndrome... your going to start dropping down to err on the side of caution and carryover to the course.

How do I get there. I think now that your working back to Ops36. When I first did that, I saw some big improvements in my iron play for a bit. It also helped the short game. This would be part 1.

That mid 80s average will hopefully equate to the next goal

  • Average a low 90s (no mulligan game) on real courses in the spring.

This is going to be super tricky... I see two problems.

  • Adjusting to be back outside and all the elements that can effect things that don't happen inside
  • Will need to get driver back in play --- you'll need to just hit a bit longer to play the courses.

I'll use a course I play often, Laytonsville. I think I would typically play the white tees at 5500 yards, which really is on the cusp of what requires driver for me. This means you'll need to practice that driver some, and your not going to get that practice inside likely because of ceiling issues.

Now back to SIM goals, I have some shorter term for mid March, but overall, I'd like to

  • Average SIM scores drop below 80

I think after you start working your irons out, it will just be slight improvements in each area. Putting, 50 yards in, Off the tee & of course the irons. Working all those a stroke here and there. Same will go for dropping the outdoor scores down in the 80s. I feel like playing at a 15 handicap by the end of the year is doable.

I should start making a video series, and learn some stuff. This might be fun, you've seen success dropping your scores to this point.

item.title: Domaine LaForest 89 - A straighter 3 wood and Ops 36 revisited.
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
While it's normally the iron game where I lose strokes, today it was more even across the game. I've been varying the courses more as of late, and the scores reflect

The stats have me losing strokes off the tee... I hit a few way shorter than needed (although more on that later, as I'm actually hitting the 3W pretty well now).

Around the green was really poor today. I missed a lot of shots... chipped over the green at least 2 times, and several others where I left insanely long putts. Probably 4 outright mistakes. Putting was not great. Last rounds 26 putts, today was all the way up at 32.

Iron game as usual, either short or long. Funny that one of the best shots I hit was a long approach with the 3W to the green.

The Adjusted Average is up to 90 right now, with the adjusted SAS at 94.4. Not terrible, considering the decrease in boost, and the randomness in the courses being played.

Now one thing I really did like about this round... I'm hitting the wood a lot better. This chart had some nice improvement. Not hitting it 'as left'. Still the mess is way more left than right, but I like that there is a cluster in the 170-190 range. Just a tad short of where I'd like it. I'm not even hitting it hard, just making good contact, and figured out something with the swing of the woods that I like (basically getting my shoulder a little down through the swing).

At any rate, that isn't great, but it's an improvement. Especially that cluster of straight shots just slightly left in the 180-190 range. That is better than the 3 hybrid, and a more playable long game going forward.

The LLM didn't think it was the great, but said it was at least consistent. The LLM discussion also agreed that i9 is a problem as the distance is all over the place (Good strike to miss), and actually gets better up the bag. Interesting stuff.

After I finished this round , I spent time with Op36. I probably should wait for the new wedge and irons, but I felt like my short game wasn't working well so wanted the practice. I quickly got through 25 (score 27), 50 yards (score 29), and 100 yards (score 35). Struggled a bit on the 100 yards with the i9, but got better as I went through. The 50 & 100 are very good practice for me.

I'm excited to do the 150 yard tees... Despite the inconsistencies in the i7, the LLM suggested I play that for that club. I often carry a good strike in the 140-150 range on the i7, so a very playable club when I'm hitting well. Perhaps a way to start getting consistent here.

One last bit, Very excited to get my i8 and see if we get some confirmation on the irons. It doesn't appear to have been shipped almost 2 weeks out now. So I'm looking at best case getting it early next week, confirming over 2 sessions and then purchasing the rest of the set. If it doesn't work... well, then back to a bit more shopping and working with what I have now for a bit longer. It's tough, because I'm seeing some swing changes, and hard to predict as I cleanup more issues whether the next set will continue to play well.

item.title: Am I getting better?
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So going back and forth with GPT to try to see 'am I actually improving'. I know the scores are going down, but I can see some anomalies with putting and short game in the early rounds, and frankly the irons haven't improved much in accuracy at all. So what about things like club path, spin and ball speed... are they improving?

I think club path tells a decent story if GPT isn't lying to me. It so wants me to think I'm getting better that I caught it in a lie making up driver paths (I don't hit driver, but have early rounds labeled driver, but recent rounds it would have had no data for. ... see table below)

If the table is right, you've had an improvement in path more on plane.

Because I was playing with a heavy boost at the start (16% now down to 5%) I want to compare ball speed because that number isn't boosted, just the carry and distance seems to get boosted. There are a bit of shenanigans going on ... because yes my i8 is broken, but I believe it snuck in some data that was labeled i8

So we do see a general increase in ball speed by about 5 mph but still have a wide range in ball speed.

Asked to analyze more... and again, there are so many issues here. One is that my club selection doesn't work correctly on course (so W3 were H3 in some cases until I fully switched)

4. The Real Story (No Spin, No Fluff)

✔ Your path is dramatically less left

This is the biggest improvement.

✔ Your HLA tightened

Still left, but not wildly left.

✔ Your spin dropped

Still high, but no longer chaotic.

✔ Your pattern is the same

  • Path left
  • Face open to path
  • Heel contact
  • Fade bias

…but the severity is way down.

✔ You’re now in a playable fade window

Not neutral, not draw‑capable, but playable.

So basically they think my plane is shifting.. that's good, speed increasing that's good, and my spin decreasing... also good. I know that my misses in some clubs appear to be a bit tighter. Not great at all, but the misses tend to be more the same than different.

Now that I have access to this data, it does appear that ball speed, path and spin are improving with the scores. I really want to get so much tighter with the data, and unfortunately my pestering of the GSPro team on the problem with it switching my club after a shot will clear up certain things (But not history).

I should start keeping the csv's ready to go from here on out so that we can make good comparisons. I think as of the last round I am hitting closer to 90% of the suggested, so this should have me get better tracking in to this year.

Looking forward to playing with the Beta today. Maybe I'll even get lucky and have the club thing fixed in this version.

item.title: DPC Pebble - 87
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I a have been converging on these high 80s scores over the last several rounds. 87,89,89,95(outlier), 86. This is a good thing, it's a bit higher than the low average, and given the mistakes I've been making these scores are actually pretty good. Cut those mistakes your in the low 80s. I've also dropped the boost from 16%, to 9%, to 7%, to 5% over the last 5 rounds. I think I will stick on 5% for a bit here, but this is generally pretty good that you can score roughly the same without the boost. You've also adjusted to 'Normal' pin placement. The SAS average is down to 93.8, and the average score @ 72 is down to 90.8. My GSPRO handicap is down to 17.3 from a ~26. So you're 9 strokes better than you were in December when the new laptop came.

The big mistakes today were shanking SW (which is actually turning in to my strongest club for 50 yards in), failing to get out of the Sand trap once, and missing a few tee shots really badly. The tee shots with the wood, while good in warmup, really went too far left during the round. It was fine though, as the left misses were generally a safer bet.

Despite the struggles in the longer game, the putter around the green were pretty good. Putting was a positive strokes gained. I had a total of 28 putts. I was able to close some of the putts that just missed the circles, converting bogey's to pars.

Most of today's game was Wood and Hybrid, and the SW... Not too many irons required (looks like a total 5 iron shots, and 2 5 hybrids) . Granted, I don't think any of those shots connected with the green. The longer end actually played better today.

Analyzing my swing warmup, and shots taken during the round:

Irons first:

Hybrids:

That was wood. Any the summary:

✔ You are way faster

Your athletic ceiling is rising.

✔ Your path is dramatically better

You’re no longer in the danger zone.

✔ Your start lines are tighter

This is a real improvement.

❌ Your face‑to‑path is still too open

This is the #1 thing holding you back.

❌ Your strike is still heel‑biased

This is the #2 limiter.

❌ Your spin is still too high

This is the #3 limiter — caused by #1 and #2.

item.title: Kiawah 91 --- what could have been?
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
A start of birdie, bogie, par to even through 3 seemed really promising, then it went downhill. Penalties (at least 3 extra strokes there), and in an inability to hit the wood today after being so successful with it the last few led to a disappointing score.

With the bad there was some good though. The GW for 50-60 shots was dead on. The putting was decent enough with only 29 putts. Despite this, I think I missed 3 putts that I should have made from within 8 feet, just outside the circle, and had a couple that went long. This stat is surprising.

The Rating/Slope on this course Red tees was also a 67.6/124. Close to Pebble. Probably about the same as Pebble, just a different kind of challenge.

As usual, the iron approach to green was the leaky part of the boat... with the tee shots coming second. I think not warming up the wood was part of the problem.

Kind of interesting, I played the 100 yard Op36 as a warmup. Today I scored a 31 (different course.. .but no easier. Prior was a 35. I scored a 31, and the strength was 'approach to green'. I figured out how to get a bit more consistent on those 100 yard shots with a non-boosted 9 iron. I was also mostly dead on for 30-50 yards, or closer.

Putting the data from today back in to gpt --- everything was shifted 2-3 degrees left today . It described this as my fatigue pattern ... which makes sense after a very deadlift day. It fits perfectly (even before I told it), it told me your neuromuscular fatigue.

Suggested actually hitting the ball right and then work to move it back to center... interesting. Also talks about 'right pocket back' to start swing, which seems a bit hard to concentrate on. Club drops, arms falling, chest soft makes a bit more sense. This is a weird one.

item.title: Rocky Gap -- A strange round
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I scored a 90, 4 worse than the last time. Up until Hole 12 I actually thought I was having an okay round. Had 2 birdies, on a not particularly good day overall. There was a blow up hole, which I probably should erase a stroke from because I believe my son actually hit a shank for me... but I'm sure that got made up later and the hole was pretty bad.

At any rate... swing was actually feeling okay for the first 11 holes, and then on hole 12 everything fell apart. Had a moment where I couldn't actually hit the ball at all. It was bizarre. Tossed this to GPT and said my sequencing temporarily collapsed because of fatigue. Makes a bit of sense since I hit another workout that was kind of tough. I keep thinking I have more energy in me than I think.

I'm not going to go through the full analysis like I normally do, as I was so shook by the breakdown. I think it's actually not bad that I ended with a 90 with all 4 double bogey's and 3 bogey's on the last 7 holes. The stats confirmed it was the usual suspects (approach shots) that failed you. A bit of problems around the green, the usual 1 or 2 mistakes, and the usual one or two putting mistakes (31 putts). The Tee shots as they've been lately, have been a liability. Perhaps I should actually use a tee.

I'm hoping this is just a minor bump in the road as the average is stabilizing around 90, and the SAS around 94 before the next big jump down!.

item.title: I'm back -- Torrey South
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So today I swung easy, stayed in my game and scores a nice 84 on Torrey South.

The wood was a strength today, both off the tee and on second shots. It wasn't particularly long, but it didn't go 'of course'. I hit it well. I made the usual few mistakes (couple shots in the bunkers than didn't come out of the bunkers on the first shot).

The hybrids were fine. The irons struggled. The wedges were okay, not as good as I've been, but very playable.

Hit a very nice birdie with the i9 on hole 8, that caught the outside of the gimme circle. That is rare for me. Brought the 'Approach to Green' metric down a bit today. Had a couple of good approaches.

The putting has been a strength the last couple go arounds, getting better at reading and gauging distance in game. I am 'going for it' a bit more from 12 feet or so out, and making it on occasion.

One really noticeable metric here... only 2 double or more today. When I score low, that seems to be the trend.

Now... while the tee shots (wood off the deck) were good, I noticed my distance seemed to be down just a tad. I'm hitting okay, but it isn't traveling.
