I was watching a video earlier of a guy, and I know he was giving legit numbers, and thinking I should be hitting somewhere closer to this guy... what is wrong with me. Today I chased a bit more consistency, and it lowered the score, but I ended up short on quite a few shots today. I felt the warmup also showed irons a bit short.

Some of this may be an adjustment to being down the 5% boost now, but at least that's a good. I just really need to start figuring out how to get more distance out of my clubs... I feel like I need to get about 10 to 15% longer to be competent this coming season --- or at least hit what I did last season when hitting well. I know, bad to chase the distance, but It sucks when you struggle on a par 4 350 yards, and only hit the ball 150 on the tee --- leaving you a par 5 like distance on the 2nd shot.

item.title: Another fun GSPro round
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Old Kinderhock GC score of an 82 on a 71 par. So a few big points

  • I enjoy the variety of courses now. At first I liked to play the same courses, now I love hitting a new course each time out, with an occasional repeat.
  • I played within my game today, hit decent 3W for the tee shot... straighter than usual, felt pretty good
  • Worked on speed prior to , and got some more distance out of the i7, but translated poorly to course, and actually increased the dispersion on the i7... it was either 140 yards, or 90... really terrible.
  • Everything else played well, a couple small mistakes made keeping from getting under 80. This is the current goal... get under 80. You've been really close

So good round, not great. A little extra distance would help in general. My iron play continues to be the biggest leak. My SW continues to be a really good club for 'getting in the circle'. Putting is deceptive, I putted okay, but it was really short game (since I mostly missed greens), that got me in good scoring position.

An interesting chart I had GPT help me with showing how improvement looks. I am still pretty much playing 'Bogey golf'. But the percentage of doubles has gone way down , while the percentage of pars has seen a fairly stead rise (although you can see I had a peak that has leveled off). The number of birdies has remained over 10% the whole time. Bogey's have actually gone up, but that is a result of a drop in the number of doubles.

The next chart is my scoring, but what it doesn't show is a decrease in boost from 16% down to 5%, and a bit of increase in difficulty of courses. The yellow line shows this some as the slope adjusted average has steadily declined from a 110 down to it's current low of 92.8. 17 Strokes better than I was a little over a month ago (was around 110 around mid-December, before it started dropping as I got to play more during the break).

I can see if I can just work out the iron game, I think I've got another 5 strokes in me at the current typical course (5000-5500 yards), with the 5% boost. After that, will consider decreasing the boost down to zero, and try to figure out a way to get courses up to around the 6000 yard range with perhaps a mini-driver or something of that sort.

After I finally get a round under 80, the next goal is getting the average down to low 80s (currently at 88.5 - so drop about 5 strokes down to 83), and the SAS about the same (at 92.8, so down to 87). From there, it will hopefully be to outside to figure out what all the means.

item.title: New clubs coming, sim upgrades, and cold golfing?
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I've been waiting for a long time on these new clubs. My 8 iron 'test club'. I'm excited to see what if any difference the shaft makes on the 8 iron with the Mitsubishi MMT. This is all a bit of a delay to get to, but I'm excited. I'll need at least 2 or sessions with it, but what I'm looking for is something in between the 7 and 9 --- hopefully closer to peak 7 distance, and a tighter dispersion, a little less punishing on the mishits. If that proves out, I'll put the rest of the iron set on order. If not... I think I'll be doing a bit more try and compare...

I'm also super excited to replace my SW with this Maltby wedge. If I love everything, the rest of the new clubs will be on the way. The disappointment in this is that it may take till the end of February to finish out this build if I like it. My clubs still haven't shipped, but they said they would ship this week (but snow... so probably not until next). I likely get earliest is Monday or Tuesday.

I've also pretty much decided I'm going to order a Callaway Big Bertha mini driver used at some point for sim use only. A 12 degree with a 44" stiff shaft should get me a little distance that should close the gap and get me moving in to the 6000 yard range here eventually. Ideally, I'd love to hit in the 230 range with a mini-driver off the tee for sim rounds. Right now a good 3W is on average in the SIM getting me around 170-180 (unboosted), and the hybrid 3 is 160 (again unboosted). Occasionally I get those downhill numbers in the 200+ range, but can't count on any of that. I feel like I should be 20 yards longer on every club on these carries. I think I'm 20 yards longer when I hit it right on course, but I definitely have made some swing changes. At any rate, I have changed course a bit on the importance of distance. I need my approach shots to be a bit more manageable. However as it is right now, some days I'd rather hit the 3 hybrid versus hitting a 6 or 7 iron.

So it's super cold out right now. Like feels like 0 degrees kind of cold. The garage has been around 44 degrees the last few days. I haven't played since the 23rd , which is a longish stretch of 5 days right now. I will workout today, so likely first really playable day is tomorrow, and will require a long time to get the garage up to a manageable temp. When the outside weather is even around freezing, the garage is manageable. Anything I think above 75 degrees outside, will start to get in to a weird state in the garage... so basically the setup will be good from fall through spring with some spots in winter that are unplayable (like now), and a maybe a few spots in summer when it cools off when it can be used again. When leaving the door open, the A/C or heat can influence the garage temp a bit .

I got a new light to hang in the garage too... hopefully provide a better experience overall with a bit more light. It's weird playing in the dark, and the extra garage light isn't perfect. I'll get some pictures soon.

Biggest disappointment right now has been the camera setup. I can't seem to get enough brightness to record. It's not simple to playback and getting the timing right has been a lot of trial and error. I still think there is a big payoff here if you can get it right, but so far no go. I also think getting the rear view could pay some dividends, but the idea of switching the camera setup around periodically seems really messy. Basically the whole technical setup is getting complicated with wires going everywhere, and adding in the camera adds a layer of time and complexity to the whole process. I enjoy playing so much, and hate the idea of spending 15 minutes to get it setup right... even last go around I spent more than 15 minutes, and then the camera went dark.

One last sim comment... I've been annoyed with a bug in the GSPro tracking. When I select a club in the app, it always reverts to the suggested club. This causes my stats to be off. I am thinking about switching back to the OpenAPI version and see if that solves it. Unfortunately though, since the square software is involved, not sure that will fix it. It's likely got something to do with the square. I suppose it could also be fixed by just playing and trusting the suggested club.

item.title: Valhalla 88 - Distance and AoA drills
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So first the round

  • Scored an 88, no mulligans. Excellent front 9 42, struggle on the back 9 46
  • I played with a 4% boost, and scored 7 strokes better than I did on the same course on January 7th with a 9% boost. This is an excellent improvement.... 7 strokes better on 5% less boost on a not particularly well played short game. Progress!
  • I finished 3 out of the last 4 holes with double bogey's. One was because of a penalty, the others were just bad short game. This should have been and 84-86 range. The number of doubles+ was high compared to recent rounds
  • Hit a birdie on 2, with a good approach. Previous time this hole was a triple bogey.
  • Putting wasn't great... setup long several times. Chipping with the SW was not great, made several mistakes. Chipper was less efficient today too... just didn't have the right feels.
  • Breakdown a bit more even... still approach is the problem, but it was equally as bad around the green and off the tee today. I felt good off the tee, and 57% of fairways... but had a fair number of balls go off course.

Before getting into the distance discussion , I finished this round with a bit of op36 practice. GSpro can be buggy... it missed the first round, which I think I went -2 on the 100 yard course. Then I was trying the 150, but trying to see if I could get enough distance on the i7. IT didn't work well, and I was tired so I cut it a bit short.

I did have one big revelation. I switched back to the OpenAPI version for GSPro, and it's recording the correct club per stroke. I actually got correct stats for the first time since I started tracking! This is exciting.

My GSPro handicap continues to fall, I'm down to 16.5, and my short term goal is to get it down below 10.

Now lets talk warmup and distance...

I did the thing were I swing forward and back which helps me stay loose and time things up. This worked today. Also of note, continued the drop to 4% boost (so these are only a little juiced). Lets throw some examples.

  • PW - Solid around 95-100 Carry --- not great
  • i9 - around 105-110 Carry
  • i7 - good shots were about 140-145 carry
  • H3 - Good shots 160-170 Carry

Those were the warmup numbers, and those are numbers than I can live with if I were at zero boost. These all played a bit longer than those numbers

Now during the round, this dropped off a bit... your good strikes

  • W3 - about 160-170 Carry (same as H3) -- Totals about 170-180...
  • i7 Carry about 110-120 -- A full 20 yards shorter.
  • i9 Carry - ranged up to 120, but the mean was about 100.

So again, if I were to describe my ideal range inside the SIM going forward ... this is where I think I can be if I can keep the speed up, these would be carry numbers:

  1. W3 - about 180 Carry would be ideal here... 180-200 distance
  2. H3 - about 170 Carry would be ideal,
  3. H5, 160 Carry
  4. I6 - 150
  5. i7 - 140
  6. i8 - 130
  7. i9 - 120
  8. PW - 110
  9. GW- 100
  10. SW 54 - 90 full swing
  11. 60 degree - 75 full swing

Add in hopefully a driver you can carry a bit longer than 200 yards, and you would have a playable indoor sim game you. these are ideals in an upboosted state based on where you swing could be with a bit more consistency.... but I seem a bit closer to this today than before.

Now the question keeps coming up for me. I've got a pattern that increases distance, but not a swing that can be applied like this. So I asked Copilot again. Copilot noticed an issue with AoA too, sees I'm bottoming a little late (kind of explains the fat misses). Anyhow... for the speed part

1️⃣ One Rehearsal, Then Hit

Before a shot:

  • Do one forward‑then‑back rehearsal at 50%
  • Step in and hit normally

No thinking. No copying. Just let the body remember the timing.

This keeps the sequence without exaggeration.

2️⃣ Grip Pressure Check (Critical)

Your speed disappears when grip pressure creeps up.

On a scale of 1–10:

  • Warm‑up drill: ~3–4
  • Normal swing: creeps to 6+

Before you swing:

  • Lighten the last three fingers of your trail hand
  • Keep pressure in the lead hand only

This alone preserves a surprising amount of speed.

3️⃣ Swing Thought That Works Under Pressure

Use one of these — not all:

  • “Smooth to the top, fast through the ball”
  • “Wait… then go”
  • “Late speed”

They all cue the same thing: don’t rush transition

The big thing I see here is that this drill is helping learn when to apply the speed.

Now the other sort of easy drill for bringing the AoA in to a better range is to put a tee an inch or two in front of the ball during your practice and make sure your not hitting the club. Do this practice with a i7. Will try this Saturday and hopefully you are starting to get some of this distance back.

item.title: Bear Dance -- mixed round
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I will preface this one with my body didn't feel great today, and I forced myself to play. I ended up scoring an 89 on a course that was rated a bit more difficult than what I usually play. The Slope was 130, and I usual play something that is more in the 115 to 125 Range. This ended up producing a slope-adjusted score, better than some of my most recent scores. So I am less disappointed.

  • 2 Birdies today. One came from a chip in, and the other was a well placed SW.
  • Too many bad holes today. I had 4 Doubles, and 3 triples! I rarely see triples anymore. The triples came from hitting in to the water on one hole, and some bad putting on another.
  • My putting stunk today. I missed all of the just outside the circle shots that I usually make, however I hit one insanely long putt.
  • GIR was as bad as it's been lately... I have no iron game.
  • Off the tee wasn't terrible, but the wood was going left again. Apparently data says path closing early, need to get it out a bit more right. I actually felt like there were good shots here, and the bad shots were mostly playable.
  • My GSPro HC index went down to 16.1 after this round.
  • This course build is fantastic, and will be played again as a challenge.

It's all about the lack of consistency in the iron game. The wedges have become more playable... SW and GW I can score with. i9-i6, not so great. I have a better shot keeping a long hybrid on the green than I do the irons lately. I just never know what's going to happen...

Interesting for the first time in a long time, putting was not a strength, perhaps it was upping the stimp back up to 8 threw me off. I've been playing at a 7 more often than not lately, but I like

Funny how an 89 feels like a failure. Back in mid-December you were happy with anything under 100 with a rolling 100 average. That's a ton of improvement. Just since December 25th, my average has dropped from 100 down to 88. 12 Strokes (The SAS is down 14 strokes). Even if half of that is 'video game improvement' , that is still a ton of progress.

Asking Copilot again, how much improvement can I expect if I can fix my irons (really thinking about this separate from wedges, except for many PW), so I improve that it thinks:

  • Gain 5 to 7 strokes and 3 to 5 more greens per round.
  • Aggressive but possible improvement of 8 to 10 strokes

Next likely bottlenecks :

  • Off the tee likely next, hitting 140 yard approaches vice 180 yard recoveries. I think this will matter even more when you start translating back to outside.
  • Expected a 2 to 4 stroke gain from this.

A total realistic improvement 8 to 13 strokes is what Copilot thinks... not a bad move.

I love looking ahead, and what they say after you hit that milestone you start getting 'real carry numbers' and getting more consistent in the 120-175 yard range. I think it assumes you have gotten good enough 120 yards in at this point.

The new clubs arrive later today. . I'm sure I will want to play again, so expect lots of comparison between the i8 and the i7 and i9 with the different shafts. Praying that I will want to order the rest of the set, and then move forward. I've got some good ideas on how to practice the irons to fix things too... fun to come.

item.title: Tahoe - Best Round ever, and the new clubs
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So this will be a long one. Let's start off with the sim round recap. Edgewood Tahoe. Played the Red Tees each time. I played on Oct 30 and scored a 99 with 6 mulligans when I was just getting started. December 16- I scored a 102 with 1 mulligan. Both of those rounds were with the 16% boost, Today -- 80, no mulligans, with the 4% boost!!! This bring my handicap index down to 14.7 in GSPro. Let's go!!!

This is also one of the highest rating and slope I have in my list. Making this extra good. I was really required to manage the course well today, and hit some excellent shots, minimized mistakes and got lucky a few times.

A bit unfortunate, GSPro had a rare crash mid round. It happened on hole 15, which I happened to double bogey with a missed putt, but the stats themselves only show holes 15 through 18, so that stinks. So unfortunate, but I won't know what my strokes gained here. I do have some info from my shots that will guide some of this.

So lets talk a bit on scorecard. So many good things happened. I double bogey the first hole, and bogey the second, but instead of getting frustrated, I just kept going, and par'ed 6 of the next 7 holes. I couldn't even tell you went wrong with hole 1 and hole 6 (2 of my 3 doubles for the day). I only recall making a couple mistakes , and a couple of holes where distance was a bit of an issue on par 4s, with long setups, or forced in to safe plays away from water.

I ended the first 9 +5. This felt really good after the first 2 holes. The back 9 I pared 5 of the holes, birdied a par 5 on 16, and hit 2 bogey and one aforementioned double bogey when the system crashed. A 39 on the back 9.

I do know a few good things happened... I hit 2 longish putts. I also hit 1 or 2 chip ins from right off the green. These easily took 4 or 5 strokes off the card. I think the histogram of shots tells a good story on the rest of my play.

Dispersion was not terrible on the Woods, a bit right bias today, but I managed it well. The new i8 played perfectly for most shots between 110-120 yards! A missing piece in previous rounds. The i6 played perfectly when I needed it. The h3 did it's job on it's one shot. The h5 was a bit of a mess, 3 shots and one that was complete miss.

The SW took a bit of getting used to early, but basically picked up where I left off, and by the end was loving the new 54!

So always nice to have a solid round, and watch the handicap go down over a stroke:

So let's talk about the i8 club first. It was different, but felt pretty good. I can attest, there is a little less feedback from the strike, but what I gained was quite a bit tighter more reliable direction. I felt like I was right in the 120-130 range during the warmup, and about 10 yard shorter while I played. The good thing though, tight dispersion and straight even on the misses. I had 6 shots during the round, I had one that came up very short, but everything else was within about a small dispersion circle. It felt 'forgiving'

This next dispersion chart tells a bit of the story too... I think a good rehearsal of the iron shots was helping. I worked a bit on keeping things centered in the practice swing and making sure my grip setup was good.

You can see the i8 was actually pretty good today too, albeit a little short. While the i6 served decently the 140-150 yard range. I purposedly didn't hit the i7 on a hole because I didn't want to mess with my groove. The i9 felt very short today.

The new SW felt more solid and weighty. It was hard to say if it's an improvement, but the build felt better. I was tight on the directional dispersion, but that is typically true on the low end of the bag. The one GW I hit, missed 5 yards right. Everything with the SW was within about 3 yards over my 11 shots.

So it's hard to trust Copilot, but just given the small sample size it says the i8 in this configuration proves out everything. It is more stable, better fit for me. The price is right (free with my company reimbursement), so I will likely hit some more tomorrow, and then pull the trigger.

item.title: The Iron Data
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I know I should wait at least one more day, but here is the initial data from the last 3 range sessions. I should add in another session to normalize for multiple days before purchasing. Right now with my 1 session of data you can make the assumption

  • The Maltby KE4 Max with Mitsubishi MM 90 S had a lower Carry and Lateral variance than other clubs. This is probably partly contributed to less data on the club and a single session
  • Lofts are higher on the 0211, making direct comparisons a bit tricky
  • The i7 0211 shows a significantly higher ceiling and distance over recent data, however there was also some speed training in this data set that may produce outliers.
  • When looking at mean carry in course played data the window tightens quite a bit, the mean gaps look about right (10 yards), with the i7 being a wildcard.
  • You should value consistency over distance at this point, but you don't' want to give up 10 yards per club, and need to find the right mix.

At a very basis look, you can see the mean carry trends a bit higher on the 0211. But maybe that is loft:

So I'm losing 2 degrees loft on the 8 up... so that could explain a bit. Not getting away from that I likely have a much tighter window and a better miss now. But asking Copliot on distance... I know you can't have it both ways, but lets take a look

That doesn't necessarily paint a great picture... your losing some distance. The way Copilot puts it, is that when I flush it I am able to create more ball speed with the 0211, but it is greatly more punishing my misses. You can see , Copilot tries to correct for loft, and you end up about 5 yards short with those normalized projections. I suppose one could hope for longer and straighter, but your gonna have to trade off somewhere.

I fear, the 7i at 117 just feels super short to me. This is where everything starts to look a little murky. But then I realized in the last couple sessions I was working on speed. So the i7 data was all over the place. I was able to get some really good 140 yard carry out of the i7 by playing with my back and forth swing drill ... I was able to max it around 150.

So today I carry that i8 max 136, and I'm more like a good hit, in the 115-120 carry range. But lets maybe just look at our best hits, and see if we deduce from there, perhaps our median hit isn't telling us the right thing

So when you look at it like this (which may not be purely fair), then you see the i8 about 10 yards longer, but only a 3 degree difference the ceiling efficiency looks higher

Carry per degree of loft (ceiling efficiency)

However when we throw the i7 in ... we get an outlier

Now, going through all this took the last several weeks of game data... not the best dataset as things move up and down.

Okay, interesting that we hit some high fliers with the i6 and i7... but the i8 and i9 tend to cluster lower. When you go back to mean ball speed though ...

When looking at those numbers:

I7 vs I8

  • Same mean ball speed (~81 mph)
  • Same carry per mph (~1.26–1.27)
  • Different lofts

That tells us:

  • The I8 is not inefficient
  • The I8 is producing exactly the carry it should for its loft
  • Any distance difference is purely loft‑driven

Digging further over a longer period, and having them filter out the long and short, to try to get to stock carry

That all seems about right. Efficiency according to Copilot at those speeds tracks correctly. I asked about spin

This actually bears out from what I've seen ... my i9 tends to launch super high... IT does feel like the i7 has some of that too. Not to say the i8 will be any different, but it did seem to be a little less floaty.

What does this all tell me... I need more data before making a decision. I will not make the perfect decision, that's impossible. I am more evaluating a move to a more predictable iron set versus a slight more distance. But what is really going to matter is the distance off the tee to setup manageable

Asking Copilot about the top bag a little now. My average carry on the wood is currently clusters around 160, I need to get 10 to 20 yards more comfortably out of that club, likely same thing with the 3 hybrid. I believe having dropped the boost over time, and I have gained about 10 % comfortably by just being more consistent (ie, my distances are the same with the boost dropping over 6 weeks), but I do think there are some things I should be doing to get more distance on the top end of the bag. There is something just wrong given my strength and body mechanics that doesn't equate to me being so short on these clubs. I've done it before outside hitting it longer...

item.title: Prarie West Golf Club
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
After yesterday's awesome 80 outing, today I fell back to earth with a 91. I decided that since I did so well on a 5474 length course yesterday, bumping this slightly up on the random course pick of Praire West to the White tees, and just 100 yards longer (5580 yards), was a safe bet.

So turns out this course was also rated much lower than yesterdays, and many courses I've played recently. This is a bit suspect... less water hazards, but the fairways were still pretty tight. 65.3, and 112 (the 112 feels very low).

Ay any rate, I once again started off with a double bogey. It was entirely on not getting near the green enough in 2, and then a slight struggle with the wedge. I then knocked off 3 pars on 315, 370, and 348 . The double was on a 358. All of these par 4s. So even though I wasn't getting the distance I wanted ... I was till scoring. My 'around the green' was + strokes gained this time.

The rest of the round was a lot of bogey golf I felt like my tee shots weren't terrible, in fact I hit more fairways then I usually do, but the irons felt even worse today . The numbers bear that out. Putting was average, and the around the green with the new SW was quite good for the most part

I had to hit the wood 28 times today... and it wasn't terrible. A big cluster around 160 170 yards distance. I just really think this club needs to be in the 180-200 range.

I know the irons are important, but I am now looking at my clubs and wanting to chase distance on the long end. Copilot really thinks I need to start using the driver. If I am being honest... I've been hesitant to, because I'm improved so much with this tactic I've taken, but if I'm really honest, it's because every time I try to tee in the sim things get wonky.

On the new i8, I have more data now... I'm still not entirely sold.

Hard to tell from the picture, but my i8 does have less variance (even though I took almost double the shots with it). It feels lumbering, where the elevate feels like you have this massive kick. Results don't lie though, it's more stable. Perhaps this is just what I need right now.

item.title: Seduced by a Callaway Paradym wood deal
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
First off, I love how image generation uses my title to come up with absurd looking images for the blog. It's fun .

So I read a review on Golf Spy on the 0311 XF 3W I've been gaming. It had the worst distance but most forgiveness of any club in their reviews. The worst distance really struck me. Even though this was a generation later than what I'm gaming, it was kind of like a oh-crap moment.

Now granted, this review is of the Gen 6, but when looking at the distance here (PXG 0311 XF Gen6 Fairway Woods Review | MyGolfSpy) it ranks way below everything else. Will get to the tradeoff in a moment...

So I got fed all these Paradym Callawys used on sale. I've been looking at the driver in X series, but then I got a bit of distance envy, and good marketing campaign, and saw a 3W that came up. The data told me 17 yards longer, and I was immediately sold!

I didn't pay too much attention to accuracy and forgiveness. It came in middle of the pack on accuracy, but forgiveness was way lower than I thought (27th, towards the low end of testing) . However, Copilot started telling me the flavor I got (HL for high launch) would behave differently on the forgiveness while still improving distance. So I was seduced and bought it. Shaft had a little more flex, but seemed like a really good deal at 150 bucks. I'm in this mode of will to pay a bit to test a variety of configurations, knowing I'll likely lose out when I go to reduce and trade. It's more a discover and not trusting fitters ... and being a bit lazy about even trying a fitting again.

Anyhow, will be interesting to see how this performs. I have a little buyers regret that I will be wild using this club. But on the other hand, it might be a good one to practice with, or even slot in while I play if I do get 20 yards longer than the XF. It's got me questioning the whole bag.

I haven't been able to play lately at all...yesterday was about to play when my water heater broke, so had to deal... today is likely a heavy workout day so likely nay on hitting again... tomorrow is more likely. I'm still looking to come to conclusion on whether I want to fill out the set with Maltby or keep testing. Right now, I'd say I'm sitting at about 66% on switching them out for the Matlby, just for the ease and price of it. Get standard and work from there to your next set of irons in the future.

item.title: Wolf Creek Golf Links
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Different than the same named Wolf Creek Golf Club... this is completely different course, and looks nothing like the desert mountain course I like.

So the score -- 89. It wasn't terrible considering I hit two in the water, had a triple and a bunch of doubles

Loved that I was -1 for 2 holes to start this round. The 3rd hole was a major disaster. I'm not sure if this was one I hit in the water or OB, but it was a mess at 3 over. I rarely do that anymore. I recovered nicely with a par, but then 2 doubles. All over the place

I hit some good putts --- it's been strong in the sim. The short game was good, only a couple small mistakes. Irons were better than the numbers say. I hit 64% of fairways today. That was kind of insane. The shots as analyzed by Copilot said they were terrible, but I actually felt like at least half the tee shots were pretty good today.

Now thinking over the course, it wasn't bad... Not my favorite, but had some fun holes to play.

Thinking about the score... I am ~4 strokes better if I don't' hit it in the water... say I turn a couple of those double to bogey... and not the triple, but a double. Your now down another 3 strokes and you score a very respectable 82. I probably had one or two things go the opposite direction.. .so lets say and 84. Still to me right now

  • 95 up - this is really bad... last time you did this was 12/20
  • 90 to 94 above - you didn't play well, but maybe it was a hard course, or you were a bit off
  • 86 to 89--- could have done better, but your playing your average. You probably just made a few mistakes but in general got the ball moving well, putted and short game were good.
  • 83 to 85 -- a really good round
  • 82 and below -- this is pretty much your high end right now, about every 10th round your getting one of these low scores.

So the iron game is still the biggest bottleneck. The tee shots are second. I'll talk about that first, as I tried the driver inside today... I am having that thing where I can't hit off the tee at all again. It's so weird that everything just pops up. I've had to solve this in the past, but it's a bit of a problem.

Then it brings me to my irons. Man what a frustrating mess this is. The new 8 iron every time I ask Copilot if it's more consistent than my 9 or 7 ... it comes out that is more consistent. I just don't like how it feels... boardy, like a big thud. The 0211 xcor have their issues... but when I connect it feels really good. The numbers tell me the configuration is right on the 8 iron, but the feel tells me I like the old irons better. They go a slight bit further, and I can feel the difference in control when I hit them right. I am perplexed by this situation and don't know what to do.

At least I can say, the SW I bought from Maltby I absolutely love.

So I asked for something in between, and this is what I got:

Examples

  • True Temper DG 95 / DG 105
  • KBS Tour 105
  • KBS $‑Taper Lite
  • Nippon Modus 105
  • Nippon 950GH Neo

Why they fit you

  • More feedback than MMT
  • More stability than Elevate
  • Smoother feel through impact
  • Controlled tip section
  • Predictable launch
  • Not boardy, not whippy

These are the “Goldilocks” shafts for someone who wants feel and consistency.

2. Smooth, responsive graphite with better feel than MMT

If you want to stay in graphite but ditch the thud:

Examples

  • Steelfiber i95
  • Recoil 95 / 110
  • Accra iSeries 90–100
  • LA Golf A‑Series 105 (if you find a deal)

Why they fit you

  • More vibration feedback
  • More responsive tip
  • Still stable
  • Better sound/feel than MMT
  • Not as harsh or dead

These are graphite shafts that feel like steel.

3. Heads that pair well with these profiles

Since you’re thinking used sets, here are heads that naturally complement the “middle‑ground” shaft feel:

Forgiving but not dead

  • Mizuno JPX 921 Hot Metal Pro / 923 HMP
  • Srixon ZX5 (any generation)
  • Ping i525
  • TaylorMade P790 (2021 or 2023)

More feedback, still stable

  • Mizuno JPX 923 Forged
  • Srixon ZX7 (if you want more feel)
  • Ping i230
  • Titleist T200

item.title: Golf is hard
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I had one of the worst rounds I've had in a long time (mid 90s, with mulligans). Before I get to that, lets focus on a bit a good thing.

I got the Paradym 3 wood... it was longer. A noticeable maybe 10 yard or so distance while I played. It floats a bit higher, but roll out was still good. Copilots analysis from the data...

What this tells us

  • The Paradym 3W has a higher ceiling AND a usable floor once you’re sequenced
  • It is not a cold‑start club
  • It rewards rhythm and intent control
  • It punishes rushed transitions and tension

That matches everything you’ve been feeling physically.

Your feel was right — in play, the Paradym 3W:

  • Flew higher
  • Carried farther
  • Was more effective than your old W3

While it's not quite fair until I have a bunch of rounds... this showed well

When I got my hips turning better, I got more speed and carry out of this. 10 yards is worth it. Those long carries were not downhill either, they were pretty flat. Time will tell, but I am pleased with this.

Okay, now the round. Everything just played terribly. I played a bit longer tee like I have been 5500 hundred yards, but I had a feeling with a bit more distance out of the tee shot I could handle it. The last 3 rounds are all 5500 range.

I just couldn't get anything going... short game struggled at points, long game struggle at points. Iron came was worse than usual which tells a lot. I took mulligans this time, because I was trying to adjust to the new club, which seemed fair, but that hid how truly bad this round was. Several penalties, lots of misses. Only 1 really good made putt.

Since the 80 I got, the last 3 scores have been really terrible... 90, 89, 94. My average is still down at 88.2, because the of the 80 round --- but some really struggles here lately.

I need to get back to basics, and work on the swing. I tried to setup the camera again today, but it was not working with the light. Very disappointing. I think getting solid video of my strikes will help hone in on what to work on. Every once in awhile I think I get the feeling right with the irons. Same thing with the longer clubs. Today everything just felt really off more than on.

I know dropping the course distance back down to 5200 would probably help. I just really was frustrated by this round. I really need to figure out new irons.

I suppose you can't hit zero green and score well.

Your probably a month away from rounds outside... you need to get get this swing back to consistent... you've been relying on hitting the wedges close to get close to the pin with feel, which won't translate outside.

item.title: Back... two steps forward, one step back
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Such is golf... your have a few good rounds , and then you take a few steps back. Today's round was a not good, but respectable 91 at Whiskey Creek. Much easier than my last round, but I also had a longer (6 day run) between rounds.

Lets give the highlights... putting was very good, made several good putts to close. Only one 'missed' putt that I would consider (15 ft out and not in the circle). GIR was really good today... 57%. The distance when I hit the new 3W is much better. Sometimes I hit it so easy and it flies. Short game was okay, a few mistakes as usual, but not terrible at all.

Now the bad... Irons. Everything was short. Directionally you were okay, but everything was 20 yards or more short. Copilot says my VLA and spin jump between warmup and round. My irons shot changes and my swing just looses. The other bad... while the 3W was good, I had lots of misses and messes. It was not consistent, and some of it was fatigue.

So where to go from here... you know you have an iron problem. It doesn't help that your clubs aren't the same... If you can get your GIR in the low 40% range, you start to make some progress and likely shave 5 strokes from the average. It's around 15% over the last 10 rounds right now.

item.title: Hating my golf game at the moment...
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I had an okay round today. DPC Pebble, 89. I've played this twice. Last time was an 87, today was am 89. 5% boost back on 1/16 --- think I was playing a bit better then, today it was 4% boost. I am dropping it down to three on my way to 0.

I was somewhat consistent with the wood, keeping 57% of the drives in the fairway. Putts brought me down today... 33 putts which wasn't that great. I only hit 2 good putts, and had a few 3 putts today.

Only 8 shots with the irons today, and nothing went well... 22% GIR. I should say, at least I hit some greens today, although I think 1 of them was with the hybrid. Off the tee was more problematic that it's been . I felt like I went long, but not quite long enough. 5200 yards is usually easier, but today I felt a bit of a struggle.

It's funny, the wood does feel a bit longer and more accurate since the switch, but the numbers don't bear out the accuracy, just a bit more distance.

I am mostly frustrated with distance and iron accuracy at the moment. The short game is playable... the rest is just inconsistent trash. I need to practice more than I play.

I just realized I had an issue with one of my charts... GIR and FIR was not right, it was all over the place before with GIR > FIR in more cases than not (I fixed that, I think it's only happened once).

Whether that actually changes the average much, I don't think so. Currently FIR seems to average between about 45 to 60%, currently at about 55%, which tracks with today. GIR sits squarely between 10-20% on average. You've occasionally had odd high 30%+ rounds, but it's mostly in that 1 or 2 a round. You need to figure out how to double that. The FIR is not effecting your score much, as you don't get the rough penalties. As you drop down to a 0% boost, you may turn that off (but you better have an average in the low 80s when you do).

Scoring as you can see the average has flattened over the last month or so.

The last 20 rounds, average has been stuck around 88 to 89, however in that time you've moved from a 16% boost, down to a 4% boost, and looking a moving further. So take this as a win that you've maintained while dropping the help.

item.title: Been unable to play
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Okay... so a bunch of crap going on keeping me out of the garage ,and down to just 1 round in the last 2 weeks! I got sick, and in the midst of a fever right now. Started mid last week with an off feeling, and had me holding off golfing , and then turned in to a full blown thing.

On top of that, dealing with a couple of 'nerve' things. I have this tricep thing when hanging from a bar my tricep seizes up. It's been slowly getting better with rest and a bit of rolling. I also have a thing with my right heel... when bending over, my right heel sends a shooting nerve thing up. Trying to leave alone to calm things down so probably okay that I am sick to let myself rest up some!!!

So without out of the way... watched some videos, I think when I really was focusing on my swing and a practice routine, I saw improvement in multiple areas. I watched what I think was a good video from my favorite online coach --- basically getting back to that momentum swing again and stop thinking about all the things. I need to rewatch, I did one of the drills already of swinging with the bag. It really comes back to using momentum and fixing my sequencing... same old problems. Also did some stuff with really using the lead leg to push the swing forward

The other videos I watched that seemed like it would help was actually slowing down the swing. I think I rush the downswing, and his advice was just try saying "One Hundred and One" --- with the "One Hundred" for back swing, "and One" for down and through. Also a bit about rotating knee slightly towards target. Basically let the backswing take longer to complete. Anyhow... two things to try next time you practice. I think the big ones in order:

  1. Momentum drills (you know this works from previous experience)
  2. Lead leg push while arms drop
  3. Slow down, and momentum
  4. Knee slight out to target.

These are the two videos

https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1FDJMSJh6j

item.title: Back and Wynn (84), and felt better about my game
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So lacking time tonight, so will make this kind of quick.

Warmup

  • i7 - 125-140 yards carry --- The Danny stuff seemed to be working. Important note, Lower Spin shots appear when strike improved. Higher spin correlate with steeper AoA
  • i6 - left biar, but carry 131-149. Your hitting distances you'd be pretty happy with at the moment.
  • w3 - 109 -163 . Totals up around 175 in the peak. Pretty short but good warmup.

Felt really good that slowing tempo (1-hundred - and - 1), along with momentum, and finish focus today. I felt good swinging ... not every shot, but many had that 'good golf feeling'.

During round, the strike analysis was the same. Pulls, and Pull-draw are the misses, but misses were fairly manageable. Still some distance controls.

Now the Round itself. An 84 at Wynn on the short course (4800 yards). I wanted to play short to take some pressure off, and that helped. I had a good front 9 (41), but had some trouble on the back (43). Had a nice run of Biride and 4 pars early round.

This was a nice round to keep my average down a bit. I don't think it will help the Slope Adjusted, as this was a lower rated slope (which actually puts it in line with recent scores in the low 90s).

I felt good though especially with some iron shots on the range. I felt like there was something to work with there. Wood was consistent. I thought I lost distance by alot a few times, but it wasn't as bad as I thought. Only a couple that went 100-120 yards that I would like back... The rest were 150 plus, peaking out close to 190 (not any hills on this course).

The GW was a really solid club today. I had a bit more trouble with the 54 degree and getting the right distance, but that there were as many good as bad.

GIR and FIR were similar to the last round. A better trend is anything that isn't single digit. Putts were higher. This is normal though, I hit GIR, but further away, requiring extra putts. I had a few 3 putts today. I had 5 putts that were probably 50/50 putts, but I only hit one of them. I missed several just slightly. That was the difference between an 84 today, and an 80.

For perspective... this is my most played course. Highest score was a 106 back in early December. Lowest was 10 days later an 80. All prior attempts had the 16% boost on, today I am down to a 3% boost.

item.title: Kapalua is my nemesis
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
This was the first course when I got GSPpro back in late October. Who knows what the settings were when I played that, but my 'adjusted @ 72' score was 126 . Today was only the second time I played, and came out of a random selection. I figured it had been long enough.

I had a very good start. 3 over through the first 6 holes. I was thinking, maybe today will be a low 80s day.

Then things started to fall apart... until they totally broke down over the last 5 holes. It was a bit of fatigue late, and just losing my swing. I don't think I'm fully over the bug that got me last week.

The stats feel about right. I felt terrible off the tee minus a few shots, and of course the irons were once again basically unplayable.

One good news story... the big fairways led to a 73% FIR. That was a almost a high. The long game however was not good at all. I started off hitting okay, and then just fell apart after that. It wasn't really a direction thing, I couldn't get the ball moving far enough. I think my first 3w hit went nearly 210 yards (just a bit downhill, carried well over 160), and it just went downhill after that, and by the time I finished I was hitting it 120 yards. I need the tee shots to be consistently over 160 yard carry, with distances around 180+ for the 5000-5500 yard courses.

Another good news story... short game and putting were serviceable today. Not spectacular, but didn't hurt me. I didn't make putts though... Again, I had maybe 5 shots within 10 feet, and only made 1. I did also like that I went long on my i6 clean (150 yard +), and the

This has the average trending in the high 80s again and creeping up a bit for the first time. I think I can recover to that slow trend I had going, but I have to sort out a few things. Part of me just thinks I should be scoring mid-low 80s on most days, but I think that is only going to happen when I am fairly hot through a round and keep the mistakes down.

If you just look a since January (chart below) ... your flat. Not much improvement in the last 2 months, EXCEPT, that you've reduced your boost from 116%, to 102%. So your

I'll figure out the plan moving forward, but I'll save that for another post.

item.title: Celebrate success... where to go next?
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I think it's important to recognize I saw a major improvement in my play since purchasing the SIM. Let me celebrate some of the success now

  • You've gone from a handicap in the system of 25.7 down 14.7. An 11 stroke improvement since November as measured in GSPro
  • Your scoring average adjusted for mulligans has gone from a 105.2 down to 89. A 16 stroke improvement, and you average went down as low 87.6!
  • Your Rolling SAS @ 72 went from a 110, down to 93. (with a low of 91.1). That's a 17 stroke improvement!
  • You did all this while dropping your boost from 116% down to 102%. So the last month of static scores, is actually still pretty good. Your playing the same length, while having the carry yardage drop by 14%. So that 180 yard three wood for a few months ago is really 155 yards today. So your longer, despite not feeling longer. You only have 2% to get to zero, and turning out some of the penalties for imperfect lies.
  • Your short game with the wedges is really a strength. Putting distances in the SIM are pretty good, but you don't know how they will translate in the real world.

So I have been down on the lack of progress and momentum since the start of the year, but I think it's important to take in to account how much different it is playing these courses without the boost and doing as well.

So there are still problems. I'll address them in order I think I should.

  1. Your Iron game sucks, and yours iron don't match. You are a trip away from just buying new irons at Second Swing, but you want to dial what you think your swing is headed to before you do that, leaving you in a bit of lurch. After the attempt of KE4 Max with the MMT shaft, your pushing back towards something that feels more like your current setup despite how all over the place you are with those irons.

This chart shows it pretty well from yesterday. These are carry numbers

A well struck 6 iron carries 145, while a perfectly struck i9 carries 120 in round. A more realistic breakdown when your hitting it right would be carry i6 145, i7 135, i8 125, and i9 115. Maybe you subtract 5 yards from that, but that is where it should be.

Warming up with the i9...

You have an amazing ceiling on the i9 from the warmup Carry of 136. You can see that carried over to an early hit, where the only time I hit the i9, I hit it pretty clean for 120 yard carry. No predictability.

When you see the i7 shots, they are a tad longer. Your ceiling seems to be around 145, so 135 feels again on an average carry feels about right. The i8 on the other hand was consistently shorter than the i9. Ceiling was closer to 120. You are a little tighter in dispersion with the 'boardy' more stable club, but it's frankly feels awful to hit.

I figured out a feeling here with the irons, but I haven't been able to put it to play. You need to just spend more time drilling the right feelings. Perhaps more par 3 courses to dial in irons over and over again. Ops36 or other. As fun as it is to measure your scores going down on Par 72 courses, the way forward requires a lot more time working on the iron game. You need to pick new irons, and keep moving this part of your game forward

2) Distance off the tee. This is your number 2 problem and comes in two or three flavors.

  • You need to get more consistent distance off the tee, whatever club you decide to hit. If it's the 3W off the deck, then you need to be consistent off the deck with it.
  • You need to learn to hit the 3W with a short tee
  • You need to figure out if you can hit a driver in your indoor setup. If not, you need to drill the hell out of it outside. The inability to hit driver will sync you in a few weeks when you go out to play.

3) Real play vs Game play. You've had a great time improving in the SIM, but now is the time to start thinking about taking the game outside. You should be 2 or 3 weeks from your first outing, but your lack of consistent irons (play, and purchase) and inability to hit a driver are holding you hack.

Copilot gave me a pretty good analysis. They still think I should move

item.title: I couldn't hit ...
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Earlier this week I did like I said, I practiced. I did some of the op36. I played terribly, the ball went all over. Contact was just bad... Fully frustrated.

I did the op36, and almost passed level 3 on a different course (150 yards). I actually started to figure something out towards the end of the session, and was starting to get closer to 150 yards out of i6 (or longer). Hence the normal problems

You can see, any of those shots that were longer than 110 were likely taken with i6. It actually was pretty good. You can see a pretty nice 160-170 yard range on the i7, I actually flew a couple shots over the green. This should be my stock shot. 145-155 Carry, and 155-165 distance. Instead, most everything starts clustering around 110-120, and 130 yard distance. Then you have a fair amount that are short (less than 120 yards total distance. How is one to play golf when your this inconsistent.

I think this is what is tough right now... you can hit the ball right, but looking a this shot... lets say you took 9 tee shots at 150 yards. 2 shots were long, with dispersion as far as 10 yards right/left. You had 2 shots that were good, just a little right, but came up 10-20 yards short of where you wanted to be. The others were either way short, or more than 10 yards off line.

On top of the above, you had trouble getting the wedge distances right. They weren't bad, it just was not consistent. Your wedges at least usually stay within a 5 yard dispersion on these shorter shots.

The Op36 exposes my weakness... When I played the i9 (100 yards), it was pretty much the same. 2 really good shots, and 7 terrible.

If I listen to Copilot:

Your swing has two different “modes,” and only one of them produces real compression.

When you’re in the good mode, you get:

  • Forward shaft lean
  • Lower dynamic loft
  • Center-ish contact
  • Predictable face-to-path
  • Real ball speed → real distance

When the bad mode shows up (usually mid‑round, hole 12–13, or when you’re trying to “hit” a shot), you get:

  • Early extension or stall
  • High dynamic loft
  • Contact high on the face or toward the toe
  • Face-to-path jumps
  • Ball speed collapses → everything flies 20–40 yards short

This is why your i7 can be a 160–170 club and a 110–130 club on the same day. It’s not strength, not equipment, not “inconsistency.” It’s delivery.

I'll disagree that this shows up late... it shows up all the time.

Pattern A: Sequenced, rotational, compressed, forward‑lean delivery → i7 goes 150–170 → i6 goes 160–180 → wedges fly the right window → contact feels solid → ball speed is normal

Pattern B: Arms-led, stalled, high-loft, early-release delivery → i7 goes 110–130 → i6 goes 120–140 → wedges balloon or come up short → contact feels thin/high on face → ball speed collapses

The fix is not “hit it better” — it’s locking in ONE non-negotiable feel

You need one feel that:

  • Starts the downswing correctly
  • Keeps the body leading
  • Prevents the stall
  • Prevents the flip
  • Stabilizes dynamic loft
  • Keeps low point forward
  • Keeps ball speed consistent

This becomes your “anchor.” Your “reset.” Your “I know this works even when everything feels off.”

Right now, you don’t have that anchor. You’re relying on hope and timing.

Okay, I see that... but how do I fix it. IT has lots of suggestions, but it's like fix one, something else breaks. I can't seem to get it all lined up.

item.title: Finally did it...
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I upgraded my irons. So much to write about here, but let me get a few top of mind things out of the way

  • More open bays, changed my swing some. My follow through was more upright
  • The trackman captured better ball trajectory than my square (which is not surprising). I believe it the same pattern though,
    • Path way left — your swing direction at impact is consistently out‑to‑in by a large margin.
    • Face most neutral,
    • Face to Path massively open
  • My problem in their sim today was too much spin, not enough height... was actually lower than what it should be.
  • My club contact was actually pretty good... I hit center a lot.

Okay, now drumroll.... Callaway Elyte X. It's the Super Game Improvement Category, but it didn't really feel that way. My misses were cleaner, but I still had plenty of distance. Paired with the True Temper Vector 90. It felt more stable, a bit firmer than my elevate 95.

I tested the Ping G425, and it was a close second, but the dispersion was wider.

Those are 3 club i7 hits. It's not a perfect science, but the brown was my old i7 0211, the purple is the ping, but you could see the misses were more punishing, the blue had a tighter right dispersion. It was just easy to hit, and the misses were good misses.

I also hit a cobra DS adapt with a dynamic golf 105 & TaylorMade Qi Max HL. I think the TaylorMade was a third place, but was a bit shorter (likely because of loft jacking with the Callaway.

Here us the Qi (Orange), and DarkSpeed in Red

Since the Ping 425 ended up not being the player, I mentioned not being a big fan of my current 5 hybrid. He had me hit a 5 hybrid that just immediately felt good. I was in a buying mood, and didn't know when I would get back to columbia to play again. He just picked a good club, and it traveled easy. I was exhausted and found this thing flying down the sim . A titelist ts2 4/5 hybrid.

So lets Club head and ball speed here... my swing is surprising that it is in the high range. Fitter thought, once I sort a couple things out, my distances will start improving. My 'smash' factor is not where it should be.

So with what copilot is telling me, with 82 mph CHS and a GI 7‑iron.

  • Carry: 155–170 yards
  • Total: 165–180 yards

So I'm working through some realistic numbers, and what I think should be rough current,

The biggest gains come from delivery, not speed.

You can add 30–40 yards to your 7‑iron without swinging faster — just by improving:

  • Path from –9° to –3°
  • Face‑to‑path from +10° to +2°
  • Smash from 1.15 → 1.30
  • Spin from 6550 → 5500

So buying club helped confirm things, and started me I think down an awesome path.

So anyhow... I was happy with today's purchases, but also a slight bit surprised with my numbers, and slight bit surprised that I went to SGI. It kind of makes sense. The rest of the clubs were squarely in the GI category, but the interesting thing was they all felt pretty good, and I could still feel it through all them.

I'm real excited again for next steps. Going to start recording more swings again, and see if I can start getting things cooperating.

item.title: In to out
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I feel like I actually learned more in the last week about my game than I have in several months. I finally have a good understanding of what's happening.

My number 1 problem , the path is too Out to In... When I started reducing that through a few drills (thinking hitting more to right field, and practice swinging 4 o'clock and 10 o'clock, it started fixing that).

I think I've been really off thinking what my swing was and what was causing the slice. I kept thinking that I was a classic over the top, but I am was a bit different. My pattern is early chest rotation with my arms stuck behind falling too late. I kept thinking for a long time to reduce this, I wanted to come more from the inside, and that was partly right, but ?I was turning the club back inside too quickly which was producing that out to in swing (image 2). I thought, your in a arc, stay in that arc.

So anyhow... I will say the new clubs a couple of good things. They still feel great, they tightened up the dispersion a bit. They did not fix the problem though, they only made the problem more consistent. This is a good really thing

First off , a bunch of couple of screen grabs. I didn't understand this concept until I saw it repeated in the trackman. I wasn't sure I could trust my square, but it was right, I just interpreted wrong!

I can see in this diagram now, I was thinking about this wrong when I was initially interpreting this. I was thinking out to in meant I was swinging in an more outward path back, and more inward path down. Flat out wrong, it just meant when I came in to the ball I was coming across it out to in. Hence, you'll see a bunch of stuff below about aiming to right field. This is going to be hard to lock in, but I think once I do, my club face control (which I think is okay, and I understand this better , open , close, and how to adjust grip to 'help'), the final piece is coming together.

A bunch of notes from Copilot.

You are not classic over‑the‑top.

You are a rotationally early, handle‑left, open‑face fade player whose path is too far left because the sequence is off, not because the club is steep.

A. Early‑Session H4 (Before Path Work)

B. Late‑Session H4 (After Path Work)

This is the most important finding: You proved you can move your path from double‑digit left into the single‑digit left range when you focus on it.

The Path Fix (Short Version)

Your data points to one root cause:

Early chest rotation + ball too far forward = path goes left

The fix is simple:

  • Close shoulders slightly at setup
  • Ball 1 ball back with irons
  • Feel the chest stay closed longer in transition
  • Let the arms fall before the torso turns
  • Let the handle exit less left

You already did this with H4 — and the path dropped from 15° left → 4–7° left immediately.

The combination that works for players with your pattern

The most reliable pairing for someone with your exact numbers is:

“Right field + close the door.”

  • “Right field” → moves path from –12° to –4°
  • “Close the door” → moves face‑to‑path from +4° open to +1° open

That gives you:

  • Start line near target
  • Small fade
  • Lower spin
  • Higher smash
  • 20–40 yards more carry

And some final notes for today

It was a bit of a downer, and you were working hard in the hot garage to try to fix. The ball was not traveling as well as it did at second swing, but it was still launching up pretty high.

Game in general, did some op36, and had my best score on the 100 yard course (29). So that's like hitting 2 over par on an easy par 3 course in GSPro.

Your goal for this week, fix the path. You figured out how to get the path better, you just need to lock it in. That should unlock less spin , better smash, and more yards. I'm not sure about 40 more yards, but I think this is the way to better. Work on this new h4, and the i6-i8.

I also noticed with videos today, I am way overswinging...There were some other issues on the Face on swings that I found, that I will have to work on.

  • Overswing
  • Bent elbow at top
  • Off Balanced Finish
  • Casting - not as bad as it use to be, but still bad

item.title: My bag
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I updated My Bag – The Iffy Lie page. I have one glaring missing piece. One possible upgrade, and a couple changes I'd like to make, and a questionable decision.

  1. The missing piece: A Gap Wedge. My new set came with a PW, and AW. The AW is a 46 degree. My Maltby wedge is a 54 degree. This leaves a ton of room in between. I could either way -- Maltby 50 degree, or Callaway Elyte to match. I am tempted to go the Maltby direction, but they currently don't have in stock (it's less expensive), but also Callaway is out of stock in that club. My GW from the PXG set is a 48 degree, so that doesn't make much sense to carry around either. At some point the Gap here will become evident.
  2. The questionable decision. So I bought the TSR2 - it's a 21 degree, but the fitter I think tuned it up slightly. It's 3 degrees off the 6i. I am not nearly consistent enough to get much a difference out of the two. The 3 Hybrid is a 19 degree. Your starting to get in a area where there could be quite of overlap. The fat that I have multiple shaft styles is also concerning. But it should get me to a place where I know how to resolve this.
  3. The changes: I like the new 3W Callaway. It's longer, easy to hit. The club is the only non-stiff in the bag. It feels different at the moment from the 2 hybrids, which has been okay, but some stuff to figure out before changing.
  4. The obvious upgrade: The driver when I get back on the course. I am only rewarding a new driver (or used) driver when I'm hitting consistent through the other clubs. I am working on the swing change to get more in to out, and nothing is happening till I get there.
  5. The less obvious upgrade: A new putter, replace the worn chipper.

So there you have it. I've been excited to play, but haven't had much a chance since I purchased the clubs Saturday. Body hasn't felt great... so many things going on, and golf has taken a back seat.

item.title: The path to more in to out
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I played my first 18 with the new clubs. I also overdid it today because I really wanted to work on moving the path. I have a bunch of analysis below, and I did improve what looks to be about 5 degrees or so closer to neutral.

I played Jack's Point, which was a beautiful course, with some easy and difficult holes. I did not play well, and treated it as practice with this new swing. Quite a few mulligans, that I don't really care about right now, I can drop those as the new swing comes in...

The basics of this is ... My path improved, but I'm not closing the face. The drill that fixes path is working the swing towards to first base base/right field. It takes a lot of practice swings to make sure I'm doing this. Surprising it worked better on the woods. Harder to get the irons in to this swing.

I scored a 93 today with a bunch of mulligans... nothing too exciting.

Now the analysis..

Your typical path over the last few months:

  • –6° to –12° out‑to‑in
  • Face‑to‑path: +6° to +12°
  • Strike: heel‑biased
  • Smash: low
  • Spin: high

This is the “wipey fade” pattern we’ve been trying to unwind.

Across the entire dataset you uploaded, your path improved meaningfully.

Your new path window today

Across all clubs:

  • Most shots were –3° to –8°
  • Several shots were –2° to –4° (this is the window we want)
  • A few were +0.5° to +1.0° (these are your best strikes of the day)

This is a massive improvement from your historical –10° pattern.

What didn’t improve yet

Even though path improved, your face‑to‑target stayed open on many swings:

  • +4°
  • +6°
  • +8°
  • +10°

This means the ball starts right, and because your path is still slightly left, the face‑to‑path stays too open.

Result:

  • Push fades
  • High spin
  • Heel strikes
  • Low smash

This is why the ball didn’t suddenly go 20–40 yards farther today — the face didn’t follow the path improvement.

The real takeaway

You DID fix the path.

You did NOT fix the face yet.

This is exactly the sequence we expected:

  1. Path improves first
  2. Face control improves second
  3. Strike and smash improve third
  4. Distance jumps last

You’re right on track.

What your next step should be

Now that your path is improving, you need to train the face to close earlier so your face‑to‑target moves from:

  • +4° to +10° open to
  • –1° to +1° (ideal)

This will automatically drop your face‑to‑path into the +1° to +3° window.

That’s when the ball speed and distance jump.

Next Step --- close the face

The three moves that close the face earlier (in the correct order)

1. Lead‑wrist flexion earlier in transition

This is the biggest lever.

When the lead wrist goes from cupped → flat earlier:

  • the face squares
  • the shaft shallows
  • the path improves
  • the face‑to‑path drops
  • the strike centers

This is the move that takes your face‑to‑path from +8° → +2°.

Feel: At the top, feel like the lead wrist “bows” slightly as the arms start down.

2. Trail‑hand “under” instead of “over”

Your trail hand currently works over the shaft, which keeps the face open.

When the trail hand works under:

  • the face closes
  • the club shallows
  • the path shifts right
  • the face‑to‑target stabilizes

Feel: From the top, feel like you’re skipping a stone or side‑arming the club under your lead arm.

3. Earlier forearm rotation (supination/pronation match)

This is subtle but powerful.

  • Lead forearm: supinates slightly earlier
  • Trail forearm: pronates slightly earlier

This rotates the face into a square position before P6.

Feel: At waist‑high in the downswing, the logo on your glove should be facing more down toward the ball, not up toward the sky.

The drills that will give you the fastest results

1. The “Knuckles Down” Drill (P6 face control)

At waist‑high in the downswing, feel like the lead‑hand knuckles point down toward the ground.

This:

  • flattens the lead wrist
  • squares the face
  • reduces face‑to‑path
  • increases smash

This is the single best drill for your pattern.

2. The “Pump to P6” Drill

  • Take the club to the top
  • Pump down to P6 three times
  • Each pump, bow the lead wrist slightly
  • On the third pump, swing through

This teaches the face to square before impact.

3. The “Toe‑Up to Toe‑Down” Drill

  • Take the club back to P2 (toe up)
  • Swing to P6 (toe slightly down)
  • Hit from there

This trains the correct face rotation pattern.

What will change in your GSPro numbers when this works

Club Path

You’re already improving here. Expect:

  • –3° to +1° consistently
  • occasional +2° to +3° on your best swings

Face to Target

This is where the biggest change will show up:

  • from +4° to +10° open
  • to –1° to +1°

Face to Path

This is the payoff:

  • from +8° to +12°
  • to +1° to +3°

That’s the baby‑fade window that maximizes smash.

What this means for your ball flight and distance

Once the face closes earlier:

  • heel strikes disappear
  • smash jumps from 1.15 → 1.28+
  • spin drops 500–1000 rpm
  • ball speed increases 8–12 mph
  • irons gain 20–40 yards
  • woods gain 10–20 yards
  • start lines tighten
  • curvature becomes predictable

This is the breakthrough you’ve been chasing.

The Most Important Drill for You (Based on Your Data)

The “Knuckles Down at P6” drill This directly fixes your open face at the exact moment your data shows it’s happening.

  • Take the club to waist‑high in the downswing
  • Feel the lead‑hand knuckles point down toward the ball
  • This flattens the wrist
  • Closes the face
  • Matches your improved path
  • Reduces heel strike
  • Increases smash

This is the drill that will turn your path improvement into scoring improvement.

item.title: Another mini-breakthrough
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
It's not that I'm doing the things right, it's that I understand what is right now and what I should be working on. I feel like there is much less guess in the last week... Now I can try the mechanics, and usually the numbers reflect it (i'd say a good 80% of the time I understand what's going to happen when the ball strikes now). This is the breakthrough ... understanding. Not necessarily distance or better dispersion or anything like that, just I get the why most of the time. I don't get it right all the time, but I usually can make some slight adjustments to improve.

So today I worked on getting the face closed. I've played with this in the past, but I couldn't quite get the numbers to bear out with what I wanted. I was bowing the wrist at the top and on the way down, and I can the face very closed, but I struggled with the path some today. I still wasn't as O-I has I have been (less than 10), but not in the goldilocks for me now, less than 3 zone. A few hits in that area, but not enough.

So this will evolve over the next couple weeks -- but I feel super good about this, like I'm actually working towards something instead of spraying and praying the ball all around.

This is the #1 drill for your pattern.

Setup: Put a headcover under your trail armpit.

Feel:

  • Trail elbow stays in front of your ribcage
  • Trail palm stays under the shaft
  • Shaft shallows automatically
  • Path shifts right without effort

Why it works: Your path is left because your trail arm gets stuck behind you. This drill fixes that instantly.

2️⃣ Closed‑Chest at P6 Drill (The Sequencing Fix)

Your chest opens too early → path goes left.

Drill: Make slow swings to P6 (shaft parallel in downswing). Freeze. Check:

  • Hips: open
  • Chest: still slightly closed
  • Arms: in front of chest
  • Shaft: shallow

Feel: “Chest stays at the ball while the arms fall.”

Why it works: This is the exact opposite of your old pattern (chest opens early → steep → left path).

3️⃣ Drop‑the‑Club Drill (Shallowing Without Thinking)

This is the easiest way to shallow the shaft and shift the path right.

Drill: At the top, pause. Let the club “fall” behind you for a split second before turning.

Feel: “The club drops, then I turn.”

Why it works: Your old pattern was: Turn first → steep → left path

This drill reverses that sequence.

4️⃣ Alignment Stick Gate (External Constraint)

This forces your path to move right without thinking about mechanics.

Setup: Place an alignment stick:

  • 2 inches outside the ball
  • 2 inches behind the ball
  • angled slightly right of target

Goal: Swing without hitting the stick.

Why it works: Your path can’t go left without hitting the stick. Your brain learns the new path automatically.

Some analysis from the day:

🔧 Mid irons (I7, I6)

Your I7 and I6 distances were very solid:

  • I7: 113–126 yards carry
  • I6: 119–132 yards carry

These are 5–10 yards longer than your typical numbers from the past month.

The reason is simple: Your face‑to‑target was consistently controlled, so even with a left path, you weren’t wiping across the ball as much.

🏹 Hybrids (H4, H5)

Hybrids were a mixed bag, but the good ones were very good:

  • H4: 133–144 yards carry
  • H5: 90 yards carry (this one was a mishit)

Your best H4 swings were longer than your practice session, and the ball speed was excellent.

The left path hurt you here (spin axis got big), but the raw ball speed was up, which is the important part.

So where to go... I have gotten the 2 pieces together. I was able to get a combine club path and a closed face together. And sometimes there was magic and it felt good. I know what I am looking for. A close to square face, along with a path in goldilocks range. Easy to close the face right now with working on bowing the wrist. Harder to figure out the sequencing with the path

Today's round saw an improvement. My GIR wasn't great, but some of my misses were really good misses just off the green. I scored an 87, but I mulligan the 'island' shot a couple times, as I couldn't quite get the mechanics of the shot right.

I think I am about 2 weeks if I can keep things up breaking my GSPro score record. The goal right now is to get this under 80, and get the boost down to 0% ... almost there.

Still need to work through this whole swing change, but I think the pieces are falling into place. At least an order of operation... work on face, then path, then some more on some basic mechanics. Rinse and repeat until you get more consistent.

item.title: Sometimes improvement is hard to see
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I felt like I was really struggling over the last few months with improvement. I had a trend of massively dropping scores from around round 30 through round 50, with a slight up tick over the last 20 or so rounds.

Here is the chart I've used most. It includes a normalized for SAS metric, and the mulligan adjusted score

Pretty good. Again, through about round 34 when you posted one of your best scores, you've been in a good range, with some occasional higher scores, and some occasional lower scores.

I wanted to look at it with the lens of what if I normalize for the boost I was using. It played a massive in some of my early scores. You also need to filter that with some distance metric. I typically play between 4500-5500 no driver. 4500 is very different than 5000, which is wildly different than 5500+

So this chart. What you see is a more gradual decrease to round 54, plateauing after that amazing 80 on the Tahoe course. The green line shows a normalized score with boost, and the lighter blue line shows a normalized score with boost + distance.

This shows you have not plateaued very long at all. Your best score was on Feb 1. You've basically been sitting in a 2 to 3 stroke average range over these normalizations since then. You've slowed a bit in frequency because of work, but you also have got new clubs (wood, hybrid, and irons now), and you've played some more difficult courses.

I feel like the next breakthrough is right around the corner. You get through this swing transition, and then in order of what strokes gained is pointing to:

  • You knock down GIR some, and scores trending to the low 80 and high 70s. More ops36 at the 100 to 150. More Par 3 work.
  • You then focus on getting consistent off the tee at 170 to 190 yards with the 3W (you've seen this pattern when hitting well). If you got consistent there, I think you shave 2 strokes. Above 2 where your short game is at, your average drops to the high 70s, with occasional scores around 75.
  • You then focus a bit on the SW, LW and putt practice, where I think you can likely then turn that into improvement and shave 3 to 4 strokes. Really around the SW as getting more shots in the circle from just outside the green will win a couple strokes a round. Now you are scoring close to PAR in the lower 70s

After that, it will all about getting outside and working the driver, and learning to hit off real grass again. I think you could easily be a mid-80s player by the end of summer if your able to get another solid month in the sim working the kinks out of this new swing.

item.title: Another new club & the Copilot solution (or problem)
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I've been at this with the SIM for a few months now. I've come down to a bit of a practice schedule since about December and I discovered the GSPro portal with all my stats

  • Practice & Play a round
  • Upload stats to Copilot and Analyze
  • Watch videos of suggested drills based off Copilots analysis of stats (This is a fairly new phenomena)
  • Test to see if numbers improve (ie, path, strike, speed, etc).

Before that, it was a bit of spray and pray, and it was working okay. I had a very real problem that my clubs and patterns were not converging, and I was trying too many different things for a bit, rather than figuring out the 'biggest' influence. It was honestly hard to tell, because I had so many different types of clubs that I was swinging. MY irons had 4 different shafts --- from whippy to boardy. Now I'm down to 2 --- The Elyte X have now been really consistent for me in having 'mostly the same problem'. And easier to predict. Just in 3 sessions I can see and feel the difference.

Funny, they are really loft jacked irons, but right now they aren't traveling super far for me. I actually hit my 0211 a tad bit further (similiar lofts, but able to whip it a bit more). However, my dispersion is better. It still sucks, but it is noticeably better. I have a prayer hitting it where I want. Some of that is swing change, but I think the club fits it.

So this is where copilot comes in. I walked in to Second Swing with a list of clubs --- Elyte X was at the top of the list from Copilot. It was really about the shaft, just getting a bit more stable, and actually the stock shafts seemed to work really well for this. It gave several other options that seemed close, but it was easy to see that the Elyte were the most consistent when I played. It was the only SGI in the bunch (most suggestions were more towards GI). Looking at Golf Spy, the irons sat at number 5 in the category (which is just above the JPX , but below the Tommy Armour that I had considered hitting. Interesting the accuracy and forgiveness rated low on these irons, so we will see how long run this plays out. Right now, happy.

Prior to this, I was hunting around Golf Spy to see how my woods should perform. Was just really looking for something that would get a bit longer off the 'tee' in the sim. My wood was about as long as my 3 hybrid. It was just a weird combo, and it was all over the place on top of that. I did some research, and found some good reviews on the Callaway Paradym. I didn't quite understand , and I will say got lucky, but ended up get the HL (High Launch) version of this club, and it's been stellar. Copilot told me I would 10-20 yards longer, and I'd say I'm consistently about 10 -15 longer. I am straighter too. This made me trust Copilot.

So now I have two Copilot recommended clubs, I have one fitter recommended (my
Titelist TSR). So now I've got one more to add to the list. I started the conversation a few days ago about a driver. It was the only missing piece that I haven't upgraded in the bag.
