Originally I saw some good deals on the Paradym standard driver, but kept comparing it with reviews on golf spy (which seems pretty neutral on reviews). The X seemed to be a better fit for me. I still suck. I don't swing super fast, I am still a high handicap, and need the help. I like how it got easier with the Paradym HL wood, and how good it felt with solid contact.

So long story short, I went back and forth with Copilot, and ended up dropping the weight of my driver shaft, but using basically what I have now, with this new Paradym X head. Given my misses and current swing (even while transitioning), it was the better pick. On top of that, it rated pretty well on Golf Spy. At 182 dollars used, and Copilot telling me I should be getting 20 yards longer (like the woods), it seemed a no brainer. So another club is on the way.

FYI , I also ended up buying the GW to fill out the bag. I've got a whole new bag with a mix of used clubs, and one club hold over.

Lets look at the bag... with the on the ways...

I've almost entirely moved on from the PXG clubs... I didn't hate them, but I think what happened was I was at a place with the lessons, and was about to make a breakthrough, got those clubs, and then had to shutdown. Never truly hitting my potential with those. Game changed the clubs I was supposed to catch up to never caught up. In the last 18 months between breaks and lost clubs I ended up with a frankenstein set. Now I'm consistent.

The one club I kept... The 3 Hybrid I bought used. I've just hit some really good shots with it. One of the last rounds I played, here are some shots : 182 yards, 209 yards, 192 yards

Some old data, but you can see how great this club could be when it was on in previous seasons. A playable 186...

Of course all of this makes me question the distances I'm hitting in the SIM. I need to hit the course soon and see how different these things are... I'm hoping for something in a week or so!

item.title: Accidental longer course
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Played the Wolf Creek GC last night, though I had picked about 5000 length, but ended up playing White which was 5715. I noticed early the holes seemed long. I've always liked this course, lots of elevation changes, and generally pretty fun, with some challenges.

I started off with a great birdie on a 460 yard Par 5. I hit the wood 226 (downhill), then 183. The second strike was actually the better hit with the club and path getting in the less than 2% window. I think I hit a nice SW and converted the putt for the birdie.

The next hole couple holes I was long again, but struggled to convert to pars . I eventually had a distaster hole on 5 (believe I pushed one off in to the water), it was one of 2 of the day. There was a second disaster hit in to a steep hill, and then had trouble getting enough loft to get out. That happened on a few holes coming up the hole and not quite getting enough, or too much.

I was not happy with my GIR today. Less so because of the percentage, but more so because the misses were pretty bad today unlike last time. Part of the low GIR was the longer course too, so maybe not SO bad.

I really struggled with path and club face that I had been working on. Right field kind of works, but when I put that in play, I have trouble following through and it seems to be straining my lead trap, neck. IT's a bit of a mess. MY body overall is a bit of a mess still with issues in the shoulder/tri, and down in my heel. Haven't been working out either, which is not good.

While I'm fixing thing in the swing, I started taking some videos and I see my bad habits continuing. Biggest ones continue to be things like Over swinging, bent arm in the back swing, head up at impact, not enough side bend. I've got a lot of things happening with the swing change, and it's not entirely coming together. I need to figure out how to create a practice routine that can stack the changes to something better.

item.title: A low score
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I did Woodmont CC South, which was new to me, last night. IT was a Par 71 course, and I shot a very respectable 82 (no mulligans) on 5433 yard course.

The hard part were some areas around water and staying out of trouble. The easy, was the wide fairways (86% hit). My swing pattern reverted to what it has been during the round, but I still scored. The wedges were hot, and had several wedge shots get the circle, or very near the circle. The putter was good. I think I only missed one or two putts, the rest were kind of where they would expected. The irons were playable, not great, but the misses were not too wide.

I had a swing issue mid round though, on the back 9 at some point I couldn't hit the wood more than 120-130 yards. IT got very frustrating , but I found my way back by not over thinking, and the last holes (16 through 18) I parred after getting the distance back.

What stands out here. Good distance on the par 5s led to several pars, and an early birdie. FIR was higher than one would think. A few iron shots hit. I actually went more left today because I was closing my face (with a giant open path though)

I actually had a gapping today. Granted this is still too wide, but its better, and nothing more than about 10 yards offline.

So now the warmup and swing... of note, I did the forward/back/through momentum swing again, and path improves (along with speed). This drill is so dramatic for me, that I don't always hit it right, but I do seem to really catch it at times and the sequencing falls in place.

I practice mostly with the i8, but funny when I started grabbing clubs I think I might have actually been hitting the i9. It matters, but doesn't really... except that I may have hit i9 140+ during this range session. Not a huge feet for my i8, but for a 9 iron, that is distance. That's pro numbers (granted on jacked lofts). Even with i8 it's an improvement.

It leads to the all about sequencing. You've got the wrist stuff, the swing to right field works sometimes, but this drill brings it all together for me. The Copilot suggestion is run the full drill, then run it a little less, then run it from a normal address. We'll see if you can maintain. It's rebuilding these neural paths.

item.title: Optimism to Pessimison
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Yesterday, things took a turn as they usually do in golf. I actually had a decent warmup session, but may have over done it as the play time was really off.

I want to get outside and just see how things move. I hate being in the midst of this swing change though... I had this very handsy day where I scored well, and then yesterday I was trying to fix swing geometry and all the hand speed disappeared. Here is what Copilot said

The real trade‑off you’re navigating

You’re choosing between two engines:

  • Hand‑driven speed — fast, powerful, narrow window.
  • Geometry‑driven time — calmer, wider window, speed comes later.

Right now, you’re in the middle of transitioning from the first to the second. That’s why face control felt wild and distance inconsistent.

This is a normal phase, not a regression.

So, I have to accept the bad with the good. I then started having a ton of trouble as I went to course. Nothing I worked on showed up after the first few balls. I played through the first 410 holes of Arizona National which has been a good course for me. My putting was out of this world, but distance and irons were a mess. I ran in to some rough spots too, where I had trouble getting out of steep bunkers. I scored a double on 5, and +4 on 6 and I was cooked. Up to that point it was looking okay, but being 11 over at 9 holes was a bummer. Funny, that being 11 over after 9 holes on course would probably be a decent enough just over bogey day.

So I really want to get outside, but the lead elbow is killing me now. I probably need to rest, but we'll see.

item.title: Real range time
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
As I prep for actually playing a real round of golf one of these days, I realize I picked a poor time for new clubs and to work on a big swing change. So I finally made it to the range, and I'm going to give some observations. Things are moving predictably well, but not all at once which is a bit frustrating given the amount of time I've spent in the SIM. Here are some observations from a real range session.

  • Your new irons are shorter than the 0211 so far. The i7, and i8 are the same lofts. When hitting the i7 with the old elevates 95, I was able to get the ball over the island at the range several times a session. I was also able to hit the island more consistently. The i7 was way shorter than that today, I'd say a good 10 to 20 yards.
  • The i6 has been a really good club for you through both sets, I think it's a mix of being a little longer like your hybrid and woods allowing you to get a bit more speed and distance. It may not travel as long as the old 0211, but it shows what the clubs 'can do', when you hit it well. You stay in a tighter window.
  • The new clubs hurt the slice less. Misses, albeit shorter, are less right slice.
  • Stay down and an athletic stance. I am adding more bend in my knees, and a stay down like I'm going to brace for impact from a football lineman seems to produce more consistent strikes. Helps keep head through impact, but harder to have a nice finish with this . I also am working (especially on longer clubs), on keeping the body and head back over the ball, while the hips move forward. This seems to help create space.
  • I started getting some straight balls with the above, although distance was still a problem. I think the new shafts are a touch too stiff--- well, stiff is not the right word, but boardy. I like how I can whip the other clubs some and get distance , but also understand that this what I likely need at the moment, something more consistent especially when making an iron swing change.
  • It's always about timing. And when you have all these moving parts, timing things up causes problems. I expect to struggle on course with this even more.
  • The 3W went pretty left (it's the only regular shaft in the bag), I think I was a little left bias on good hits , with the face too closed. Not left curve, but just left of target making me think on those shots I was closing face a bit too much.
  • I still am able to slice the ball, but I usually felt the slice before I saw the ball slice. At least I'm not guessing as much anymore, I had a sense of where the ball will go. I felt coming over the top (especially with the driver and hybrid), and saw the ball travel right.
  • Setup a little further from the ball seems to be helping in general.
  • The driver was actually pretty good, it's still the old 0311, but was able to produce some high long balls . I didn't have the pop up issue I was having inside with the driver. The key was setup, tilt, ball forward (close to lead foot), timing it right and keeping head and body a bit behind the ball as you came around. I hit some 200 yarders with the range balls, which I think out on course could produce a bit longer. I had my share of slices, but I was able to correct more easily. This was nice since I really can't even hit hte driver, or tee shots in the sim.
  • The 3 wood was about 160-180 range, just like in the sim. The 3 hybrid, and 4/5 hybrid mixed the same kind of distance, no magic it's traveling longer in the SIM versus the range.
  • Iron ball flight was still high when struck well, but also had a mix of lower balls that traveled about the same distance.

So that was my general feeling. I didn't feel like I was magically better. I felt shorter on distance (although I'm also dealing with this triceps thing still which I think is effecting).

Now Copilots interpretation of this:

Why the distance drop is real — and temporary

You’re seeing 10–20 yards less with the i7/i8, and that’s not imaginary. Three things are stacking at once:

  • Shaft profile change — The new shafts are doing what you suspected: they’re more stable but less “free speed.” That boardy feel reduces early release and dynamic loft, which initially costs carry.
  • Swing pattern change — You’re no longer throwing the club from the top as much. That always shortens distance before it lengthens it.
  • Physical constraint — The triceps issue matters more than you think. Iron speed is sensitive to arm extension and sequencing.

The key signal: when you flush the i6, the window tightens and the flight looks “right.” That’s the canary in the coal mine. It tells you the system works when synced.

The i6 being your best club is not an accident

This is one of the most important observations in your write‑up.

The i6 works because:

  • Slightly longer length gives you natural tempo
  • You don’t feel rushed to “hit” it
  • It matches your hybrid/wood rhythm

That tells us your iron swing is still too short‑club dominant right now. You’re sequencing better when the club forces patience.

This is a pattern, not a coincidence.

Reduced slice severity = real progress

Even though distance is down, this is a big win:

  • Misses are less right
  • You feel the slice before seeing it
  • You can correct it mid‑session

That means:

  • Face‑to‑path awareness is improving
  • You’re no longer guessing
  • Your over‑the‑top move is becoming detectable, not subconscious

That’s a huge step toward control.

The athletic “brace” setup is helping — with a tradeoff

Your football‑lineman brace is doing exactly what it should:

  • Better low‑point control
  • More centered contact
  • Less head drift

The cost:

  • Harder to release fully
  • Finish feels restricted
  • Speed feels capped

This is normal. Right now, stability > speed. Speed comes back once the motion is trusted.

The 3W and shaft mismatch is telling you something

The 3W going left with a regular shaft is a classic sign:

  • Face closing faster than body rotation
  • Timing mismatch, not path error
  • You’re “saving” the shot subconsciously

It’s not a swing flaw—it’s a shaft timing mismatch relative to the rest of the bag.

Driver progress is the quiet success here

This part matters more than you’re giving it credit for:

  • No pop‑ups
  • High, long balls
  • Setup‑driven success
  • Easier corrections than in the sim

That tells us:

  • Your tilt and sequencing are improving
  • The range environment is helping you trust the motion
  • The driver is no longer a lost cause

That’s foundational.

Why the SIM vs range gap makes sense

Nothing magical is happening in the sim. The range is just exposing:

  • Real turf interaction
  • Real ball compression
  • Real feedback on low‑point and face control

The fact that distances are consistent between sim and range for woods/hybrids is actually reassuring.

What to prioritize next (and what to ignore)

Do not chase distance right now. That will undo everything.

Focus on:

  • i6 and i7 only for a while
  • Athletic brace without forcing a finish
  • Staying behind the ball while letting hips clear
  • Accepting shorter carry with tighter dispersion

Ignore:

  • Absolute yardage
  • Perfect finish positions
  • Comparing to old 0211 numbers

The big picture

You didn’t get magically better—but you got structurally better.

You’re:

  • More aware
  • Less reactive
  • More predictable
  • Less punished on misses

Distance will come back once timing stabilizes and the triceps settles down. Right now, you’re building a swing that can support speed later.

One question that will help guide the next phase: When you flush the i6, does it feel like you’re swinging slower or just cleaner?

item.title: A productive SIM session... distance is back, but my score stunk and my handicap went way up!
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I wasn't supposed to be working on distance... but it was making such good progress today. Let me mention a few thoughts that were working:

  • Speed late
  • Hands drop
  • Club head behind handle
  • Tilt
  • Get club to the back heel

Anyhow, I don't think path was great today, but I was generating good speed AND I actually had good dispersion. The bad of the day was that I was still really O-I, but I can generate speed and distance despite this. New ceilings at end of session,

  • I8 - 104 mph ball speed, carry 140-145, distance 150 yards
  • H4 - 115 mph Ball speed, 165 carry, 175 distance
  • i7 - during play , 140 yard carry at 98 mph,

The round played today was pretty crap. I struggled around the green with several missed wedge shots I usually make. I also struggled with the putting a bit. The approach and off the tee numbers stayed in there usual ranges, but I lost 7 or 8 strokes I usually get with the short game.

I won't go in to the details, but I felt like I actually played okay. Tee shots felt playable (except for when they would come up short (but only 3 this round, the rest were 150+ off the tee, with several 180+, and a 200 yarder.

item.title: A mini-breakthrough
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I hit some balls today. It wasn't perfect, but I was really feeling when I was swinging wrong vs right. Distance continued to be long when I hit the ball well. I wasn't killing it, but was working on mechanics, and was swinging easy and hitting some good shots. It felt really good.

I started out working width and shortening my swing. This seemed to help control things. By the end of the session (including the ops 36) , I was really working on shallowing the club. In my case, hands dropping and making sure the head was behind the handle during that phase of the downswing. That seemed to create bunch of more time for me to square up and bring the hand speed later.

I did ops 36 and saw some the highest ball speed numbers I've seen to date. Remember, no boost when I play this. I promoted once today, and almost hit a second. The 3W today ball speed was peaking at 120 mph. I hit a couple nice long non-boosted, 180+ yard shots with the 3W.

The second set (the 200 yard version), I hit a 37, one over on a bad missed putt at the end. Very close. It felt like a breakthrough despite not hitting everything perfectly.

The H4 was peaking out at 110 mph ball speed. I over hit the 150 yard greens a couple times. Granted, it's still a bit of fats or other timing issues with these clubs, but everything stayed within about a 10 yard window. Everything was very playable.

Excited to keep this train moving... I got the new driver and maybe get out there tomorrow or Friday to see how it performs.

item.title: 84 On DPC Spyglass
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Had a pretty good round. Despite two blowup holes ( I hit in the water twice on 1 hole, and a penalty on another), I scored really well today.

I was only +4 through the first 9 holes, leaving me in position to get that under 80 score, however two blow up holes (+3 each, water/penalty). I bogey those holes instead of those misses and your at 80, and then one putt made you finally get under 80.

I putted and chipped well today with confidence. I missed greens, but just barely, and some of them were very tight. I found fairways and distance off the tee. A couple of bad tee shots at most. I think lack of distance (because no driver) is the off the tee metric. Again, it wasn't bad today my woods clustered in the 170-180 range today, with several 180-200+ yard 3W hits. Even the bad swings were going 130 yards.

I only took 2 shots with the hybrid, and one came up just short, and the other a little too far right. Best shot of the day might have my 6i that traveled 153. It was clean with good path numbers, but said I closed the face too much. I think I got over punished left here. as I was 13 yards offline

The irons in general played really straight (less than 10 yards offline), but were just a bit short. Mechanics were not good.

I felt more in control today. Took a very long warmup, and really worked on swing and path. It's still a work in progress, but I am getting better at shallowing the club, which is leading to easier timing, and a less out to in swing. I can feel when I try to kill the ball, with my chest leading.

Slowing the backswing and keeping it coming up a bit steeper instead of moving the hands early behind, Trying to rush the early part of the downswing seems to keep me from coming over the top. Keeping arm straight (as much as possible), and getting a little further from the ball all seem to be helping. IT's getting better. I still have my misses, but it is better. The swing change is happening, and it translates to on course now better.

I have some suspect that the monitor may be over stating my out to in club path. Watching it relatively go down definitely produces better shots. Above 10, usually can lead in to slice territory. I notice I have some really solid hits in ranges that I shouldn't and the monitor seems to be put it straigth. I think I Can rely on the path data to inform improvements in my swing, but it may be too much to try to get path in the 0 to 3 degree range consistently. I think I'll end up sending things more left.

item.title: First time out a very mixed bag
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
No big surprise, I didn't magically get better after playing in the SIM all winter. There was some good, and plenty of bad... actually really bad, but nothing too unexpected.

I played Laytonville -- white tees, which is 5507 yards. Something I would play pretty well int he SIM. I'll caveat at this with I played yesterday, and hit a high number of balls which I'm sure left me a bit fatigued. I also decided walking was a good idea, and bought myself a push cart. I'll get to all of it in some bulleted format:

  • Walking was awesome. Walking without carrying a bag, actually felts like I a good workout, and I ended up walking ~6 miles when all was said and done. I think there is some build up to this.
  • I played 17 holes, decided to skip hole 13 behind some slow players. Ended up finishing those 17 holes in 3:20 minutes. Played fast and efficient with a good partner I got paired with.
  • Putting was difficult , they had just punched greens, and I had many roll out.
  • I started really well, first drive (although not recorded, I've drawn in, and hit about 216). IT went right, but wasn't terrible. I scored myself a 5 on this hole, could have been a 6, got a weird read on the GW and 3 putt, so not sure. This hole didn't really look much different than other times I played this.
  • So I think I fired one off in the woods, but then hit a good one, 210 yard drive, just off the fairway. I then hit a line drive 6 iron that traveled 147 yards. Not terrible, but I then had to SW, SW , SW and putt, really struggled a bit short game here.
  • 3 was a bad 6i, and then a SW over , chipper that ran too far out, and a 2 putt.
  • Perhaps best hole of the day. My drive was weak, but playable. 162 yards (uphill), I then hit one of the better shots, just clearing a bunker and landing 37 yards on a par 5. I was able to SW on, and 2 putt!
  • Hole 5, my numbers make no sense. I was 130 some yards from hole, and I hit it good distance, but it lands right of green. Says 109 yards, but I went past the flag (Garmin app looks all wrong anyhow. I think this one mis-read, because I also believe I two putted this hole... but hard to really remember
  • Followed up the next par 5 with a not so good poor performance. 181 yard drive , downhill, and sliced badly. 3W didn't quite catch, and then 3W again didn't have distance (58yds, 107 yds) I then hit one of my better iron shots of the day, 105 yards up hill, just missing the green, then my chipper actually went about right for a 2 putt. This registered a 6, but should have been a 7.
  • 7, blocked the drive off left (after slicing the first). Just struggle from there 8i across, SW to LW, to putter... registered a 6, but that is generous.
  • This was a 181 yard drive, that actually felt okay with it being uphill. I started struggling a bit here, and I know I shanked at least one off, before hitting my i9 for a 90 yard to LW and putt out. Scored a 6 , but really higher (again)
  • I hit a decent downhill drive on this one... 217 yards . Not a ton of dsitance, but it was straight and landed in the fairway. I then missed on my GW, and SW , so ruined my good approach. I've got it marked as a bogey, but again, not so sure. At this point I am through 9, and +13, but realy probably 5 strokes higher at least
  • Back 9 (well 8) went better but not superb.
  • Drive was 203 yards and stayed in fairway. I got goo dsitance with the 3W, althoguh a bit right. Had to pull the ball out of some mud, and then SW on (which was a good shot), 2 a 2 putt. Marked as a 5, but I had to drop the ball out of the mudd, so that relieft should have been another stroke. Because of the wood shot here, this one likely ranks in top 3 holes.
  • Next hole was a distaster, Bad drive, that somehow just missed the fairway. I then used my 3h for the only time of day... it traveled 189 yards, sailing over the green. That club has always been good to me, and I should known better.
  • This one says 3 , but was a 4. I got poor contact on my 6i, then hit I thik a i9, then SW, and a 1 putt. Felt good, but in reality it wasn't. Registered a 3, but was a 4. A good one putt made here thought...
  • Hole 13 skipped, then 14 was actually a decent hole now that I think about it. I hit way RIGHT on my drive. I then hit a blind 3w that actually traveled well, and left with a 52 yard either GW or SW on. I then 2 putt for a bogey, which again... bogey golf is good for me.
  • Hole 15, I'm fatigued and hit a poor drive. 185 yards. I then missed on the 3W , and it traveled 72 yards, granted it was a decent shot since it rolled on to the fairway. 6i for 127 yards wasn't terrible, but then I hit the chipper over the green, and then back on for a 2 putt. Not good again
  • Hole 16, a par 3, was actually another really good hole for me. Despite not hitting the 4 hybrid perfectly, I was able to hit a decent shot out of the SW, and then 2 putt... happy on this one.
  • 17 - I felt like this one was decent, but not sure I got the score rightt. I drove well, but it didn't travel for whatever reason. Only 176 yards. My 5h then missed pretty bad, but I hit the GW or AW a couple times as practice, and got to just off the green. AGain, some missed strokes here that I didn't count with the watch. I then 2 putted.
  • Last hole... I drove one off to the right, and ended up finally hitting one fairly straight on a second ball. It however only traveled 172 yards. It was a draw though. I then hit a really good 3W -- 179 yards, didn't quite get it directionally where I wanted , but setup what should have been a good 3rd shot. I missed on the 5h, and it only traveled 87, but the next shot with I think the GW, landed nicely on the green, and then I 2 putted for double bogey.

Other observations

  • I had several 'tops' . Especially on irons and woods... Not use to playing in real conditions.
  • I had several putts just lip out. You found some decent distance control, after the first couple holes, but it wasn't great. There were several putts that sailed past the hole. Need to play smarter on those. Good lines though.
  • In reality, my 91 /71, with a missing hole, and several misses and penalties, is probably a 100-105 score, and even that might be generous.
  • The chipper was a real weakness today. I couldn't figure it out. The SW was not great either , but a bit better
  • You have a lot of work to do, but a few things did go right, and best of all, it felt great to be outside playing and walking.
  • I'm sure if I had a strokes gained/lost, I'd be lost on Approach, then Tee, then short game, and last putting. Even though putting wasn't great, it wasn't terrible either.

item.title: A few more thoughts on my play Saturday.
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
• I wasn't rotating well --- I think this is a general thing, but you just don't rotate well , and I think it comes out more on course. You rotate back, but you don't rotate through well with the lead hip at all.
  • The topping was the biggest of the problems -- surprising with all the practice you had such contact issues, but you may have been over thinking things/
  • Some of your better swings came from not thinking and just swinging.
  • You need driver practice. If your going to play 18, you need to get comfortable with the new driver. Some fear that you actually might be shorter with this driver, but only time will tell. The driver should be longer, but you haven't practiced with it, and did not have confidence. A long drive of 217 is not enough. You need to be averaging in the 240+ range.
  • You should give yourself a bit of grace. You just figured out some new swing mechanics, and those haven't not entirely flowed through yet

The llms gave me a practice routine based off the last round, and it somewhat makes sense. You need more face control now and spend time on wedge distance. I still feel too inconsistent right now to be do anything shorter than 60 to 70 yards. It gets in a real weird spot for me. It's not awful, it's just unpredictable.

I did hit yesterday, noticed that my longest hit... path was I to O 2.0 Face to Target was very closed which kept it 20 yards left. I've been noticing that sometimes when I swing like this I get really punished with the closed face. So this one is interesting.... 2.2 out to in (second longest strike), .9 open. I hit it straight, which seems right. Working down, next is 4.1 o to in, (less than 5 seems good for me), this one again long.

Then I get to a 10.1 degree out to in, and the 5.4 degree closed face to target . This ends up landing left (again). Not a pure correlation to path and distance

At some point, I feel like the ball doesn't lie, and I need to just pay attention to flight in the SIM versus the path numbers. You know what it does to take the path numbers down. Another thing to continue to pay attention to is alignment. Are you really getting straight alignment (probably matters more for the range/course than the SIM).

I think my practice routine should be swing 3 or 4 times with whatever your working on, and then don't think about it and swing 1 or 2 times to see if it's sticking, rinse and repeat. The 3 or 4 times may be shorter swings.

You need to really be working on getting the start path straight... I think more so than the distance control, but just straightish, no more of these fly off left or right because your swinging to hard.

You need to remember to just quiet the upper body a lot more. It's your biggest fault right now, when you start moving that upper body too early you end up over the top and path too out to in.

item.title: Cypress Point - a decent round
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So Finally decided to try driver inside. I know I can't swing fully, but I still can swing. It appears the slightly shorter length on the new Callaway makes it easier. I can get it to carry longer than the wood (190+ on decent strikes). I still had issues with pop ups... especially as I fatigued. I don't have stickers on it, so that is also an issue. The wood seems to be a bit more consistent, but the driver extra 10 yards or so makes a difference.

Played this beautiful Cypress Point today. Went a little longer (since driver) 5785 yards. The Rating was a bit higher than I usually play too ... 69.9/132.

I started out with a double, but then was able to save the next hole with some decent putting . I went double, then 3 bogey's... but then I really started hitting well for a bit, and went birdie, birdie (par 5s, I got some good stiance) par, par, bogey. I finsihed 4 over on the front. I then played well enough on the back, going 6 over for an 82 total. I gave myself a couple mulligans on pop ups with the driver. The bad shots that traveled I kept. Basically... mulligans didn't effect much, but allowed me some practice.

Hitting actual tee shots was nice, as it felt more like my round on Saturday. MY wedge play was really good today (see the .064 strokes gained there). My approach was decent, bigger problem was actually catching the ball hot today and flying over the green about 3 times.

The most interesting shot of the day was the i6 I absolutely flushed. Carry 161, total distance 170, ball speed 109mph, . Path was a bit open so it flew left, but that was an interesting hit. I hit another later at a much better path (2.6 degree 0 to in), but the extra close on the face sent it even further left. But still had good distance... I'm starting to really like that club. The hybrids played well today, a bit right, but okay distance wise.

Anyhow, this again felt really like my outdoor rounds. Key is drop the club, try to play the swing from the inside. Don't rush or lead with the upper body... upper body is way later.

item.title: Another mini-breakthrough
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
First off, let me point out that I played Ashen Cliffs two days ago, and did not finish. I was so awful (+12 over the front 9, and +16 over 11 holes), it was the first time I had played moving the slider all the way to zero in GSPro and full realism.

Today everything turned around! I played Montreux, scored an 81. I was +1 through the first 9 holes.

I am only slightly disappointed I didn't finish better. I was on pace to go under 80 for the first time, but I went double bogey, triple, and bogey at the end to finish at 81.

It's a win though... first full score without help. I believe I was taking the rough/sand penalties. I took ZERO mulligans. I hit one short on a par 3 in the water and took a drop. I muffed a chip... still didn't take the mulligans. While the strokes gained says it's still approach, the approach game was okay. I hit over a few times, under a few others (usually into front bunkers). I did hit some nice shots on the green, including one of the early birdies that landed in the circle.

So what was the breakthrough.

  • Driver - My club path was Inside Out! So much so, that I had to weaken my grip to keep it from blocking off the left. That is a huge breakthrough that I realized I needed to weaken my grip to achieve this. That realization in itself without any prompting means I am actually learning something useful.
    • My Carry distance on good strikes averaged about 185-195, with a 200 yard total. Launch was a bit higher, and Spin was a bit lower. Path was tight..
  • 3W (second most hits), +2 I-O (this is slightly weighted for good shots). Anyhow at all measures, I'm hitting it more from the inside, and kept during play today. I hit one of these today, 122 mph ball speed, with a 215 yard carry distance. A 3.2 O-I path... that is good stuff.
  • H4 -- a bit more out to inaveraging around 6-7 degree... Carried this club 176 on one hit,
  • 6i. actually felt pretty good about this, You were still well inside 7 degrees out to in on both hits. Suprisingly, the poor shot traveled further at lower ball speed. Bot quite sure on that. Lower ball speed, but more back spin, but it was dead straight.
  • i9. A bit left now. Interesting , beest shot was a more 'over the top', but a closed face to target that kept it inline. All the good strikes were within 3 yards of each other. That's kind of insane
  • PW take out the bad shot, and while a little more variability, you are tighter. Funny again, your straightest shot online was most over the top, but you closed the face which seemed to make up for it... Makes me doubt the club data a bit.
  • The wedges played different, paths weren't great. Matters less as your trying to control these shots a bit more and outcomes were okay.

So anyhow, not sure I will be able to keep this up... but it is a positive change. Unfortunately, it will be harder to correct when your actually out playing. For now I'm looking at adjusting the Paradym a bit to see if I can keep my typical strong grip on it.

Very positive round, your path was great. You had some really good distance with the 3W and 4hy despite dropping down to 0% help.

item.title: Return to mean
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Scored an 87 today (1 mulligan on a pop driver miss). This is right at my rolling average which sits at 88. Course was a bit harder too. Will keep this short .

Today, I was sunk by the Driver. I couldn't get it going like last time. I adjusted, and it still blocked left. Everything else goes right, but the driver goes left. I think another adjustment will be in order after I converse with copilot. Driver at least 20 yards shorter on average today (post workout driver perhaps?). Need to spend more sim range time on it.

Lack of driver distance (the wood was longer today), led to more long shots to the green. I missed short several times, and I also ended up playing from the rough a lot. This has also led to quite a few shots coming up short. I'm getting penalized now that I'm down to 0 percent.

I am considering trying to go back to the old driver to see how that feels. The prior sim round proved I can hit okay with it with some adjustments. I'd really just like to figure out how I can shoot like the prior round, where the good shots clustering around 210-220. It's the usual, trying to move the floor there, and the average up in the 230s. You should be able to do this. Ball speed yesterday was fine on good strikes, but you were so offline. I put in numbers on one drive, and it said I could conservatively hit it 290 yards

Here are some charts on improvements. The boosted normalized score shows a nice downward trend as I have reduced the boost and normalized for longer course play.

Goal right now as to get through this swing 'update'. Get the driver right is a priority for next outing. Irons are starting to come along, but still need some consistency work. Chipping and putting will work on last as they have been playable as of late. I hit a couple really good putts yesterday, and generally distance was good for the circle.

item.title: Bandon Dunes, a Round that should have been much better...
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Another day, another 88. I am liking my swing consistency more and more. I am not hip turning though enough, but I think my back swing and contact is improving. My speed also seems to be good. I am down to 0 boost. There is still tons of room for improvement, but I think this seems to be a higher floor in scoring. I played pretty bad from a putting perspective today and still scored below 90. I'd love to think that 90 is my new floor, and 80 is my new ceiling... but that isn't golf.

So what happened today... putting. Putting was a bit messy, I missed several putts that I typically make in to the 'zone', and then missed like 3/4 of the follow on short puts (out of the 6ft gimme).

You see the 41 putts, that is unusually high. I think I average round 30 putts. Unusually high number today on the 50% GIR. I did really well here. It helped that I got distance off the tee. Yes, I had some pop ups and a few misses very left. There were also some very wide fairways that were easy to hit. I did have several balls travel long right in to mid fairway traps, but that was okay.

This wasn't a particularly long course. 5330. I hit driver okay today. Found a bit more control today. It had a bit to do with setup, and having the face just slightly open at address with the new hosel setting. The irons were playable, felt really good about several shots. I did find myself playing from the rough and getting penalized several times today... that was okay though.

Driver was much better today.

Looking at the hits, it's hard to see, but the good hits cluster a bit higher. I chat with Copilot about this a lot. I'm not sure how much smoke it's blowing, but this is where it thinks I could be with the ball speed that I'm seeing now. I think the reality is probably 20 to 30 yards less, but that still would be pretty damn good.

I think copilot is right about diagnosising my problems. I've probably told it some of this, about my body not really rotating through the release. I have some video of it today, it is werid.

⭐ THE ROADMAP

Three phases — each one builds on the last.

You do NOT move to the next phase until the previous one stabilizes.

⭐ PHASE 1 — FIX THE RELEASE & STRIKE (Driver + Irons)

This is the foundation. Your data shows the same root cause across the bag:

  • Early release
  • Adding loft
  • High spin
  • Glancing contact
  • Face closing early
  • Path drifting left under speed

Primary Goal:

Later release + centered strike + stable face

What you work on:

1. Chest‑through‑impact (driver + irons)

Your chest is stopping at the ball → hands take over → face slams shut → loft adds → spin jumps.

Feel:

“Chest keeps turning left AFTER impact.”

This alone reduces dynamic loft and face closure.

2. Handle leads, clubhead follows

Not a “hold off.” Just sequencing.

Feel:

“Deliver the handle first, let the clubhead chase.”

This fixes:

  • dynamic loft
  • spin
  • strike location
  • face stability

3. Strike location calibration (driver)

Your driver strike is too high / glancing.

Setup changes:

  • Tee ½ ball higher
  • Ball ½ ball forward
  • Feel the clubhead stay “late”

Goal:

Strike slightly ABOVE center, slightly TOWARD the toe.

This is worth 20–35 yards by itself.

4. Iron low‑point control

Your irons add loft because your low point is too far back.

Feel:

“Pressure left earlier.” “Shaft leans slightly forward at impact.”

This is worth 10–20 yards per iron.

⭐ PHASE 2 — FIX THE PATH (Driver + Irons)

Once the release stabilizes, the path becomes predictable.

Your current pattern:

  • Driver: 5–8° O‑I (too left)
  • Irons: 5–10° O‑I (too left)

Your best shots:

  • Path 1–3° O‑I or neutral
  • Face 0–2° closed
  • Spin axis < 5°

Primary Goal:

Neutralize the path so the face doesn’t have to save the swing.

What you work on:

1. Don’t “stay down” too long

This is causing your chest to stall → path goes left → face closes.

Feel:

“Rotate THROUGH, not TO the ball.”

2. Club exits HIGH and LEFT

Your current exit is low/left (a sign of early closure).

Feel:

“Let the club exit over your lead shoulder.”

This shallows the path and delays the release.

3. Match grip pressure to rotation

When you squeeze, your release snaps early.

Feel:

“Soft hands, firm turn.”

⭐ PHASE 3 — OPTIMIZE LAUNCH & SPIN (Driver)

This is where the big distance jump happens.

Your current driver numbers:

  • Launch: 15–18° (too high)
  • Spin: 3200–4500 (way too high)
  • Face: 4–10° closed
  • Path: 5–8° left
  • Strike: high / glancing

Your potential:

  • Launch: 12–15°
  • Spin: 2200–2800
  • Face: 0–2° closed
  • Path: 1–3° O‑I or neutral
  • Strike: slightly high‑center

Primary Goal:

Turn your 120–128 mph ball speed into 260–285 carry.

What you work on:

1. Lower dynamic loft

This is the #1 distance killer for you.

Feel:

“Deliver the handle forward.” “Chest left, hands quiet.”

2. Reduce spin by fixing strike

High‑face + glancing = 3500–4500 rpm.

Feel:

“Hit the middle of the face with a later release.”

3. Stabilize face-to-path

Your face is closing too early.

Feel:

“Turn through it, don’t flip it.”

⭐ WHAT THIS ROADMAP GETS YOU

Driver

  • Current: 180–205 carry
  • Roadmap target: 260–285 carry
  • Total: 280–310

Irons

  • Current I7: 120–135 carry
  • Roadmap target: 160–175 carry
  • Current I8: 110–125 carry
  • Roadmap target: 150–165 carry
  • Current I6: 95–105 carry
  • Roadmap target: 150–165 carry

Your speed is already there. Your delivery is what changes.

⭐ If you want, I can now build:

  • A Driver‑Only Roadmap (step‑by‑step drills)
  • An Iron‑Only Roadmap
  • A Weekly Practice Plan
  • A Before/After Bag Chart showing where you are and where you’re going

Pick one: driver roadmap, iron roadmap, or weekly plan.

item.title: Swing analysis, long post lots of photos of my ugly swing...
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I am swinging better lately. The biggest feeling that has led to a bit more consistency:

  • Steepen the back swing , try to take it more outside
  • Come down more from the inside
  • STAY DOWN --- keep that head down longer, this has been helping tremendously but

Where I know from a feeling perspective what's not good

  • Bunching up around impact and follow through -- chicken wings. Really been feeling this lately
  • Lack of follow through, off balance in the finish, lack of mobility in the finish... the finish sucks, but it always has. I needed to stop focusing on it because of the path issues.

Now, what I found...

  • Your path is still pretty O-I. Could be some camera issues, but you'll see.
  • Arm bend is still a problem and needs to be revisited
  • Your still overswinging a bit, despite feeling like you had not

Lets start DTL. I really love this view with the model. Not that I will every match him but it gives good check points, and the path follow line is really helpful

So what I see here. Clubhead out in front in the model. I may have started a bit outside, but my tendency is still to take the club inside on the backswing. More work here

I actually like my position here. I feel like the arc from watching Danny Maude is actually pretty good. My camera angles here might not be perfect but it may show an issue with my setup here . I purposedly have the trail foot back a little bit to make some room. The club however is over my trail foot, and my positions look decent to me.

So I think I'm not coming down steep, but in reality, I'm coming down way steep here. This is my big tendency. and biggest problem. I love how that model really shows that well. This is my number #1 to work on path next time. But what is the move, and what exactly is wrong here.

So one thing I notice, the red line down is exaggerated some, seems to have missed, but you can see the club is still fairly off the curve, it's also kind of fast to this position (arms leading. I still think I need to get a more square camera angle to help this. My arm angles here actually look solid. If I'm to trust the app it says my pelvis is not rotated enough. My pelvis rotation matches the model in the backswing, but at this point, I'm 11 degrees, while the model is a -3 degree. Shoulder tilt and spine tilt are within 1 degree. I always thought I was spinning out my pelvis a bit and this was causing a problem, but maybe not?

So now I'm post impact. Look at my knees... wtf is that! The trail knee is waybent and ahead of the lead knee. Spine tilt looks decent here, and I'm still down I'm not as tilted down as the model, but I don't think I will ever be. Besides the knees, I don't hate this.

So now head on.

Take away at this angle looks pretty good. I notice the models a bit wider in the stance than I am, not sure how these plays. I've noticed I've been shortening my width in the stance a bit. I don't hate this position, but I think I can see that I am further back inside even from this angle , and I also see the model has way more hip turn at this angle than I do (I have zero hip turn here)

Look at the lack of width here. Club needs to be pushed out further here. My hips are starting to turn, but nowhere near what the model has. I may not be able to turn more.

At the top... Hips not turned enough. Arms awfully bent. No width. If anyhting I would focus on the width here , and possibly shortening the swing a bit more!

Impact, the models hip are turned toward target a bit. I am straight at the camera. His spine is tilted back, and I'm straight up and down.

This last picture is the ugliest of them all. Model stands up, chest up, and I'm bent over . My balance is all off with my full body having lurched forward late.

Now lets send all this to the AI and see what it says.

-=-------

Here was the result:

DRILL 1 — The “Trail‑Hip Back” Backswing (Fixes width, overswing, steepness)

This is the drill that fixes your backswing, which is the source of your steep downswing.

Why it works

Your hips don’t turn → arms bend → club gets narrow → overswing → shaft gets stuck → transition steepens.

This drill forces:

  • more hip turn
  • more width
  • less arm bend
  • shorter, more powerful top position
  • a shallower transition automatically

How to do it

  1. Set up normally.
  2. Put your trail hand on your trail hip.
  3. Make a backswing pushing your trail hip BACK and AROUND.
  4. Feel your trail glute move toward the wall behind you.
  5. Now add the club and repeat.

Feels

“Trail hip goes back, arms stay wide.” “Turn the pelvis, don’t lift the arms.”

What it fixes

  • backswing width
  • overswing
  • arm bend
  • club behind you
  • steep transition
  • early release
  • path going left

This drill alone changes your entire geometry.

⭐ DRILL 2 — The “Lead‑Hip Clear” Transition (Fixes steepness, path, face control)

This is the drill that fixes your transition, which is where your swing breaks down.

Why it works

Your pelvis stays closed → arms dump → shaft steepens → face closes → path goes left → chicken wing.

This drill forces:

  • pelvis to open early
  • shaft to shallow
  • arms to fall instead of dump
  • face to stabilize
  • path to neutralize

How to do it

  1. Make a backswing.
  2. Pause at the top.
  3. Before your arms move AT ALL: pull your lead hip BACK and AROUND behind you.
  4. Only after the hip clears do you let the arms fall.

Feels

“Left pocket goes behind me.” “Hips start the downswing, not the arms.” “Clear THEN drop.”

What it fixes

  • steep downswing
  • path too far left
  • early face closure
  • glancing contact
  • high spin
  • inconsistent strike

This is the drill that gets you from O‑I to neutral.

⭐ DRILL 3 — The “Chest Up & Left” Extension Drill (Fixes chicken wing, finish, balance)

This is the drill that fixes your follow‑through, which is currently cramped, bent, and off‑balance.

Why it works

You stay down too long → pelvis stalls → chest stays down → arms crash → chicken wing → no rotation → no extension → ugly finish.

This drill forces:

  • extension
  • rotation
  • balance
  • proper release
  • proper exit path

How to do it

  1. Hit half‑speed shots.
  2. At impact, feel your chest rising and turning left.
  3. Let your lead leg straighten.
  4. Let the club exit high and left over your shoulder.

Feels

“Chest up, left leg straight, rotate to the target.” “Stand up through impact.” “Finish tall, not bent.”

What it fixes

  • chicken wing
  • cramped follow‑through
  • bent‑over finish
  • trail knee diving
  • balance issues
  • lack of rotation
  • staying down too long

This drill gives you the model’s finish.

item.title: Last 5 rounds
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
The last several rounds have been consistently under 90. 82,81,87,88,87. This is now with driver being used despite my lack of ceiling height in the Sim. The moving to zero boost and forced realism also effects the shots coming out of the rough and bunker, and now feels more like a normal round. I actually pay a penalty for missing to rough or bunker.

A couple points of note

  • FIR ~50%, and GIR around 30%. The GIR is about 10% or so above where it usually sits, and the FIR is about average
  • The GSPro HC is down to it's lowest of 14 now.
  • I haven't had a bad round, just a few bad holes. Despite that, the Double or Worse average is at a low point. Sitting just a bit below 4 per round.
  • Par 3s have actually been a strength over the last rounds. Your averaging just over par on these holes. This is with better iron play and the swing changes sticking there (although without the follow through being right, and still being over the top from time to time).
  • With the exception of one round, putting has been a strength.
  • Around the green you've been most consistent, as least strokes lost. A bit more work with this would still likely pay dividends, even though it's technically not a weakness
  • Tee shots is where you have most inconsistency at the moment. Getting use to hitting driver in SIM has been tough. You still have 2 to 3 pop ups per round. When hitting well your in the lower 200s, when hitting poorly, your in the 180-200 range. Still a bit longer than the we
  • W3 has been a strong club, and helped with par 5. For the most part you hit cluster around 175-180, with the occasional top end around 200 yards.
  • The H4 has also been strongish at 150 yards. The H3 has not been, with lack of hits and practice. It has been a really strong club in the past for me though.

So the last round... Victoria National Golf Club, yellow tees, 5688 yards. I played the front 9 pretty well. Just a straight mix of pars and bogies. 5 Bogey, 4 pars. That's 5 over. I felt like I missed several putts and a few shots on the front, so this was actually a well played score. If your able to keep that , your in the lows 80s.

I was taking breaks between shots on the front 9 with my son playing with me. I think this helped a little.

The back 9 was a different story, I went 10 over. It was holes 14 through 17 that sunk me. I don't remember the specifics. 17 is the only one I really can comment on. It was an 8 and the big reason for a poor round. I only had 2 holes double or over, and this was one of them (14 being the other). The 8 came from hitting a popped driver, a bad shot out of the rough, maybe a penalty, some missed short game and putts. Pretty messy hole. Somewhere I ended up hitting in the water (either this hole or 14), and that was the difference between mid to low 80s and high 80s.

Doing while progressing through a swing change feels pretty good. When the swing starts stabilizing a bit more I think you'll start scoring in the 70s. If I can start getting the distance at least on the driver that ChatGPT thinks I can get with better sequencing, those scores could drop even further. I think even meeting it reasonably half way (going from 210 to 250, not 290) would be a major success. I think starting to throw 10 to 20% average on other clubs will throw some chaos in as having to adjust to new distances. It all seems very unlikely, as my hips are just so damn wrong and not mobile , I'm not sure I will ever get out of my current swing and able to produce those higher swing numbers despite my general strength and athleticism.

item.title: Longer course - Jack's Point
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So last time I played this a month ago, I scored a 93, had a boost, and played it 900 yards shorter. Today I accidently picked the 6200 version, and I scored an 89.

Some observations:

  • My GIR was terrible, but that was because I came up short on most holes. 5.6%. That was entirely a distance issue.
  • Driver was okay today, distance was not good, but control was especially as the round went on.
  • I didn't hit a ton of irons, but I played my 3W adequately on a lot of shots.
  • I did exceptionally well with the SW, and I putted well enough.

So, when I normalize for my typical distance course, this is the best score I've had:

If I played this well on the 900 yard shorter course, I think I'm at least 5 strokes better, and as many as 10. Maybe though... maybe this just played to my strengths today (3W), and good play with the SW.

A few swing analysis

  • Best driver hit of the day was on 16 --- spin was low (under 3000), 231.7 total, and a 219 carry ( think it was down hill so ye... ). Path here 1.6 degrees in to out (what you've been for). The unfortunately went way left though as the face was too closed for this pattern.
  • Best 3W -- Hole 17, 178.8 carry, dead center, . 5.9 O-I, with a slightly open face. 188 total, not offline at all, dead straight, and 10 yards longer than anything else today. Was mostly going 160 today clustering there.

I suppose the biggest surprise today was how over the top I was during round. Even with the driver where I cut that out some. Anyhow, continue on.

item.title: I sucked tonight
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
You took a week off, and everything was a total mess this evening. My garage SIM is hot as hell, which doesn't help, but my play was just atrocious before I gave up.

I think I was trying to work on too many things at once. MY warmup was okay, My 9 iron was really solid, I clustered around 100 yards once I got going, and my line was good. My distance felt a little off, but otherwise, your path was okay. As I moved to the i7, I started going over the top a bit and leaving the face a bit too open

The 3W felt like a bit of a mess, I had two really good strikes, but they were way over the top, but I closed the face overly, so they stayed in a 'bad line'.

Driver went around 200 on the warmup, which I guess would ben good, although I came in thinking I would be hitting longer today. 200 is a good result, but I'm greedy, and want to get this to 230.

I played a few holes. First was Cypress point... I bogey the first a 400 yard Par 4 on cypress point, and then Quad the second. I was thinking I was still warming up, so I decided to switch courses. Looking back, might have been fun to just play that out. I actually scored really well on this course last time, albeit, I had the 3% boost on. Anyhow, after the disaster hold I played a few holes of :

The reserve at moonlight basin. I continued struggling (maybe also because I left the stimp on 10), but I went triple bogey, bogey, par, bogey, double. On the 6th, I was not having it, and decided to say f it, it's not your day, go back and practice.

Overall, 12+ over 8 holes. That's about scoring around 100... that is just unacceptable after the latest run (81, 87, 88, 87, 89).

At any rate, copilot is starting to piss me off in it's analysis. It 's getting confused with ball speed vs club speed (which the LM doesn't provide). I think my analysis from a few weeks ago is way off. After yelling at it some... it gave me a new prediction that seems more in line with reality. I asked it to dig deeper, and it's been digging for a bit, this is before it finished:

item.title: Tale of two 9s
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Front 9 +2, back 9 +18.

Wynn, I played from the yellow which was new for me. Front 9 I was just on. Even when I missed I was able to recover.

The front had 5 pars, a birdie, and 3 bogeys.

The back 9 started weird. A 207 yard par 3 that I hit a driver way off. I tripled, then 8 consecutive double bogey! Finished with a single.

Crazy... why did this happen.

That tells you a bit. My off the tee was as bad as my approach game. My drives were all over the place. The first drive was a dead center 3.5 O-I, 1 degree open 201 yard drive. Somewhere about 3 or 4 drives again, things went off. I was either topping or it was going 140 yards. Alot of it appeared to be closing the face too much again. You were way left today (again)

The wood was spordaic --- I had some travel in my 160-180 range, but euqally as many or more travel under 150!

The hybrids were okay. A little right, and very over the top

Irons... with the exception of the 9 were over the top, but played well enough. More of the old swing than the new.

SW was pretty good today, and LW was also good,

The course wasn't really done right for this distance IMO. I had a 173, 207 and 160 yard par 3! There were a couple that were shorter (125, 116, and 145), but those other ones seemed like lazy design. When I did the other course (6200 yards, so 300+ longer), the par 3s long was 163, which feels about right.

For the Par 5s, your starting to see lots of 500 yard holes. 200 off the tee, 170 with the wood, leaves you usually in the 130-150 yard range on these par 5s in the low 500s. A mistake with either club, or not finding your distance your looking at 200 plus out

The par 4s, your seeing some in the low 400s, and plenty in the high 300s. Yo you need to get 200+ off the tee. This is where distance I think is really becoming a problem. If you say you go 180 (which is pretty average for me), your now 200+ to the green. Occasionally you have that great wood shot, but it isn't reliable. I'm getting better , but need more distance.

I struggled a bit in warmup too. My irons I have a pattern, but when I try to start 'doing stuff', things tend to go awry. My swing looked ugly on video again. Always seem to come back to some mobility thing, but I get the ball to move.

At any rate, yesterday went from potential breakthrough on the front 9 to total disaster on the back.

item.title: Another poor round
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I felt like I was hitting the ball much better today, BUT the score didn't come through.

I played Montreux where I posted one of my best scores (81). Today was and 89. I blame it on a slow start, and hitting into too many penalty areas. I also blame a few strokes on bad short play. Was disappointed to be playing 500 yards shorter and not play better.

The good news today... Distance. I averaged a total of 211 off the tee, with a long of 223. Looking at my chart, I had one bad pop up (110), one shank left (135), and a few shorts (150-175). Everything else was 180 plus. Pretty good. I however hit in to trouble enough times that sometimes took an extra shot because I was in heavy rough (or hit trees on the way out).

The wood was inconsistent. Two 90s, a coupel 120s (I think one was out of rough), and one good 180 yard hit. I didn't hit the hybrids much, but I got plenty of speed out of the one that came out of the rough, it just didn't go far, and the H4 I had one that played well (156)

I hit all my irons. Missed several shots long with Irons today.

  • I6, struck poorly, one really over the top, and another fat (a little better)
  • i7 - One good one bad, a 137 yarder which is right where you should be and only 3 yards left (although if I remember this one actually went in the sand
  • i8 one misstrike bullet (I think this was my penalty), the other 2 were good playable in the 115-118 range
  • i9 - one shot 102 yards, good path, but 18 yards left. Hard to make sense, but the HLA was left. path and everything else good
  • PW -- problems here, I caught one good 115 yards (same as my i8), and then one 94, and another 74. No consistency
  • GW - hit 5 here, which encompasses two clubs. 80 yards. Tends to go left with a closed club face
  • SW and LW -- lots today , not as good on distance, but it's straight within 50. You average less than a yard offline.

Putting was adequate. I did miss some putts though, and so I think this is deceptive.

This was just misses, but playing at my level. High 80s with a ceiling of low 80s. I played everything average one over par.

One thing I did differently today... more focus on knuckles down on my drives. Yes gets the face more closed, but it also led me to hit it longer

I was frustrated after this round, because I thought I was capable of a much better score. However, I notice from last round here, I may have averaged less (177 yards average drive), but I hit way more fairways... that helped a lot.

item.title: Everytime I think I'm about breakthrough.... I don't
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
It's frustrating. I spent some time just hitting short shots yesterday trying to control the path, and the face. It was okay, path was harder with short swings, so maybe I should keep working on it. My distance was actually really good on these

I played a few holes before I couldn't anymore... what happened. I hit terribly. Driver was not on to start, so that was a problem. I was back in the 160-170 carry range... terrible. When I finally started playing it went up a little, but control of course dropped, and then I just started trying to slam it, and the face was too closed. Terrible... and higher speed balls were more O-I

GPT sums it up

Your problem isn’t “I can’t get the path in.” Your problem is when you try to get the path in, your face control collapses. And when you swing your old pattern, your face and path sync up naturally, even though the path is still left.

Anyhow, it gets frustrating. During my warmup, hitting anything hybrid or wood related was hard, till the last couple shots where the 'whip' starting working some. I just feel like I should be 20% longer on everything

Anyhow, I played 8 holes at a shorter course. Lack of distance, and fatigue played a role. I played the first hole well, but then struggled. Nothing really good after that. STurggled off tee, which lead to struggle to green. I guess I hit a couple good wedge shots, but then also shanked one off (fatigue).

PArt of me thinks I need to get outside and play, but the other half says that will just keep reinforcing the old patterns. Outside may allow me to swing more free.

Also on top of all my struggles, I am still struggling tunring the hips through and finishing. I don't seem to have a problem getting back, but shift and through is an issue (again). I kind of know what to do back and to the ball, and where the faults are and how to fix them, but concurrently doing them with the follow through issue is hard. As soon as I try to add that in, things start feeling off, and usually the ball flies in every direction.

It does seem to come back to a few things I should be doing , that seem to have positive impact lately.

  • Think drop hands, and then turn.
  • Swing from the inside.
  • Keep lead wrist bowed a little. This seems to have added distance on certain days.
  • With my irons, just staying down and rotating around the ball at least to impact, seems to keep thigns pretty straight. It feels different than hybrid and wood strikes... those feel more whippy.
  • Start your back swing without pulling the club back towards you, but steeper path up , start with the body more
  • Think about the circle and a more in to out path through
  • Think about the tilt, and not standing up, and keeping the tilt through with your ear dropping the water each side.

And here is my chat: that boils down to this:

🎯 “Up… drop… turn.”

THE THREE PILLARS OF YOUR SWING

Everything you listed fits into one of these.

Pillar 1 — Start the swing correctly (backswing organization)

This includes:

  • Start with the body
  • Don’t pull the club inside
  • Steeper takeaway
  • Stay on the circle
  • Maintain tilt

These are all the same thing: A clean, organized backswing that doesn’t trap the arms.

Pillar 2 — Transition correctly (your master key)

This includes:

  • Drop hands, then turn
  • Swing from the inside
  • Right elbow in front
  • In‑to‑out path

These are all the same thing: Arms fall first → body turns second.

This is the ONLY move that fixes your sequencing.

Pillar 3 — Deliver the club correctly (impact & finish)

This includes:

  • Lead wrist bowed
  • Stay down with irons
  • Rotate around the ball
  • Keep tilt
  • Woods feel whippy

These are all the same thing: Stable face + stable body = predictable strike.

HOW “UP… DROP… TURN” TRIGGERS ALL YOUR GOOD FEELS

1. “UP” = your entire backswing checklist

  • Steeper takeaway
  • Body starts it
  • No pulling inside
  • Stay on the circle
  • Maintain tilt

All of that happens when you simply think UP.

2. “DROP” = your entire transition checklist

  • Hands fall
  • Arms get in front
  • Club shallows
  • Path shifts inside‑out
  • Right elbow slots

This is the move that fixes your whole swing.

3. “TURN” = your entire delivery checklist

  • Lead wrist stays bowed
  • Rotate around the ball
  • Maintain tilt
  • Irons stay compressed
  • Woods get width + whip
  • Finish becomes natural

This is why your finish only works when the transition is right.

⭐ Your new, simplified swing blueprint

This is the version you can actually take to the course:

Backswing:

UP (steeper, body‑driven, no inside pull)

Transition:

DROP (hands fall before the body turns)

Downswing:

TURN (rotate around the ball, stable face, full finish)

That’s it. Three words. One pattern. Everything you listed fits inside it.

item.title: And just like that, first sub 80 round
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
After yesterday's struggles today I finally break 80.

Granted... it's an easier course, and lots of opportunity to get some distance down hill on drives, but I'll take it.

I've played this 3 times. The first time I scored a ~126 (first course I played on recommendation), second time 93 (February), and now 79!

The eagle listed was not an eagle, it was a birdie. I originally thought, oh well the designers made a short par 5, it was just a mistake on there part. They meant to have hole 5, be a par 4 (just look at the distances) I thought I was playing a Par 4, but it registered as a Par 5, but only 299 yards. I had a really great approach shot on that one that landed in the circle. On the following hole, I birdied again, but If I remember right, I had to actually make a putt.

My average is not considerably changed, as I've been stuck in the high 80s and low 90 for the most of April, so nice to get a good score. Rolling average dropped to an 86.7 and rolling SAS to an 89.7. These are both lows.

What went well. Short holes, decent enough drives, and good approaches that hit the green. A few outstanding putts, a few good chips. Only three real 'mistakes' -- one chipping over the green, bad decision. One Out of Bounds drive (took a drop), and one chip that didn't do what I wanted. PW, and GW were really good today, lots of 60-80 yard shots, that played pretty decent.

I've seen much worse distributions in recent rounds. I felt like the driver was really good in the front 9.

There were several pop ups on the driver, that's the 130-140 ones later in the round. A few where I pushed it out, in the 160-170 range. One that I really hit solid straight 217 was nice. Lots more straight paths, especially early.

Interesting, I hit no i7 through i9. The course length and driver dictated that. If I hit the driver well, I was in that ~!100 yard range. I hit 6 PW, which is unusual, and 4 GW, which is a little less unusual (Even though that is a 2 clubs A, and G)

The PW averaged right around 90 yards, and the 2 GW, averaged 61. Those were all finese shots with

Interesting miss pattern here, I'm averaging 6-7 yards left on both those clubs. My path was a bit over the top on these, which makes it kind of interesting too paired with an open club face, doesn't entirely make sense, except that my launch angles are all left (across all clubs)

My other shots fell in W3, H3 (which I hit 4 of unusual), 1 H4, and a few I6. Looks like I had a bad miss on one i6, but they may have hit an obstacle or out of the rough. I would say I hit these pretty average -- again, lack of consistency in distance hurts me. MY ceiling is 80 yards longer than my floor on the wood today. 110 to 190. The W3 trended right. The H3 trended left and the I6, was a bit right. The i6 is a club I know hit well well go around 140, but lacked distance today.

The H3 has a higher ceiling, of the 151 top I hit today. That's one that I've hit 180+ on course, and usually can get in the 160-170 range in the SIM.

Looking through my warm up data. I spent alot of time hitting half shots with the 6 and 7 (although this doesn't feel right... wonder if they reintroduced the bug on selection... says I have a bunch of PW shots, which I don't recall and think were i7 or i8). Not sure I can believe any of this data today... something seems off from this practice session.

item.title: An 80, an unboosted scoring
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I did Jack's point today, and scored an 80. I missed by a few inches on the last putt to do back to back under 80, but I'll take it, second best score!

Most birdies in a single round today with 3! Length today was 5371. Last time I played the longer course, at 6202 and scored a respectable 89 with no boost (that was just 2 weeks ago). Today's equivalent SAS was 4 strokes better.

I had trouble keeping it on the fairway, especially early. I was really over closing the face and launching left, but I was able to get in under control by the end of the round. I wasn't going particularly long, but I was hitting it good enough (180ish)

The wedges were really the star again, SW, and GW. I've hit them well and straight, and had good distance control, hitting few within the icrcl

The one double bogey was where I made a pretty big mistake and not chipping on the green properly coming up short, and the 2nd chip didn't leave me with an easy putt. A bit of fatigue .

In the LLM analysis, ball was all over the place with the higher clubs. Pray and Spray with the driver. Fortunately the spray left (most of the big misses), stayed in bounds and was able to recover. I saw balls go up to 50 yards left, with 4 total 35 yards left or more. I had 3 that went 20 yards left, and then 6 that were in a windows of 15 yards left, or 10 yards right.

All of the wood trended right, and I was way over the top with the club, but I got a lot 'snap' with it. Irons and wedges again played good with distance control. Irons could be a bit longer in the 7 and 9, but the short misses weren't terrible today.

You can see, Gained strokes through putting, putting was good, I hit one really good longer putt, and save another medium range. Around the green was good, good chips with the 56. Approach was typically because the distance off the tee was poor. Even on this shorter 5300 yard course, I still need more distance on some holes.

Since I've dropped the 'boost', two things happened. One, I get a rough penalty now, and have to play to that. Club up in the rough. Since I've made the switch, (4/8), I've played 9 times, and I'm averaging 85. 5. My GSPro handicap is down to 13.1! I feel like at the current shorter course length, I could get things down to single digits, but my next goal is really to get a little bit more distance through my clubs to play around the 6000-6500 length courses well. Basically, move up a tee

That is a pretty nice chart, the green line is the 'bossted normalized' score, and the green line adds in distance to the equation (just adjusted to make it square root of 5300 / distance). You can see they are starting to converge over the last few weeks as the socres have

The view without boosts it a little less of a steep downtren

Even that one, we are at a low point with the rolling adjusted average (after mulligans) is down to 85.6. I haven't used a mulligan in 5 rounds now! So it's a pretty honest improvment.

I've gone from a 105 average down to 85 since getting the SIM. 20 shots improved since October, 7 months. I think I can the average down a bit more in the next few months , but I likely won't get to play much with the sauna my garage is.

Just as an aside, my GSPro handicap started at 25.7, and is now 13.1, which is a 12 stroke improvement. Because of hte boost though, I don't think it fully shows the improvement.

If I look at boosted normalized improvement with distance, you've gone from low 120s (lets say 123, down to about an 87 now. That's a 36 stroke improvement. Pretty damn good...

Now, if I could only just stay pretty consistent with this, keep the floor just below 90 , and the ceiling in the high 70s for a few weeks. I fear, your always not far away from a 100+ round though...

item.title: 36 holes, 2 rounds in a session
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I did this, and now my back is aching quite a bit. But it was fun. Plenty of good and bad.

First up DPC Spyglass Hill. I did this last in late March, 103% boost, and had a really good score of 84. Today I struggled off the tee, and only managed and 87 at the same distance. I really was spraying the driver all over the place. I'm not sure when I transitioned from wood to driver. I notice the last one was during that very good run I had (84, 82, 81).

Besides the fairway misses (14% fairway hit, vs 50% previous time), GIR was the same at 28%, which isn't bad playing out of the rough. I played well with most of my chipping and putting . Found greens a bit easier on this course. It was two disaster holes that sunk me. It was because drives ended up in rough, and losing a couple strokes getting out. I had another where I went back and forth over a thin green. It was very much played to the average. Despite the storkes gains saying approach was the problem, driving was the problem. I did also take a mulligan on one that I hit out of bounds.

Contrast with Wolf Creek. I scored an 84. My driver performed much better, My fairway hit went up to 43%, and I struggled a bit less. Still had a share of mistakes, and a couple of double+ holes. No birdies (although quite a few chances). This was significantly shorter at only 5037 yards too.

In contrast, I've played this 6 times! It's a favorite. I played yellow today. Last time I played a longer White at 5715, and scored a 90 (March again). This time I scored an 84, which felt like a bit of a defeat, but still the best i've ever scored on this. I had a breakthrough on this course with an 86 back in December of last year. Was my best round to that point. I used a 16% boost back then though. My FIR improved this round, and I got the driver moving straighter, but less long. 43% FIR, and 28% GIR again.

Anyhow, there was some fatigue towards the end of this round, as the back 9 once again scored higher (4 strokes) than the front. Same on Spyglass hill,

Also worth mentioning, I played 5 holes at top of the world ops 36 challenge. .. .yea, 40 holes no wonder why my back is hurting. I hit the ball really well during this until like hole 6, where I had to bail because I got stuck and the physics wouldn't let me out. Before that, I was par on 1 through 4. Went 3 over because I hit long on a shot over and had trouble getting around the physics, and then stuck on the last.

item.title: This was going to be a negative post, but ends very positively.
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I played yesterday outside. Unlike my previous outing, this one did not feel good. Less about how I played, but more about the group I played with. Sometimes your with a personality that doesn't gel with you, and yesterday I had one of those golfers. Just seemed a bit annoyed to be playing with golfers that weren't as good as he was.

In this foursome, there was one guy who I would say was a little better than I am. Probably a low to mid 90s kind of player. Other guy was probably a low 80s player, and yesterday I played at about a 100, and the other guy was about my level.

Anyhow, the one guy was just really off putting, and it threw me off a little made it hard to relax. I was struggling with the usual swing pattern that was happening when I transition to real turf (I'm topping shots). With that said, I made some really great shots, like I do in the SIM, but it wasn't consistent. So with that, lets get on with the review.

Northwest, played 14 holes. I was a pretty dismal by the watch +24, and never got in to a rhythm.

Lets start with overall play. Driving was decent, but my lack of distance was exposed on a longer course of 6300 yards. This was one of those situations where another 20 yards off the long clubs would make a huge difference.

The Driver --- The good, was that I only hit one that I could not play, otherwise, I kept it in play. The distance was okay, but not great, but I missed the fairway most of the time.

Drives - 198 (just off fairway), 200, left of fairway, 206 (fairway), 230 (left fairway), 165 (this was your miss), 190 (miss left) , 178 (miss left, uphill) , 208 (just right fairway, really good strike), 188 (just right again) , 183 (left fairway). Average (removing the miss), 197 yards. That is the best you've done to date, but it wasn't enough on the longer course.

Wood - Had to play this a lot because of the length. Hit it more times this round than any
