3W - 55 (obvious miss) , 101 (bad bullet) , 103 (same bad shot), 179 (finally a good shot, landed on the green!) . 190 (good distance again), 113 (top[ped it again) , 83 (topped again) , 218 (probably best shot of day, but bounced off the green) , 159 (but missed way left). 195 (and hit the green, but skidded up it). AVERAGE 190 for the non misses!

I'll highlight a couple other shots of the day with the rest of the clubs:

  • 4 hybrid 154 yards, just missed because you missed right a bit on a long par 3, this was more an aim miss with the wind blowing.
  • 6i - 138 yards -- missed right . There is a trend, as the club shorten, I miss right.

So I'll do a best hole. The only par on the day, which had a outside chance of a birdie.

5th Hole Par 5. Hit that long drive of the day 230 yards missed left. First 3W (marked 3h, but it was the wood), traveled across the fairway instead of up the middle. Left about 180 yards to go, I hit the 3W and lands softly on the green. So despite a bad 2nd shot, a good first and third left me in position. About a 20 or so foot putt, good lag, and knocked in the 5 footer.

Second best was the last hole. 3W off the tee on a 200 yard par 3. This was luck, but I hit just on top of the sand trap, and ball rolled way on to green and stopped. Two GIR!

It says 2 putt above, but it was 3. This was basically a par if I took a little more time. I had a good lag on the downhill long putt, but then the ball whireled out the hole on my tap in. I count it 4, but easily could have been a 3.

Let's say bogey's are also good holes. Hole 4 I was finally starting to get more comfortable. I hit a good drive, 200 yards on a dog leg, and actually did hit the fairway. 4 Hybrid came up just short of the green at 135 yards, but I it was centered. Chipper on and then a 2 putt. Felt good about that. This was right before I par'ed the next hole. A bogey, par sequence is good .

The par 3s I struggled with short game after missing green, both times right, both times in the sand traps.

Another really good bogey hole. I drove 188 yards, which wasn't great, but very playable. on hole 11, I then hit that long ass 3W 218 yards that was way better than driver. Unfortunately, it went off the green, and then I chipped and 3 putted for a bogey, it was a waste of that 3W because of the short game.

So why so much higher than my SIM rounds. 1) Distance --- on this type of distance, I think I scored like this in a sim. 6300+ yards is hard for me. 2) Pressure -- playing with others, not familiar, rushing the swing because of this 3) Putting - I think I lost double the strokes I normally would playing in the sim. 4) The lies -- it didn't effect the scorecard as much, but some of the misses were bad lies. I had some plain mulligans I took (not a lot, but they were in there), where you topped it and it dribbled forward 5-10 yards. 5) Walking fatigue -- it feels so great to walk and push, it's a great workout, but it fatigues later)

One of my biggest frustrations is my distance. I see guys (and women) not as strong hitting the ball way further. It's all a sequencing issue for me, that I just can't seem to figure out so that I can get the distance my body should be able to create! The group I played with was consistently out hitting my on the driver in particular. My 3W seemed to play long when struck well, but driver seems 20 to 40 yards shorter than what my body is capable of

Passing in some data may have just revealed something with the AI. I think I might have a real thing here, this is direct from last driver session.

Here's the cruel irony: your "good" shots still have terrible attack angle (–2.5°). They work because you're generating enough ball speed (avg 115.7 mph on good ones) to overpower the bad delivery. You're muscling distance out of a flawed impact — which is exactly why you see smaller people out-hitting you. They're delivering the club better with less force.

And your "bad" shots — the only ones with a slightly positive AoA — are the topped/mishit ones (Hole 2 at 77 yards). Your body associates "hitting up" with disaster. That's learned avoidance, and it's keeping you stuck.

The Diagnosis

You don't have a speed problem — 111 mph average ball speed is solid. You have a delivery problem with two interlocking issues:

  1. Negative attack angle (–1.6° avg): You're hitting down on driver like it's a 7-iron. This adds ~1,300 RPM of unnecessary spin and kills launch efficiency. Fixing this alone is worth 25–35 yards.
  2. Over-the-top path with closed face: You're swinging out-to-in and compensating with a shut face. This produces pulls, pull-hooks, and cuts across the ball that waste energy sideways instead of forward.

These two are connected. The over-the-top move causes the downward strike — your club is descending because it's approaching from outside and steep. Fix the path, and the attack angle tends to follow.

The sim is your lab. Chase these numbers in your next session: AoA above +2°, spin below 3,000, path inside +2° in-to-out. Forget where the ball goes — just chase the delivery numbers. When those three line up, you'll see your carry jump 30–40 yards without swinging any harder.

If this is right, this is another breakthrough moment. I've been tracking the swing path for so long, and not really understanding AoA at all because the AI never revealed it as a problem... but now that driver has become important again, this is leading me to the right spot. I am so excited . To think complaining about the wood traveling well on good strikes off the deck and comparing to driver got the AI moving really in the right direction. Wood has proper attack angle, driver does not... spins too much, and here we are!

Man... I went from negative on the round, to feeling really positive about practice this coming week.

item.title: What exactly to work on
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I somewhat disagree with what Copilot is telling me as far as priority to fix. I think I need to work attack angle first with driver, and then simaltaneously continue to work on path. Here was there overview, but this is mostly coming from driver data:

Your Data Profile (What We're Fixing)

Critical insight: Path and AoA are connected. The over-the-top move causes the downward strike. Fix the path first — the AoA improvement will follow. Spin and left miss are symptoms, not root causes — they'll clean up as path and angle improve.

Phase 1: Kill the Over-the-Top (Weeks 1–2)

This is the foundation. Nothing else matters until the club stops coming from outside.

Drill 1A: The Headcover Gate

What it fixes: Forces the club to drop inside instead of casting over the top. MyGolfSpy

Setup:

  • Place your driver headcover (or a towel) 6–8 inches behind the ball, just outside your target line
  • Take your normal stance

Execution:

  • Make half-speed swings. Your only goal: don't hit the headcover on the downswing
  • If you clip it, your hands are throwing outward from the top. Reset, slow down further
  • Feel like your chest stays "closed" (pointed right of target) while your arms drop under and behind you
  • Start with no ball. Then tee up a ball and hit at 50% speed

Reps: 20 dry swings, then 15 balls at 50% effort. Every session for 2 weeks.

Sim metric to track: Face-to-Path direction. You're currently 92% out-to-in. Goal: get 50%+ of swings showing in-to-out or neutral.

Drill 1B: The Trail Foot Step-Back

What it fixes: Makes it physically impossible to come over the top by shifting your weight and path.

Setup:

  • Normal driver address position

Execution:

  • At address, pull your trail foot (right foot) back 6–8 inches, dropping it behind you so your stance is extremely closed
  • This forces your shoulders to close, which pre-sets an inside-out swing path
  • Make full swings from this exaggerated stance
  • The ball will want to go right — that's good. A push or push-draw means the club is coming from the inside for the first time

Reps: 20 balls per session. If the ball starts right, you're doing it correctly.

Sim metric to track: Club Path. Looking for any positive number (in-to-out), even 1°. You've almost never produced this in 118 shots.

Drill 1C: The "Back to the Target" Pause

What it fixes: The transition — where your body fires toward the target before your arms drop, causing the over-the-top throw.

Setup:

  • Normal driver address

Execution:

  • Take the club to the top of your backswing. Stop. Hold it for a full 2-second count
  • Feel your back facing the target. Your belt buckle should still point away from the target
  • From this paused position, start the downswing by dropping your hands straight down toward your trail hip — like you're pulling a rope from a pulley above your right shoulder
  • The feeling is "down before out." Arms fall, then the body rotates through
  • Hit balls at 60% speed with the pause. It'll feel absurdly slow. That's the point

Reps: 15 balls per session.

Sim metric: HLA (Horizontal Launch Angle). You're averaging 6–8° left. Goal: get it within 3° of zero.

Phase 2: Hit Up on the Ball (Weeks 2–4)

Once the path starts coming from the inside (you'll see it on the sim), layer in the ascending strike.

Drill 2A: The Tommy Fleetwood Tee Drill

What it fixes: Directly trains positive attack angle with instant visual feedback. GOLF.com

Setup:

  • Tee up your ball normally
  • Place a second empty tee in the ground about 4 inches in front of your ball (toward the target), along the target line

Execution:

  • Hit your driver. Your goal: hit the ball and miss the forward tee
  • If you're hitting down on the ball (your current –3.4°), the clubhead will clip or snap that forward tee
  • If you're hitting up, the club ascends after impact and passes over the forward tee cleanly
  • Fleetwood: "If I was going to hit down, the driver would hit the tee. I'm going to have to sweep up." GOLF.com

Reps: 20 balls per session. Count how many you miss the tee on — track the percentage.

Sim metric: Attack Angle. You need to go from –3.4° to positive. Even +1° is a massive breakthrough. Every degree up is roughly 4–5 yards of carry.

Drill 2B: Ball Position + Spine Tilt Exaggeration

What it fixes: Pre-sets your body geometry for an ascending blow before the swing even starts. caddiehq.com

Setup changes (make ALL of these):

  1. Ball position: Move it to your left instep — further forward than you think. Off the heel, not the toe
  2. Tee height: Half the ball should be above the crown of the driver. Uncomfortably high
  3. Spine tilt: At address, drop your trail shoulder (right shoulder) noticeably lower than your lead. Feel like your spine leans 5–10° away from the target
  4. Lead hip bump: Before you start the swing, bump your lead hip 1–2 inches toward the target. This shifts the swing's low point behind the ball MSN

Execution:

  • Make smooth swings. The setup does the work. Don't try to "lift" or "scoop" — just swing through with normal rotation
  • The ball should launch higher and feel like it jumps off the face

Sim metric: VLA (Vertical Launch Angle). You're averaging 18.4° with high spin — a balloon ball. With proper AoA you'll see VLA drop to 12–15° but the ball will carry further because spin drops from 3,750 to under 2,800.

Drill 2C: The "Swing Up the First Base Line" Feel

What it fixes: Gives your body a feel cue for ascending delivery.

Execution:

  • Imagine you're standing at home plate. Your target is center field
  • Feel like your club exits through impact toward first base (right-hander) — up and to the right
  • The exaggeration in your head will produce maybe +2° of actual upward movement. What feels like hitting a pop-up is actually optimal launch

Pair with: Drill 2A (Fleetwood tee). Swing toward first base and miss the forward tee. When both happen together, your sim numbers will change dramatically.

Phase 3: Face Control Integration (Weeks 3–5)

Your closed face (85% of shots) is a compensation for the over-the-top path. As the path improves, the face may start going right (because you've been unconsciously shutting it to prevent the OTT slice). You'll need to recalibrate.

Drill 3A: The Knuckle Check

What it fixes: Grip pressure and hand rotation that closes the face.

Execution:

  • At address, check that you can see 2–2.5 knuckles on your lead hand (left hand). Not 3, not 4
  • If you see 3+ knuckles, your grip is too strong — this closes the face through impact
  • On the range/sim, hit 10 balls with a deliberately "weak" feeling grip — rotate your lead hand slightly left (clockwise) on the club. The face will feel open. Shots may go right. That's the calibration happening

Sim metric: Face-to-Target. You're 85% closed. Goal: get within ±2° of zero.

Drill 3B: The Lead Wrist Awareness Check

What it fixes: The bowed (flexed) wrist that's slamming the face shut. hackmotion.com

Execution:

  • Take the club to the top of your backswing. Pause
  • Look at your lead wrist — is it bowed (flexed downward) or flat?
  • For a neutral face at impact, you want a flat to slightly bowed lead wrist at the top, not excessively bowed
  • Hit half-speed shots feeling like your lead wrist is flat (like the back of your hand is a tabletop) at the top and through impact

Sim metric: Face-to-Path. When this is within ±2°, your spin axis drops, slicing/hooking reduces, and the ball starts flying straighter.

Your Sim Practice Protocol

Each session on the sim (30–45 min):

Your Progress Scorecard

Track these after every session. This is your real progress — not where the ball goes.

--

Back to my own commentary. This hitting up is a Driver problem only. An AoA problem with the driver, and that is different than the rest of the bag.

The iron problems continue to be an over the top swing path, and once you really fix that (you've gotten close and lost it), the variance in your AoA which is the problem will fix itself. So continue working the over the top on the other clubs. Slow it down, and see if you can get things moving.

Now, I await the analysis across the last 10 days of 3W and hybrid data. I think I'll see it will continue to be over the top on those clubs, but probably to a slightly lesser degree. It will be more about face control on the hybrids.... and the verdict is:

The wood feels better because dispersion is better, not much else it said about that. The hybrids are too steep.

What This Means for Your Game Strategy Right Now

Short term (next round): Honestly? Off the tee, your 3-wood is more playable than your driver. You give up ~25 yards of carry but you cut your offline dispersion in half and your misses go to the safe side. On courses under 6,300 yards, the 3-wood off the tee is a legitimate scoring play.

Longer term: The fix is the same one we identified for driver — kill the OTT path. When the club approaches from inside, every club in the bag benefits:

  • Driver: path fix → ascending strike → 30-40 yard gain
  • 3-Wood: path fix → consistent face → it becomes a reliable 175–190 club
  • Hybrids: path fix → shallower approach → they start carrying 150–170 instead of 110
  • Irons: path fix → stable low point → consistent compression

You don't need 14 different fixes. You need one fix that cascades through the entire bag. The OTT path is the single thread connecting every problem we've found across 433 shots and every club you own.

Everything here is path fix, path fix, path fix, then fix the other problem. Ascending strike on the driver, shallower approach on the hybrids (less angle of attack, like 1 to 3 degrees)

On the hybrids, I should be sweeping, and on the irons I've got close to the right AoA on well hit shots (just variance being the problem).

I asked it lastly about HLA and VLA. HLA I think really is a function on aim and also face path (and a bit of club path), and VLA is a function of AoA and face path.

So the result... I trend to move the ball left on my swings. The VLA analysis is just that I tend to get it wrong the logner the clubs. Driver should have the lowest vla, and then 3w, the 3h, then 4h... it's inverted.

Your VLA should ladder up as clubs get shorter (driver lowest, 8-iron highest). Here's what's actually happening:

Overall, it always comes back to the same over the top will have the most bang for the buck...

#1: The Headcover Gate

Why it's #1: It's the only drill that gives you a binary pass/fail on every single swing. You either came over the top or you didn't. No ambiguity, no feel — just physics. MyGolfSpy

Setup:

  • Place a headcover (or towel, water bottle, shoe — anything) 6–8 inches behind the ball, just outside your target line
  • Tee up a ball normally. Take your regular stance
  • Add a touch more hip bend at address — this makes it easier for the club to swing around you instead of lifting straight up

Execution:

  1. Take the club back normally. On the downswing, feel like your chest stays pointing right of target while your arms and hands drop under and behind you
  2. If the club clips the headcover → you came over the top. Reset, go slower
  3. If the club misses the headcover → the club dropped inside. That's the path you need
  4. Start with dry swings only — no ball, half speed, just miss the headcover
  5. Once you can miss it 8/10 times dry, tee up a ball and hit at 50% effort
  6. Gradually build to 75%. Don't go to 100% until it's automatic

The key feel: Your arms drop straight down from the top, like they're falling into your right pocket. Then your body rotates through. Down, then around — not out, then across.

Sim metric to track: Club Path. Right now you're producing out-to-in on 92%+ of swings. Goal:

Do this drill: Start of every session, 10 dry swings + 10 balls. Non-negotiable warm-up.

#2: The Trail Elbow Slot

Why it's #2: The headcover tells you if you came over the top. This drill teaches your body what to do instead. It reprograms the transition by giving your trail arm a specific job.

The concept: In an OTT swing, your trail elbow (right elbow) flies away from your body at the top, dragging the club outside and over. In an inside-out swing, the trail elbow drops down against your rib cage first, pulling the club into the "slot" — the inside track.

Setup:

  • Tuck a glove, towel, or headcover under your right armpit at address
  • Grip the club normally over it

Execution:

  1. Make your backswing — the towel will start to loosen. That's fine
  2. Start your downswing. Your only goal: keep the towel pinned against your body through the first half of the downswing
  3. If the towel drops before impact → your elbow flew out → you came over the top
  4. If the towel stays pinned until after impact → your elbow slotted against your body → the club came from inside
  5. Hit balls at 60% speed. The towel gives you instant feedback

The key feel: At the top, your right elbow points straight down at the ground, not out behind you. On the downswing, it feels like your right elbow is driving toward your right hip pocket. The club has no choice but to drop inside.

Why it works for your specific pattern: Your 433-shot data shows the face closes more as clubs get longer (–5.3° HLA with driver vs. –2.6° with 8-iron). That's because the OTT move gives the face more time to rotate shut. When the elbow slots and the club drops inside, the path shortens, the club spends less time rotating, and the face arrives squarer. This drill fixes path AND face simultaneously.

Sim metric to track: Face-to-Path direction. When this flips from "Out-to-In" to "In-to-Out" or "Neutral," the elbow is slotting. Also watch HLA — it should migrate from –5° toward zero.

Do this drill: 15 balls per session, right after the headcover gate warm-up.

#3: The Alignment Stick Plane Gate

Why it's #3: This is the "graduate level" drill that trains the full path through the hitting zone — not just the transition, but the arc of the club through impact and beyond. MyGolfSpy

Setup:

  • Stick an alignment stick (or a long dowel) into the ground at your shaft angle at address — angled from the ground near your ball, leaning away from you at roughly 60°
  • Place a second alignment stick on the ground along your target line
  • The angled stick creates a "plane gate" — a visual reference for where the club should travel

Execution:

  1. Make slow swings. On the backswing, the club should travel inside and under the angled stick
  2. On the downswing, the club should drop under the angled stick again — not over it
  3. If you come over the top, the club will hit the angled stick or pass above it. Instant feedback
  4. Start without a ball — just swing through the gate. Feel the club arc under the stick on both sides
  5. Add a ball at 50% speed once the path feels grooved

The key feel: The swing feels flatter and more around you — like a baseball swing tilted on an angle. Less "up and chop," more "around and through." Your hands stay closer to your body through the whole swing.

Why it's the finisher: The headcover drill fixes the transition moment. The elbow drill fixes the body mechanic. This drill trains the entire arc — it grooves the feeling of an on-plane, inside-out path from takeaway through follow-through. Once all three click together, the path change becomes automatic.

Sim metrics to track: Club Path (degrees in-to-out) and Spin Axis. When the path is inside-out, the spin axis will shift from left (draw/hook axis) to more neutral. You're looking for Club Path to show consistent small positive numbers (+1° to +3° in-to-out).

Do this drill: 10 balls per session, last drill before full integration swings.

And lastly... what drill for the driver

The Forward Tee Drill (aka the Fleetwood Drill)

This is the one. It gives you a binary pass/fail on every swing — you either hit up or you didn't. No guessing, no feel, just evidence on the ground.

Setup

  1. Tee up your ball at normal height — half the ball above the crown of the driver
  2. Push a second empty tee into the ground 4 inches in front of your ball (toward the target), directly on the target line
  3. That forward tee is your judge and jury

Before You Swing: The Pre-Sets

These setup changes shift your low point behind the ball before the swing starts. Without them, the drill just punishes you without fixing anything.

item.title: A good practice and exceptional front 9, and back to the PXG driver
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I worked on the I-O bit. I was able to achieve some success with driver. I ended up switching back to the old driver. It honestly felt a ton better. It seemed little less hot off the face, but I had way more straight shots with it than the 'new driver'. I will play my next few rounds with that and see how we do.

I was able to get the club AoA up. Not a ton, but it was up on plenty of hits. Crazy that my club path for driver during my play was 1.5 degrees O-I (with a peak 8.5 I-O) and a .5 Down AoA. A peak 2.9 degree Up AoA. My long strike went 220, with a 193 carry. Playable... but not great given the numbers

My distance was nothing special, but my dispersion was better, and I felt like I had more playable balls. This ended up leading to ana mazing front 9, where I went +1. Granted it was the shorter side (2500 yards), but I went birdie, birdie, bogey, birdie , par through the first 5. On hole 2 I had a 'short' par 5 of 362 yards where I came just with about 8 feet of the hole on 2nd shot approach. I had the putt just lip out for eagle!

I played the rest of the front 9 pretty good, until I either hit in a penalty or failed to get out of the sand on 8 (those were my two big early mistakes). Even with the double bogey, I still scored a 37 on the front 9. Very close to my first 9 hole Par.

I thought I had a good shot of playing under 80, but the back 9 fatigue got me. A few drives that went off kilter from the tee, a couple of greens just missed, and I played my usual bogey golf on the back 9 (+9). The two pars, balanced around two doubles, and the rest were bogey golf. I made some really good recoveries.

OF the other clubs... I struck my irons 6 & 7 pretty terrible (fat) over 4 shots. The i8 and i9 were in there normal range. Nothing particularly good or bad. I had one i8 that carried 103 yards, with almost a perfect 0 club path. The i9, I had a nice less than 4 degree O-I, and was able to keep it online right to stick 120 yards.

Wedges were predictable, except for a couple misses. Sometimes I come up a bit short on the green with these, don't have full control under 50. The hybrids were way over the top except for one shot with 3Hy, that went about 170. The wood had a mix of very playable, and a few that went too far right. Once again, I got path down to very low O-I on the the best strikes (180 yards).

I didn't find the distance that I thought I would with working the AoA. It improved, but it didn't actually increase my distance. I believe it was because the spin numbers were still too high. LLM thinks I'm hitting off the heel , and also leaving the face too open. Quite possible... need shoe powder to verify.

item.title: Good trend going...
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I think switching driver is helping. I scored an 80, on a par 71 course with big fairways. Super fun (Whistler Nicklaus North). 5537 yards, so right in my playable zone.

The big breakthrough today. Nothing worse than bogey. There were alot of bogey's (10), but nothing worse than that. 1 biride, and 7 pars, and 10 bogey's.

First off Driver again. I started out hitting really straight, but very short. I eventually started hitting it a little harder, and it stayed in the zone. Looks like for the most part, I kept it within 30 yards , with plenty in the middle. This helped. I hit an insane high 92% of fairways.

I was not long, until I started moving better later in the round. Not quite sure what exactly did it, but it just started popping another 20 yards or so carry after the initial difficulties. It was nice to play out of the initial problem.

I hit everything else pretty good, Woods, Irons, Wedges. A few shots that didn't travel, but in general, I had pretty good lines. I could have been a little better with the irons, they tended to drift left.

The problems are still the same, I have the OTT tendency. I also had that same issue with the angle of attack down on way down (average 4 degrees down, and I want it 1 to 3 degrees up. Woods and hybrids have similiar issues (should be down, but I'm too down), and Irons are about right.

My spin on the driver is too high again... it's the steep attack and OTT open face. Same sort of issue with the longer clubs, Spin on the other clubs, where we want (although I didn't hit it as far i'd like so

item.title: Still trending down
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So interesting phenomenon in the last 10.

  • Front 9 : 38, 39, 37, 40, 41, 41, 39, 36, 44, 37,
  • Back 9: 47, 41, 45, 44, 46, 51, 41, 43 , 45, 53

Last 10, Average 39.2 on the front 9, and 45.6 on the back 9. A 6.4 stroke drop-off

Yesterday was Annandale Golf Club, I played a really strong front 9, with several good biride shots, and finally converted one on 9 (313 yard Par 4), to be just 2 over at the turn.

Then I went straight back to bogey golf. I started making mistakes, and having to hit out of rough and trees losing strokes. Nothing worse than a double, which is good, but not enough pars to make up for that. If I replicate the front I shoot a 76, but instead I shoot an 85. Not a terrible score, but I felt like I left a shots on the table where I could have done better.

For instance, my strokes gained show

around the green being great. And I would agree, except I had several shots that were flat out misses. The old chip and be happy to get on the green, has turned into chip, and put yourself in a chance to par or birdie the hole. My game has changed, and my expectations are much higher. I want to constantly be hitting my ceiling on shots that I make.

Another for instance, hitting a 9 iron 100 or so yards out. It's a shot I know I can stick, but lately that has been moving mor left. It's still my highest strokes gained (10 vs 5 off the tee). The driver seems to be a streaky thing. 2 Days ago, I'm hitting it nice and straight, yesterday I start moving it left again. Not all, but enough for it to be a pattern. And putting... you had several near misses from 10 ft out, not getting anythign but maybe 1 medium putt to drop. Part of this is aim points on the game, and also not being able to keep a straight line off the mat with the ball.

So this is great, but where do I go form here. I remember somewhere in this journey, I had a goal to get to 0%, and try to at least hold score. I got there about a month ago (5/8 moved to 'realistic'). Since then, I've done better hold my average. My average dropp from 88.1, to 85.7 (2.4 strokes). My rolling SAS dropped from 92.6 to 88.8 (3.8 strokes). My GS Pro index has drop[ped from 14.3, down to 13.5 (.8 strokes). So I've improved lets just round down to 2 strokes, while making the game harder by doing full realism.

So right now, averaging an 85.4 on a 5530 yard course fro the month. GIR is 28%, FIR 47%. The correlation of predictors is:

  1. GIR - higher GIR == better scores.
  2. Double Count - less blow up or worse holes, lower scores.

Interesting thing we've also seen. SAS and course length has very weaker correlation to scores right now (I think part of that is because I don't play long). Also FIR has weak correlation.

So making some goals movign forward. It's gonna be tough if the weather gets warmer, and the garage becomes unusable for practice. I obviously know the areas on swing

  1. Keep working the OTT problem, getting your sequencing down.
  2. Hit up on the ball for driver (reduce spin, further distance)
  3. Consistency in Iron and approach swings

You can actually ignore putting and chipping at the moment, they are not the current leaks.

  1. Work on maintain poise and focus on the back 9. Reset your swing during the back 9. Play it safer
  2. Work on the GIR, playing even more to mid-green

So you achieved your goal of mid-80s golf in the SIM. On current 5300 up to 6000 yard courses, your next stop is to drop the handicap by another 3 or 4 strokes down to low 80s. Consistently scoring in the high 70s to low 80s. You want your new ceiling to be around 86-87 (as opposed to 92-93).

The other big goal is to get the distance so you can move to 6500 yard length courses. These is primarily a sequencing based thing.

item.title: Had the higher score round... but didn't feel that way
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I scored a 90 today, Royal New Kent, first time played. Red 5563, which is just about right for me to score well, but I struggled. It was a higher 'slope' than I've played in a bit, but in general (except for 1 hole) I played pretty well. I scored a +4 on 17 that did me in, along with a couple of misses that I get out of trouble on the way. But besides that bad hole, I played bogey golf, 3 pars, 14 bogey's, and the one bad hole.

Let me start with the good, which mostly came from the practice

  • I was able to move the path more in to out today. Putting a head cover just outside the ball helps, along with keeping that back turned. This worked effectively with the i7, but not with the driver!
    • Average with the i7 was 2.8 O-I, which is much lower than 7-10 I usually have.
    • Best shot with i7, a 160 yard shot with 152.8 at ball speed of 110 mph with i7. It went way left , but still, I was able to create some serious distance with the i7 today,
    • The two next few shots were 141, 145, and 149 yards. They were both more over the top though, so who knows.
  • What I'm still noticing is that my arms bunch up as I swing through when I am able to get inside. It might be because now that I am coming inside, and the body isn't rotating, I've got nowhere else left to go, but to lose my arms.
  • For driver I had a more upwards AoA today - that stuck a bit more than usual, although final results were mixed. I had a ton of trouble getting inside on the path with driver.
  • My driver average in warmup was 201 total, with carry long of 213. This is good for me for flat range. Back spin on that long oen was 213. Path was 9.9 over the top, but the it flew straigth with a very open face. Another interesting one.

I hit one really good i6 during the round, 112mph ball speed, carries 151, total 160, I think this would be pretty good if this were my stock. Once I started playing the round, most everything was Out to In. It was like everything in the warmup went to shit right away. I think the driver and wood dispersion played a role in the round being pretty poor today. A few wedge overs too.

It wasn't terrible though, I made enough good shots, and hit the green 33%, which isn't terrible for me. I did 3 putt a few with very long putts though. The appraoch -15, and then -4.6 off the tee, and -2.4, and -2.3 for around the green and putting.

I think I rushed it after the driver hits were flying long. I wanted to take advantage before I fatigued... bad idea

Anyhow... with practice there is some hope here.

item.title: When an 86 feels like a 96
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So after Friday's 90, that felt more like a mid-80s, today I scored an 86, which felt like the worst score ever

I did not drive the ball well.. while distances were long, the shots themselves were didn't carry long. My putting and short game were not great, and my iron game was all over the place. I couldn't hit the ball right.

Red Hawk Ridge, white, was one of the shortest, and lowest rating I've played in a long time. 64.2/105. My SAS on this was actually 95, 4 strokes worse than the 90 I posted 2 days ago. My distance, slope adjusted score also was quite high after posting some of best socres.

The good was that I hit I still keep my double+ in check, 2 holes, and they were both doubles, no worse.

This is a course playing normal I should scored low 80s, and a little better below 80. Very dissapointed.

I think I was both a little sore from working out the day before, sweating a ton from the garage, and over working issues at the moment instead of swinging more freely. My carry was a good 30 yards shorter today than just a few days ago.

This gives us the best view of how are playing

The last 2 posted scores were a bit high after a nice run of low or well played courses. You can see a slight trend on the green line (That's the boosted score), but still pretty flat on the one with a normalized distance (blue line). It looks like you've been roughly in a channel in the last 20 rounds (since #70), showing capabilities of going pretty low), but also the odd higher scored round.

This chart I think tells a pretty good story, the number of doubles or worse is dropping steadlily still (even with the last 2 not so great rounds. I

You can see in the last 20 or so rounds the number of Pars (Red line), and Bogey( Green line) have replaced that. I does appear we are replacing the doubles with bogey's more often than not.

The handicap in GSPRO has stabilized to about 13. Let's say I'm 10 more on course, I'm still a whole lot better than I've every been. I think that is only on 5500 yard courses, and I still have the issue of moving to the 6000-6500 yards (Where I would like to be playing)

The FIR and GIR is also telling a story

I believe it was about 20 or so rounds ago I started playing more driver (and also dropping boost). I am missing more fairways as of late,

I am slowly climbing nad getting more consistent on hitting greens. Lately, it's about 1/3rd.

And the last chart. These are 'my normalized scores.

Basically I've stalled at the mid-80s average. I 'm ready to make a jump, but I dont' think I can do that without a bit more distance, and getting my swing fixed to that I'm actually swinging from the inside.

I've figured out how to get inside with the irons, but not without scooping. I feel like I'm at a spot where I'm starting to get close to my potential with my current swing, but I can't hit the next level, until I fix my fundamental swing problems. Once I'm able to do that I think the FIR and GIR go up a bit, but most importantly, my swing starts stabilizing to something repeatable.

Through all of my SIM rounds, so far, 1300+ holes, I think my ceiling right now with my current swing mechanics at courses 5000-5500 yards, is mid to high 70's. I can still improve my wedge and putting game. The iron game I could probably save about 3-4 strokes if I just hit the same shot and had a bit more consistency, and of course the long clubs can play well enough to usually give you a chance if you keep them in play.

The problem comes when I try to move to the next level, and I need the distance. I'm caught between trying to build some more distance and score lower. I'm still hitting super inconsistent most days on distance. Good shots travel where I think they should (albeit, rarely as long as I think I need to be), bad shots come up 10-20 or more yards short.

item.title: some notes
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
• To work on your OTT
    • Out over 2 - down over 4 (o'clock') , the is from this
      • (1) Facebook
      • 2 rehersals
      • 1 clip the mat
      • then hit the ball.
  • Relax it - Slow the f* down
    • (1) Facebook
    • 1-2 two tempo
    • Point A -> Point B, don't worry about the ball
    • Reduce tension through the body --- your crazy tense lately when you , face shoulders and arms
    • Best drill LEAP FROG! --- keep the tempo, but hit it soft, then 10-20 yards further, then keep moving up!
  • Why you can't turn through the ball --
  • (1) Video | Facebook
    • Setup a bit taller (one fist away from wall (bag, box)
    • Chest on top of hips.
    • Hip depth in early rotation- right hip back while dropping the club- this is one I'm not sure it will work. Bring You chest forward in the downswing, so you actually get in bent over.
    • Get your left shoulder at the ball

All from cogorno golf ... I think this is actually all good stuff for next practice block. I've gotten stiff through some things, and need to loosen back up. I think the first one is really good for path, the last good for the hips clearing, and I just love the leap frog drill to loosen up. I think all are simple and good for me right now.

I'm still on this path, I'm feed distances and stats, and if I didn't leak (ie, if AoA, spin, and club path/face delivery were better, how long would you be.

When I pass in some of the good driver shots, and go, well if I hit more up, and decreased spin, and my path came from the inside at those ball speeds how far do you think your going... and we are getting distances in the 250-270 range (total). I would be very satisified if I could make that the next spot for driver. That will pay the dividends.

For the i7 good example, I'm leaving less on the table maybe 5 or so yards. A 150 carry on good, and 160 yard totals. This would also be very satisfying if this is what we play, (you know you can do that, it's just not consistent at all) .

This is my dream gapping

This would make playing 6000 yard plus courses feel like the 5000-5500 courses you typically play now.

To get to the back tees (7000+) you'd need another optimization round to get yourself over 255 driver total (maybe more than that, 260-270+, and the i7 carrying at least another 10 yards. So going through my goals now, it's to get these distances at no boost inside, and take it to the 6000 course. The 7000 course would be a push goal for late in the year , as you need a ton of work to figure out the swing delivery. Part of me thinks though, if I can figure out swing delivery, I might actually jump the line up the distance chart.

item.title: Frustrations
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I wrote the below post last night, skip down to the end... I've got a real analysis of what is happening:

I am really struggling with my game. I've figured out a couple things in the last few days.

Swinging in to out (especially with the longer clubs), does produce less spin, and can hit the ball longer, but I tend to not get enough power in it when I actually get it inside. Still part of a learning process I guess...

I really struggle at low speeds even to get the club moving in the right path. The only drill that seems to help this is placing something outside the ball. Backswing more out, and then back in, helps zero in my case. It's a real struggle for me to get any club consistently inside. I find myself coming even more OTT lately.

My distances across all clubs has tanked in the last week. Not entirely sure what it happening, is it because of swing changes, or the changes not sticking. I can't quite figure it out. I was slice city with the driver today, which hasn't been an issue in what seems like months. I had that block left issue more often than not, and now I'm over the top slice again. Everything across the bag is coming severely over the top again and it's just ugly.

Whatever I was doing a couple weeks ago to get the driver moving 200 yards or so, has gone out. I haven't seen any carries within 20 yards of that in more than a week. In general, everything feels about 20 yards short of what I was doing a couple weeks ago. Very frustrating. AT least with the OTT swing, I could generate a lot of power with bad mechanics and have a play at decent play at it. Now it just seems like I am playing weak distance shots that I have no control over. At least before I was getting enough distance to make a good play , even if I was off the fairway. Now I'm short and on the fairway and spraying the ball all around. My mid hybrids to irons look even more terrible, and I'm scoring in the 90s again. I'm not taking the step I want to take, and I'm super frustrated by the whole thing. At the end of today's golf (after 3 days in a row), I told myself … I need to just take a week or two off, and reset again. I am so hard headed though, and I want to adjust my swing and get to my real potential. I've seen flashes of it, and it keeps me coming back. I feel like I am willing to put the work in… if I can just figure out the right work.

The headcover outside the ball with slow swings worked for a bit, but it's hard to maintain. Swinging to right field helps a little too. It's just not consistent. Hold the back and swing from the inside works a bit too, but I still get all bunched up with the irons. I have all this knowledge now, but can't get it to the right spot. I want to be swinging easier, but that isn't working. I think could be a bit away from getting this right, but I think there is a ton of pain to be had in my game before I get there. 1 step back, 2 step forwards. My 1 step back feels more like 2 or 3 right now though. The misses are amplified by the lack of distance right now. A 160 yard drive followed by a 150 yard wood shot , and coming up short is really demoralizing, especially after you got your game up to a decent place. Bad swings, good scores. Decent short game, you could get enough out of your woods and hybrids to get around the green especially at around 5500 yard courses. Losing 20 yards on most of these shots screws you big time. taking a step back torches you too…

I'm feeling very down, thought I was about to make that next step with a good understanding of my swing, but alas it was not to be.

Real Analysis:

This isn't bad, your just being hard on yourself. I took a look at the last couple weeks of rounds your averaging about 175 off the tee. Yes this sucks, but your not doing any worse or better. Occasionally your a little higher (highest average is 181), and a little lower (170). Nothing changed this weekend, your just not getting any better. That's it.

You may also have struggled a little with the 3W and hybrids, but not terribly. I think it's definitely a case of the body not catching up to the changes your trying to make, and it just feels like your way behind, but it's more than that!

So it seems your impact position could be a bit of a problem (it has been for a bit), and that might be another thing to work. You can keep watching the numbers, and watching what drills actually improve performance versus others.

So the real truth... your just not improving despite working on improving. Whatever you practicing is not working. Sometimes you hit the ball a little bit better, and sometimes a bit worse. In general, you tend to hit to the mean.... a bunch of bad, and bunch of okay, and occasional good shot. The good shots keep you coming back, but you have a ton of trouble recreating those.

What's crazy is that you can score really well by just keeping it in play and consistent short game keeping your score manageable in the 80-85 range, a few extra bad shots a round moves you in to

I am noticing the W3 average seems to vary a lot more, and that seems to be a better predictor of how your play is going. I should do a full analysis.

I think overall , I'm starting to cap at what I can score with current swing. High 70s, low 80s. You can play okay golf, but a few mistakes and your score can start ballooning quick. You have to play nearly perfect sim golf to score a 80 with your current swing at 5500 yards. You have proven that this is doable. You can hit good SW on to the green consistently, and 2 putt out.

item.title: Scored an 88, with some mulligans...about the same
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
SO I'll keep this short. Waited 5 days to play, played not so well, but there were some bright spots.

  • You actually were able to get a few drives with a bit more distance today, not great, but close to 200 yards on a flat course
  • You birdied one hole
  • You shot 42 on the front, despite getting an 8 on a par 4.
  • Your putting was better today (minus the 8 on the front nine, where you 3 putt)
  • You par7 of the first 10 holes

The bad

  • You were popping driver again
  • You hit 11% greens!
  • You fell apart on the back 9, scoring a 46. You really struggled on the final hole with a 7 on par 4.
  • You took mulligans... a few shots flew off, not the kind of contact you had been doing well with in the past... mid swing change nonsense.

OVerall, I'm in the midst of a swing change, coming from the inside, but I still hit it longer when I'm able to apply power over the top and get the face in a position that the ball is kind of straight. It's not really playable, but it's what I'm doing at the moment.

I feel like my time in the SIM may take a back seat for a few months here in summer... the garage is just too damn hot.

item.title: Still trending up...
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Bear Dance... this is a really fun course, a mix of some easy and hard holes. I played it yellow last time back 4 months ago, at a Yellow length (5384 and a 4% boost). Today I played it at 6278 (I chose this, because it plays higher elevation), no boost. I scored a 91 with a mulligan.

Now, I had a really good front 9 , 3 pars , 5 bogeys, nothing better or worse. 6 over... this is consistent play, you minimized mistakes and scored well. Again, I was struggling with distance a bit, not any longer or shorter, just about what I've been experiencing. Basically everything was still very over the top after some decent warmup shots.

Very frustrating back 9. I was okay, then things started falling apart (I had to take a break around hole 13, which played in to this). I struggled with 4 doubles, and one triple! 2 bogey's and a 2 pars.

So then I decided to just keep playing the same course, because I felt like I had a better game in me. This time I decided to really just hammer the ball, and try for more speed. I felt like the ball was traveling further. Ball speed was up, and I saw plenty of shots above 120 mph. Distance was only averaging a bit longer 6 yards longer). Delivery was still the same, but I was swinging a bit more free and focusing.

It felt better, I figured I would see a noticeable difference, and yes there was some occasional long really hammered shots, but actually dispersion went up some.

So swinging harder and faster, didn't make too much a difference. You had some shots that traveled a bit further than normal (H3 averaged 175, 10 yards longer, but they were not all good shots).

So I walked away feeling... just free your body, and swing free and fast and forget about all the stuff, and see how things go. I felt like things were going better when I was doing this. I could tell there were plenty of swing mistakes (my old swing in full force), but it felt playable.

The stats really tell a different story, swinging harder is having negligible effects. IT feels faster, but not producing a much better result .... 10 yards on one club, and 6 yards on the driver , while tells me something, isn't an overall massive improvement.

I want to try this a bit more though... I felt like not going after the ball was really costing me something... but I also think the stats don't lie...

I think it's also worth mentinoing, I hit a 228 carry in practice (same course where I'm getting a boost on the elevation, but still a good long hit). It traveled 241. What was interesting about this shot, it was pretty straigth. Face to target slightly closed at 1.2, O to In was 5.5 degrees, with an open club face of 4.4 degrees. Spin was 3184, which is lower than alot of hits before that. That was one of the lowest spinning shots, and it correlated a bit with a less over the top swing.

The i9 exhibited this the best. Best shot was .9 deg, out to in with a .5 closed face. AoA 2.0 Down, speed 85.1 ball, carry 125, , total 138. Spin seemed a bit on the high side 7100). I hit another shot with a more out to in path(7.5 degrees, and closed face(2.4 degrees) , that traveled the same distance at slightly higher speed. However spin was down to 5191.

Again, the drill that helps the most with getting the path inside is the putting a tee or cover in the way of the swing to guide it. I am finding that that right field does work a bit, but I tend to keep the face more open in this situation.

I tend to not be able to hold on to the i-o for very long when I do find it... it's very inconsistent, but occasionally put together runs (5 or so shots)with lower O-I (single digit), and occasional I-O.

item.title: Bay Hill
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
84! Finally a score below 85! It was a more difficult course, and a bit longer than I had been playing (5800).

Why did I score better... less mistakes, and pretty good with the wedges. Slightly higher FIR (50%) then recent, but lower GIR( 17%). I made a few mistakes, but stayed out of penalty areas. There were about 2 or 3 really bad

My speed was down a bit today. I think a bit of fatigue... I was a good 6 mph slower on the driver, and I think it trended the same through the bag. Shorter shots. My dispersion wasn't terrible though. Usual misses.

My Gspro HC went up, because it's been so long since I scored well, that I am went to 13.6. But again, not terrible. This was a good score, on not an easy course

Again, the win here was distance control within 50 yards with the SW. I hit the SW 12 times! I set myself up for plenty of putts, and converted 2, but missed probably 3 or 4 makeable putts.

I think of note here, the front 9 was just ho-hum. 2 pars, and then a couple double bogeys on 6 and 8 (6 I failed getting out of a sand trap on a shot so lost a stroke). I was 9 over playing bogey golf. I thought headed to another high 88-92 score, then things turned. I made a couple pars, a bogey, double, then 5 straight pars to finish out. Back 9 +3. I really dialed in and hit shots. While I did end up in Sand Traps a lot, I was hitting consistently with the SW and getting out with high soft light shots (at least sim shots)... that probably wouldn't translate as well on course.

So I think I should start tracking in my spreadsheet, 'Strokes Gained'. It's almost always in this order : Approach to Green, Off the Tee, Putting, and Around the Green, with the last two sometimes swapped

I think the 'Off the tee' is slightly under represented. Because I don't get good distance, or I end up playing from rough, I have a more difficult approach shot. It's not to say that I play 120 vs 160 all that different (would love to have that stat), as I think my hybrid or wood versus iron , might actually show about the same. At any rate, would be good to track. It's hard to figure out what would actually improve things.

item.title: Played 36 holes tonight
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
In the time it would take me to walk 9, I played 2 courses, all 18 for 36 holes.

First up U of MD my alma mater. I played this a couple weeks ago and scored a 92. It's isn't rated very high, but found some challenges here. Today I scored a much better 83!

I struggled some at the start, but kept it to bogey golf over the front 9 as I adjusted after not playing for a few days. Was hitting the ball okay, and mostly not making mistakes. So +8 over that first 9.

On the back 9 things really came to together. I scored a +4, all pars and bogeys. So 5 pars, 4 bogeys.

Interesting today, the strokes gained on this course were pretty close. The putting was +3.1, around the green + 2.5, and appraoch 5.8, and tee 5.6. The putting, as I recall (Throughout all 36 holes), I had lots of putts just miss by inches. At least 3 or 4 per round, and only converted a few.

Next up was this Ukiah Valley Golf Course. It was a tougher one, and slope rated much higher. I struggled, but the challenge was fun. VERY small greens, some very tight fairways (says I hit 71.4%, don't think that was right on the FIR).

This was a more typical distribution on strokes gained... approach to green -14, tee -4.6, around the green essentially 0, and putting -.5.

I faitigued over the last 3 holes, and had 2 doubles and par, but overall felt like I played well, and had some fun.

Of course, my swings are still over the top, and it got a little worse the longer I played. I didn't hit it particularly long today,

I'm still working on coming more from the inside, and I do see some improvements from time to time. TOday the driver was really slicing right in the first round, and stabilized a bit in the second

At one point I hit the PAradym driver again for a few holes. I smoked one way left (like I had been doing with that club, and that pissed me off so I went back to the PXG... still don't like either driver all that much... I will say, it was slightly easier to get AoA on the Paradym, ... but my spin was higher, and then eventually I blocked one off way left with a really closed face.

Anyhow... I can't seem to figure out where to work on things right now, but I do know it's fun as hell when I'm just hitting balls hard, and making some good shots.

I don't think I have much more time in the SIM this year... the heat and the garage seem to cause issues, and I think it may be shutdown till September/October pretty soon. Hard to say though, since when the A/c cranks it sometimes makes it bearable to be in there (today was upper 70s, sweaty but tolerable.

item.title: The distance conundrum
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Two players, same score… but NOT the same ceiling

Player A (Who I want to be)

  • Driver: 250–275
  • Scores: mid‑80s, occasionally high‑70s
  • Misses: usually directional, not catastrophic
  • Ceiling: low‑70s with modest improvements

Player B (This is me right now)

  • Driver: 190–210
  • Scores: mid‑80s - to low 80s
  • Short game: can be excellent
  • Ceiling: mid‑80s unless distance improves

Why? Because distance is a scoring multiplier. Short game is a scoring patch.

1. Too many long approaches

From 190–200 off the tee, you’re hitting:

  • 170–190 into par 4s
  • Hybrids/long irons into greens
  • More missed greens → more scrambling → more bogeys

Even elite short game can’t overcome constant long‑iron approaches.

2. Par 5s become 3‑shot holes with no birdie looks

A 250–275 player gets:

  • 7–9 birdie chances per round
  • Tap‑in pars on par 5s
  • Occasional eagles

A 190–200 player gets:

  • 0–2 birdie chances
  • Par 5s become “try not to make 7” holes
  • No scoring momentum

So getting kind of real here... LLM finalyl was blunt, and saying your in the bottom 10% of amateurs. It's conclusion

From 190 carry, your average tee shot leaves:

  • 150–180 yards into par 4s
  • 220–260 into par 5s

That means:

  • More long irons/hybrids
  • Fewer GIR
  • More scrambling
  • More doubles

If I am to believe Chat GPT --- it says focus entirely on fixing your driver speed and everything else will come along

did some calculation with projected medians over the last 2 or 3 weeks. A little bit of weirdness around the irons on median data, but it give me a goal on distances if you exectue this.

Adding the rough 10% on distances, this would get you playing around 1000 yards longer, in what I think is appropriate 6500 yard course which to me would be quite respectable.

This is where I am:

item.title: Driver practice and playing US Open course
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I went the driver practice route. I tried. I had a ton of trouble at hte start getting the club I-O instead of out to in.

I had to tell myself, you need to come from inside and hit up. I eventually starting having some good shots...

I had a good run at one point --

  • 0.0 degree club path, .3 U, Face 1.4 closed. 3250 spin, carry 205, total 222
  • .7 O-I club path, .1 D, 1.0 face closed , spin 2092, carry 212.8
  • 3.2 O-I, path, .3 D, 3.9.0 face closed, 2818 spin, 190 carry (this pushed left 60 yards, so not really a goo strike

Now... proved I can do it, and it goes further when you get these things right, but hard to repeat. I'll show you my max too from today, 208.6 carry, 218 total with a 2.5 degree O-I path and .6 up. Spin however was high a little high 3234. AGain not bad, but went left 28 yards. The rest of my shots were in the 160-180 range, with modest carry... but a tighter dispersion than usual.

Everything else was really coming up short today. Dispersion wasn't terrible, but I was definetly short when I needed to be a bit longer

So anyhow, I played Shinnecock. It will host the US Open in a couple weeks. It's a shorter course Par 70 --- but plenty of long holes. Tremendous putting and play around the green, again kept the score low. Really good putting today. I hit as many as I missed, so it evened out. Only one 'putting mistake'. Getting out of bunkers and play near the hole was good to. USually was in position. I might have had one wedge shot that was bad in the round.

Irons and hybrids were short, and the tee shots minus a few good ones were short, but in play. Only one double bogey, and 7 pars. That is pretty solid play.

My theory from earlier holds though... I can't score much better here without getting longer. I think my average approach was 170 yards, which is just not really playable. If I could of held those 200-210 carries, it would have played quite a bit better at this length, and of course the next tee up would require something a bit longer than that!

Fun course... like the idea of playing this a few times before watching in a couple weeks to see how close the course is.

Also of note... hit 64% of fairways, but only 1 green! Again that was partly because I wasn't getting enough off the tee. It says only -3.7 for tee shots, but -11 for approach. I think that stat is deceptive. Putting was slightly positive (.3), and around the green slighty negative (-.7)

Clear that I need to figure out how to lock in the distance!

The LLM explains:

Your median driver carry is ~195, total ~210.

On a 400‑yard par 4:

  • Scratch player: 260 total → 140 in
  • You: 210 total → 190 in

The SG baseline expects:

  • From 140 yards: ~3.1 strokes to hole out
  • From 190 yards: ~3.7 strokes to hole out

You’re starting 0.6 strokes behind before you even swing the club.

Multiply that by 10–14 approach shots per round and:

You lose 5–8 strokes per round on approach — not because of your irons, but because of your tee shots.

I need to flip this, and get he another 25-35 yards, and then we are having maneagble approach shots, and likely hitting irons to do that.

item.title: Drawing the irons
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I did a warmup today and I started with the i9. Really again working on getting the path more inside... and funny enough, I had success. I just threw the file to the LLM and said draw!

Today the pattern.... i9, 0 to 3 in to out! The i6 was 0 to 2 degrees in to out. Both had a few problem shots where I came over the top, but it wasn't as bad as it usually is

The pattern continued at the start of some on course round practice. I hit a couple beautiful inside, or neutral drives, before things started breaking down. Fatigue set in quick in the 80 degree stale air of the garage --- felt more like 90 and sweat was pouring down.

I just really felt good about how that early swing went. Loose, focus on coming inside, trying to use the ground (but only a little successful), and having some more hip movement (bump and turn).

It was the best I've been able to drawn the ball since I started. Perhaps I am finally making progress. I figure if I can really start drawing the ball, when I start adding speed, maybe I'll be lucky enoguh to get back to neutral.

Because I was really focusing on this, I took the 'round practice as more practice then trying to put up a score. It was good.

Best drive was second shot, a .6 O-I, with 2950 spin. 1.5 degrees up. I struggled getting the driver back inside after that, and it effected distance greatly.

The 3W was the same, but it's less punished by the over top swing... hybrids, kind funny were actually pretty close to neutral, but distance and speed were pretty bad.

The irons, from the warmup stayed better on path, with the exception of the PW, which was a bit more wild. SW was it's usual pretty good shot

So with this, I think the practice needs to be keep it slow with this swing in warmup with the irons, working on that inside path and coming through, and then add the speed as your swing feels stable... easy peasy --- right?

Hoping I am on the way to something better. I finally felt that bit of extra time today to square up, that I haven't felt in ages.

item.title: Decent Warmups -- okay play
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So get this -- my last warmup my path average on the 9i was 1.0 I-O. Let's contract this some, with best shots, the best shots actually came with a less than 3 degree O-I path

My I-O shots varied more in distance, and didn't quite get to top distance. They all also went left, as I closed the face too much

The i6, had a smaller than usual, more inside path, but by this point the body started taking over and you started coming more over the top. Best shots again were more over the top paths. As I moved through the woods, same sort of thing.

Here was the bit of an ah-ha moment from the warmup though. I've been doing a few things to get my path more inside out, I'm going to add two more to this master list over the last week

  • New: Get Back to Target on Back Swing
  • New: Hip Bump as your going back (still timing off on this )
  • Takeaway should be more be more 'outside' and vertical
  • Practice your figure 8s --
  • Get your shoulder back just a slight bit more
  • Aim right field (this is the hardest to get right at the moment)

So anyhow, warmup came and went. I played, scored a 90. A few blowup holes, as usual (3 over on 4 because you hit in the water, 2 over 2 holes before for the same reason). Penalties killed me. Around the green as usual was pretty good

My driving actually felt pretty good yesterday. It wasn't long, but was a bit more consistent, and a 64% FIR and -3.8 strokes gained tells a decent story. The approach shots were abysmal. Some of this due to lack of distance off tee, and some due to poor hybrid and iron play. Even when I did hit greens, I left pretty long putts usually. When I'm close off the green (within about 40 yards), I tend to do pretty well on distance control with the SW.

I hate being in the midst of this swing change.... It's going, but I tend to fall back or make more mistakes as I work through this. It is painful, and is keeping me off course at the moment. I need outdoor time to make this right likely.

It's way more fun to swing my old swing. It's fun to feel like I'm crushing my drives and woods over the top, even though they dont' travel far.

It still kills me how poorly my driver flies... My good carries are 190-200. My average was 180 on a good day, with totals in a good range 195-210.

I see some good shots in my log, for instance I had a nice 193 yarer that was mostly neutral path and 2 degree up angle of attack. It actually took off right, and curved a little back cdraw, but my speed was low on this (about 10 mph slower than the best over the top shots). Spin seems to rise quickly with the combo of Ott and hitting too down.

As I moved from practice to play, everything was moving more over the top. Not as bad as I usually am, but not coming from inside. It was fun though, just not fruitful in locking in new swing mechanics.

So that's it... it's nice out... I should go play 9 holes this afternoon, but I likely won't, and stick to the garage again

item.title: The Plateau
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I've plateaued, moved from a 25.7 down to 13.3 index since last year. A pretty good run of improving by 12 strokes at least in the game. I would say even outside I've likely improved by about the same. Being honest, I was probably in the 100s if I counted my mulligans outside, now I'm likely in the low 90s if I play the right distance course. I think I can score in the high 80s now on a good day outside (despite not having the reps)

I haven't been able to move the handicap in the game for a variety of reasons. #1, is the sort of constant swing change I've been under for the last several months. I finally am swinging more inside, but it's not consistent (Except sometimes in practice). This leads to more inconsistency in shots. I notice my GIR and FIR are still about where they were, because I'm still always working on that swing, and sometimes I get it and other times I'm awful. It's coming along though, I think there is progress despite this plateau.

I'm capable of a very good round in the 5000 to 5600 range, above that I start having trouble with distance, and this is likely number 2 reason I'm not dropping. You still lack adequate speed and distance to move to the next level. So along with sequencing, your trying to hit the ball harder than you need to , leading to a bit of pray and spray.

What has been working. It's been the same narrative for a bit now:

  1. I make 'big mistakes' less --- less hitting in to water, less lost balls
  2. You make more Bogey's and Pars than doubles. This is huge, you generally play bogey ball , converting some to pars, and a few to birdies (2 this past round)
  3. You work around the green well, your 56 is good, 50 yards in, you often setup for at least a putt,
  4. You 2 putt way more than you 3 putt.

And again why you can't

  1. You don't hit enough distance on some holes to make an easy approach shot
  2. You miss with the irons and hybrids way too often
  3. Your distance control on the irons PW and up is terrible, you just don't hit well

So what has been working on the swing. Get backed turned all the way to target, and try to use your lower body for power instead of power from the top with the shoulders. Easy to say, hard to do, especially when fatigued. Face control is still a struggle, but it's not the worst thing in the world. You need the hip bump, but not sure you have that full sequence right yet. It creates space I didn't have before when I was too static. Your lack of internal rotation in the hips though still likely a big source of power leak!

You tend left with your face closed about as often as you go right. When your HLA is right or close to center, that is typically good.

Latest round was pretty good. I had a phenomenal start, with the typical bad ending. 2 birdies, 10 bogey, 4 pars. I had one double, and then tripled the final hole! I went from a solid 82-83 if I par or bogey to the hole to an 85. Still a good round.

I hit a 40 ft putt somewhere in there, and made a few solid short putts, only 25 total putts, and a 1.7 strokes gained. I think part of that has to be my solid around the green. It was negative today, because I had mistakes there, but I also hit quite a few good shots.

Driving/ off the tee was 6 strokes gained. I was still at average 175. I need to get this to a 200 average, with the occasional 250s or so down hill. MY higher distance drives, were both left and right, my AoA on ave34rage finally moved to Up, and my O-I average 2.4 degrees. This is decent enough. When I look through the driver, best shot was 2 dgree up, but 4.2 O-I , spin sat 3100, carry 197. However this is only good in the sense that it went far. 210 yards. BUT it went 37.5 yards left. My face to target was too closed (which also likely helped that I likely knuclked down on this ballthat reduced the spin. This is driver progress... and I think actually outside with new balls I might get a bit more distance.

The rest of the bag, looking at averages --- I'm averaging about 4 degrees out to in on the club path, with a a more closed faced. Averages don't tell the story though, it's still all over the place, and you may make it good swing with a bad face control, or good swing with bad AoA, it's not quite there.

Opportunity to lower score is probably working the 80 to 150 yard shot a ton at this point. I think dedicated work there would likely get you to down a 2 or 3 strokes, and then of course a bit more distance (moving from 175 average to 195 average on the drives) would get you another 2 or 3 strokes combined and your now down in the 70s. It's really about just getting consistent with both I think. If your able to more consistently hit your longish drives (move the current ceiling to average), and same with the irons (move the ceiling of good shots to the average).

I think giving myself a little grace here too --- You took that boost down to 0% in April. This was a huge move down, and you've been playing in a window for some time now! This is some real improvement that should be celebrated... now on to down to the 70s in the SIM through the rest of the year, and getting to the 80s outside.

item.title: A solid 78
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
Best score yet today. Palma Ceia GCC. It was a par 70, so while it is the best score, it isn't quite as good Kapalua score back in April (79 on par 82), however on normalized distance , this being longer over a 70 par, the normalized score is better

So what went right

  • Putting -- was insanely good, I made most of my putts within about 12 feet, a couple small misses. Zero mistakes (putting past the circle) . 3 Gained STrokes from putting
  • Short game - I hit a lot of sand traps, and just off the green. Lots of within 50s, and the 54 degree was just fantastic setting up those makeable putts. Despite a 11% GIR, I was hitting the short shots well on the green and converting the putts for pars. GW was also good, and consistent. I only recall one wedge or two wedge shots that I would qualify as 'not good'.
  • Lots of Pars and Bogeys --- 9 Pars, 7 Bogey, 1 Birdie, and 1 double. That kind of distribution wins
  • Driving - I was shorter by average today, but had a nice cluster of about 6 drives that were between 190 - 200 yards and were offline less than 10 yards. I had some misses too, but mostly solid . I was still over the top, but not as bad as I usually am.

What didn't go right

  • Irons - I suppose it wasn't terrible, but it wasn't great. I either catch it or I don't. See distribution below. A good i6 hit is the only redeemable thing here. That shots was was over the top
  • Woods and hybrids were about the same. More bad than good.

I warmup well with the irons, but it never converts... something about shifting between longer and shorter clubs gets things messy.

The funny thing with all this, is I just play my swing the normal way, and I can score. I just can't seem to improve on distance and consistency this way. This represents pretty close (maybe 2 or 3 strokes) from the ceiling of your current swing at a 5500 yard course. This is just what you can do

Your gspro HC dropped to a new low --- 12.9. I suppose a small bit of progress. I need to get outside and start playing on real conditions to see what is translating.
