item.title: Played outside...played terrible
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
...but had fun. It's really hard to adjust to playing outside again. I may have been a little fatigued too.

So I thought the driver would have been better (and it may of in a weird way), but overall it wasn't. Too many bad misses. I lost 2 drives , which may have actually just rolled too long (rolled longer than 200 yards), that caused me to roll in to 2 creeks.

So good news... long drive of the day was 230 yards. I followed that up by a nice 120 yard 7i that landed to give a long putt. I then had to 3 putt, greens were tough today.

I'll just cover the other holes...

  1. Not a good start, sliced drives off. I then failed a 3hy shot, and then hit another that also failed. Eventually hit a good shot with the 54 on the green 2 putt in - 7
  2. Above covered, bogey, but not terrible
  3. I dropped my ball on what I think was a 209 yard drive... but likely this rolled 20 or 30 more towards the creek and was lost. I then PW 88 yards up on the green. That was 2 holes in a row that were sort of GIR
  4. Same thing... I think I hit the ball 220 in to the creek--- never did this before. I took a drop and then shanked, then wedge, then terrible putting.
  5. Another GIR... PW 80 yards, very short hole as they are fixing the tee boxes --- I then 3 putt...
  6. The dreaded 6... played about as bad as I always do... bad tee shot, dribbled down 127 yards. Then a bad 3W that failed to clear the creek. Drop, and then a bad 7i that went right. Wedge, and putter bad play, a 9!
  7. Technically... this could have been a biridie, I hit a drive... lost it, so played with the kids off the junior tees --- 181 yards to just right of green --- then chipper on and 1 putt in ... So another decent hole like #2 ---
  8. I GIR again -- but I played it from junior tee again. I didn't want to try 180 yard par 3, just not a good look for me. I 3 putted again
  9. Driving okay on the last hole, 185 yards in play, 102 yards 7i to sand trap.. Wedge and 3 putt, for a double.

So I hit a few good shots given the 44% GIR , that wasn't terrible. A bit of luck.

Hard to say what really went wrong here. I had trouble with contact... weird being on turf versus mat. Maybe just take a break entirely from the sim and focus on playing outside. IF you can start adjusting to hitting on the turf it might do some good. I could have used a bucket of balls warmup... I think that left me cold for the few hits.

A little disappointing... but also, this is a tough narrow course. I just need to do it more often. Also, the kids were easy this time, but it still involves a bit more mental organization when I play with them.

item.title: Haven't played in a bit
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I'm refocusing on some strength and a bit of cardio work. Combine this with the garage being a sauna has led to zero golf in the last 2+ weeks! Last time I played outside was the last time I hit a ball. I needed a reset anyhow as I was struggling.

I say I haven't been swinging , but I have been swinging in the basement without a ball. I have been trying to do the 'get to top of backswing -> shift/hip bump -> start turning hips while hands drop' --- keep arms dead if you can and let the hips do the work. GPT doesn't like me saying arms dead, and prefer quiet, and later. I think that is where I have been headed. It feels pretty good, but needs some more work to lock in . I fear if I go back to hitting balls I'll just let the old stuff creep back in.

I'd like to get outside and play some, but it's just been hot, and now humid as hell, and stormy in the afternoon, leaving us in less than ideal golf conditions.

I think a short garage session, and outdoor session either playing or driving range is next up... but might be a week more away.

item.title: Interesting practice.
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I setup the sim for the kids , but before they showed up I hit about 40 8 irons just to see where I was.

First off, dispersion was all over the place, but contact was suprisingly good. What was really interesting, is my half swing were carrying 110+. I think I carried one of those half swings 131 yards... this is something to practice. I was getting 140 yards hit out of my i8, which is where I would want to be, with i7 at 150 would be ideal.

I feel like the practice I've been doing in the basement, using the hips to swing has been effective. Quieting the arms, but it got even easier when I just had the club at about P6 (just slightly above P6 and through), I'm getting just as much distance as going all the way through the swing. This should tell you a lot, and give you something to work on.

I think if you work from p6 and just make the right, and then keep working the club back a bit further, then P5. Quite honestly, and I don't know if this will carry to the longer clubs, but I'd be fine just swinging half swings if I got consistent distance like that for awhile. I could imagine my scores would fly through the roof.

item.title: Less Garage play...
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I haven't been playing in the garage much. Last week I played... and ended up scoring my lowest round (minus a couple mulligans). A 78 on bear dance. So what happened, here are some notes, and it's been a few days so memories not that fresh

  • You were loose, and figured out a few things during warmup. I wasn't fighting trying to bring the club inside, i just let my swing go, and it just felt better. Despite that, the back to target thing helped me move better.
  • Looking at your dispersion --- it looks more normal, especially around irons this time. Driver was a mix
  • It was only 5300 yards, which a course you CAN score on
  • i7 averaged 140 yards --- so you were hitting longer than you typically do, with a 150 yards shot. The i6one shot went 158. These are the numbers I 'think' I can play at. May have been higher elevation help. I did have some balls fly over the green, was just hitting the ball better.
  • Driving was long enough. You had good drives (251 total long -- that was a bit downhill, but still good ball speed in the 120 range). There were a couple of drives off in to danger zones, but your misses tended to just be a bit off the fairway, not way off.
  • Strokes gained show 2.7 on putting. I believe that was actually because of a combo of good short game play --- you were getting the ball closer to the cup on the short game, and even had some approaches that were decent. Even so, I did hit some putts, and didn't make many putting mistakes . I am usually a zero to -2, so this was almost a 3 to 5 stroke improvement over the typical. When I start the next season of indoor golf, I will track the strokes gained as my key thing this year.
  • I had 3 birdies, hole 8, hole 10, and hole 11. I wish I could see the shots, but this was pretty impressive.
  • Despite starting with 2 doubles on the front 9, I grinded early and found pars and that birdie on 8.
  • The mulligans were a clear miss off the tee, and one that I shanked off because the mat moved, so they weren't as bad as usual. But still, like to get these elminated.
  • Some of my best swings felt easier.... Slowing down today helped get more distance.
  • I did better on the back 9 as I got warm. I score +1 over the back 9, just missing the par on the last hole to go even. 492 yards was long and I was tired
  • The garage is really humid, and it just isn't conducive for summer usage.
  • HC dropped to 12... not great, because this was an outlier, and you won't be able to hold it when you get back to more garage play.

Playing less, led to better playing better --- however, fixing some things in warmup and getting loose worked well

The i8 during warmup at 133 yards, with a 127 carry is about right... if I could just play this shot. 140 at the i7,150 at i6, and 160 h4, 170 at h3, and 180-200 w3... and Driver 200+. Those numbers are where you would like to be...

I really want to play today to see if this momentum carries over at all, but that always can be problematic. We'll see, hopefully a kid will want to come along.

item.title: 9 hole outdoor play
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I played NW inside 9. Despite it being a shorter course, it has lots of elevation changes, water hazards, difficult greens, dog legs, etc. It's short but challenging.

Yesterday, despite a poor start, I had one of my best outings on this course I have ever. The first 4 holes were painful, but the last 5 I played decent golf. It was the kind of score I think would equate to getting in the 80s... granted, it's a short course.

First off ... driving. Played this course 2x in a row, and what the hell, I can't find my ball... I keep driving way over and losing balls. There are creeks at around 180- 220 yards in 3 locations, and 2 of them --- couldn't find the first ball (had to use provisional). And then on hole 1 I hit a drive that shocked the hell out of me, but then couldn't locate the ball!

I think on that first one I didn't hit it quite as far as I thought. I really though I actually hit it over the fairway in to the rough... not realizing that would have been 280+. So I ended up dropping, hitting a 50 yarder on to the green and 2 putting for a 'par'. This was a decent start, but was pissed I didn't locate my ball.. I think it could have been a legit 250 yard drive that I usually never see... especially on that first hole.

Hole 2 was the worst of the holes, I just lost all control here. I duffed the first drive off, 131 yards (last time I hit a 225 yarder), and then the 3w I hit too far right, duffed a wedge, hit a decent SW and then 2 putted. Double Bogey

I then hit hole 3, which I usually play pretty well, except today... I hit 3W off tee hoping to center the ball on fairway and lay up. Nope... I hit in to the trees. I punch out , and then don't have a great shot as the punch didn't quite give me a clear path to the green. I hit a 9i well, and would have landed on the green except it ricocheted off a tree to a corner. Then had to pitch up , and putt... triple bogey.

The pain continued before things got better... So hole 4, I hit driver, great... it flies high and long, at least I thought it did. Pretty straight shot, but my ball is nowhere to be found. I do wonder, I think I overhit twice now in to the guys in front of us, and if they just got pissed and kicked or took the ball... I can't see much beyond 200 yards.

So at any rate, I drop, and I hit I think a PW which is 70-80 yard shot, and I end up in the sand trap. I then whiff at the ball before getting out and 2 putting... just ugliness

Finally an easy hole... at this point I said lets just try to bogey holes. Success, I use pitching wedge on the this par 3, however it is a shit shot but lands just off the green, I try the chipper, which chips across the green... chipper again, but not enough on it, leaves a long putt. I however sink a 10 to 12 footer this time. Pretty good

Now the dreaded hole 6 -- first off, I've never socred better than a double bogey on this hole. It's just a tough one. Even if you drive it 200 yards, it still leaves a shit look at the hole, with lots of trees in the way on an elevated green that is unforgiving. So I hit another great drive -- it goes in to the tree area, so I hit a provisional just in case, which leaves me a a shot to get over the creek. The i7 doesn't travel, but clears the creek. I hten I have about 100 or so to the hole, I hit the 9i... but I miss again and SW on , to a 1 putt. The short game was good here leaving an easy putt...

2 Bogey's in a row, things are improving. Now on to 7. I hit what I felt like a less powerful drive... but still got 187 yards out of it... hwoever it pins it up off the narrow green by a tree. I then tried the 4h cause I think I had about 150 to go. I topped it, rolls on to the fairway leaving 82 to middle... I PW on, then 2 putt. Another bogey... this actually feels like good enough golf

Now 8 --- I hit a bad i6 off the tee, but it somehow trickles on to the long green. I must have lag putt well here because I have it marked as a 2 putt

And finally 9 -- the hole of the day. I hit what I would consider a decent drive -- 204 yards. This left I think 100 to the green. I think I hit the 9i, I was aiming a little left of the pin, to the middle of the green, but of course it starts heading a bit right, but catches a nice bounce just off the green and rolls right within about 3 to 4 feet. I sink the putt, and got my first real biride in my outings this year.

I really haven't played much at all this year. Total 48 holes outside across 4 outings. This was the best, despite some struggles. A biride, lots of single bogey's , and a maybe par. I'd love to play more... I just hate playing with random ass holes and having to make friends. I actually like playing with the kids, as that usual calms everyone else around.

item.title: 1 Year Sim coming up, not a lot of golf
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I started the whole build out about a year ago. I started ordering in September and finished the build in October. I did pretty well. I'll go through some of my lessons learned on build , and golfing, and other things

First up Build, the good:

  1. The roller with motor is amazing. Heavy screen + Roller and super wide is awesome. It's not that crisp off the projector, but the realism is pretty good, and the picture I would say is good enough.
  2. Buying the used projector --- good purchase saved some bucks. It's been going strong for a year. Could upgrade at some point.
  3. The Square, it's a good little launch monitor, it really feels like playing golf. Putting is awesome, I think it gets my launch pretty right. Helps me work on things. I want the new version (Omni), but can't really justify an extra expense at this point as it does what I want , and I don't need the outdoors.
  4. GSPro - it's just a good piece of software, so many good courses. I know there is a ton of new stuff coming out now, but it's still really good, and I'll be paying for it for 1 more year. First round was 10/26
  5. The Foam Tile ceiling protectors. Super cheap from walmart, and do the job, and protect well. This was the best of the 'mods' I made, but was a lot of work to get it all up there.
  6. The lighting -- this could be an okay, but the lights you put in have worked out well, but would be nice if you could fade them down and direction them. I still don't the lighting setup like I should ...
  7. The television -- nice touch watching news or sports while playing
  8. The controller box -- it's pretty awesome when playing... I can't imagine playing without one.
  9. The magnetic hangers.... this could be a good or bad. One of them is broker, and it's tough to carry the whole weight of the clubs, but it generally works.
  10. Garage storage upgrade --- this was actually unrelated, but pretty nice.

The Build, the bad:

  1. Getting the screen size right on order annoying, the first cut was just wrong and delayed build by about a week. I provided correct, but I should have triple checked the order. Vendor was good about it though
  2. The stupid foam I tried to get between the screen and cieling by the roller. I've had 4 of the foam pieces come down. Tape didn't work well, nor did screwing them in to the ceiling. I will work it again this year, and see if I can come up with something better, but it was a failure at this point of a few hundred dollars and time wasted.
  3. The curtains. That has been a mess. They are useless, sometimes I use them with the kids, but usually I leave them down... rarely shank something that bad with a 13ft wide screen. I had an incident when the kids rolled the roller before putting the curtains away... it caused a mess, and they haven't been good since. At first really good , then not so great, and not really worth it.
  4. The temp -- not sure how to put this, all through winter I played and played and played. 3 to 4 times a week. Even in to june I got some rounds in, but at about mid june it started getting hot, and the garage rarely cooled off. I got a couple of short rounds in and a bit of practice, but it was mostly misreable in a too hot, too humid garage. For winter when really cold it wasn't so bad with the space heater, but for summer it's entirely unusable.
  5. The flooring... It works, but I'm not sure it's great. Maybe go in the 'okay category'. The stall matts are claimed to still stink. Crappy carpet I left in there is fine. It's pretty ugly, I never did attach the grass to the mats. Could do that this year, but not so sure about ROI
  6. The setup. It's not exactly easy, it takes about 5 to 10 minutes depending on if you pull the car(s) out. It beats driving to the range, but it's still a pain. Nothing is permanent. Along those lines, my wiring up isn't so great. It's all DIY and ugly. I have a 2x4 that I sit

The Build, what I'd do different:

  • Not quite sure I'd do much different, besides not do the curtains (they were a pain and now are rarely used.
  • I'd figure out how to get the gap between screen and ceiling right with the foam. A better solution there
  • I might try to figure out better flooring and setup , but I'm not sure given that it's not permanent, how well it would all work

So that is the build... overall, super happy. It's pretty awesome, even if unusable for about 2 to 3 months. I'm sure I will continue playing plenty over the winter.

So lets talk about my play:

The good

  • I hit the ball better... sometimes. I started out kind of short on my shots, and got better as time went on, dropping scores from the 100s, to the 90s, then 80s, all while dropping the boost from 16% in October, down to 0% in April.
  • The chart down below shows a working down of high 130s, down to 80s during year one. Pretty damn good. Short game and other things got better. You made less mistakes.

The bad:

  • I didn't really work on the swing in a concrete way. I went through so many different changes through the 'chat gpt' experiment. I had glimmers of hope that faded, but didn't really change that much. I got better... yes, but I didn't gain distance, or effectively change my swing. I got a better with a shitty swing. I started getting more inside, but I still come over the top. I still bend my arm. I still do all the bad things, I just score better with those bad things.
  • I didn't play much outside golf this year. When I did play it was 'okay', but not great. I almost didn't even want to play outdoors, because I hate stranger golf and I also enjoyed it inside so much. Probably some fear around how much practice I put in vs how I played outside and not wanting to disappoint played a role.
  • My distance still sucks... this still bugs me, as I just really want to be longer on all clubs compressing and getting more concrete. Maybe this is unfair, as I'm sure everything got a little better indoors... but I think compared to outside it's just about where I was when I was taking lessons a few years back. I am still chasing a simple average 240-250 yard drive, and a 7i that travels in the 150-160 range. It's not crazy numbers, but annoying that I haven't gotten there... I haven't figured out what is killing my distance.
  • I've turned into a " I don't want to play outdoors unless I'm ready and feeling uber confident" This is not helping my game. I probably can keep working and get my average indoors down in the 70s this year

What I want to work on this year.

  • Distance --- it's my killer right now. I want to play courses up around 6500 yards without the strain. That means I need more distance off the tee, more distance through the rest of the bag. That is really the crux of what I need to do.
  • Fix the over the top swing. I was getting closer as time went on, but it was messing with so many things. I just want to be neutral and maybe even start hitting some more draws.
  • Consistency... fix the faults and get consistent. Perhaps even get some lessons . It's tough because it's so much fun to just play, but perhaps a real skills development is needed.
  • Get really really good with the wedges in the short game. I already was pretty good.
  • Actually get back outside and play real courses again... Two or three weeks indoor crunch and then outside at least once. Do that through the winter and you'll probably have some fun and actually develop a real game.

That's my thoughts today... haven't done much of anything this year... so here is to upcoming year of sim and real golf. I'm supposed to play once in October, a scramble, and hoping to get some sim time before then to get things 'right' again.

In 2025, I played 11 times outdoors... In 2026 I played a mere 4 times outdoor ... that could grow tremendously in the next few months if I am able to find time.

item.title: 2026-2027 Season Start and goals
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I played my first round that I'm tracking as the 26-27 season, as I think I'll at least get a round in a week here on forward. I played what I later found out was a fantasy course called premonition. I actually played half decent despite the last hole where I scored a 4 over, otherwise it was pretty much bogey golf.

I fatigued on the final 2 holes and just had bad shots... while paring 17, I just blew up 18. I also had one hole where the ball got stuck and I had to concede the hole, so a 90 feels about right for the day. A few putts I think if I stuck would have dropped strokes, along with a couple of 'around the green' shots that I would typically have made in a month or two back.

Longest drive of the day was 229.1, but I faded as I played, and the average fell to 171 with a couple pops and shorter hits especially on the last 6 holes.

So I am starting off with the handicap in the game at an all time low of 12.2. I had over a 20 stroke improvement last year while dropping the boost down. When I practice, even with my crap swing I can play 80s golf. However the caveat is , I need to be playing about 5500 yards. 6000 yards up I tend to struggle.

So the goals this year. I think at 5500 yards, I can get the handicap down to single lower single digits. I think a reasonable goal is to move from 12, down to about 5 or lower. Like last year though, I'd like to do this while getting the distance up. I reduced the boost last year, and won't be able to do that again, instead I'll have to slowly starting moving in to the 6000 up to 6500 range.

With those types of numbers, I feel like I could do a lot better outside. My swing went back to the still 'very over the top' --- I'd like to get rid of that this year. I made movements towards that last year but it's not been able to stick. I think lessons of some sort are in order.

I have started tracking my Shots Gained this year. I think that will help... clearly it's the iron approach (or lack of distance on my driver shots leading to difficult second shots). I feel like I can make a ton of progress this time around, I'm just going to need to learn to fix the swing a bit more this year.

item.title: Hitting again
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I've been hitting a lot more balls , as the temp in the garage has gone down to about 70 degrees, and much more comfortable to play. I hit 3 times this week, but wasn't really ready to play 18 till today.

Today I scored a solid 87. It felt like an easier course, despite a few difficult holes over water or sand traps placed in front of the green. Overall, it was pretty good. Length was 5763 yards.

So I find I'm making mistakes that I would have mostly had cut out last year. My SW was a real weapon a few months back, now it's a bit inconsistent. I hit one or two really good shots with it, but on the other hand I hit a few clear over the green causing me to double back. This will cut down in a few weeks --- but needs some work.

Now approach was at SG -10 strokes today, and except for I think 2 holes, I was mostly missing greens. I was just missing them though, and many of them were just short.

I'd say at least 1/3 to 1/2 of the misses on approach were due to driver being short today. I did a good job at the start of keeping it in play, but I was very short as the day went on. I 'popped' several. This is something I was rarely doing back in April/May--- so that is also fixable with some more practice.

Overall though, I was carrying the 3W further than the driver today. I know I need some lessons to figure out how to get more distance... I put way too much effort into this to hit the ball so short.

Last year at this point I was shooting above 100 , with a boost turned on, so I'm both better at golf and also better at the 'game'. I'd say I'm starting the year about 15 strokes better, so hopefully I'll see a coupe of high 80s, followed by some low 80s I get back in the groove.

Today I did just play an old and comfortable swing. It's not pretty, but it keeps the ball in front of me most of the time. I'm not sure I'll be doing the scramble next week, but if It is on the books, I'll be playing at least 3 times this week through the weekend to prep my body.

I had a little copilot chat, and asked what would be a good goal. Despite dropping so many strokes, they think (and it's honestly probably more right than it's usual blowing smoke up my butt) is to drop the average in to 83-85 range, with a stretch of 81-83.

My personal goal would be to actually get that to high 70s with a 6500 average course, but that may be too far a stretch. I feel like if I can get there though, that really opens up the game for me ... but I think I need to figure out the distance thing, and that will require some more swing changes and probably lessons and a step back.

item.title: This years scramble
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So year 3 of playing the company scramble. It was a ton of fun this time around. It was more an even set of golfers, and each hole it seemed like one of us would make a decent shot, and we played it.

I REALLY struggled driving early, but by the end I was hitting most fairways, and it was mostly my ball that we played because I found the fairway. They weren't particularly long (175,199, 175, 204), but I found 4 fairways in a row.

There were some decent iron shots, mostly a bit shot --- my distances were where overestimated, and so I tended to come up a little short except a few poorly hit shots that rocketed a bit further. Hybrids were a super struggle, and I broke my wood. Big disappointment, as that has been my go to club for that 180 to 200 yards (or longer). Club snapped at the bottom this time. I will probably just buy another used one, an go with that.

So I can say, playing in the garage regularly does improve things... but it's all very temporary . It is good when you do it 3 times a week, but when you haven't been hitting them regularly, it goes away quick.

So the putting and chipping were actually pretty good. I had a couple real darts with the 54 in the 30 yard range. Putting was okay, but greens were pretty tough. The real problem seems to come down to my distance yet again. I can hit the ball, I can start to get consistent, but I have no 'snap' , no distance, no tempo, poor flexibility... all the same problems

Anyhow... I am ready to get after this for this year --- move from short hitter down to long hitter. If I need lessons , I'll get lessons.

Talking with Chat gpt the following analysis feels right, but no guarantees. I think I don't get my right shoulder under at all with any side bend. It's arguing with me about left shoulder staying down, but the left shoulder has to rise some... anyhow

DRILL 1 — The “Lead Shoulder Down” Side‑Bend Builder

This is the #1 fix for your pattern. You don’t side bend → you stand up → the club dumps → speed dies.

How to do it

  1. Take a mid‑iron.
  2. Make slow motion downswings to P6 (club parallel).
  3. At P6, freeze and check:
    • Left shoulder DOWN
    • Right shoulder UNDER
    • Chest still CLOSED
  4. Repeat 20–30 reps before hitting balls.

Feels

“Left shoulder goes down to the ball.” “Right shoulder goes under like I’m side‑crunching.” “Stay closed longer.”

Why it works

This single move:

  • prevents early extension
  • keeps the handle moving
  • stops the flip
  • creates late speed
  • stabilizes the face

This is the move that strong guys never do naturally — and it’s why they hit it short.

⭐ DRILL 2 — The “Handle Past the Thigh” Anti‑Dump Drill

This is the drill that fixes your early release. You dump the club from the top → ball speed collapses.

How to do it

  1. Hit half‑speed punch shots with a 7‑iron.
  2. Your ONLY goal: Get the grip past your left thigh before the clubhead releases.
  3. Ball flight doesn’t matter.
  4. Do 10–15 reps, then hit normal shots.

Feels

“Drag the handle.” “Clubhead is late.” “Hands outrun the club.”

Why it works

This drill forces:

  • lag retention
  • shaft lean
  • delayed release
  • lower dynamic loft
  • higher ball speed

This is the drill that turns your strength into actual distance.

⭐ DRILL 3 — The “Trail Elbow External Rotation” Shallowing Drill

This is the anti‑flip, anti‑steep, anti‑dump move.

How to do it

  1. Make slow motion downswings.
  2. At the top, freeze your trail arm.
  3. Start down by externally rotating the trail arm:
    • elbow stays tucked
    • forearm rotates palm more up
  4. Let the club fall behind your hands.

Feels

“Elbow stays tight.” “Palm faces the sky longer.” “Club shallows automatically.”

Why it works

This move:

  • prevents the dump
  • shallows the shaft
  • stabilizes the face
  • creates late speed
  • sets up side bend naturally

This is the move that stops your “throw from the top.”

item.title: 2 Big cues to get my swing back
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
My swing has been a bit of a wreck as I return... I keep coming back to a couple of cues

  • Back to target later --- p6 (club parrallel in down swing)
  • Trail shoulder to the ball after this

GPT gave me and move your lead (left pocket) back as you move the trail shoulder 4

The other one that I know helps is throw the club more outside at the start of the backswing. When I'm outside this may be a bit steeper

🔵 Your 3‑Cue Downswing Sequence

1. Back to the target until P6

This sets your entire geometry:

  • Arms fall
  • Club shallows
  • Hands drop into space
  • Right heel stays light
  • Right knee stays inward

This is your transition timing cue — not a position. It gives you the inside path before you even rotate.

2. Trail shoulder to the ball

This is your “go” cue:

  • Starts rotation without throwing the club out
  • Keeps the shaft behind your hands
  • Preserves the shallow you created
  • Matches your natural athletic motion

This is the perfect continuation after P6.

3. Left pocket back

This is the lower‑body cue that syncs everything:

  • Opens the pelvis without spinning the chest early
  • Gives your trail shoulder a lane
  • Prevents early extension
  • Lets you rotate through the shot with power

This is the anchor that keeps your sequencing clean.

So something to work on to see if I can back to something consistent, maybe find some more distance again.

I do notice --- the ball goes further (less spin) when I hit it more inside, at typically lower ball speeds? It still conflicts some, my top speed with the i8 was 94mph, and 130 carry or 135 yards total. That's still 30 yards off typical scratch. A +10 (what I'm aiming for) you'd still be off by about 10 yards --- and this is YOUR Best shot. So something is wrong here, very wrong with my swing

A +20, well, now my top end is right in there --- but I still have an issue, because that is the top end

I'm now in the overanalyze phase again... distance is the issue... a 20 handicap (which I should be close to given my gspro scores.... On the driver 225 is the average for handicap 20. I'm probably 25 yards or more shorter than that... so now I'm in 30 handicap territory --- 181-190 yards... this makes no sense though.

That is my 'true averages' removing statistical annomalies... and this is when you were playing well. I was playing indoors to +12 HC with these numbers... imagine if you could jsut get these to a normal distribution

Compare this to a 20 handicapper.

I am capable of each of these shots, but my averages are way below... I am 50 yards off the driver, 20 yards off the 7i , 26 off the i8... roughly 25% across the bag shorter than I need to be.... this is insane.

I need to fix this.

item.title: Practice is not perfect
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So the garage cooled off a bit yesterday and got a good round of practice in. I started with my stay down, keep your back turned cue at the start. I was entirely practicing with i9 and and i7 to start. I was stalling, which I think is okay, because I could still feel swinging from the inside.

I then started moving to dropping the club and trying to keep in turn. Varying success on this, I had a lot of mishits as I moved towards this. I then would move back to my more free flow swing , but then I would be more over the top.

Just taking my best i9 hits during this session --- 5.6, 5.4, 10.1. The first two less over the top, but still over the top, and the last one the longest of the i9 way over the top... but I was swinging free and finding speed.

Same sort of thing was happening with the i7... best shot was a 8.6 O-I club path. Of the next best swings (distance wise) --- I was 7-12 O-I so still very over the top, but the ball was carrying...

Even when I got occasionally under the 3.0 O-I or even I-O, they were fat shots... and did not carry far. My face was all over the place as I tried a bunch of different things today.

So as much as you would try to get this out of your system, you couldn't get the path to the inside most of these swings

So writing this, this was the top 3 suggestions

1. “Right elbow in front of the right hip”

This prevents the stall AND prevents the OTT.

2. “Chest closed until the hands reach the trail thigh”

This gives you time to shallow without fatting it.

3. “Rotate the right side through the ball”

This is the missing piece for your speed pattern.

These three together create:

  • inside path
  • stable face
  • solid contact
  • speed
  • repeatability

🥇 Phase 1 — Establish the Inside Path (No Ball)

This is where you teach your body the movement without worrying about strike.

Feel 1 — Right elbow chases the right pocket

What it should feel like:

Your right elbow moves forward toward the target faster than the clubhead.

Checkpoint:

  • Hands stay close to your trail thigh
  • Clubhead stays behind your hands
  • Shaft feels like it’s “falling behind you”

Why this is first: This is the primary anti‑OTT feel. It gives you inside path even if everything else is wrong.

Feel 2 — Chest stays closed until hands reach trail thigh

What it should feel like:

Your shirt buttons stay pointed behind the ball while the hands drop.

Checkpoint:

  • Right shoulder stays lower
  • Club shallows without you “doing” anything
  • No rotation until the hands are at your right leg

Why this is second: This gives the elbow time to slot. Without this, your elbow gets thrown out and path snaps left.

Feel 3 — Right side rotates through the ball

What it should feel like:

Your right hip and right shoulder chase the ball after impact.

Checkpoint:

  • Right hip moves toward target
  • Right shoulder moves around, not down
  • No handle yank left

So those are ideas... could work. It always is this moving target with me, and maybe I don't give it enough time to get better.

So let me at least discuss one good thing --- I did the op36 again, this seems to be a good transition to better scores when your getting back into things. I went through 3 successful level (50, 100, 150). Scores were 27, 30, 36.

The first two worked well, I focused on the SW for the 50 yard and that has been a great club. Then I moved to the PW for 100, and that actually swung well, where that club had been a struggle. I'm not sure it was right, but it said I hit 100% of greens from 100 yards in

For the 150 , I started off with the i6, but that was a mistake because it was only going 130. Then switched to the hybrid 4, and that was a better club.

What does this mean... at 100 yards in you average 3.3 strokes. What that means --- your paring most of the time, your are playing to a +3 if you somehow got yourself in position to hit within 100.

As I move up to 150, it gets worse, harder to hit greens, and when you do, longer puts.

Now where the real problem lies is with a swing change. If I actually get the distance that I think I should be able to do with this. My PW becomes a club down in this. My SW stays the same, so that is a different swing all together at 50 yards in. 150 yards should be a club or two down. Ideally, you want i7 to be that 155 yards club (That's a 15 handicap average).

Funny that gemini gives me a completly differnt version of thisL:

1. The Towel Drill (Eliminate Fat Shots from the Inside)

To safely bring the club from the inside without hitting it fat, you need an instant feedback barrier behind the ball. [1]

  • The Setup: Place a flat golf towel on your simulator mat exactly one hand-length behind the ball.
  • The Goal: Hit your i9 or i7 without touching the towel.
  • Why it works: If you stall, tilt back, or flip your wrists to force an inside path, you will strike the towel first. The only way to miss the towel and swing from the inside is to shift your weight forward onto your lead leg so the lowest point of your swing happens after the ball. [1]

2. The Hands-to-Pocket "Pump" Drill (Neutralize Path)

Since "dropping the club and trying to turn" is causing timing mismatches, isolate the transition path in half-speed pieces before firing. [1]

  • The Feel: Go to the top of your backswing and pause. Keeping your back strictly turned toward your simulator screen, pump your hands straight down toward your trail pocket twice.
  • The Visualization: Your hands should drop down inline with your trail bicep/shoe before your upper body unwinds.
  • The Strike: On the third pump, drop the hands and let your hips aggressively rotate through impact. [1, 2, 3, 4]

3. Flare the Feet (Create Easy Depth)

Because you noted that you are fighting stalls when swinging from the inside, you may simply lack the hip clearance required to get the club through. [1]

  • The Tweak: Flare both your lead and trail toes outward by 25 to 30 degrees at setup.
  • Why it works: Flaring the trail foot gives your pelvis automatic clearance to get a deeper turn on the backswing. Flaring the lead foot gives your hips a clear, uninhibited path to rotate forward into transition without stalling. [1, 2]

item.title: Keep it loose
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I'm working through getting my swing back and better... this is what I learned from just hitting balls this weekend.

  1. I'm hitting the ball too high. My VLA is higher in general, on some decent shots I getting closer in range, but I have too much loft. I have a table down below that shows optimal ranges based on loft --- Just looking at the 7 yesterday, I'm 8 or more degrees higher on average! Your distance leak is here....

2. Swinging loose is helping... take the tension out for speed. That old swing forward back, forward back loose actually unlocks speed. This isn't very new, but more a reminder on to swing loose. The strange corollary to this is the more loose I am the better I seem to stay on plane, the more on plane I am. This gets hard as I rehearse things, and then try to get in position... sometimes I think this can be counter productive. Swinging forward back/forward back/ forward, seems to be the best swing you can do.

3. My crappy hip turn . No problem going back , but coming around and using the swing in the hips has always been a problem. If was suggested to setup with a more duck footed stance (feet 15-25 degrees out). This felt weird, but could use a bit more work.

4. Getting my lead shoulder to the ball and making a full turn unlocks a lot of power for me... I actually feel the coil now.

5. Keep the club behind you in the slot , the further the head is behind you when you drop the club , the more inside your path will be.

5. One thing I learned of interest. Swing right while using the body to square the arms. I know before when I swung more right it brought the path in a bit. I need to keep at that.

I have a little concern I was using my lower back a little too much this last go around. As UI was trying to use the ground more and 'be athletic', I felt some work in the lower back.

I think this is progress... I think about where I was at a year ago , looking at some of the stats from that time... I was playing with 16% boost, and not quite as long as I am today. That's progress, but also shows how bad my swing was likely back then (and currently). it took my till april to get it down to 100% boost. I think my distances are about the same as they were back in April/May.

My number one goal is to get the distance with i7, and then see if I can start translating that back to the driver and woods in general. It's taking the current ceiling and moving that to a floor... VLA is the next thing to attack.

item.title: I've hit a wall
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
I hit balls three this week... and golf is not fun. I can't figure out my swing at all, I felt like today in particular I hit a dead end. I went to swing my old 7 iron just to see, this might have messed me up to start with.

Basically contact was really poor. I kept trying to get the numbers to cooperate. I kept trying to do things with my hips... bumps, turns, feels,. Everything seem to make it worse. Then I got too many swing thoughts in my head.

This was not fun, this was the most frustrated I've been in a very long time. Swing changes are obviously hard, and I am so desperate to get more stiance, but know it needs to come from the ground , or sequence and not from chasing the ball with my shoulders and arms.

After watching a gazillion different drills... I seem to be getting worse, and the only thing that seems to work is staying loose... and also doing my over the top swing at least moves the ball distance wise

I'm back to watching Danny Maude ... at least with Danny I was feeling a bit more free... every other online instructor had me swinging free... even if I was still coming over the top ... perhaps just sticking with him I'll eventually get it

I just feel like my hips are so in the way right now, and there is another feel that I am desperately searching for. It sucks that this has been taking the fun out of playing in the garage... but I have to figure out how to hit the ball further before I want to get back to playing. I can't play with the old swing and then practice with a new swing... this part just sucks.

item.title: Hit some balls, felt a little better...
item.dc:creator: jacksod
item.content:encoded:
So I'm still working on this trying out a real swing change.

My swing 'last season' was over the top, but I got to a point where I could play with it. I didn't always hit it straight, I missed both left and right, but I tended to keep it within a window I knew. I tended to keep the ball in play. The best club was likely the 3W, and it got used a lot because I tended to be less than 200 yards off the tee, leaving long approaches.

Irons were less all over the place by the end of season, and the short game was pretty good. I could control the 54 and typically land on green and 2 putt. But alot of times the 54 was a 3rd shot on a par 4 (or 4th shot on a par 5). I was still inconsistent, but I was able to make good decisions and play well enough to score in the 80s in the SIM.

My big conclusion was --- you need more distance. Here were some distances from earlier this year. The shots are showing Carry/Total

So lets take a look at HC targets with a 15HC form some good data that the LLM collected:

So then... so now I want to take a good and typical typical HC and got some good data around

So what I am seeing my typical distances are in that 20% short or more across the board. When I do typically get good distance I get closer to the 15 HDCP range, but I'm still quite a bit short (5-10%)

So now... I have to fix the swing, and while I'm fixing it I need to get it consistent. Hard to do at the same time. I believe the biggest problem is over the top, and fix that will lead to sequencing

I'm going to include this chart in my dataset that shows things well:

I am getting some suggestions from the AI again... I feel like maybe this had a positive effect last year, and maybe I just need to stick with things. I have enough understanding now, I just find the body doesn't cooperate as much.
